cosmology.world: Beyond Arret the world of Zallen holds other lands across the Crassac Ocean — Ru Ailmen's silk and spice come from them. What is out there is deliberately thin in this book: the far shore arrives as PEOPLE (a ship, a stranger already ranked, an invitation) rather than as geography. The hand-drawn world map is the authority on the shapes.

sacredTrees.summary: Each realm has a sacred tree; the fifth (Knobdimmon, Knakknthazn) is a closely held secret of the Empress and the five realm leaders.
sacredTrees.portal: The five trees lock a portal to Demonholme - the frozen demon-realm beyond the world - ripped open almost 500 years ago and sealed by the founders of Torrentath.
sacredTrees.mobility: The four above-ground trees are protected by a magic that lets them be only where they feel safe; rulers know how to find them. They offer sanctuary and seem sentient. Knobdimmon alone is stationary.
sacredTrees.godItems: Eight god-items pair with the god symbols at each tree portal; only five are needed to open a portal.

villain.name: Amurt Sselkcer
villain.note: Amurt Sselkcer is embodied by Essax to shield their identity.
villain.goal: Open the portal and release Kelethtonreth in exchange for immortality and the reshaping of the world in an image of his desires.
villain.mortalOrigin: Born Robert ('Bobby'), a tiefling; driven insane by Kelethtonreth's psionic touch at the sealing 129 years ago (per the Thane's account). Operates as Essax; true name Amurt Sselkcer.

knownAgents.name: Koth'Tavuth
knownAgents.note: Possesses the Princeps - the intelligence leak tracking the Champions.

knownAgents.name: Thron
knownAgents.note: Field commander; performs the border teleportation rituals that deliver monsters onto the party's trail.

knownAgents.name: The Kobold Sniper
knownAgents.note: Fired the shot at the Empress through a rend in space using a slender long pipe; never caught.

waters: Sea of Radjure (center of the Twins Channel)
The Crassac Gyre (the great maelstrom west of Arret)
ranges: Draybalt Mountain (near the Kitetown trade route)

gyre.name: The Crassac Gyre
gyre.public: A permanent maelstrom in the open Crassac west of Arret, wide enough to be drawn on a world map and old enough that every chart marks it. Ships do not enter it. Sailors will tell you what it is and then change the subject.
gyre.dm: DM ONLY — NOT DRAWN, and its absence from the map is what keeps the map safe to push. At the centre of the gyre the water is calm, and in that calm sits a FLOATING ISLAND: THE STILL. It is inhabited — not visited, lived on — by Si Jo, who come and go by means that are their own business, and it is one of a handful of places in the world where they gather. A party who crosses to fetch Kairon Malveth for a panel is the party that discovers the tenth dan is reachable at all: the fourth Si Jo is not a quest target to be tracked across an ocean, but a person who is already home when you arrive.

history.theIncursion: 129 years before Year 50 of the Reign, Kelethtonreth stepped through the portal onto the mortal plane and devastated Arret before being pushed back into Demonholme and sealed. A great wall of earth was raised, splitting the land as a barrier against his armies.
history.theBand: Kaddrin Vurrath, the Banner of the Red Hawk: the adventuring band that stood at the sealing - young Arith (now Empress), Abra of Pand, El, Lebby of Teg, Lid (now Sovereign of Aria), and Kili (now Thane). Kelethtonreth touched each of their minds before the seal closed, promising revenge.
history.essaxOrigin: Essax was then 'young Bobby' - Robert when they were testy - a gaunt young tiefling with a chip on their shoulder. Kelethtonreth's psionic touch drove them insane; they now rule the Bronze Storm Empire with an iron fist and serve Kelethtonreth in hope of staying their own punishment.
history.brozeStormResistance: Cal Nai - the Red Knife - a resistance within the Bronze Storm Empire opposing Essax.

gazetteer.description: Home of the Empress and her family. Castle Trei at the center; 50-ft walls encircle the inner city (2-mile radius); a 25-ft outer wall ~23 miles beyond; the Far Gate city sprawls outward toward Lake Sala'amas.
Home of the Steward. Coastal city of white limestone; slum timber is whitewashed to match. Glitters in the sun from quartz deposits.
Twin city to East Omaththyr, in a valley on the trade route to the Bronze Storm kingdom; a trading village grown into a stronghold city.
Small city split by its namesake river and the Bethal-Omaththyr trade route.
Small city on the White Water and the main trade route from Bethal to Mutemere.
Small city on the west coast of Lake Sala'amas; last major city on the trade route from Bethal to the realm of Essa.
Small canal city; southernmost in Pand and source of Bethal's limestone; split by the White Water and the coastal trade route.
Transient home of the Panarch; twice the size of its twin West Omaththyr, on the border of Pand at the river Hart.
Dense forest home of the Panarch, elves, and rangers; treetop houses glimpsed only by the keenest eyes. Namesake of the sacred tree Aedlab.
Sovereign's palace on the northern tip. Port city known for silk and spice imports from beyond the Crassac Ocean.
Palace of the Council of Twelve on the northern tip. The Council and the Sovereign rule Aria together, the Sovereign being the greater among equals.
Home of the Lord of Teg; closest capital to the Imperial Capital; near the Drrosh Doors, the only known entry to Knakknthazn. Renowned for dwarven-made arms and armor.
Small city SW of Kitetown at a trade-route split (north to Kitetown, east to Brimwater); Trenlem River to the south. Most Aria trade passes through.
Small city SE of Kitetown; a stronghold on the northern shores of the Trenlem. The now-defunct southern trade route ends at the cliffs of the World Spine Mountains.

Enormous underground city beneath Lake Sala'amas: a perfect stone dome of 250-mile radius, hub of a wheel spiraling beneath all four realms. Four cardinal runes: no scrying on the realm; climate conversion of Sala'amas waters plus the annual Week of Sun & Sky; a mass sanctuary spell (+10 to attackers' required WIS save; failed saves cannot retarget); the mass seal protecting Knobdimmon. The tree stands at the city center in the Sanctuary of the Tree beneath the Keep. Its keyed streets — the shops, forges, manors and reserves of the eight clans — are Thig Dural Thane, the Royal District (per Infrastructure records).
Small city where the trade route splits north toward Pand and east toward Teg.
Small city split by the capital-Teg trade route and the Irricam River.
Small city on the Teg border along the trade route, west of the Jade River.

Ebony Camp

# Description

As with all Inns within the Twin Cities the roof tiles are Blue. The three story stone structure is adorned with beautiful worked iron fenced balconies on the third and second stories. Entering the front door from the street you enter a comom room with a small stage in the corner to the left and six tables with chairs that seat four and six. Behind a bar at the back you will most likely find  the proprietor Rinys Glowseeker (she/her, 180). Rinys is a stout Halfling with a blue coat, white ruffled undershirt and brown britches encompassed by a bleach white apron around her waist.

There is a halfway to the left just beyond the stage that leads to two private dining rooms with tables and chairs set for a dozen people in the large room and eight people in the small room. At the end of this hall is the stairwell. The second and third floors are rooms for rent. The second floor has six rooms at 2 GP per night and the third floor has four rooms at 4 GP per night. Staying for a Tenday is given a discount of 16 GP and 34 GP respectively. 

There is a door to the right behind the bar that enters the kitchen and a door to the left that leads to the chamber room. The cook Panver Applehands (He/Him, 122) has been the cook for this establishment for over 50 years. He was an apprentice here when he started cooking.

# Description

As with all Taverns within the Twin Cities the roof tiles are Red. This sprawling two story Channel side stone building on East Channel Street has two large windows, shutters thrown wide on either side of its double doors. Walking in, there is an aisle down the center of the Tavern splitting two sets of six round tables that seat six. There is a door and the same open windows mirroring the ones behind you. Out the window you can see a partially covered patio with six more round tables, though four of them are up against the (human) hip height wall so they only sit 5. Looking a little further you see Gulls in the wind above what you cannot see but now feel in the dampness of the air, the Channel. Two bars, one on each side from the middle of the building to the far set of the back windows servering when customers walk up to the bar or windows, though the tenders will not leave from behind the bar with the exception of trying to eject a customer that is not following the rules. “The Rules” Marked on a chalkboard on the wall above each bar.

Sovereign Palace

# Description

Walking up Sovereign Rode and entering the cul de sac in front of the Sovereigns Palace, this Large Palace has walls ten feet tall and spires capped with brass cones. Beyond the walls the multicolored Tiled roofs of several keeps can be seen. A huge arch with a drawn Portcullis,  large spikes pointed at their resting holes below looks to be the only entrance. Sovereign Guards flank the entrance, two on each side, armed with spears all pointed at the same angle at their shoulder and a short sword at their hips .

Soldiers 

- Sergeant on Duty

- Perumo Glowsky, Halfling, He/Him, 59

- Corporal

- Joret Earthsurge, Halfling, He/Him, 54

- Specialist

- Quinpos Teabrace, Halfling, He/Him, 49

- Wenumo Bronzeshine, Halfling, He/Him, 45

- Zenbin Roseearth, Halfling, He/Him, 39

Pass the Portcullis is an arched tunnel that ends 30 feet at a closed, huge, hinged iron bound double door that matches the arch. The wicket gate is open showing a paved courtyard. The walls to the left and right are barracks that house a Sargent on Duty, two Corporals and twelve specialists.There are two murder holes in the celing. Each one is accessible by one of the barracks each. The door to the left barrack is open.

The barrack on duty will always have its door open and the Sergeant on Duty will most likely be sitting at the desk in the reception room. The reception room is small and has one door toward the inside of the Palace Wall.

# Hideout

The Moonlight Strategy is a transient  group by trade. Without moving around they would be easily found and that would be bad for business. It is known on the streets of Ru Ailmen where some of its members frequent. Most frequently at The Rare Coin Tavern though unknown to most that are not members, Ebony Camp Inn is their hub of operations. In a side room down a hall on the first floor off the main dining room there is a door to a storage room. In this room there is a secret door. That door opens to a small closet space with a hatch that goes straight down thirty feet. There is ample space for a medium creature to go down the sturdy ladder. The room opens below to a large domed structure carved from the bedrock of the island. The proprietor of the inn, Rinys Glowseeker is the gatekeeper to the den. A former Master Thief of the Moonlight Strategy.

There is a Bar to the left with a hulking Warforged tending, heavy brow made of steel as well as its hinged jaw. Blue gemstones set as eyes glow faintly in the warm light of the lamps set in the walls. He’s wearing a white button down shirt with a collar that covers his mettle chest. Also, what looks to be some dark pants behind a bleached white apron. He is wiping down mugs with a white towel. There are four tables in front of the bar with four seats each. It looks like two of the tables had recently been pushed together from the position of the stools.

To the right there is a cordoned off area that looks to be a sparring pit of some sort. With a closer look a circular ring is painted on the floor with a twenty foot diameter. There are two lines painted opposite each other, about ten feet apart. There are ropes tied to posts that encircle the ring a few feet back from the painted circle with an entrance opposite the bar.

To the back, opposite the entrance, there are what look to be three thresholds. They are all three covered with beads, so that any breach to those thresholds could be heard. 

The left entrance opens to a kitchen. The center leads down a hall with two doors, one on the left and one at the back. The one to the left opens to a storage room. The one at the back of the hall opens an office/bedroom. Xannys Truebridge occupies this room as is her right as Master Thief. The threshold on the right opens to a short hallway with a door at the end. This door opens to a stairway down. The stairway leads to the underground tunnel system used by the city for infrastructure and sanitation. This door is guarded by a Half-Orc Blackcap at all times.

Two people are pulled up to the bar, Valfer Keenlade and Elielle Nimblesurge drinking and talking with no concern for the newcomers. Ruglal Vuzrubor sits with his cowl drawn and tight leather gloves on in an alcove back and to the left of the entrance portal in position to watch anyone coming through, nursing a drink and going over maps and layouts of manor houses. He has extinguished the lamp that lights this area.

How to Enter

To be granted entrance you must pass through Rinys Glowseeker first. Of course all the members that live in the city are known to Rinys. Those that are not must be vouched for in some way. This includes by a member of significant rank (Operative or higher) or with significantly convincing physical evidence that can be handed over for inspection (this requires the person in possession of the evidence to give it away temporarily to be inspected by an active member of the club to inspect, normally available in the den. This method requires 24 hours as a test of patients on behalf of the possessor). The Empire Rank insignia is also accepted of course.

Ways to find Rinys

Finding someone who is a member for the Moonlight Strategy for those versed in the criminal world is not a hard task. Members of the Moonlight strategy have been known to congregate at The Rare Coin Tavern as of late. The tale tell sign of  a member being the crescent moon with an adjacent four pointed star, shining out in four other directions tattooed to the web of the left hand between the thumb and forefinger (this can be easily hidden by closing the webbing with the thumb against the forefinger):

Empire Operative Tattoo

A small open traveling Carnival with wagons set as trade stalls backs with canvas shades held up by poles in front.

- Hosts the Flowers in the Bouquet game

- Tiny clockwork dragonfly that slowly beats its wings (cannot fly) when wound up

- Glossy mushroom with a reg, bell-shaped cap that jingles when shook

- Tiny sundial that casts a shadow only in moonlight

- Tibac pipes

- Gnarled root

- “Dragon” horn

- Bone

- Leather Tibac pouches

- Tibac

- Strawberries 2 copper a piece

- Honeyed Strawberries 3 copper a piece

- Apples 3 copper a piece

- Caramel Apples 5 copper a piece

- Honeyed Apple 4 copper a piece

- DC 18 Dexterity Check to win 

- Price 3 rings 3 silver

- Prize

- Strawberry

- Caramel apple

- Description: post ten feet out must stand on the rug. Ring is a 3 inch piece of copper. A Glimmerkin named Lareth sits upon a wooden box with a purple cloth covering most of it dangling her legs and holding three brass rings almost as big as she is. Her wings start to flutter as you neer and she flies up to greet you. 

“Hello! I am Lareth and this is the Ring Toss! 3 Silver for 3 rings! You have to stand on the rug and ring the post! One point for each ring on the post. Three levels of prizes!”

- +2 for the apprentice and +4 for the master 

- 3 wins in 5 turns

“Hello, I am Hans and this is Frans and we are here to… pin you. The price is 2 silver but the prizes differ for I am Hans the apprentice and he is Frans the master. Which do you choose?”

- DC 20 Wisdom gives away the correct shell DC 18 gives a 50/50 chance

- Price: 1 silver

- Prize: Face paint (disguise self for 1 hour) 3 wins out of 5 

# Flowers in the Bouquet

- DC 22 Intelligence check gives away the correct number including the one tied around its stems

- Price 1 silver

- Prize

- Right number of Flowers - gain that bouquet of flowers

locations.name: Ru Ailmen Sick House
locations.detail:
Ru Ailmen Sick House

# Description

This one story building with white washed stone walls and a blue and yellow tiled roof is long and simple. The entrance leads into a receiving room where a healer in white robes can triage patience and let the less severe wait in chairs if necessary. Beyond the receiving room through double doors is the treatment room where six beds on each side of the room can house twelve patients. A door at the back of the largest room leads to a smaller room with a single table where life threatening wounds are treated with utmost priority.

Staff

- Receptionist 

- Lahorn Wisebloom, Halfling, she/her, 88

- Arlan Hogcheeks, Halfling, he/him, 84

- Orderly 

- Cror, Half-Orc, he/him, 30

- Zisre, Half-Orc, she/her, 24

- Apprentice Healer

- Qicaryn Humbleman, Halfling, she/her, 67

- Thamprys Proudwoods, Halfling, she/her, 45

- Chenree Goodflower, Halfling, she/her, 76

- Healer

- Wisys Moontopple, Halfling, she/her, 120

- Valeigh Highshadow, Halfling, she/her, 102

- Uvifice Keencrest, Halfling, she/her, 88

- Conace Heartspark, Halfling, he/him, 69

- Davdak Swifthands, Halfling, he/him, 99

# Campaign Notes

Lahorn Wisebloom was there that day that Jazz came to visit and received her and was amazed by her offering of help. She brought her to the treatment room where Jazz proceeded to heal everyone in the room of their various injuries. Cror, Qicaryn Humbleman, Thamprys Proudwood and the lead healer Wisys Moontopple were all witness to this. The four that were healed were very grateful. One man with a broken leg and three others with minor scrapes and bruises. Quowrick Stillspirit, Halfling, he/him, 67 - Zalton Mossbrush, Halfling, he/him, 34 - Falton Leafearth, Halfling, he/him, 44 & Trynni Strongtop, Halfling, she/her, 25 respectively. Once Jazz had completed the healing she offered four gold pieces to the person in charge (Wisys) to assist with the needs of the Sick House.

locations.name: North Docs Market
locations.detail:
North Docks Market

# Description

A sprawling marketplace where you can find all manner of trinkets, bobbles, artifacts, food and services. The dock is shaded by canvas tarps and each of the stalls seem to be a permanent fixture made of heavy canvasand in some places plank walls. Some of the stall owners stay to keep an eye on their wares while others pack up their valuables for the night and head home with them.

# Campaign Notes

The party with no name, in search of Diamonds were given a description of an old lady that sells trinkets and bobbles, but also has been known to sell diamonds from a cache that seems to be replenishable. Bethal Kurneal Shaseth, Dragonborn, she/her, 74 sits in her rocking chair at the back of her shop. She is old, yet a battle hardened fighter who has not lost her strength yet. When she sits in her chair, she slouches and hides he bulk behind her robes. When asked about diamonds she will croak about her bobbles being nicer than the diamonds. She keeps her cache in a burlap sack next to her rocking chair. There are always at least 5 large diamonds at 100 GP each and 7 medium diamonds at 50 GP each. She will always find a way to get out of the chair and reach for something, a bobble or trinket and make sure to loom to her full seven feet and flex her massive biceps after showing anyone diamonds for the first time.

# Description

The Storm Hammer Garage is a working being. A bit cluttered and grungy, but solid wares for the hard core adventurer.

Wares

- Hammers

- Sledge 2 gp

- Axes

- Stormcleave 2000 gp

- Arrows

- Poison Cloud arrows

- On hit, the arrow releases poisonous gas in a 10ft sphere, lightly obscuring vision in that area. The cloud lasts for 10 rounds, unless removed by a strong wind. Creatures take 1d4 poison damage on entering the cloud, or 1d4 poison damage on the start of their turn if they are in the cloud.	

- 150 gp

- Magefire arrows

- Fire arrows that magically ignite once fired. Deals 1d6 extra fire damage and ignites non-worn, non-carried flammable materials.	

- 50 gp

- Explosive arrows

- These arrows explode on hit. All creatures within a 10ft radius must make a 15DC dex saving throw or take 2d10 fire damage. Ignites non-worn, non-carried flammable materials.	

- 150 gp

- Ice arrows

- These arrows are cold to the touch. On hit, the target takes 1d8 cold damage and must pass a 15DC con saving throw or suffer -10ft to their movement speed and have disadvantage on dex saving throws for 3 rounds (does not stack).	

- 150 gp

- Acid arrows 

- On hit, the target takes 1d8 acid damage and must pass a 15DC con saving throw or suffer -2 to their AC and have disadvantage of con saving throws for 3 rounds (does not stack).	

- 150 gp

- Thunderclap arrows

- These arrows release a thunderous explosion on hit. All creatures within a 10ft radius must make a 15DC con saving throw or take 2d8 thunder damage, are pushed back 5ft and fall prone. Loose objects are automatically pushed 5ft away.

- 150 gp

- Lightning arrows

- These arrows cast a streak of lightning in their wake. Any creatures within 5ft of a line between you and your target (including your target, but not yourself) must make a DC15 dex saving throw or take 1d8 lightning damage.	

- 150 gp

- Arrow of Fiend Slaying +2 

- 2500 gp

- Contract Arrow Work

- Free Quote with a ask of 24 to 48 hours for research.

locations.name: The Puzzled Voyage
locations.detail:
The Puzzled Voyage

# Description

An arcane house behind an iron plate stamped with a wand crossing a four-pointed spark. The shelves are arranged like a riddle — charts that match no coast anyone sails, compasses that settle on questions rather than north, and wares that hum faintly when the door closes. Yuddoul Barrelaxe keeps the wards, and enjoys watching a customer work out which aisle they actually needed.

locations.name: Wicked Arsenal Wand Store
locations.detail:
Wicked Arsenal Wand Store

# Description

A narrow arcane shop under the same spark-and-wand plate as its neighbors, racked floor to ceiling with wands resting in iron cradles. Nothing crosses the counter until Whuzzurum Platehide has sized up the buyer — the arsenal is wicked, the ownership is careful. Test firings happen in a stone-lined cellar, one customer at a time.

locations.name: The Floating Wall Pet Store
locations.detail:
The Floating Wall Pet Store

# Description

The Floating Wall Pet Store is a blast to the senses as you enter. There are all manner of pets for sale here. If you do not see what you are looking for, we will find a way to get one here.

locations.name: Bittermaster Forge
locations.detail:
Bittermaster Forge

# Description

A working clan forge under the hammer-above-anvil plate, the Bittermaster mark beneath. The floor runs hot and loud from first bell, and commission work is taken by arrangement rather than off a shelf. Nokdrotir Oakback keeps the floor and holds every piece to the clan's old tolerances — work leaves when it is right, not when it is due.

locations.name: Barrelshoulder Forge
locations.detail:
Barrelshoulder Forge

# Description

A working clan forge under the hammer-above-anvil plate, the Barrelshoulder mark beneath. Heavy work is the house pride — cart axles, gate hinges, anchor chain — and the clan's smiths are built to match the name. Bhamnorli Hammermaster keeps the floor, beside a wall of finished commission tags going back three generations.

locations.name: Kegborn Forge
locations.detail:
Kegborn Forge

# Description

A working clan forge under the hammer-above-anvil plate, the Kegborn mark beneath. The Kegborn name rides half the barrel hoops and tap fittings in the district, and the forge still turns out the banded kegs that earned it. Vozmaeg Blazingtank keeps the floor, and commission work is arranged at the front bench.

locations.name: Woldtank Forge
locations.detail:
Woldtank Forge

# Description

A working clan forge under the hammer-above-anvil plate, the Woldtank mark beneath. Quieter than its three rivals, the shop does slow, exact work — locks, hinges, fittings that have to sit flush the first time. Dorromli Mudbrand keeps the floor and takes commissions by arrangement, with a ledger of promised dates kept where every customer can read it.

locations.name: The Needy Flower Pharmacy
locations.detail:
The Needy Flower Pharmacy

# Description

An apothecary under the mortar-and-pestle plate. Shelves of the district pattern — tinctures, salves, dried simples hung in paper sleeves — and honest advice given whether or not it makes the sale. Modribena Caskbow keeps the shop, and keeps a bench by the window for anyone who needs to sit down before they can say what is wrong.

locations.name: The Wishing Elixir
locations.detail:
The Wishing Elixir

# Description

An apothecary under the mortar-and-pestle plate, brighter inside than its name suggests. The house trade is tonics — bottled in colored glass, labeled in a fine hand, and sold with plain instructions rather than promises. Barikhaemora Magmabow keeps the shop, and will not sell a second bottle until she hears how the first one went.

The Rapid Grape

# Description

An apothecary under the mortar-and-pestle plate, named for the cordials that are its front-room trade. Behind the cordial racks the working shelves hold the district pattern — tinctures, salves, and honest advice. Gratmala Koboldrock keeps the shop, moves fast, talks faster, and measures to the drop.

Mercy Vale

# Description

The district's hospital, under a plate showing a candle cupped in an open palm. Clean halls, quiet voices, and healers who do not ask twice before they help. Beds are given by need, not by purse, and the wards run through the night. Kadreahilda Mountainbrow keeps the wards and the beds, and what is said inside the Vale stays inside it.

intro.title: The Saga of the Empire
intro.tagline: A Torrentath campaign for characters of levels 3-12
intro.synopsis: Fifty years into the reign of Empress Arith Tezaibel Kethith, an assassination attempt at her anniversary celebration binds a band of strangers as Champions of the Empire. Their charge: investigate the corruption of Oospufmorn, one of five sacred trees whose living hearts lock a portal to Demonholme. The necromancer Essax - once a young tiefling named Bobby, driven mad by the touch of Kelethtonreth - hunts the tree hearts as anchors for a ritual that will carry the Demon Lord, his legions, and a piece of his frozen realm onto the continent of Arret. The Champions will lose before they learn how to win, chase the war under two cities, over one felled god-tree, and finally into Demonholme itself - where a goddess pours tea, and every choice has a price.
intro.background: THE VILLAIN, TOLD ONCE. One hundred twenty-nine years ago Kelethtonreth stepped through a portal onto the mortal plane and devastated Arret before an alliance drove him back and sealed the way, raising a great wall of earth that splits the land to this day. Among the sealers stood the adventuring band Kaddrin Vurrath - the Banner of the Red Hawk - whose surviving members now rule: young Arith became the Empress; Kili became Thane of Knakknthazn; Lid became Sovereign of Aria. With them stood a gaunt young tiefling, Bobby - Robert when they were testy - a nice enough person, most days. As the seal closed, Kelethtonreth touched each of their minds and promised revenge. It drove Bobby insane. They became ESSAX (true name Amurt Sselkcer), seized the Bronze Storm Empire to the east, and have spent a century preparing to buy their own safety with their patron's freedom. The five sacred trees - Oospufmorn (Aria), Vum (Teg), Chanfirch (Pand), Aedlab (Essa), and the hidden Knobdimmon (Knakknthazn) - are the locks on Kelethtonreth's prison. Their hearts, extracted, become ritual anchors. Three are enough for a lesser working: a plane shift that drags Kelethtonreth and a piece of Demonholme back through.
intro.engine: THE TRACKING ENGINE (read this twice). Throughout the campaign, monsters find the party with impossible precision - Death Dogs on a lonely road, Berowls pacing a river ship, an Unkindness of Sleapless delivered to a deck at dusk. Two mechanisms drive it, and the party should discover them in this order: (1) THRON, a glabrezu field commander, performs teleportation rituals that place hunters ahead of the party - every such site bears the faint whisper of a teleportation circle, the campaign's recurring clue; (2) KOTH'TAVUTH, a glabrezu possessing the Princeps of the Empire, is the intelligence leak - the reason Essax always knows where to send Thron's deliveries. And beneath the possession lies the uglier truth: the Princeps STRUCK THE BARGAIN. Tricked by Essax with the promise of the Empire once the ritual of the trees completes, they gave away the knowledge of the Aria tree - Oospufmorn's existence and hiding place - as payment. The demon in their head is merely the collateral Essax took on the deal. Plant the Princeps' wrongness in Chapter 1 (standing composed while the whole court drops at the shot - DC 25; the deviant smile) and let the players carry the suspicion for the whole campaign. Do not confirm it early; the payoff belongs to the endgame.

hooks.name: The Warden's Child
hooks.text: A PC raised near a sacred tree learns a parent is one of its secret Defenders, is shown the tree, witnesses the dark mark of Essax appear on the Defenders' list, and is sent as envoy to the capital. Best for: rangers, druids, anyone with a homeland.

hooks.name: The Mentor's Favor
hooks.text: A beloved mentor asks the PC to represent their order, mission, or guild as an honored guest at the Empress' celebration. Best for: bards, clerics, folk heroes.

hooks.name: The Palace Insider
hooks.text: A PC serving in the capital - guard, sword master, court functionary - receives intelligence worth carrying to the Princeps personally, earning a seat in the honored-guests section and a front-row view of the campaign's secret villain. Best for: fighters, monks, soldiers.

hooks.name: The Realm's Emissary
hooks.text: A PC is sent by their people - a dwarf carrying a warning from Knakknthazn, a labor hero elected by their town, a guild alchemist with a letter of invitation. Best for: everyone else. The only requirement the campaign truly has: every PC is in the amphitheater when the shot cracks.

intro.pacing: Milestone leveling is assumed; the table above marks the beats. A chapter is one to three sessions depending on your table's speed - a full run of this material has taken thirty-one sessions. Chapters 1-6 are a spine: run them in order. Chapter 7 is a downtime hub - let it breathe as long as the table is having fun. Chapters 8-12 accelerate; once Aedlab falls, the fiction should feel like a countdown.
intro.usingThisBook: Each chapter opens with an overview and RUNNING THIS CHAPTER guidance, then presents keyed scenes (1.1, 1.2...). Scenes that carry a DM SCRIPT open with it: the through-line as numbered beats you can speak or paraphrase, each editable in place so your own table voice persists - with ▶ PUSH callouts marking exactly when to send something to the player screen. All pushable content - boxed read-aloud text and player cards - is gathered at the BOTTOM of each scene under PLAYER PUSHES, out of the eyeline until the script calls for it; tapping a callout fires the push directly. BATTLE blocks give setup, combatants, tactics, an adjusting sidebar, and aftermath; creature names link to full stat blocks in Appendix A - homebrew equivalents are provided for every non-SRD creature so this console needs no books at the table, and each block carries its own substitution advice for a DM who would rather run something familiar. Roll tables live where they are used and can be rolled from the page.

chapters.title: Session Zero - Building the Vignettes
chapters.overview: Before the celebration, the camera. This campaign opens with a chained sequence of character vignettes - short, cinematic introductions that pan across the continent from one PC to the next, each ending with the same destination: the Empress' fiftieth-anniversary celebration in Trionshen. This chapter is a construction kit: the technique, the anatomy of a vignette, a fully worked example, and ready seeds for every hook, so you can build an opening scene for any character your players bring.
chapters.running: Budget five to eight minutes per seat and hold the line - the energy of the sequence comes from momentum. Order matters: open on your most confident player to set the tone, and save a shy player for the middle, never first or last. Between vignettes, narrate the transition yourself ('Our focus lifts, and we fly east over the farm fields...') - the camera language is what makes six separate introductions feel like one opening scene. Everything in this chapter happens before initiative is ever rolled; the payoff is that when the shot cracks in Chapter 1, every player already knows who they are and why they came.

scenes.title: Character Creation
scenes.body: Characters begin at 3rd level (milestone advancement thereafter - see the Introduction's table). Any origin fits: the Empire spans five realms, two great port cities, an underground dwarven nation, and every trade road between. The one requirement is written into the premise: EACH CHARACTER HAS A REASON TO BE AT THE CELEBRATION, as an honored guest or in service. The party does not need to know each other - the campaign binds them in Chapter 1. During session zero, match each PC to one of the four hooks from the Introduction or hand them an opening from the Vignette Menu (scene 0.5) - doubling up is fine for two PCs with a shared background, such as siblings or a mentor's two students). One more standing rule, set here and honored for the whole book: EVERY PLAYER SKETCHES A BACKUP character at the same level. If a character dies or is otherwise removed from the current scenes - and this book can do both - the player comes back in on the backup.

boxes.title: Building Your Character
boxes.text: Build a 3rd-level character of any origin - the Empire of Torrentath spans five realms, two great port cities, an underground dwarven nation, and every trade road between them. One requirement only: your character has a reason to attend the Empress' fiftieth-anniversary celebration in the capital, as an honored guest or in service. You do not need to know the other characters yet. The story will take care of that.

boxes.title: Your Backup Character
boxes.text: Alongside your character, sketch a backup - same rules, same one requirement. This campaign plays for keeps: a character can die, be captured, or step through the wrong portal, and if yours is removed from the current scenes, you come back in on your backup. Keep it a sketch or build it full - but have it ready.

scenes.mechanics: Table conversation to have now, not later: this campaign includes demonic possession of a sympathetic NPC, the on-screen death of beloved places, and one scripted loss the party cannot prevent (Chapter 6). The console's TONE & SAFETY page (Run the Table › Tone & Safety) carries the full content advisory, pushable player briefings, an interactive Lines & Veils checklist, and live table signals - run it as part of this scene.

scenes.title: The Camera-Pan Technique

blocks.text: DM CRAFT (yours alone). The sequence works like a film's cold open. You control the camera; the players control what it sees.

rows.name: 1 · START IN MOTION
rows.note: open each vignette on the character mid-activity, doing the thing they are best at or most known for; never open on someone waiting.

rows.name: 2 · PLACE THE MIRROR
rows.note: the 'describe yourself' prompt lands mid-scene, at the exact moment another character looks at the PC: a mentor pouring tea, a sparring partner squaring up, guards muttering as a traveler passes. The player describes their character while the world is already watching them.

rows.name: 3 · END ON THE INVITATION
rows.note: every vignette closes with the same logistics: honored guest, arrive one day before, free board and food, leave the morning after. The repetition is the glue; by the fourth vignette the players hear the campaign assembling itself.

blocks.text: Push the player card when you begin, so the table knows the shape of what is coming.

boxes.title: How Our Opening Works
boxes.text: We will open on each of you, one at a time, like a film - a short scene of your character in their element, mid-motion, doing the thing they are best at. Somewhere in your scene, someone will look at you, and I will say: describe yourself. That is your moment - tell us what the world sees. Every scene ends the same way: an invitation to the Empress' celebration reaches you, one way or another. How your character feels about that invitation is yours to play. Then the camera moves to the next of you.

scenes.mechanics: Transition lines to steal: 'Our focus changes, way out to the imperial capital.' / 'We pan out once again and shift our focus to...' / 'Our ocular vision moves away from this room, up and over the farm fields...' Small skill beats inside a vignette are welcome (an opposed Stealth to notice a lurker) - keep them consequence-light: failure changes flavor, never outcome.

scenes.title: Anatomy of a Vignette
scenes.body: Five beats, in order. Build every vignette on this spine and improvise the skin. The player card is the same spine from their side of the screen - push it and give the table five quiet minutes to jot answers before you begin the first vignette. Their answers ARE your vignette materials.

boxes.title: Your Vignette - Five Things to Bring
boxes.text: 1. YOUR ELEMENT - where is your character most at home, and what are they doing there when we find them? 2. YOUR PERSON - who might interrupt them there: a mentor, a parent, a superior, an old friend, a stranger with a letter? 3. YOUR FACE - when all eyes turn to you and I ask you to describe yourself, what does the world see? 4. YOUR ANSWER - an invitation to the capital arrives. Excited, honored, suspicious, reluctant - how does your character take it? 5. YOUR LOOSE END - one small unresolved thing from your past. A debt, a name, a keepsake, a question. Say it out loud; the story is listening.

scenes.mechanics: DM SPINE: BEAT 1 - ESTABLISHING SHOT: the PC in their element; one sentence of place, one of activity. BEAT 2 - THE INTERRUPTION: a message, mentor, superior, or stranger breaks the routine; this NPC carries the invitation. BEAT 3 - THE MIRROR: 'describe yourself' - prompted by the interrupting NPC's attention. BEAT 4 - THE ASK: the celebration invitation with its logistics, plus the hook-specific duty (envoy, representative, report, honor). BEAT 5 - THE THREAD: one dangling detail that will matter later - a parent's bracelet, a superior's odd smile, a word overheard in Dwarvish. Plant it and move the camera. The players' five answers map to your five beats one-to-one: their element is your shot, their person is your interruption, their loose end is your thread.

scenes.title: Worked Example - The Warden's Child
scenes.body: The vignette below is the campaign's original, built for a tiefling ranger raised in the Forest of Aedlab. The beat labels show the spine at work; everything else is skin you can reshape for your own player's character.
scenes.boxedText: We begin with me dancing in the southeast of the Forest of Aedlab, in the nation of Essa. [BEAT 1] A hawk circles above the tree line. It lands on a limb in front of me. I know this hawk. Tied to its leg: a message from my mother, requesting an audience in the deep forest center - a day's travel. [BEAT 2] When I arrive, she steps out from behind a touching oak, dressed to fade into the forest - not unlike myself. [Character Description Here] [BEAT 3] 'I am one of the Wardens of the sacred tree Aedlab itself. Today, a special dispensation is granted you.' She touches the green-gem bracelet I have never seen her without, and the air opens into a meadow - and an ancient tree whose trunk forty people could not encircle. On the platform below its boughs she shows me the Defenders' list written in the living bark - and beside the tree called Oospufmorn, a dark mark, rotten and dabbed: a name. ESSAX. 'We must send an envoy to inform our Panarch and the Empress at the celebration. You are our choice.' [BEAT 4 - and the bracelet, the list, and the mark are all BEAT 5 threads the campaign will pull.]
scenes.mechanics: Adaptation notes: the parent can be any trusted elder; the tree reveal requires only that ONE party member sees a sacred tree before Chapter 1 (it makes the Champions' visions in scene 1.3 land twice as hard); the dark mark should be shown, not explained - refuse all questions with 'she does not know.'

scenes.title: The Vignette Menu - Pre-Generated Openings
scenes.body: Nine ready-made openings covering the common character shapes. Each is written to be PUSHED TO THE DISPLAY and read aloud as-is - a player whose life is too busy for homework, or who is new to the process, can take one whole hog and be fully in the campaign in ninety seconds. Players who brought their own answers from the prep card can use these as examples instead. Swap pronouns, places, and named NPCs freely; the DM threads for each opening are collected in the mechanics block below.

boxes.title: The Warden's Child (ranger, druid, child of the wilds)
boxes.text: We find you dancing - alone, unwatched, perfect - in the southeast of a great forest. A hawk circles above the tree line and drops to a limb in front of you; tied to its leg, a message in a hand you know: your mother's. Come to the deep forest center. A day's walk, and she steps out from behind an oak, dressed to fade into the woods, not unlike yourself. She looks at you a long moment. Describe yourself. What she tells you next changes everything: she serves something older than the realm - and they need an envoy at the Empress' celebration. You are her choice.

boxes.title: The Storyteller (bard, entertainer, wandering voice)
boxes.text: A kitchen that fits exactly two people perfectly - you, and your oldest friend and mentor, who is pouring the tea. You have carried their letters and your own tales from village to village for years, trading stories for suppers. As the cup reaches your hands, they look up at you with that particular smile. Describe yourself. 'Now I have a favor to ask. Not for me - for you. They've asked our mission to send someone to the celebration of the Empress' fiftieth year. They want our very best. And I believe that to be you.'

boxes.title: The Sword of the Palace (fighter, monk, soldier of the capital)
boxes.text: The practice yard of the Imperial Palace Guard: ranks ten deep and ten wide performing forms in crisp unison. But we find you in the dueling sands, mid-bout, clearly the better of the two - correcting your partner's guard even as you beat it. The Master of Arms watches. The whole yard, between counts, watches. Describe yourself. Your newest orders arrive before the bout does: you are named to the honor detail for the celebration - and the court has questions only someone of your station can carry.

boxes.title: The Deep Emissary (dwarf, or any child of the under-realm)
boxes.text: The great doors grind open and you walk out under the enormous, terrible, open sky. Behind you the door-guards mutter in the old tongue - 'Too much open air can kill you, me mum says' - and you hear them draw the doors tight against catching their death. You have a report to carry, and only the surface roads will take you there. The road unrolls ahead, unroofed the entire way. Describe yourself - and tell us: how does someone raised beneath a mountain wear all this sky? Your destination: the Empress' celebration, and her ear.

boxes.title: The People's Champion (folk hero, commoner, voice of the streets)
boxes.text: A town hall, mid-argument, and the mayor is losing it graciously: 'We're calling it the Inclusion Act. It isn't everything - but it's what your strike won, and I never dreamed we'd get this far.' The room turns to where you're standing. Describe yourself. The mayor clears his throat. 'The Empress requested our leader attend her celebration as an honored guest. And we all know that is you. There'll be free board and food - and like you taught us: everyone's got to eat.'

boxes.title: The Alchemist's Letter (artisan, alchemist, maker of things)
boxes.text: Your workshop, at the good hour - cauldrons settling, the day's last vial corked and crated. You know every sound this room makes, which is why the letter on your desk keeps pulling your eye: heavy paper, a seal you've only seen on proclamations. You sit, finally, and open it. Describe yourself - the hands breaking that seal, the face the words reflect off of. It is an invitation: your work has been noticed, and the court requests your presence at the celebration of the Empress' fiftieth year.

boxes.title: The Reformed Hand (rogue, urchin, one foot out of the shadows)
boxes.text: A rooftop over the harbor at dusk - your office, once. An old associate finds you there the way old associates do, with a job you've already refused twice. You turn out your empty pockets to end the conversation - and find a letter that was not there this morning, heavy paper, an imperial seal. Someone put it ON you, and you never felt it. Describe yourself - and describe the face you make at being outplayed. The letter names you an honored guest at the Empress' celebration, 'for services rendered the crown, quietly.' You have rendered no such services. Yet.

boxes.title: The Devoted (cleric, paladin, keeper of a flame)
boxes.text: Dawn ritual, your temple, your turn to lead. The words are old friends; the light through the windows lands exactly where it lands every year on this day. As you finish, your superior does not dismiss the gathering - instead they turn to you before everyone. Describe yourself. 'The temple must be represented at the celebration of the Empress' fiftieth year,' they say, 'and the auguries were... insistent that it be you.' They do not tell you what the auguries said. Their hands, you notice, are not quite steady.

boxes.title: The Far-Walker (barbarian, outlander, blade of the border)
boxes.text: Three days you have walked the trade road with your people's tribute on your back and a warning in your mouth that the towns only half-believe: something is wrong in the borderlands. Livestock torn apart. Tracks that begin and end in the middle of open ground. Tonight's fire is low and the road is long, and tomorrow you reach the capital at last. Describe yourself - the shape the firelight throws, the way you sit with your back to nothing. The invitation is stitched inside your coat: your people's chosen, to stand before the Empress as an honored guest.

mechanics.title: DM threads — beat 5 of each opening, and where it pays off

rows.name: WARDEN'S CHILD
rows.note: the parent's key trinket and the Defenders' list; this seat should witness the dark mark (run the full reveal from 0.4)

rows.name: STORYTELLER
rows.note: the mentor's unfinished traveling-days stories; the court requests two hours of their time after the speech

rows.name: SWORD OF THE PALACE
rows.note: PREFERRED DREAMER (Ch. 7.7 -> 9.1): a palace blade is the cleanest carrier for the recurring dream - right after the champions are chosen (the binding, 1.3) the Princeps can arrange the quiet abduction and memory-wipe of one of their own without a ripple, so the dreamer's missing night never needs explaining. Steer a willing player here if you can.

rows.name: DEEP EMISSARY
rows.note: the word Knakknthazn, which no one above ground may speak; the Empress will speak it in Chapter 1. You are the Grandchild of the Thane, you know and are bound to all of the secrets of the realm below. Bound is literal - every citizen of Knakknthazn is baptized in Knobdimmon's waters and magically sealed against revealing the fifth tree; the Thane's own line most of all. The lineage pays off twice: Hurdatin Underfall, Mayor of Kitetown, knows this seat as estranged family on sight (Chapter 2), and the Thane's Tale (10.4) is told by their own grandmother.

rows.name: PEOPLE'S CHAMPION
rows.note: the strike's enemies took names; free board is real, the seating chart is political

rows.name: ALCHEMIST
rows.note: who noticed their work, exactly? No one will say.

rows.name: REFORMED HAND
rows.note: who planted the letter, and how; the answer can become any recruiter you need later (the Moonlight Strategy in Chapter 4 loves this seat)

rows.name: DEVOTED
rows.note: the auguries stuttered on a word the superior will not repeat: 'tree.'

rows.name: FAR-WALKER
rows.note: the impossible tracks are the campaign's tracking engine showing its hand early; this seat's suspicion is your Chapter 2 accelerant

blocks.text: Every opening ends on the same logistics: honored guest, arrive one day before, free board and food, leave the morning after.

THE DREAMER IS PIVOTAL - NOT OPTIONAL. One seat carries the recurring dream that drives Chapters 7-9 (first seen at 7.7, paid off at 9.1, where they wake speaking Abyssal). Make sure SOMEONE at the table can receive it. The Sword of the Palace is the PREFERRED fit - the Princeps tie lets the abduction and memory-wipe happen seamlessly right after the Chapter 1 binding - but any seat the demons touch will serve: the circle-rider (Contingency C3), a demon-marked origin, or simply your most roleplay-hungry player. The choice is always the DM's; just do not leave the chair empty.

scenes.title: The Lore Primer
scenes.body: Read the boxed text to the whole table once all vignettes are done - it is the shared floor of common knowledge. PCs raised in Essa (Forest of Aedlab) additionally know the four trees are REAL, not rumor, from oral histories passed down generation to generation. A PC from Knakknthazn knows of the fifth tree and is magically sealed against revealing it - a delicious burden to hand a player who can keep a secret.
scenes.boxedText: All who live in Aria, Teg, and Pand know of the sacred trees as legend and rumor - four great trees, old as the Empire, hidden where only crowns and their chosen may find them. Fifty years the Empress has reigned, and on the fifteenth of The Melting the whole Empire will gather to celebrate her. Everyone has time to make preparations before traveling - brew your potions, write your letters, sharpen what needs sharpening. The roads to Trionshen are full of your neighbors.
scenes.development: Everyone gets prep time before travel - honor purchases, brewing, and letters now; it pays the fiction forward.

scenes.title: Binding the Party

boxed.title: The Amphitheater - Morning of the 15th
boxed.text:
Morning light comes down through the eastern arches in long slabs, and the amphitheater is already half a city. Three tiers of stone rise around you in a great oval, huge arches open at every level to the north, south, east, and west, and through them the roofs of Trionshen fall away toward the water. Banners of the five realms hang from the rim, snapping in the wind - and above them all, the crowned heart of House Kethith.

Your seats are in the honored-guests section, down on the floor itself, close enough to the dais to count the rings on a steward's fingers. Where you sit within it is up to you - some of you may be peppered about among strangers, some shoulder to shoulder with a familiar face from the road. Choose your seats. Around you the section fills with people invited the same way you were: a farmer in her best coat, a priest fussing with his sleeves, a soldier home from somewhere far. Servers work the rows with trays - bread still warm, cold fruit, small cups of something sweet. Guards hold every aisle mouth, polite and immovable. The wide floor of the second tier stands open and empty above you. Somewhere up there, a band is tuning.

The dais is still bare. The Empire is settling in around you, one seat at a time. You have time. Talk.

scenes.body: Close session zero with all PCs seated in the honored-guests section of the amphitheater, morning of the 15th of The Melting. Give them ten minutes of in-character mingling - seat neighbors introduce themselves, food is passed, banners are named. Do not force bonds; proximity is enough. The shot in Chapter 1, scene 1.2 will do the rest.
scenes.mechanics: Pre-flight checklist: every PC has a hook and took the invitation · at least one PC has seen a sacred tree · the table knows the tone and safety tools · you know which player to spotlight first when the goblins come · the words ESSAX and Knakknthazn have each been spoken exactly once, and explained never.

chapters.chapterDevelopment: Session zero ends at the amphitheater - and with every vignette your players wrote entered into the VIGNETTE MANAGER below, so Chapter 1 can push each one to the player screen as it is read aloud. Chapter 1 opens with scene 1.1 already half-done - skim its Arrivals scene for anything your vignettes did not cover, then go straight to the portals of 1.2.

chapters.title: The Celebration of the Empress

sigil.label: The Sacred Tree
sigil.caption: The sigil of the sacred tree

chapters.overview: The fiftieth anniversary of the Empress' reign draws the whole Empire to Trionshen - and every PC with it. Teleport rings bloom on the amphitheater floor and goblin raiding parties pour out as fodder; mid-battle, over the din, a sniper's shot cracks - and just misses the Empress. In the aftermath the Pendant of Torrentath chooses the party as Champions of the Empire, bound to investigate the corruption of the sacred tree Oospufmorn. In-world dates: 11th-15th of The Melting, Year 50 of the Reign.
chapters.running: Session one carries three jobs: introduce each PC in the vignette THEY wrote with you in session zero, stage a battle that makes them look heroic in front of the crown, and seed the campaign's two long secrets - the Princeps' wrongness and the name ESSAX. Run 1.1 from its DM Script: camera pan, vignette, camera pan, vignette - the pans are yours, the vignettes are theirs (pushed to the player screen while the player, or you, reads aloud). Keep each seat to five-to-eight minutes. In 1.2 the ORDER IS THE STORY: the portals open and the fight starts FIRST; the shot arrives out of the chaos the goblins were sent to create. The battle is deliberately winnable; the ceremony afterward is the real climax. If your table skipped session zero, open cold at the portals and flash back.

scenes.title: Arrivals - the Vignette Sequence

blocks.title: RUNNING THE SEQUENCE
blocks.sub: your table's opening: the vignettes your players wrote with you in session zero, run as one continuous camera move
items: Enter them in Chapter 0's VIGNETTE MANAGER (character name, the vignette text, an optional player-made image); they appear below under PLAYER PUSHES, each with its own push.
Between vignettes, fire a CAMERA CARD - a pan across the land, all grandeur and no names; the specifics wait until the camera lands on a character.
Close a pan with a LANDING LINE, push the next vignette, and let the player read it aloud from the screen - or read it for them if they would rather listen.

blocks.text: If one PC took the Palace Insider hook, run their audience with the Princeps after their vignette.

scenes.boxedText: The amphitheater of Trionshen holds more people than most towns. Banners of the five realms hang from the rim - and above them all, the crowned heart of House Kethith. When the Empress steps to the podium, fifty years of the Empire draw one breath together.

blocks.title: THE AMPHITHEATER
blocks.sub: the amphitheater floor, as it lies
lines: An oval of THREE TIERS, with huge arches set at all three levels opening on the four cardinal directions.
Seating sweeps in a crescent down to the dais; the second tier's floor stands open and unoccupied; beyond the dais, left and right, the ground is open and guarded.
Guard lines hold every aisle mouth; knights flank the upper arches; the honored-guests sections (the party's seats) flank the floor nearest the dais.

rows.name: The Empress
rows.note: her personal guard RODSONN at her shoulder

blocks.title: PRINCEPS AUDIENCE (if played)
lines: The Princeps is tall and sleek, long black hair combed back between purple horns, resplendent in a deep purple ceremonial gown, white trousers, gilded boots.

rows.result: when rumors of trouble in the west are relayed, a faint deviant smile - hidden at once by a sip of wine.

blocks.text: Do not explain a success. Ever.

script.text: Set the shape: 'We open like a film - on each of you, one at a time, mid-motion, doing what you do best. When your scene arrives, your words go up on the screen; read them to us, or I will.'
Fire the first camera pan and let it sit on the screen a breath longer than feels comfortable - the land is the first character.
Close the pan with a landing line, then push the first vignette. The player reads; the table watches the screen. Do not rush the silence after.
Repeat the loop for every seat: pan, land, vignette. Vary the land - forest, mountain, river, lake, plain - and save a shy player for the middle, never first or last.
If a PC took the Palace Insider hook, run their audience with the Princeps now (Mechanics: the DC 20 Insight and the deviant smile). Do not explain a success. Ever.
All vignettes played: push the amphitheater and seat them as honored guests. Ten minutes of in-character mingling; proximity is enough - 1.2 will do the binding.

time.label: Festival days before the ceremony — how many pass?

scenes.title: The Portals, then the Shot

blocks.title: ORDER MATTERS
lines: The portals open and the battle begins FIRST. The goblin assault is theater - fodder deployed ahead of the shot to fill the amphitheater with chaos, so that the true firing point opens unnoticed: a 'magic window' on the wall opposite the Empress.

The shot itself is fired through that rend in space by a kobold sharpshooter with a slender long pipe - the party cannot learn the shooter's identity yet (it arrives in Chapter 3 with Diana's testimony), though sharp eyes may glimpse the window itself (Mechanics, detail 3).

blocks.title: THE THREE TELEPORT RINGS
blocks.sub: the rings - tactical notes
lines: Two on the open second-tier floor at the upper arches.
One on the lower floor between the honored-guests sections - which is to say, at the party's feet.

blocks.title: 1 · WHEN THE SHOT FIRES
lines: DC 25 Wisdom (Insight) for anyone with eyes on the dais: the whole court drops to the deck in one motion, and the Princeps DOES NOT SO MUCH AS FLINCH - still standing, composed, unbothered, mid-battle, as if the crack were part of the program.
Award it; never explain it; it will feed the table's suspicion for eleven chapters.

blocks.title: 2 · THE EMPRESS' CAPE
lines: A warded shield-cloak: as a reaction, once per scene, it can turn a hit against her into a miss - which is why Rodsonn's dive still mattered, and why the court armorer will be asked hard questions about why it was needed at all.

blocks.title: 3 · LOOKING FOR THE SOURCE
blocks.sub: any PC scanning for where the shot came from in the moments after the CRACK rolls Wisdom (Perception) against the wall opposite the Empress

rows.result: a hole - a dark, wrong opening hanging on the wall where no hole should be.
it isn't a hole in the wall at all - through it lies open land, forest, somewhere that is not here.
framed in that distant land, a shadowed figure lying prone, blended into its surroundings - a shape, nothing more.
for a PC who hit DC 17 or better: that terrain is no land within the Empire.

blocks.text: DM note: the firing site sits just beyond the southeastern border line - which is why border patrols, not imperial forces, stumbled onto it; fully consistent with Diana's testimony in Chapter 3.

Award what they earn and move on; the window seals within moments, and no tier reveals who or what fired. The full answer still arrives with Diana - a DC 25 here just means the party recognizes her story on sight.

battle.name: Blood at the Anniversary
battle.setup: Three raiding parties deploy from teleportation circles at tactical points around the amphitheater floor - THE FIGHT STARTS HERE, before any shot is fired. Guards (x48) and Knights (x4) are present but committed to the crowd and the Empress - the PCs are the free blades that matter. Civilians everywhere: reward crowd-protecting play loudly. The shot arrives mid-battle (script beat 3): do not fire it until the party is engaged.

combatants.name: Goblin Rag-Crown
combatants.note: One per raiding party; each wears a one-way teleportation wristband and flees with it at half HP.

combatants.name: Goblin
combatants.note: Eight per party. Bomb-Rigged: for each goblin, roll a d20 - on 1-5 it carries 4 crude bombs; when it dies, each creature within 5 feet makes a DC 12 DEX save or takes 3d6 fire damage.

combatants.name: Guard (allied)
combatants.note: Holding the crowd lines; not under player control.

combatants.name: Knight (allied)
combatants.note: Screening the Empress.

battle.tactics: Bosses hang back and shove goblins forward; goblins swarm the nearest armed resistance (the PCs) and ignore civilians unless unopposed - they are here to make noise, not to win. When a party is broken, its boss triggers the wristband and vanishes.
battle.adjusting: Weaker party: 6 goblins per band, bombs on 1-3 only. Stronger party: bosses fight to two-thirds HP before fleeing, and one band spawns adjacent to the Empress' box forcing a rescue.
battle.aftermath: Investigation of the opposite wall finds the 'magic window' - the true firing point, now sealed - but no shooter, no weapon; a PC who spotted it mid-battle (Mechanics, detail 3) can lead the guards straight to the spot. If nobody caught the unflinching Princeps at the moment the shot fired (scene 1.2, Mechanics detail 1, DC 25 Wisdom (Insight)), grant one more chance here at the same DC as the court reassembles: the Princeps is not bothered by ANY of this. Award it; never explain it.

scenes.treasure: A recovered teleportation wristband (inert, one-use, already spent) - the campaign's first physical clue that someone is moving monsters by circle.
scenes.development: Once the field is secure, the Empress insists the defenders join her in the sitting room behind the dais. Proceed to 1.3.

boxed.title: The Portals
boxed.text: The Empress raises a hand for silence - and the floor answers instead: three rings of violet light bloom across the amphitheater, and goblins pour out of them, shrieking, blades already out. Guard lines collapse inward toward the dais; ten thousand voices become one scream. Whatever this celebration was, it is now a battlefield.

boxed.title: The Shot
boxed.text: Over the din of the fight - the world CRACKS. The Empress staggers; Rodsonn, her personal guard, is already there, taking the shot through the shoulder. In one motion the entire court drops to the deck - behind the dais, among the seats, everywhere. The goblins do not so much as look up. They were never here for her.

script.text: The Empress steps to the podium and raises a hand for silence. Hold the beat - then push the portals and ROLL INITIATIVE.
Run the opening rounds hot: goblins swarm the nearest armed resistance (the party), bosses shove from behind, guards hold the crowd lines. Reward crowd-protecting play loudly.
Round two or three, mid-swing, push the shot. The court drops; Rodsonn takes it through the shoulder; the Empress lives.
THE INSTANT the shot fires: anyone watching the dais may roll DC 25 Wisdom (Insight) - the Princeps does not so much as flinch. Award it; never explain it (Mechanics, detail 1).

Any PC scanning for the shot's source: Wisdom (Perception) vs. the far wall - DC 12 the hole, DC 17 the land beyond it, DC 25 a shadowed prone figure hiding in its environment. On DC 17+, an optional DC 15 Intelligence (Nature): that land is nowhere within the Empire. The window seals moments later. Say what they see; explain nothing (Mechanics, detail 3).

Bosses trigger their wristbands and vanish at half HP; broken bands rout. When the field is secure, run the aftermath: the magic window on the far wall - no shooter, no weapon - and the second-chance Insight if nobody caught the Princeps.
The Empress insists the defenders join her in the sitting room behind the dais. Proceed to 1.3.

scenes.title: The Choosing
scenes.body: This scene is the campaign's hinge. Everything before it was a party; everything after it is the Champions of the Empire, and the table should feel the temperature change. Three rules. SLOW DOWN - cut your pace in half; the court is silent, so let the table be silent too. BREAK BEFORE IT - do not stack this onto the end of the battle; call a stretch, then reconvene INTO the sitting room so the scene starts on its own breath. PLAY THE FACES, NOT THE EXPOSITION - the choosing has happened only a handful of times in the Empire's history, and every person in this room knows it. The party learns what this means by watching the most powerful people in the world go still.

boxed.title: The Sitting Room
boxed.text: The sitting room behind the dais is small enough to feel like a secret. Thick carpets, a single hearth, chairs made for one family rather than a court - and the most powerful people in the Empire standing in it, still catching their breath. Beyond the door you can hear the guard moving ten thousand people through four arches. In here, it is quiet enough to hear the Empress set down a cup of wine untouched. She looks at each of you in turn - not the way a ruler inspects. The way a person decides.

boxed.title: The Choosing
boxed.text:
The Empress rises, and the room rises with her - a Steward, a Panarch, a Sovereign, a Lord - and at a single look from her, all of them step back to the walls, leaving you alone at the center. She takes her pendant in both hands. It was a plain thing at her throat until this moment. Now it wakes. You feel a wave of arcane wash over you like the pressure before a storm, and each of you glows, faintly - and around you, the rulers of five realms bow their heads.

'The Pendant of Torrentath has chosen! You are chosen by Torrentath itself as Champions of the Empire - should you choose to accept it. If you accept: kneel before me. All others must leave this chamber, save the high court of the Empire.'

boxed.title: The Visions
boxed.text: The moment your knee touches the floor, the room goes away. Power soaks into your bones - not granted, RECOGNIZED, as if it had been waiting in you and the pendant only spoke its name. And with it comes an awareness of four distant, living things. You see each sacred tree in turn - Vum. Chanfirch. Aedlab. Then Oospufmorn - and your sight will not leave it. On its trunk: a map of five trees, names written beside each. And below Oospufmorn's list, where no name should be, a smudge - dark, rotten, dabbed like a thumbprint in something that was never ink: ESSAX. Then the room returns, and the Empress is watching you come back.

scenes.mechanics: THE VISIONS - run them once, shared, after everyone who will kneel has knelt; then invite each player to name one detail their character cannot stop seeing. Permanent boon: any Champion can close their eyes, turn in place, and point unerringly toward each surface tree. Award it; never explain it. IF A PC HESITATES: the glow does not fade and the Empress does not press - 'The pendant has never been wrong. I will not argue with it - and neither should you. But the choice is yours.' A firm refusal walks out under the eyes of the high court; the door, at your discretion, stays unlocked. DREAMER SEED (preferred path, DM only): if the recurring dream (7.7 -> 9.1) is going to the Sword of the Palace, this is where the Princeps plants it - right after the binding, one of their own is quietly taken, mind-read, and returned with the night wiped clean. Nothing shows now; the dream begins to surface in the Chapter 7 downtime. Any other dreamer instead takes the demon's touch later (Oospufmorn, or the circle-ride, C3).
scenes.development: Marching orders, verbatim: 'The Empire needs you. Go to Oospufmorn and find out what you can. Whatever resources we have are freely given. Make haste - the Empire is counting on you.' Close on the door: they entered this room as guests and leave it as the second sentence of a notice that will hang in every town in the Empire (Appendix D: Proclamation of the Empress, public text - seed it now; it reaches their hands on the road. The sealed official text exists in parallel and reaches only officials - the party sees it first in Kitetown, from Underfall). The route is not chosen so much as felt: the boon points every Champion toward Oospufmorn, and the pull draws them south-east by land to Kitetown, then by river (Chapter 2). This is a rail, and the book lays it without apology - the tree is calling, and Champions answer. If the players push for another path, don't argue; let the pull tug wrong-feeling with every mile off-line until they correct course. Reward cleverness along the road, not off it. Milestone: the party reaches 4th level.

script.text: Settle the room. One breath of aftermath - let the PCs speak first if they want to; the Empress thanks no one yet. She is deciding.

A court wizard bursts in: 'Your Excellency, Oospufmorn has been compromised!' - and casts a scrying that shows the tree and its Defenders list. DC 25 Wisdom (Insight): the name ESSAX is obscured behind the wizard's body.
The Empress takes her pendant. Push the choosing; every PC glows; the rulers of five realms bow their heads. Read her lines exactly - do not paraphrase them.
Take the kneeling one PC at a time, by character name. If a player hesitates, use the valve in Mechanics - the glow waits, and so does she.

The chamber is cleared save the high court. The Empress works the room - give each PC one exchange in character. If a dwarf is present she speaks the forbidden word Knakknthazn aloud and the court gasps ('I am allowed to speak that word only in the most dire of circumstances, and only when the Empire has chosen Champions').
The visions - run them once, shared (Mechanics). Award the boon; never explain it.
The marching orders (Development), verbatim. Milestone: 4th level - and seed the public Proclamation (Appendix D) as the last image of the session.

chapters.chapterDevelopment: If the party investigates the Princeps now, stonewall gently: they are the Princeps. If they head somewhere other than Kitetown, the River Serpent's cast can meet them at any cove on the Trenlem - move Pendant Cove, keep the ship.

chapters.title: The Road to the River
chapters.overview: Overland from Trionshen to Kitetown and on to Yririe - a tenday of travel during which something hulking paces the camps, always to the east, always patient. In Kitetown the party finds two routes to Aria: a slow honest one and a fast illegal one. On the Yririe road they turn ambusher into ambushed against four Death Dogs, and at Pendant Cove the Dark Star thieves' guild springs a trap of its own. In-world: about a dozen days on the road.
chapters.running: This chapter teaches the campaign's travel rhythm: roll the Daily Travel table each morning and the Night Watch table each night, and let the stalker appear at least twice before the Death Dog fight - distant, circling, always to the east, avoiding the west. The ROAD LEDGER above the Daily Travel table keeps the tally: each leg is measured in leagues (three miles - an hour's honest walking), a fair day's march is 8 leagues, and every New Day roll deducts the day's progress automatically - rainstorms cost half a march, entry 19 costs time, entry 20 buys it back. The Kitetown split (the Lithgow vs. the smugglers' drop) is a values choice, not a puzzle; both routes work and both are fully supported - the Serpent is faster and bloodier, and the Lithgow's whole voyage lives in CONTINGENCY C1: the honest road, the salon, and the first night out of port. The Bowl ambush lands hardest if the party has started feeling safe - and thanks to Ru, it is coming whether they feel safe or not.

legs.name: Trionshen → Kitetown
legs.arrive: The road is spent — Kitetown raises her rooftops before you, smoke from a dozen forges on the wind.

legs.name: Kitetown → Yririe
legs.arrive: The road is spent — Yririe sits low against the water, and somewhere past it lies a hidden cove.

tables.name: Daily Travel Events
tables.note: Roll once each travel day. Each entry carries the day's march for the Road Ledger: a fair day makes 8 leagues, a rainstorm halves it, entry 19 costs time, entry 20 buys it back.

entries.text: Rainstorm - travel pace cut by half today.
Sunny day.
Cloudy day.
Random encounter: Warg Riders - 3 orcs mounted on worgs (Appendix A: Orc, Worg).
Light mist - and out of it, a traveling band of Tinkers: repairs, gossip, and one wildly inaccurate map for sale.
Sunny day.
Cloudy day.
Light snow - Stealth checks are at disadvantage today.
Cloudy day.
Random encounter - roll a d6 or choose:
subs: 1. A large bullfrog aggressively squats in the middle of the road, biting anyone who gets close. If attacked, it sprouts a pair of raven-like wings and flies away.

subs.text: 2. The lead traveler makes a DC 12 Perception check or DEX save; failing, they trip over a small, heavy glass object covered in DO NOT OPEN in many languages. Inside: an angry genie who grants one wish in word-twisting fashion. Whenever a carrier falls or takes heavy bludgeoning damage, roll a d20 - on a 1, it smashes.
subs.label: The Bottle (App. D)

subs: 3. A dark-skinned foreign merchant shows his wares: a particularly good warm beverage (coffee). He will demonstrate the brewing and sell beans. A cup removes one level of exhaustion.

4. A bognil traveling potion-seller, day 1 of a 10-day circuit (in case the party decides to remove his wares from him): Vial of Acid x4; Antitoxin 50 gp x2; Healer's Kit 5 gp x4; Potion of Healing 50 gp x4; Greater Potion of Healing 100 gp x2; Superior Potion of Healing 500 gp x1.

5. A baby lies in the middle of the road; whoever approaches sees the face and stature of a child from their own past. On approach it becomes an imp, sprouts wings, and flies away screaming (Appendix A: Imp).
6. A party of mounted soldiers rushes past - they seem to be in a great hurry.

entries.text: Rainstorm - travel pace cut by half today.
Sunny day.
Cloudy day.
Light mist - and inside it, a random encounter: Orc Warband - 6 orcs on foot (Appendix A: Orc).
Light snow - Stealth checks are at disadvantage today.
Sunny day.
Rainstorm - travel pace cut by half today.
Quiet road - nothing stirs but the wind in the grass. A full day's march.
Trouble on the road - a washed-out ford, a thrown shoe, a wrecked cart blocking the narrows. No blood, but only a half march today. The road takes its toll.
Smooth going - firm road, kind wind, good company. The best march of the journey: 10 leagues before dusk.

tables.name: Night Watch
tables.note: Roll once each night on the road.

entries.text: No issue.
A band of thieves probes the camp - 4 bandits led by a bandit captain (Appendix A).
No issue.
A blink dog watches the camp from beyond the firelight - curious, benign, and gone if approached rudely.

scenes.title: The Stalker in the Hills
scenes.boxedText: First camp, in the rolling hills below Draybalt Mountain. On the last watch, something hulking circles half the perimeter at the edge of sight - patient, unhurried, keeping always to the east and never once crossing to the west.
scenes.body: The stalker is a Death Dog, teleport-delivered ahead of the party by Thron's rituals (see Introduction: The Tracking Engine). It observes and withdraws. Repeat the sighting on a later night between Kitetown and Yririe. Investigation of any vantage it used: nothing but pad-prints that begin and end impossibly.

script.text: First camp in the rolling hills below Draybalt. Run the Night Watch as normal - and on the last watch, push the stalker.
It observes and withdraws - patient, always to the east, never once crossing to the west. Answer no questions.
Any vantage investigated: nothing but pad-prints that begin and end impossibly.
Repeat the sighting on a later night between Kitetown and Yririe - the party should see it at least twice before the Death Dog fight (2.5).

scenes.title: The Farms South of Kitetown
scenes.boxedText: Endless golden fields of wheat, broken by the occasional patch of tabac, root vegetables, and bush beans. A half hour's walk brings you to a cluster of farms: midwives talking over fences as they hang laundry fresh from a stream not far off, farmers and children out in the fields weeding with hoes in hand. Four thatch-roofed houses stand in a row, large barns not too distant, livestock pens - cattle and sheep - and curing shacks beyond.

lines: The road into Kitetown runs through its breadbasket, and the breadbasket has names. If any PC clanks, towers, or otherwise announces themselves at fifty paces, open on the original prompt, adapted: '[Name], what do you do, clanking up to this group of fields and homes?'
The farm folk trade river knowledge for cheese and receive the gospel of potatoes with suspicious enthusiasm - and they are the party's first honest read on the road ahead.

blocks.title: THE WHISPERED POTATO PALADIN
lines: Some weeks back, another armored figure came clanking up this same lane - plate dented and honest, a sack of seed potatoes over one shoulder - asked no bed but a barn, paid in labor and seed stock, and preached the glories of potatoes with a sincerity no one could withstand.
The farm folk call him the Whispered Potato Paladin, and he is why an armored stranger at fifty paces gets a wave here instead of a barred door.
His seed row stands in the Sewell field, tended like a shrine (Side Quests: In the Wake of the Whispered Paladin).

blocks.title: SIDE
blocks.sub: river people - Hors IS the river knowledge

rows.name: Hors
rows.note: hauled barges on the Torrentath for a decade; talks freight and current like other men talk weather

rows.name: Pulri
rows.note: first up the lane to meet any stranger, fearless because the last clanking stranger was wonderful

blocks.title: JOFILL
blocks.sub: Wiphar is the honest read on the road

rows.name: Wiphar
rows.note: has watched this road his whole long life: which stretches run quiet, where the hills turn lonely past Kitetown, what has changed lately that he doesn't like

rows.name: Maaris
rows.note: the daughters run the dairy; theirs is the cheese worth trading for

rows.name: Batkin
rows.note: tends the Paladin's seed row like a shrine

rows.name: Isot
rows.note: teases him for it

rows.name: Matilda
rows.note: wants every scrap of news from the capital

blocks.title: FERNHARE
blocks.sub: nothing moves on this road the Fernhares don't hear about

rows.name: Xina
rows.note: runs the curing shacks; feeds anyone who stands still

rows.name: Zefda
rows.note: appraises strangers over her spectacles and is never wrong

blocks.text: Kindness spent here is a savings account: these are the faces the endgame will put on the word EMPIRE.
