script.text: A half hour's walk from the road, the breadbasket opens up - push the farms.
If any PC clanks, towers, or announces themselves at fifty paces, open on the original prompt: '[Name], what do you do, clanking up to this group of fields and homes?'
The four families (Mechanics) trade river knowledge for cheese and receive the gospel of potatoes with suspicious enthusiasm - the party's first honest read on the road ahead.
The seed row in the Sewell field is proof of passage - the Whispered Potato Paladin came this way, weeks gone.

sq.label: In the Wake of the Whispered Paladin

script.text: Kindness spent here is a savings account: these are the faces the endgame will put on the word EMPIRE.

scenes.title: Kitetown and the Mayor's Manor
scenes.boxedText: Kitetown wears its trade on its rooftops - smoke from a dozen forges, the clang of dwarven-made steel being argued over in three languages, and beyond the eastern foothills, the road that ends at Drrosh, the only door to the realm of the dwarves. The Mayor's manor is stone-built with a red tiled roof like much of the town: two stories, large oak iron-banded double doors set dead center, shuttered windows flanking them and lining the floor above.

blocks.title: THE RECEPTION HALL
lines: A clerk's desk opposite the doors and six more desks behind it, clerks busying themselves with paperwork. The half-elf woman at the front desk rises: 'Welcome to the manor of Hurdatin Underfall, Mayor of Kitetown. I'm Lislanis - how may I assist you?'

Given a good reason (or the family connection), Lislanis opens the appointment book: three slots today - half an hour, two hours, or four hours out - with an offer to wait in the second-floor receiving room, where food and refreshments are laid on.

rows.result: clocks it instantly: UNDERFALL is a Dwarven name - a friend of the family, albeit an estranged one, as this dwarf chose to represent his kin above ground. The PC had no idea he'd been elected Mayor.

blocks.title: THE STUDY
lines: A small room they all fit in comfortably; a desk opposite the door; a single chair against the left wall beneath a crossed war hammer and battle axe; a small refreshment table to the right - pitcher of wine, one unused goblet, bread and cheese, the same offerings as the receiving room; bookshelves flanking a shuttered window, heavy black curtain down; the desk piled with paperwork and lit by a single candle.

The man behind it is obviously a dwarf - desk and chair scaled to fit him, nothing else in the room is, save the weapons on the rack. The SEVEN CONJOINED RINGS of the office of the Mayor hang about his chest on a chain, all silver by the look of them.

blocks.title: PLAY THE REUNION
lines: 'Ah yes, my next appointment...' - he looks up, sees the dwarf, eyes go wide: 'Do my eyes deceive? [Name]? How fair thee, and what brings you to the surface?'

Then, sobering: 'Aye, dark days ahead it seems. Have you seen the proclamation from the Empress? It has been posted by criers all across the Empire, so I am told.' (Hand over Appendix D: the PUBLIC Proclamation - push it.)

Then he crosses to a locked drawer: 'And this one came under seal. It is not for the post boards.' He sets the official copy beside the public one - a mayor is an official, and Champions are named in it. He does not hesitate. (Hand over the OFFICIAL Proclamation - push it. He has decided they have earned it.)
And finally, with a wry look: 'Well, all that said - what can I do for... you, [Name], and the other Champions of the Empire?'

blocks.title: THE HONEST ROUTE
blocks.sub: at a word, he sends for passage

rows.name: Vessel
rows.note: the LITHGOW, a passenger vessel out of the Brimwater Docks

rows.name: Sailing
rows.note: next sailing at dawn

rows.name: Passage
rows.note: a comfortable tenday out, at the known rate of 4 gold per person

rows.name: The catch
rows.note: safe, scheduled, and slow: three days longer than the river road the party doesn't know about yet

blocks.text: If they take the Lithgow - they may; the option was honestly given. Run CONTINGENCY C1: THE LITHGOW - the honest road, the salon, and the first night out of port. They skip the fight, miss the information, and pay three days for it without ever knowing the price.

scenes.development: Two routes now exist: the Lithgow (honest, slow, scheduled) and whatever a streetwise PC can dig out of the west side of town. Scene 2.4. If they book the Lithgow instead, jump to Contingency C1.

script.text: Arrival at the forge-smoke skyline - push Kitetown and the manor.
The reception hall: Lislanis rises to greet them. A dwarf PC with a DC 10 Perception clocks it instantly - UNDERFALL is a Dwarven name, the estranged friend of the family.
The study, and the reunion - play it: 'Do my eyes deceive? [Name]?' Then the public proclamation - push it as he hands it over.
Then the locked drawer: the sealed official copy, not for the post boards. He gives it to them anyway - they are named in it. Push it.
The honest route: the Lithgow out of Brimwater Docks at dawn, 4 gold a head, a comfortable tenday - three days slower than the river road they do not know about yet.

Two routes now exist. The other one lives on the west side of town - 2.4 - and the connected PC has known about that option since they walked the gate: let them announce the plan during the Mayor scene, as the record's rogue did.

time.label: Town business in Kitetown — how long?

scenes.title: The Drop Site
scenes.boxedText: The west side of Kitetown is all industry: the robust smells of smelters and tanneries, more warehouses than homes, and the particular quiet of streets where everyone is paid not to look up.

blocks.title: WHERE THE NETWORK CAME FROM
blocks.sub: seed it before you spend it
lines: If a PC took the REFORMED HAND opening (0.5), pay that thread here: they simply NOTICE the signs of a drop network working this side of town - chalk marks on brick, a knotted cord under a warehouse eave - and the markers that point to the drop point for travel information. No roll; this is their world to read. The thread's second coin comes in Chapter 4.
Criminal, urchin, or similar background: the same signs are there to find - DC 15 Investigation to spot the markers and read which drop handles travel information.

No such PC at the table: a day working the west-side taverns (DC 15 Investigation or Persuasion) surfaces a Moonlight Strategy footpad willing to broker an introduction - or let the beggar child from the STROLLING result, caught mid-lift, trade a name for their freedom.

blocks.text: A drop point is the underworld's answering machine: a loose brick, a hollow eave, a coin left with the message and a reply within hours. The party never needs to meet the guild to use it - which is exactly why Ru can read the mail.

lines: A streetwise PC working the drop-point network learns of the RIVER SERPENT - the fastest smuggler on the waters of Torrentath - lying at a hidden cove near Yririe, and leaves a message arranging passage.
Ask the question the original DM asked: 'Are you skulking, or strolling about?'

rows.result: a beggar child materializes asking for a copper - opposed Sleight of Hand (+11) against passive Perception, advantage if the mark is distracted; on a failure the money pouch is gone before the copper lands.
DC 20 Stealth to reach the drop point unseen by rival eyes.

blocks.title: THE GUILDS OF KITETOWN
blocks.sub: for texture

rows.name: MOONLIGHT STRATEGY
rows.note: the party's contact network - the same guild whose Twins chapter they'll meet in Chapter 4

rows.name: DARK STAR
rows.note: their sworn rivals

rows.name: EARTHSHROUD · RUNNING SMITHS
rows.note: two smaller outfits

scenes.mechanics: WHAT THE PARTY CANNOT SEE (DM only): the contact was not stealthy enough. RU, a watcher of the Dark Star, was posted on a rooftop across from the drop point - she read the party's message, resealed it, and put it back. The reply the party receives is genuine; the ROUTE is compromised. An ambush is being set on the road to Yririe. One thin chance to catch it: DC 25 Perception handling the return note - the wax seal has been tampered with.
scenes.development: The party leaves Kitetown with passage arranged and a tail they have not met. Scene 2.5, on the road.

script.text: Push the west side as they cross into industry and the particular quiet of paid-not-to-look-up streets.

If nobody at your table brought a guild contact, seed one now - the Reformed Hand's letter-planter, a criminal background feature, or a caught pickpocket trading a name for their freedom (WHERE THE NETWORK CAME FROM, above).
A streetwise PC working the drop network learns of the RIVER SERPENT at a hidden cove near Yririe, and leaves a message arranging passage.
Ask it the way the record did: 'Are you skulking, or strolling about?' Strolling - the beggar child and the opposed Sleight of Hand (+11). Skulking - DC 20 Stealth to the drop point unseen.
DM only: Ru of the Dark Star read the message, resealed it, and put it back. The reply is genuine; the ROUTE is compromised. One thin chance: DC 25 Perception on the return note's tampered wax seal.
They leave Kitetown with passage arranged and a tail they have not met.

scenes.title: The Ambush Inverted
scenes.body: Breaking camp for Yririe: three days' travel ahead (including today) - which puts the party in town a day before the River Serpent is set to sail. The schedule is real pressure; let them feel the clock. By the third day the party has every reason to trap their stalker - the large dog-like creature patrolling the east side of their camps. Let them plan it fully - then spring the truth: not one beast but four.

battle.name: Death Dogs on the Yririe Road
battle.setup: The party's ambush site, their terms - honor every bit of preparation with advantage, surprise, or position. Then four two-headed hounds answer the bait instead of one.

combatants.name: Death Dog
combatants.note: Unquenchable once engaged: they never flee, never parley.

battle.tactics: Pairs. One pair pins the bait; the other circles wide for casters. Two heads mean no flanking advantage from mundane distraction and advantage against being blinded or frightened - let the players discover both the hard way.
battle.adjusting: Weaker party: 3 dogs, and their disease save DC drops to 10. Stronger party: 5 dogs, and one is a variant with 52 HP and a howl (recharge 6): each enemy within 30 ft, DC 12 WIS or frightened 1 round.
battle.aftermath: Nothing on the bodies explains the pursuit. A careful search of where they waited (DC 13 Investigation): the faint whisper of a teleportation circle - the first confirmed instance of the campaign's recurring clue. The disease: DC 12 CON on a bite or poisoned until cured; every 24 hours, repeat or lose 5 (1d10) hit point maximum.

scenes.development: Yririe by dusk. The party should arrive victorious and newly paranoid - the correct emotional state for 2.6.

script.text: Break camp: three days to Yririe, one day of slack before the Serpent sails. The schedule is real pressure - let them feel the clock.
By the third day they have every reason to trap their stalker. Let them plan it fully - honor every bit of preparation with advantage, surprise, or position.
Then spring the truth: not one beast but four. Roll initiative (battle block - pairs, one pinning the bait, one circling for casters).

Aftermath: nothing on the bodies explains the pursuit. DC 13 Investigation where they waited - the faint whisper of a teleportation circle, the campaign's first confirmed. Track the bite disease saves.
Yririe by dusk - victorious and newly paranoid. The correct emotional state.

blocks.title: NIGHT BY NIGHT
lines: First night out: last watch catches it - a low shape at the eastern edge of the firelight that is simply gone when a torch is raised. Morning shows prints: canine, but too large, too heavy, pressed deep.

Second night: closer, and no longer troubling to hide - twin points of eyeshine hanging in the dark, unblinking, pacing the east side in time with the watch rotation. By morning the prints circle the entire camp.
Third day: it shows itself in daylight - a distant shape keeping pace along the treeline, stopping when they stop. It is not scouting anymore. It is waiting.

blocks.title: TURNING THE SCREW
lines: Every beat lands the same message: it is patient, it is getting bolder, and there is exactly one night of road left. If the party doesn't choose the ground, it will.
Feed any plan they hatch - tracks to backtrail, terrain to exploit, bait to stake out. The scene wants them to act; make acting feel like winning.

blocks.text: If they never act: the pack attacks the third night on its own terms - no surprise round for the party, dogs opening from two sides. Their ambush inverted twice over.

scenes.title: Yririe
scenes.boxedText: Unlike Kitetown and Brimwater with their enclosed walls and military presence, Yririe sprawls north of the river Trenlem. With the swamps to the west there is a heavy air of humidity, the scent of earth and water on the light breeze. Coming in from the north you can see the entirety of the city at once, all the way down to the bustling docks - Yririe is set on the slope of the river valley - and beyond it the east-west trade route runs along the Trenlem as far as the eye can see.
scenes.body: The town in brief: Mayor Devan Runewhirl (human) is welcoming but knows nothing useful; warehouses and the market crowd the docks; the town hall sits centered behind the dock district with a small barrack beside it; homes sprawl across the rest of the slope. TAVERNS: the Clever Dove (mid-town - Kieran Qtile, elf), the Excited Bow (riverside - Ham, half-orc), the Foamy Child (riverside - Fun, half-orc). INNS: the Golden Ridge (mid-town - Eldar Eljeon, elf), the Aqua Marine Oyster (riverside - Pyria Yllaris, elf), and the Quiet Star on the north edge, kept by Serell 'the Kicker' - a retired Knight of the Empire who notices the party's bearing the way old soldiers do, and asks nothing.
scenes.mechanics: FINDING PENDANT COVE: asking around town (the dock urchin, a tag-team of charm and streetcraft at DC 13, or a round bought at the Excited Bow) locates it - ONE MILE UPRIVER, a hidden cove shunned by reputable river captains for its shallow waters, reached by a 'game trail' through thick brush and trees a short walk off the trade route. Scouting the trail confirms the route. Supplies, an inn, a rest - let them buy the night's peace, because Ru's ambush is already in position on that trail.
scenes.development: The Dark Star knows they are coming. Scene 2.7.

script.text: Coming in from the north the whole city shows at once - push Yririe.
Mayor Runewhirl is welcoming and knows nothing useful; let the taverns and inns carry the evening (the Quiet Star's keeper notices their bearing the way old soldiers do, and asks nothing).
Finding Pendant Cove: the dock urchin, a DC 13 charm-and-streetcraft tag team, or a round bought at the Excited Bow - one mile upriver, a game trail off the trade route.
Sell them the night's peace: supplies, an inn, a rest. Ru's ambush is already in position on that trail.

time.label: The stop in Yririe — how long?

scenes.title: The Bowl
scenes.boxedText: The game trail widens into a bowl of earth filled with fallen leaves and undergrowth; the path splits and continues along both sides of the rim. As you take either way toward the lip, a figure emerges from the game trail on the far side of the bowl: a human in a blue coat, an orange bandana wrapped at his temples.
scenes.body: DC 15 Wisdom (Insight) - or any PC with underworld experience - reads the solid black SEVEN-POINTED STAR tattooed on the left side of his neck: allegiance to the DARK STAR thieves' guild, sworn enemies of the Moonlight Strategy. He doesn't wait for the recognition to finish: 'MOONLIGHT STRATEGY SYMPATHIZER SCUM! Our agents found your message and resealed it - and you fell right into our trap!' Roll initiative.

blocks.title: THE LEVER
blocks.sub: pride is his weakness - the duel is the opening
lines: As an ACTION, any PC the Captain can hear may goad him: insult his skill or courage, feign weakness, or offer a false challenge.

ON A SUCCESS: on his next turn he abandons cover and moves straight at the provoking PC by the shortest route - provoking opportunity attacks if the path forces it - and attacks only that PC that turn. Out of the trees, away from his First-Mate, alone in the open bowl.
ONCE PER FIGHT: after any success, or on a failure by 5 or more, he wises up - 'Cheap words from a corpse.' - and cannot be baited again.

rows.result: insult his skill or courage - he comes for you.
feign weakness or offer a false challenge - he takes the opening.
reads him plainly: he cares more about looking dominant than winning.

blocks.text: TELEGRAPH IT: he announces the duel, postures, and visibly bristles when struck - straightens the coat, spits 'lucky.' Players watching that behavior should smell the lever without a roll.

battle.name: The Dark Star Trap
battle.setup: The bowl's interior is open ground ringed by trees, the outer slopes difficult terrain in every direction. Cutthroats hold positions around the bowl's inside and rim in cover (opposed Stealth vs. passive Perception for surprise); the Captain enters from the far trail behind a tree, his First-Mate a wave behind him.

combatants.name: Dark Star Cutthroat
combatants.note: First wave, thrown daggers then blades, fighting from the rim's cover.

combatants.name: Dark Star Agent (First-Mate)
combatants.note: Second wave.

combatants.name: Dark Star Captain
combatants.note: Blue coat, orange bandana, the seven-pointed star at his neck; carries the identification rings inside his belt.

combatants.name: Doman Bail (Rescue Valve)
combatants.note: ALLY - enters from the cove side ONLY if the Rescue Valve fires; zero him at muster otherwise. Ket (Veteran) and three crew (Bandits) arrive with him.

battle.tactics: Cutthroats focus lightly-armored targets and retreat toward their officers when halved. The Captain duels the strongest-looking PC by preference - pride is his weakness; a successful bait pulls him out of position (full ruling: BAITING THE CAPTAIN, Mechanics above).
battle.adjusting: Weaker party: 4 cutthroats. Stronger party: 8 cutthroats and the Agent gains a second use of Uncanny Dodge per round (one per attacker). THE RESCUE VALVE: if the party is losing, DOMAN BAIL (Appendix A - his own block) and four of the Serpent's crew (Ket as a Veteran, the rest Bandits) crash in from the cove-side trail, crossbows first - he is allied with the Moonlight Strategy and hates the Dark Star. His opener, in full dialect: 'DARK STAR DOGS! Off my beach approach or feed the river!' Cutthroats still standing break for the trees; the Captain fights to the last. Doman spares the party any commentary on their performance - he counts their number instead, exactly as he will again on the sand, then turns and walks. Do NOT run introductions here; the half-spoken words land in 3.1. It costs the party nothing but pride, and buys the Serpent's crew instant standing.
battle.aftermath: Inside the Captain's belt: DARK STAR IDENTIFICATION RINGS (Appendix C) - proof of guild rank, and the key that opens the Moonlight Strategy thread in Chapter 4. Keep them visible in play; remind the party they have them when they reach the Twins.

scenes.treasure: Dark Star identification rings; 47 gp in mixed coin; a fine scimitar; the Captain's route notes naming no employer.
scenes.development: Down the game trail lies Pendant Cove and the River Serpent - Chapter 3. If Doman intervened, his first words on the sand are already half-spoken. If the party buried the bodies in the bowl's center, note it: tidy habits earn quiet reputations.

script.text: On the game trail, the path widens - push the Bowl.
DC 15 Wisdom (Insight) - or any underworld-experienced PC - reads the solid black seven-pointed star at his neck: DARK STAR, sworn enemies of the Moonlight Strategy.
He does not wait for the recognition to finish: 'MOONLIGHT STRATEGY SYMPATHIZER SCUM! Our agents found your message and resealed it - and you fell right into our trap!' Roll initiative.

Run the trap as sketched: cutthroats in cover around the rim (opposed Stealth for surprise); the Captain duels the strongest-looking PC and postures with every hit - telegraph the pride. BAIT (action, once per fight): DC 14 CHA (Intimidation or Deception) pulls him out of cover and away from his First-Mate, fixated on the taunter for one turn; a failure by 5+ locks it off. Full ruling in the Mechanics block.

IF THE VALVE FIRES: Doman and four crew crash in from the cove side, crossbows first - 'DARK STAR DOGS! Off my beach approach or feed the river!' He counts the party's number, says nothing else, and walks. Introductions belong to the gangplank (3.1).
Aftermath: the DARK STAR IDENTIFICATION RINGS in his belt open the guild thread in Chapter 4 - keep them visible in play. Down the trail lies Pendant Cove and Chapter 3.

chapters.chapterDevelopment: Advancement: the party should be solidly 4th level with two signature victories and one unshakable suspicion - that something is placing monsters in their path.

chapters.title: The River Serpent
chapters.overview: Nine days down the Trenlem aboard the fastest smuggler on the water - fast because she alone runs the Trenlem at night. Captain Doman Bail's hospitality buys the party a witness (Diana, who saw the assassination's other side), three night battles (animated polewights and shadows; a shore massacre by Berowls; a boarding by the Unkindness), one captive whose confession names THRON - and a grand arrival at the Twin Cities. At the table it runs as nine dusk rolls - nine nights on the river (+3 days on the Lithgow branch, C1).
chapters.running: River travel runs on the DUSK ON THE TRENLEM table at the top of this chapter - press ☾ Dusk Falls once each evening as the sail is stowed. That one press is the whole night: the Unkindness luck check, the night's color, and the day's advance together - it is the ONLY thing that moves the calendar in this chapter (the scenes carry no advance of their own; nine presses reach the Twins, and the panel counts the nights for you). Add the SHORE WATCH from the crow's nest (DCs in 3.1 Mechanics). Interweave the fixed scenes with the quiet nights the table deals; the ship should feel like home by the time it is attacked on. Rules of the dice, enforced by the console: the Unkindness never hunts the first night, and once the Berowl fight has happened the next dusk forces the attack. If the party sailed the Lithgow instead (CONTINGENCY C1), this chapter travels with them, not the ship: same dusk table, same shore, Diana already aboard - skip 3.1's fare scene and run the nights as written from night two, arriving three days behind the Serpent's schedule.

scenes.title: Pendant Cove
scenes.boxedText: A beautiful inlet in the shape of its namesake: a narrow entry off the Trenlem opening between vibrant green cliffs to a wide beach, the forest ending abruptly in a wall of trees split only by the game trail at the beach's dead center. The River Serpent rides at the sand with her gangplank down - and her captain already counting your number.
scenes.body: Doman Bail knows exactly who they are (the compromised note cut both ways - and if he pulled the party out of the Bowl himself, he already counted their number on the trail: the greeting below is the second half of a sentence he started there). His greeting, verbatim: 'Aye, I be the capton of the River Serpant. Do you be the party going to Aria, and thereby Ru Ailmen' - he says it ALE-men - 'and Yuvluil Ilmern' - YOU-vl-ule - 'the twin cities of the south?' Then, palm out: 'I agreed on one gold for each of ya. Pay up or be on with ya.' Fare paid, tour given, crew introduced. Below decks: Diana, a Paladin of Teg of the south-eastern border tribes, traveling to the capital.

blocks.title: THE CREW
blocks.sub: stat references in Appendix A

rows.name: DOMAN BAIL, Captain
rows.note: human, he/him - his own block (App. A). Fights only when his crew or his passengers are threatened.

rows.name: KET, First Mate
rows.note: half-orc, he/him - Veteran, with a quartermaster's glare.

rows.name: OKTUX & THUSH
rows.note: half-orc deckhands, they/them & he/him - Bandit.

rows.name: LIGART, ANDREU, GIB, WILL, TOMAS, SANSON
rows.note: human crewmates - Commoners with good sea legs.

rows.name: KEYA
rows.note: elf scout, the Serpent's eyes aloft - Scout. Nothing gets close before she has named it.

blocks.title: THE SHIP
blocks.sub: per the original deck plans
lines: Crow's nest above; main deck with mast, gratings, and stern doors; cabins and cargo below; a lower deck of sweeps for when the wind sulks.
Theater-of-mind shorthand: three levels, one ladder between each - and Keya sees everything first.

Her secret is no secret aboard: sail up by day for the trade winds, stowed at dusk for the night drift - a skeleton crew on deck and Doman reading water no one else can. Other boats anchor at sundown. The Serpent never stops. That is why she is the fastest smuggler on the Trenlem.

blocks.title: THE RIVER RHYTHM
blocks.sub: the chapter's engine - two dice, every dusk
lines: UNKINDNESS LUCK CHECK: press ☾ Dusk Falls on the Dusk on the Trenlem table (top of this chapter) each evening as the sail is stowed. On 1-10 the Unkindness attacks - run 3.5 early. The same throw deals the night's color and advances the day: the sole day-mover this chapter. Rules of the dice: never on the first night; forced the dusk after the Berowl fight.
SHORE WATCH: someone in the crow's nest each night - usually Keya - per the DCs below. This is how 3.3's poles and 3.4's wreck are spotted at all.

rows.dc: DC 15 Wisdom (Perception) - Shore Watch from the crow's nest
rows.result: trouble ashore is spotted while it still matters: the scarecrow poles, the wreck, lights that should not be there.

rows.dc: DC 20 Wisdom (Perception) - Shore Watch from anywhere else on deck
rows.result: same sighting, worse angle.

blocks.title: PROW WATCH: THE RIVER'S TEETH
blocks.sub: two-hour rotations through the night — flavor for the watches
lines: Keya's voice carries from the crow's nest: 'Pale water on the starboard bend.' Doman is on deck before the second watch even registers the call, reading the shallows by moonlight alone. The Serpent sidesteps like a dancer.

The night is thick cloud and darker river. The watch strains to see anything at all. But Doman does not sleep—he stands at the rail, one hand trailing in the water, feeling the current's whisper. 'Log ahead,' he says quietly. Not spotted; felt.

A scrape along the hull—the kind that makes everyone stop breathing. Doman does not swear; he simply corrects with a hand on the wheel, and the Serpent glides past something large and half-submerged. 'That one was close,' he says to no one. Keya grips the crow's nest railing.

Dawn comes soft over the water, and the watch changes over. The night held no sightings, no shouts, nothing but the river and its rhythm. But looking back at the bends they navigated in darkness, the party understands: this swiftness is not boast. It is earned on nights like this.

The Serpent's bow rises to meet a riffle of fast water. Doman is already altering course before the spray hits—a small adjustment that transforms a grind into a glide. 'The river speaks if you listen,' he says, and keeps his hand steady on the wheel.

script.text: The trail breaks onto the beach - push Pendant Cove.
Doman knows exactly who they are. His greeting, verbatim - Ru Ailmen said ALE-men, Yuvl Ilmern said YOU-vl-ule - then the palm: 'One gold for each of ya. Pay up or be on with ya.'
Fare paid: the tour, the crew (Mechanics), and below decks - Diana, Paladin of Teg, traveling to the capital.

Start the river rhythm tonight and keep it: ☾ Dusk Falls each evening is the night AND the day - the only calendar-mover this chapter (1-10 fires 3.5 early; never night one). Post the Shore Watch from the crow's nest (Mechanics).

scenes.title: Diana's Testimony

blocks.title: DELIVER AS CONVERSATION, NOT EXPOSITION
lines: Diana witnessed the assassination attempt's FAR side, at the eastern border. Her patrol walked in on a ritual in progress - a large bipedal creature, horns, a face harsh with large teeth, FOUR ARMS (the upper pair huge and clawed, the lower human-like), orchestrating goblin teleportations and an unorthodox rend in space.
Prone beside the rend: a kobold with a slender long pipe aimed through it - and the CRACK her patrol heard is the same CRACK the whole amphitheater felt.
The demon teleported away; the kobold melted into the forest past senior rangers.

rows.result: any PC with demon lore: the four-armed description matches a GLABREZU.

blocks.text: Tethered to the night counter: Diana is aboard from night one and departs at the fifth ☾ Dusk Falls, at the cove near the Jade-Trenlem confluence - carrying her testimony to the Empress with Doman's map and letter. The Dusk on the Trenlem panel calls the beat the night it lands.

scenes.development: Two campaign facts are now on the table: the shooter was a kobold firing through a portal, and a glabrezu ran the operation. Diana departs at a cove near the Jade-Trenlem confluence on the fifth day on the river, carrying her testimony to the Empress, with Doman's map and letter to speed her upriver.

script.text: Deliver Diana's testimony as conversation, not exposition: her patrol walked in on the ritual - the four-armed demon orchestrating, the kobold prone at the rend with a slender long pipe, and the CRACK her patrol heard is the amphitheater's CRACK.
DC 15 Intelligence (Arcana): the four-armed description matches a GLABREZU.
Two campaign facts are now on the table: the shooter was a kobold firing through a portal, and a glabrezu ran the operation.
She departs at the Jade-Trenlem confluence - the fifth day on the river - with Doman's map and letter. Whether she reaches the capital is a thread you control.

scenes.timeNote: Rides nights one through five - Diana departs at the fifth ☾ Dusk Falls (the confluence); the night counter tracks it

scenes.title: Polewights at Dusk
scenes.boxedText: From the crow's nest, Keya calls it down: four of what seem to be scarecrows, their poles stuck in the water, spanning the narrower part of the river mid-channel. Sagging, crow-picked, absurd. The captain confers with her - Keya sees only the poles in the clear water, nothing beneath them to snag the boat - and Doman orders full sail, straight through. As the hull strikes the first two, the scarecrows MOVE.

battle.name: Boarders in the Rigging
battle.setup: The polewights smash off their poles and leap to the gunnels at full sail - fighting on a moving deck (DC 10 DEX to run or charge across it this round; failure means movement halved). As the last polewight burns, two Shadows slink over the stern where no one is looking.

combatants.name: Polewight
combatants.note: Vulnerable to fire - let the first firebolt teach the lesson loudly.

combatants.name: Shadow
combatants.note: Enter on round 3 or when the polewights are down, whichever is later.

battle.tactics: Polewights split among the crew to force the party to protect; their Sack Turns targets whoever is doing the most damage. The shadows hunt the lowest-Strength PC and use the mast's shadow to hide.
battle.adjusting: Weaker party: 3 polewights, 1 shadow. Stronger party: 6 polewights, and the shadows arrive while the polewights still stand.
battle.aftermath: The crew's reaction matters more than the loot: a show of force with no ask for aid is not the normal response on these rivers - the party has just become family. Doman's regard is worth a favor later; write it down.

script.text: Keya calls it down from the nest - push the polewights.
Doman confers, sees nothing beneath the poles, and orders full sail straight through. As the hull strikes the first two - they MOVE. Roll initiative (moving deck: DC 10 DEX to run or charge).
Do not forget the two Shadows slinking over the stern as the last polewight burns - they hunt the lowest-Strength PC and hide in the mast's shadow.
Aftermath: the crew's reaction matters more than the loot. A show of force with no ask for aid is not normal on these rivers - the party just became family. Write Doman's regard down.

rows.dc: DC 10 Dexterity - THE MOVING DECK, any round a creature runs or charges across it
rows.result: failure: movement halved this round. Applies to both sides - the polewights do not care.

blocks.text: Two Shadows slink over the stern as the last polewight burns - they hunt the lowest-Strength PC and hide in the mast's shadow. Do not forget them; the table will.

scenes.timeNote: A night on the river - time rides with ☾ Dusk Falls, no separate advance

scenes.title: The Night Battle
scenes.boxedText: Screeches from the dark northern shore. In the wreck of a wagon, six hulking shapes hunch and tear - two oxen, mostly gone, and by his clothes and the hay he lies in, what is most likely a farmer.

blocks.text: Triggered by the Dusk on the Trenlem table - a 10 after the fifth night, forced at the eighth dusk if the dice never find it; the panel calls the beat. The sighting can pass without engagement - the original party let the sleuth finish its meal and sailed on, and paid for it when the beasts returned fatter and bolder. Engaging or not, once this night is dealt the console checks the scene off at the next dusk.

rows.dc: DC 15 Charisma - GETTING ASHORE, first: persuade Doman to anchor and lend the rowboat
rows.result: he anchors mid-channel, lends the boat, and watches from the rail.

rows.dc: DC 10 water-vehicle proficiency - then: land the rowboat clean
rows.result: failing by 5 or more capsizes it: DC 10 Athletics to swim in, DC 15 to save another.

rows.dc: Group Dexterity (Stealth) vs. the Berowls' Perception - last: the approach
rows.result: failure: they turn from the kill and charge the bank - the kill-box works in reverse.

battle.name: Berowls on the Shore
battle.setup: Six Berowls feeding at the treeline, 60 feet of open bank between them and the water. The party chooses the engagement - the first crew fought most of it from the ship and the water's edge, denying the beasts their charge, and it worked beautifully.

combatants.name: Berowl
combatants.note: Teleport-seeded pack hunters; see the stat block's Pack Frenzy.

battle.tactics: Berowls charge the nearest blood and frenzy around downed prey; they will not enter deep water. Kill-box tactics (missile fire from the boat, control spells at the bank) turn this from deadly to one-sided - reward the thinking.
battle.adjusting: Weaker party: 4 Berowls. Stronger party: 6 plus a second wave of 2 arriving from the treeline on round 4.
battle.aftermath: Shore investigation (DC 13 Intelligence (Investigation) or Detect Magic): the faint whisper of a teleportation circle. These beasts could never pace a river ship - someone is placing monsters AHEAD of the party. Let the players say it out loud before any NPC does.

script.text: Screeches from the dark northern shore - push the wreck.
The sighting can pass without engagement - the original party let the sleuth finish its meal and sailed on, and paid for it when the beasts returned fatter and bolder.
Getting ashore: DC 15 CHA to borrow the rowboat, DC 10 water-vehicle to land clean (5-under capsizes), group Stealth against their Perception.
The fight (battle block): they charge the nearest blood and will not enter deep water - kill-box tactics from boat and bank turn this one-sided. Reward the thinking.
Aftermath: DC 13 Investigation or Detect Magic ashore - the circle whisper again. Let the players say 'someone is placing monsters AHEAD of us' out loud before any NPC does.

scenes.timeNote: A night on the river - time rides with ☾ Dusk Falls, no separate advance

scenes.title: The Unkindness
scenes.boxedText: From north and south at once, two great conspiracies of ravens converge above the mast, clashing in a wheeling dance that swallows the last light of the day. When they break apart, six too large ravens hang in the air - and in one synchronized instant morph grotesquely and are six raven-headed soldiers, wings wide, weapons drawn.

blocks.text: Triggered by the Dusk on the Trenlem table (1-9) - never on the first night, random through the fourth, and forced at the fifth dusk if the dice never find it: the murders will not let the Serpent pass the confluence unbloodied. The console enforces the rules of the dice and checks the scene off at the dusk after the attack.

battle.name: The Unkindness of the Bronze Storm
battle.setup: Six Sleapless board at dusk as the sail is stowed. Doman fights beside the party - his crew is watching him. Two hold reserve on the wing, joining when the first four falter. At the opposite end of the deck, KET leads the rest of the crew - the hands not fighting beside the party - in cornering one of the wing reserves with cold iron in hand: beaten down, trussed, and dragged below, held.

combatants.name: Sleapless
combatants.note: 4 board immediately; 2 in flying reserve.

battle.tactics: The Sleapless pair up on isolated targets and try to drag the fight to the rails. Their regeneration makes them arrogant - until someone improvises with the ship itself (see the stat block's Iron-Shy trait; the first crew discovered that ship-hull iron hurts them, and it became legend).
battle.adjusting: Weaker party: 4 Sleapless total. Stronger party: 8, and the reserves target the helm to force a piloting crisis.
battle.aftermath: The captive is guaranteed: at the far end of the deck Ket and the crew take one of the wing reserves alive - apart from the pack that strikes the party - trussed, dragged below, held. A combination of magic and GENUINE healing opens him up. Run 3.6. (If Ket fought beside the party instead, hand the capture to Gib and Sanson.)

script.text: Triggered by the nightly luck roll - never night one, forced at the fifth dusk if the dice never find it. Two conspiracies converge above the mast: push the Unkindness.
Six Sleapless board at dusk as the sail is stowed; two hold reserve on the wing. Doman fights beside the party - his crew is watching him.
Their regeneration makes them arrogant - until someone improvises with the ship itself. Ship-hull iron hurts them (Iron-Shy); let the table discover it and become legend.

The captive is guaranteed - at the opposite end of the deck, Ket leads the rest of the crew in taking one of the wing reserves alive, apart from the pack that strikes the party. Trussed, dragged below. Run 3.6.

scenes.timeNote: A night on the river - time rides with ☾ Dusk Falls, no separate advance

scenes.title: The Captive

blocks.text: TONE & SAFETY - This scene carries the campaign's most intense beat. A dedicated deep dive on the Tone & Safety page holds the full set of dials: canon, veil, and three story-hook rewrites that preserve every plot output. Choose your dial before you run the boarding night.

THE HOW - during the boarding (3.5), KET led the rest of the crew - the hands not fighting beside the party - in subduing one of the Unkindness's wing reserves, apart from the pack that struck the party: beaten down with cold iron, trussed, and secured in the hull, bound and guarded. Magic and genuine healing open it up.

blocks.title: WHAT THE CAPTIVE GIVES UP
lines: He is a soldier of the Bronze Storm Empire, east of the border.
His lycanthropy is - his word - a GIFT, granted to enhance his prowess, bestowed directly by ESSAX: a mist-shrouded shadow figure who led the ancient ritual.
Pressed further he confirms the party is being tracked somehow (he does not know how).
He gives the campaign a name: the demon who performs the border teleportation rituals - the same one who delivered his attack to this deck - is called THRON.
He raves that Essax will destroy 'your evil Empire' and bring back THE ONE to do it.

blocks.text: His fanaticism is extreme. His final act proves it - and leaves the party with a body in a box that the crew wants off the ship at port (it becomes the customs scene opening Chapter 4).

blocks.title: THE CAPTAIN ON THE BOX
blocks.sub: why the body does not go over the rail
lines: Doman, if the party suggests the river: "River gives 'em back. Always has. Bloated, three days on, right at the feet of the Shore Watch — they walk both banks at the mouth, and there's an outpost on the far side keeps a man for a week at a stretch."
"Now I've a writ. Man like him, took under it, that's lawful as bread. But a writ's a page with two ends, and only one of 'em's signed."

"He goes over my rail, that page stays open, and some morning a Watchman fishes him out with my name still on it. He rides in the box. He gets a name on a page. Then he's the city's problem, and I'm a captain again."

DM — Doman is not afraid of being caught. The kill was lawful under his writ of custody. He is afraid of an OPEN writ: a discharge unfiled, with a matching corpse recoverable at the river mouth. That is a charter problem, and Doman does not have charter problems.
The Shore Watch is texture, not threat. Two banks at the channel mouth, a week-long outpost on the far side. They never go upriver. Nobody is hunting the Serpent.

scenes.development: 'The One' stays unidentified until the party's own research (Chapter 7). Keep Thron (field commander) and the still-unknown palace leak distinct in your notes - the players will conflate them, and the eventual separation is a gift.

script.text: The how: during the boarding, Ket led the remaining crew in taking one of the wing reserves alive - apart from the pack that struck the party. It sits trussed in the hull, under guard.
Magic plus GENUINE healing opens the captive up: his lycanthropy is - his word - a GIFT, bestowed directly by ESSAX, a mist-shrouded shadow figure who led the ancient ritual.
The names: the party is being tracked somehow (he does not know how), and the demon who runs the border teleportation rituals - the one who delivered his attack to this deck - is called THRON.

He raves that Essax will bring back THE ONE. 'The One' stays unidentified until the party's own research in Chapter 7. Keep Thron (field commander) and the still-unknown palace leak distinct in your notes.

If they float the idea of dumping him: Doman refuses, and it is bookkeeping, not fear. The kill was LAWFUL under his writ of custody — but an unfiled discharge with a recoverable corpse is a charter problem. The Shore Watch walks both banks at the channel mouth. He rides in the box.
His final act proves the fanaticism - and leaves the party with a body in a box that the crew wants off the ship at port. It becomes the customs scene opening Chapter 4.

scenes.timeNote: The morning after the boarding - time rides with ☾ Dusk Falls, no separate advance

scenes.title: The Twins Channel
scenes.boxedText: Before you on your right, a city almost as big as the imperial capital: miles upon miles of stone buildings, tile roofs red and blue and yellow and every color between, riding a great sea wall that keeps the tide from Yuvl Ilmern. Giant arching bridges leap the channel to her twin - Ru Ailmen, as beautiful as her sister. Floating mooring docks and stairs line the walls as you pass through the core of the Twin Cities, and beyond the third arched bridge - a hundred feet above the mast - sprawl the north docks.
scenes.body: Doman berths just below the Sovereign Docks. His parting gifts: (1) a year of ports and dates for the Serpent - 'keep that close to your chest, but should you need us for travel, we will assist you' (Appendix D: player handout); (2) the TILE CODE of the Twins - Inns blue, Taverns red, General stores yellow, Magic purple, Apothecaries green, Warehouses brown, Official buildings gray, Markets orange (Appendix D; it is also this console's Atlas color-coding); (3) a note that a small carnival sits outside the city wall, for anyone who needs joy. Milestone: the party reaches 5th level.
scenes.development: Doman walks them personally to the dock gate, squares them with the Dock Master's office, and says his farewell. Chapter 4 opens at the gate - with a body in a box and a city locked down tight.

script.text: The approach to the Twins - push it and let it breathe; this is the campaign's home base arriving.

Home base is arriving — this is the moment for the city map. Open The World › Maps and push the city map (and, if the table likes to plan, the Tile Code legend) so the players watch the Twins resolve out of the description into a place they can point at.

The bridges overhead carry the channel's favorite rumor - something old and rich sleeps at the dead center of the channel, and retired bridge guards tell it best. Plant it now if you want it in the water early: the dive is a side quest, open the moment the table has the rumor and a way to breathe.

sq.label: The Treasure of the Twins Channel

script.text: Doman berths below the Sovereign Docks. The parting gifts: the Serpent's ports-and-dates ('keep that close to your chest'), the TILE CODE, and the carnival note - the first two are Appendix D handouts; push them as he hands them over.
Milestone: the party reaches 5th level.
He walks them personally to the dock gate and squares them with the Dock Master's office. Chapter 4 opens at the gate - with a body in a box and a city locked down tight.

scenes.timeNote: Night nine lands here - the last ☾ Dusk Falls delivers the Twins

chapters.chapterDevelopment: Everything the river taught them compounds: the kobold and the glabrezu behind the assassination, the name Thron, the certainty of being tracked, and a captain's friendship. If Diana reached the capital safely is a thread you control - her fate can raise the stakes in any later chapter.

tables.name: Dusk on the Trenlem
tables.note: Press ☾ Dusk Falls once each evening as the sail is stowed - the night's luck and its color in one throw, and the chapter's ONLY day-advance: each press moves the calendar one day, nine presses to the Twins, and at the ninth the button rests. Rules of the dice, enforced by the console - two hunts, two windows: nothing hunts the first night; nights two through five belong to the Unkindness (1-9 attacks, forced at the fifth dusk if the dice never find it, and a 10 cannot come up); nights six through eight belong to the Berowls (10 is the fight, forced at the eighth dusk if never rolled, and 1-9 is retired). Each hunt is dealt once - at the next press of Dusk Falls its scene checks itself off, and the checkmarks are not editable. Quiet nights (11-20) are spent as they are dealt; ↺ Reset restarts the river: nights, calendar days, spent entries, and both hunts.

entries.text: THE UNKINDNESS ATTACKS. Two conspiracies converge above the mast as the sail is stowed - run scene 3.5 (the battle block lives there). If the party is mid-task below decks, the first arrows buy them exactly one round of warning. Live nights two through four; forced on the fifth if the dice never find it.

THE BEROWL FIGHT. Screeches from the dark northern shore - the sleuth is at a kill in a wrecked wagon, and the party chooses whether and how to engage; run scene 3.4 (the battle block lives there). Live only after the fifth night; forced on the eighth if the dice never find it.
Quiet water. The crew brews black-leaf tea on the aft brazier and Doman tells a story about a cargo he swears on his own fortune was legal. Downtime night: brewing, scribing, repairs.
Sanson loses at cards again, loudly. A PC who sits in and loses gracefully earns the crew's ear: one question about the river, the shore, or the Serpent's business answered straight.
Scribing weather - flat water, bright moons, Keya naming every light on the far bank from the nest. The best night aboard for long talk: Diana's testimony (3.2) fits here if it has not landed yet.
A barge passes upriver showing green lanterns. Doman trades news across the water: prices, weather, and which docks are searching cargo this month. Useful color for Chapter 4's locked-down city.

POLEWIGHTS AT DUSK. Four poles stand mid-channel, crowned with sagging scarecrows. Keya calls it from the nest; Doman sees nothing beneath, orders full sail straight through. As the hull strikes the first two—they MOVE. Run scene 3.3 (the battle block lives there).
Fish leap at the bow all evening - a good omen, the crew insists, and confidence is contagious: the first check any PC makes tomorrow gains +1.
Gib's night to cook. It is terrible. Doman eats two helpings without a word, and the party learns what loyalty looks like when it is fed.

Lights ashore where no farm stands. By the time anyone looks twice they are gone. No roll, no fight - just let the table sit with it. (It waters the seed 3.4's aftermath plants: someone is placing things AHEAD of them.)
Keya comes down from the nest and drills whoever asks: how the water lies, what a wrong shadow looks like. A PC who trains with her gains advantage on the next Shore Watch they personally attempt.

The Serpent runs perfect and silent, Doman at the wheel, humming. A PC who joins him hears him talk about the river the way other men talk about religion - and he answers one honest question honestly.

chapters.title: The Locked Twins
chapters.overview: The party lands in a city holding its breath: the Twins are locked down - no one in or out - the Sovereign's Steward has not been seen in a tenday, and guard pairs sweep the streets with aggressive nonchalance whispering about a dark elf. The way to Oospufmorn is across the channel, and the channel is closed. The Dark Star rings from Chapter 2 buy the answer: the Moonlight Strategy, the Twins' native thieves' guild, knows a way under. In-world: two to three days in the locked city.
chapters.running: Two clocks tick side by side: the Steward mystery (which the party CANNOT solve this chapter - it seeds Chapter 7's politics) and the practical problem of crossing a sealed channel (which they can). Let them bang on official doors first; every polite refusal makes the criminal door more attractive. The guild thread requires the identification rings - if the party lost or sold them, a streetwise PC can re-earn access with a night's work and a favor owed. Spend the city day generously: the Twins are the campaign's home base from here to the endgame, and every shopkeeper met now is texture later.

tables.name: Street Talk of the Twins
tables.note: Rumors overheard in queues, taverns, and market stalls - all true, none complete.

entries.text: "The Steward? Not seen in a tenday. And that one's usually easier to find than the sun."
"Guard pairs on every third corner, walking slow and looking hard. That's not a patrol, that's a hunt."
"My cousin works the clacks - messages still cross the channel just fine. It's PEOPLE they've stopped."
"There's a carnival pitched outside the wall if you need your fortunes lightened honestly for once."
"The smith on the central road works mithral, true mithral. Waiting list is a year unless you're interesting."
"Old dragonborn lady at the North Docs Market sells baubles. My gran swears one of her 'glass beads' was a diamond big as a knuckle."

scenes.title: The Gate and the Box
scenes.boxedText: The dock gate of Ru Ailmen is polished, official, and thoroughly jammed - a queue of travelers arguing with guards who keep repeating the same sentence with the same tired courtesy. And your party is the one carrying a corpse in a box.

blocks.text: Doman has already squared the party with the Dock Master's office — a standing favor: they may visit the Serpent's slip whenever she is in port.

blocks.title: THE WRIT OF CUSTODY
blocks.sub: the paperwork that behaves
lines: Issuer — a standing writ of the Sovereign against river raiders, held by Doman Bail as master of a chartered vessel.
What it covers — the taking of a raider, alive or dead, in defense of the charter. The captive's death aboard the Serpent falls squarely inside it.
What discharge requires — the body, delivered to a gate desk, named on a page. Delivery closes the writ.
Why the guard is grateful — the handover does not OPEN a file. It CLOSES one. On a morning when a manhunt has buried him, the party hands him the only thing on his desk that finishes.

blocks.text: The handover goes smoothly if the party is organized and honest. The writ is airtight; the only way to fumble this is to lie about something the page already says plainly.
A sneak-eyed PC who angles for a look at the desk earns it: a manhunt is on, and the ways in and out of the city are guarded until further orders.

scenes.development: The party is IN the city; the problem is leaving it westward across the channel. Scene 4.2.

script.text: Push the gate - the queue, the tired courtesy, and the party carrying a corpse in a box.

Doman has squared them with the Dock Master's office (a standing favor: the Serpent's slip is theirs to visit). The handover behaves because the WRIT OF CUSTODY behaves — the body discharges it. The desk guard is grateful for the one page on his desk that CLOSES a file instead of opening one.

If a PC asks why they carried a corpse nine nights instead of putting it in the river: the captain's answer stands — lawful kill, open writ, Shore Watch at the mouth. He rides in the box, he gets a name on a page, he becomes the city's problem.
A sneak-eyed PC angling at his desk earns it: a MANHUNT is on, and the ways in and out are guarded until further orders.
They are IN the city. The problem is leaving it westward across the channel - 4.2.

Orienting the party: the gate sits at the Sovereign Docks, the northern tip of Ru Ailmen. The city map (The World › Maps) puts every street they are about to walk in front of them — push it here so the lockdown in 4.2 lands on a city they can already see.

scenes.title: No One In or Out
scenes.body: Official channels fail in instructive ways. The Mayor's office: appointments a week out, at best. The Sovereign's Steward: the Sovereign Guard turns everyone from the Palace doors before an appointment can even be requested. Locals: the Steward has not been seen in public for a tenday. Each bridge entrance is held by a sergeant, a corporal, and twelve specialists, all repeating: 'We were told to lock down the city. No one in or out. I'm sure it'll be only for a short time - this type of thing happens from time to time. Go to the City Guardhouse for further information if you wish.' The Guardhouse, naturally, has none.

blocks.title: THE INVESTIGATION LADDER
blocks.sub: Investigation or Persuasion

rows.result: The Steward was last on procession to the Council of Twelve, a tenday ago.
'The location of such a public figure is generally known to us. This mystery is definitely out of the realm of normal.'
It has to be a manhunt.

blocks.title: WHAT THE STREET SHOWS
blocks.sub: Perception

rows.result: A rapid increase of guards searching the streets in pairs, as nonchalant as possible about it.

blocks.title: DC 25 - OVERHEARD
blocks.sub: save this for a payoff moment
lines: A soldier to his sergeant, almost pleading: 'I swear to you, sergeant, on my life, it was a Dark Elf.'
'I believe you, Johnny. You're not the first to see one on these streets.'

scenes.development: The mystery is a wall on purpose. When the party runs out of doors to knock on, the rings in their pack start feeling heavier. Scene 4.4 - after they've had a day in the city (4.3).

script.text: Let official channels fail in instructive order: the Mayor's office (a week out at best), the Sovereign's Steward (turned from the Palace doors), the locals (not seen in public for a tenday).
Every bridge: a sergeant, a corporal, twelve specialists, the same sentence - 'No one in or out... Go to the City Guardhouse for further information.' The Guardhouse, naturally, has none.
Run the investigation ladder (Mechanics) as they dig; save the DC 25 overheard whisper - 'I swear to you, sergeant, it was a Dark Elf' - for a payoff moment.
The wall is a wall on purpose. When they run out of doors to knock on, the rings in their pack start feeling heavier. City day first - 4.3.

scenes.title: A Day in Ru Ailmen
scenes.boxedText: Ru Ailmen wears its tile code proudly: blue roofs promising beds, red promising drink, a purple one on the central road humming faintly if you stand too close. Between the sea wall and the market cries, the lockdown is almost possible to forget.

blocks.text: Let the World Atlas carry this scene - the city is fully keyed there, tile colors and all. And put the map in their hands: The World › Maps holds the city map and the Tile Code legend, both pushable. This is the scene the Tile Code was built for - push the legend once and the party navigates the crawl by roof color on their own.

rows.name: The central road
rows.note: arcane curiosities and a master blacksmith who works true mithral

rows.name: North Docs Market
rows.note: an old dragonborn lady sells 'baubles' among which sharp eyes find improbable diamonds

rows.name: The sick house
rows.note: better for the party's visit (healers are always short-handed; kindness here echoes later)

rows.name: Ancient Blossom Inn
rows.note: the party's rooms in Ru Ailmen — Bresira Deepwind keeps good rooms and better counsel

rows.name: The carnival
rows.note: small, outside the wall, for anyone who needs joy - run its games live from Run the Table > Carnival Games

blocks.text: End the day at the inn - and if any PC runs streetwise, let them slip into the dark side of town after midnight and come back with scene 4.4 already half-arranged.

scenes.development: Rest, resupply, and one night of city texture. The knock on the inn door after midnight - or the morning errand to a certain tavern - opens the guild thread.

script.text: Push the tile code skyline and let the lockdown become almost possible to forget.

Let the World Atlas carry the day - the mithral smith, the dragonborn lady's improbable diamonds, the sick house (kindness here echoes later), the Ancient Blossom, and the carnival outside the wall for anyone who needs joy.
End the day at the inn - and if any PC runs streetwise, let them slip into the dark side of town after midnight and come back with 4.4 already half-arranged.

time.label: A day (or more) in Ru Ailmen — how long?

scenes.title: The Moonlight Strategy
scenes.body: The Twins' native guild despises Dark Star, and the captured identification rings are proof of work against the common enemy. Working the streets locates the guild's lower ranks; the ranks lead upward to a tavern, a proprietor, and a hideout. Once inside, the party deals with the guild's chain of command: Valfer Keenlade, Mastermind (halfling, he/him, 165); Elielle Nimblesurge, Ringleader (halfling, she/her, 123); and Ruglal Vuzrubor, Captain (dark elf, she/her, 200). They are professionals: courteous, unhurried, and pricing everything said in the room.

blocks.text: The Moonlight Strategy is the Twins' native thieves' guild - a den, not a metaphor. To its own members it is 'just a social club': those who like the finer things and know how to get their fingers on them. Master Thief Xannys Truebridge (halfling, she/her, 136) sits at the top of the chain of command; the three officers below her - Mastermind, Ringleader, and Captain - are who the party will actually deal with.

blocks.title: FINDING THE RANKS
blocks.sub: Investigation

rows.result: Toad
Wet Ear
Footpad

blocks.title: THE CHAIN UPWARD
lines: Wet Ears and Toads point to THE RARE COIN tavern to find Footpads.
Footpads know the proprietor of EBONY CAMP, Rinys Glowseeker, knows the hideout.
Showing an Empire Operative tattoo (if they chose the "The Reformed Hand" card) grants instant access; otherwise the rings plus a DC 10 Persuasion open the door.

blocks.title: RP — STREET LEVEL
blocks.sub: Toads & Wet Ears · table talk
lines: The bottom rungs work the gutters, market edges, and dock stairs. Toads are street kids — the smallest is ten, the oldest nineteen — eyes and ears who answer questions with prices. Wet Ears are the recruit tier; several Mondobeth siblings among them cover for each other by reflex.
A Toad, palm already out: 'Information's a copper. Good information's a silver. I'll tell you which one you're buying after.'
A Toad, deflecting: 'Never heard of any club. There's a tavern on East Channel Street where nobody's heard of it neither.'
A Mondobeth Wet Ear, shrugging: 'You want my sister. Or my brother. One of them, anyway — I just carry things.'
Any of them, asked directly what the Moonlight Strategy is: 'It's just a social club.' Flat. Every time. Every rank.

blocks.title: RP — THE RARE COIN
blocks.sub: Footpads · read-aloud & table talk
lines: Read-aloud: red roof tiles, a sprawling channel-side stone building on East Channel Street, double doors thrown wide. Through the far windows, a covered patio against a hip-height wall — and gulls wheeling over water you feel in the damp air before you ever see it. Two bars, one to each side, a chalkboard above each: THE RULES — NO CREDIT. NO FIGHTING.
Every soul on staff is a Brightmeadow. The tenders never leave the bar — except to throw someone out.
Bellos Brightmeadow, polishing a mug: 'Rules are on the board. Everything else in this room is negotiable, and none of it's mine to negotiate.'
The tell: a crescent moon with a four-pointed star tattooed in the web of the left thumb — closed against the forefinger when it wants to hide.
A footpad, brokering: 'Clubs take introductions. Buy the table a pitcher and tell me why anyone should vouch for you.'
The same footpad, eyeing the rings, thumb pressed to forefinger: 'Those come off Dark Star belts one way. Ebony Camp. Ask for the proprietor. Say nothing to anyone else.'

blocks.title: RP — EBONY CAMP & RINYS
blocks.sub: the gatekeeper · read-aloud & table talk
lines: Read-aloud: blue roof tiles, three stories of stone with worked-iron balconies on the upper floors, a small stage in the corner of the common room, six tables seating four and six, and the smell of a kitchen that has had the same cook for fifty years. Behind the bar: Rinys Glowseeker — a stout halfling in a blue coat, white ruffled undershirt, brown britches, a bleached white apron — counting the room without looking up.

The house: a hallway past the stage leads to two private dining rooms (a dozen seats and eight) and the stair. Six rooms at 2 gp on the second floor, four at 4 gp on the third; tenday stays discount to 16 gp and 34 gp. The cook is Panver Applehands, apprenticed here and never left — his kitchen anchors the whole street's opinion of the place.

DM only: Rinys is a former Master Thief of the Moonlight Strategy. She retired upward, not out. Nothing crosses her floor unpriced, nobody reaches the storage room without her leave, and she has heard every clever approach the party is about to invent.

Her method: one unhurried question at a time until the vouch is established. Wrong answer, and the conversation is suddenly about rooms and ale again — no anger, no tell, just a door that was never visibly open.
Rinys, first pass: 'Rooms are two gold on the second floor, four on the third. Tenday discount if you're staying. Are you staying?'
Rinys, tested: 'Lots of clubs in this city. Sewing clubs. Rowing clubs. Which is it you think I keep?'
Rinys, taking evidence for the 24-hour test: 'Leave it with me. Come back tomorrow, same hour. If that's a problem, the door's where you left it.'
Rinys, opening the way — she never says yes. She picks up a lamp and walks toward the storage room: 'Mind the ladder. Thirty feet is thirty feet.'

blocks.title: THE THREE DOORS IN
blocks.sub: how strangers reach the Den · pick the one the party earns
lines: A vouch from a member of rank — Operative or higher. The party has no such friend yet; earning one is a session of favors, not an evening of charm.

Physical evidence, surrendered: the Dark Star rings, handed over for inspection by an active member below. The test is patience — 24 hours, come back the same hour tomorrow. This is the door the book expects the party to use.
The Empire Operative tattoo (if a PC took "The Reformed Hand" card): shown to Rinys, the way opens the same visit. No test, no wait, and a longer look from Ruglal once they're down the ladder.
Whichever door opens, the tell is the same: Rinys never says yes. The lamp comes off its hook, and she walks.

blocks.title: IF EBONY CAMP GOES SOUTH
blocks.sub: contingencies · the inn absorbs almost everything
lines: They refuse to surrender the rings: Rinys shrugs — 'Then we've nothing to talk about' — and the inn absorbs them as paying customers. Let a Footpad from the Rare Coin re-approach a day later; the guild has heard, and curiosity outbids caution. The test restarts. The price does not change.

They lean on Rinys: she neither argues nor moves. Within minutes two half-orc Blackcaps arrive to drink at the nearest table and watch. Being leaned on is, for a former Master Thief, a Tuesday. Threats add a full day to any test in progress and quietly close the third floor to the party.

They snoop for the hatch: the storage room sits off a first-floor hall in full view of the common room, and its lock is guild work (DC 18). Getting caught means the club knows them as burglars before it knows them as allies — every social DC in this scene rises by 5 and Rinys's questions start over from a much colder place.

Open violence in the inn: nobody fights them here. Staff clear the room, Rinys walks out through the kitchen, and the Den seals beneath their feet. The guild goes dark on the party — jump to Contingency C2 — and the City Guard of a manhunt-locked city arrives with no patience at all for tavern brawlers.

blocks.title: RP — THE DEN
blocks.sub: beneath Ebony Camp · read-aloud & table talk
lines: Read-aloud: a secret door in the storage room, a closet, a hatch — and a sturdy ladder dropping thirty feet straight down. Lamplight blooms below into a great dome carved from the island's bedrock.

First arrival — let the quiet do the work: the Den is mostly empty and the sparring pit is dark. This is a room built to hold sixty that currently holds four. Two officers drink at the bar with no concern for the newcomers; the scattered stools around two pushed-together tables say it was fuller an hour ago.

Behind the bar to the left: GROTHEN — a hulking warforged, heavy steel brow, hinged jaw, blue gemstone eyes glowing faintly in the lamplight, white button-down under a bleached apron, forever wiping mugs. The staff call him G. Everyone else is normally intimidated enough not to ask.

The room: four tables before the bar, two recently pushed together. To the right, the roped sparring pit — a twenty-foot painted circle, two lines ten feet apart, lamps above it unlit tonight. At the back, three beaded thresholds, so any breach is heard: kitchen, the hall to the Master Thief's door, and a guarded stair down — a half-orc Blackcap on it, always.

In an alcove left of the entrance, lamp deliberately extinguished: RUGLAL VUZRUBOR, cowl drawn, tight leather gloves, manor-house maps spread before her. She prices everyone who comes down the ladder.
Grothen, without looking up: 'Bar stools are for members. Tables are for guests. You look like tables.' The jaw hinges into what might be a smile.
Valfer Keenlade, genial, patting a stool anyway: 'Sit, sit. Rinys doesn't send us people, she sends us decisions. Let's find out which you are.'
Elielle Nimblesurge, needling: 'Nice rings. The belts they came off — walking, or not walking?'
Ruglal, from the dark, four words at a time: 'Names. Then the price.'

blocks.title: FIGHT NIGHT — GROTHEN'S BOOK
blocks.sub: the pit · run it live from Run the Table › Fighting Pits
lines: The roped circle is dark the night the party first descends — but every few nights the Den fills, the pit lamps come up, and the painted lines earn their keep. Blackcaps and Bandits work the circle for the room's coin; known guests can be invited to step in.

Grothen keeps the book the way most pits run one: the house posts odds on each fighter, every bet is laid against the house at the chalked line, and the house has not lost a night in living memory. One-off wagers — method of victory, which round, first blood — are taken at Grothen's discretion, if the ask amuses him.
Pit rules, chalked by the entrance rope: NO STEEL. NO SPELLS. FIRST YIELD OR FIRST SLEEP. The Blackcap on the stair enforces all three without being asked.
Grothen, taking a bet without looking up: 'House odds are on the board. Your coin, your funeral. G doesn't argue with the chalk.'

PCs in the pit: DC 13 Athletics or Acrobatics satisfies the Blackcap that they won't embarrass the room; then run the bout to first yield or unconsciousness — fists, grapples, and nothing that leaves a mark the Sick House would ask about.

The tool: Run the Table › Fighting Pits seeds the house fighters by tier, posts the suggested line, runs the bouts round by round, takes the table's bets — including Grothen's one-offs — and settles the house ledger. A PC who steps in goes on the chalk at Tier I and earns a stamped chip for each tier they climb; the chip is honored by any pit boss, and their line moves with their last result. Fight night pushes to the player screen: the fight card and the house line, bets opening and closing, every round as it lands, the pit boss calling each one, and the chalk itself between bouts — Live mode keeps the board current on its own.

blocks.title: IF THE DEN GOES SOUTH
blocks.sub: contingencies · steel below the world
lines: Steel comes out: the response is total and immediate. Grothen vaults the bar — he protects the room, not the guild's pride — the stair Blackcap and all three officers close ranks, and the beaded thresholds mean Xannys Truebridge hears every move from her office. The guild does not fight to kill guests; it fights to end the conversation.

If the party wins anyway: they have beaten a room, not a guild. Sixty members across two cities now know their faces, the Rare Coin goes cold, and the sewers route is gone — jump to Contingency C2 for crossing the channel without the Moonlight Strategy.

If the party loses: they wake at dawn in the alley behind Ebony Camp, coin purses intact, weapons stacked neatly on a rain barrel one street over. The message is precision, not cruelty. Pinned to a cloak, in a careful hand: 'Names. Then the price. Same terms.' The door is somehow still open — at half again the price.

They insult the bargain: lowball the NAME, the TIME, and the PASS PHRASE, and Ruglal relights her lamp — the meeting is over. Valfer, apologetic, walking them to the ladder: 'She doesn't haggle. I'd sleep on it.' The offer stands one tenday; then the terms get worse.

They mention the guild to the City Guard: word beats them back to the Den — there is a Toad on every corner. Any test in progress becomes a tenday freeze-out, and surrendered evidence comes back by street kid, no note. Repairable, but only by a service rendered, DM's choice.

blocks.title: WHAT THE THIEVES GUILD KNOWS
blocks.sub: rings shown + DC 10 Persuasion
lines: The Steward truly has not been seen in a tenday by any of their number.
Last seen crossing the Sovereign Bridge - middle of the three - to visit the Council of Twelve.
The clacks still deliver information, but nothing else crosses the channel.

blocks.title: WHAT THE GUILD HOLDS BACK
blocks.sub: Perception · against the officer who just answered

rows.result: Whichever officer delivered the answer above - Valfer, Elielle, or Ruglal - is sitting on more. Press, and they give up the way across the channel.

blocks.title: RP — THE CROSSING
blocks.sub: the sewers · the guild's last free word
lines: The officer, relenting: 'Well, of course I was going to say - above is not the only way across the channel. There are the sewers that tie the Twins together. Commissioned by the Twins, the dwarves carved out the greatest sanitation system in the Empire. They say it rivals none but their very own, whatever that means. Either way - we figured out a way through.'

This is the last information the guild gives freely. Everything spoken after it is price: the NAME, the TIME, and the PASS PHRASE. Do not let the reveal and the bargain land in the same breath - let the table sit with the sewers first, then let Ruglal name the terms.

scenes.treasure: Not gold - a NAME (Banminster Co., Ru Ailmen Holding Warehouse, southern docks), a TIME of the party's choosing, and a PASS PHRASE. The guild keeps the rings.
scenes.development: The southern docks looked so small from the Serpent's deck. Chapter 5 opens at the warehouse door.

script.text: The captured rings are proof of work against the common enemy. Run the ladder up: Toads DC 10, Wet Ears DC 15, Footpads DC 18 - to the Rare Coin, then to Rinys Glowseeker at Ebony Camp.

Rings plus a DC 10 Persuasion open the door (an Empire Operative tattoo, if a PC took the "The Reformed Hand" card, opens it instantly). Inside: Valfer, Elielle, and Ruglal - professionals, courteous, pricing everything said in the room.
What the guild knows (Mechanics): the Steward truly missing a tenday, last seen crossing the Sovereign Bridge; the clacks still deliver, nothing else crosses.

DC 15 Perception - the officer who answered is holding more: 'Above is not the only way across the channel...' The sewers. The dwarven Underbelly. This is the guild's last free word; what follows is price.
The payment is not gold: a NAME (Banminster Co., southern docks), a TIME of the party's choosing, and a PASS PHRASE. The guild keeps the rings.

time.label: Arrangements at the guild - the party names the day of the meet

chapters.chapterDevelopment: Leave the Steward mystery deliberately unsolved - the party should cross into Chapter 5 with the itch intact. If they befriended Rinys or the guild's officers, note it: the Moonlight Strategy resurfaces whenever you need the streets to have eyes.

chapters.title: The Underbelly
chapters.overview: Pass phrases at a warehouse door, a 380-foot cage elevator, and a scrap of paper disguised as a ship's manifest: the thieves' road under the Twins Channel. Junction rooms stocked with other people's secrets, a four-locked door that should not be opened yet, and - in the vast dark of the Channel Expanse - demons that should not be here at all. In-world: one long day under the channel.
chapters.running: This is a dungeon crawl wearing a heist's clothes. Navigation runs on the manifest (scene 5.2): read each direction aloud only as the party commits to it, and make them track position - getting lost down here is atmosphere, not punishment. The side rooms (5.3) are optional greed with real rewards; the four-lock door (5.4) is a fixed refusal - it exists to be remembered. The Expanse battle (5.5) is the chapter's set piece and the campaign's third teleport-circle clue. Total darkness throughout: track light sources, and let the party hear everything before they see it - except in the Expanse (5.5), where the vanes kill sound and nothing is heard until it is close.

tables.name: Crossing Ambience - The Channel Expanse
tables.note: Atmosphere for the long crossing (5.5) - roll as often as the silence needs breaking. No mechanics.

entries.text: Salt crust crunches underfoot for a hundred yards, then smooth stone again.
A cold current of air sighs down the lane between two vanes and is gone.
Your light crosses a drift of sand rippled like a tide went out of it an age ago.
A sound arrives flat and directionless - one knock, stone on stone. It does not repeat.
A barrel stave stands upright in the silt like a grave marker.
The next vane's salt line sits exactly at the height of your throat.
Somebody's step lands wrong - the floor dips a hand's width, a shallow scoured bowl.
For a dozen steps the silence is so complete you can hear your own pulse.
A smell moves through - brine and something faintly rotten - and moves on.
Far off, a pale smear at the edge of darkvision: just another vane. Probably.

tables.name: Debris Pockets - The Channel Expanse
tables.note: Odds and ends in the sand and silt (5.5) - trinket-grade unless noted. DC 10 Investigation to find anything at all.

entries.text: Nothing but pebbles and pottery shards.
A rusted iron barrel hoop and a fistful of square-cut nails.
A salt-crusted dwarven chisel, the maker's mark still legible - old Imperial work.
A child's wooden top, paint long gone. It still spins true.
A shipping tally on a lead tag: '14 casks - GATE PORT - paid.' A Thieves' Cant reader notes the tally hand matches the manifest's.
A boot. Just the one. Dwarven-sized, sole worn through.
Three greenish copper coins of a mint nobody recognizes - a collector in the Twins would pay 5 gp each.
A small oilskin pouch, sealed: a dry tinder kit and a stub of chalk - somebody's crossing kit, never reclaimed.

scenes.title: Banminster Co.
scenes.boxedText: The southern docks looked small from the river; up close they are merely quiet. At the Banminster Co. holding warehouse, a halfling in a worker's smock looks your party over and says, as if remarking on the weather: 'The flying fish is striped and blue.'

rows.name: Phrase
rows.note: 'The flying fish is striped and blue.'

rows.name: Response
rows.note: 'Why wear a vest when that coat comes with no arms?'

rows.name: Confirmation
rows.note: 'The coat of arms is green with a field of stars.'

blocks.title: HALWRICK TWILIGHTCHEEKS
blocks.sub: halfling, he/him, 86 - the contact; he does not want to give his name, though he will if the party insists
lines: He leads them through a side door, down a hallway to the left, into a room roughly thirty feet square: a basin at the back fed by pipes of brackish water draining through a floor grate, and in the corner a large wood-and-iron cage.
He slides the door, steps in, beckons: 'Keep your fingers in if you want to keep 'em!'
The descent is smooth and LONG - one minute, another, another, most of a fourth: 380 feet.

blocks.text: His parting words at the bottom: 'The exit phrase is: This grave is too deep for my still-warm blood. Good luck on your journey. Be on your guard - those you are affiliated with are not the only ones who use these tunnels.'

scenes.mechanics: If the party botched the pass phrase, Halwrick simply is not there, and the guild's price for a second appointment includes a favor. Do not soften this; phrases exist because the tunnels have other users.

script.text: At the warehouse door, the smock and the weather-flat voice - push it.

Run the exchange verbatim: phrase, response, confirmation. If the party botched the phrase, Halwrick simply is not there, and the second appointment costs a favor. Do not soften it - phrases exist because these tunnels have other users.
The cage: 'Keep your fingers in if you want to keep 'em!' The descent is smooth and LONG - most of four minutes, 380 feet. Count it out loud.
His parting words at the bottom: the exit phrase - 'This grave is too deep for my still-warm blood' - and the warning. Make them repeat the phrase back.

time.label: The descent begins the next morning

scenes.mechanics: Dole out one instruction per commitment and make the mapper at the table earn their keep. The bridge d20 is rolled per crossing, per bridge - a broken bridge is a DC 12 DEX save (half the span drops; 20 feet, 2d6 bludgeoning, and a wet, echoing climb back). The waterfall stairs are exactly what they sound like: slick, loud, and beautiful in torchlight.
