scenes.title: Junction Rooms and Side Doors

lines: Off the route, doors - every one somebody's storage on the thieves' road. An UNLOCKED door: roll Side Rooms (Unlocked), d4, and drill into the contents tables as found.
A LOCKED door: picks at DC 15 unless the registry says otherwise, then roll Side Rooms (Locked), d6 - the better containers live behind locks.

blocks.title: POOL OF POISON
blocks.sub: the junction room (19) - place by hand
lines: Harvest either way: fill a vessel (a vial's worth per dip), or dip a blade or up to 3 pieces of ammunition straight in the pool.
One application coats a blade for 1 strike, or 3 pieces of ammunition. The coating loses its potency after 1 minute.
Any creature the poison gets into - struck by a coated weapon, cut, or drinking it - makes a DC 10 Constitution save or takes 1d4 poison damage.

blocks.title: ROOM 22 - THE POTATO ROOM
blocks.sub: side quest hook - In the Wake of the Whispered Paladin
lines: A chamber with a single word written in a dozen scripts - Sylvan and Draconic on the floor; Celestial, Infernal, Goblin, Abyssal, Giant, Druidic, Elvish, Thieves' Cant, Gnomish, Dwarvish, and Primordial across the ceiling. Every one of them says: potato. No one knows why.

This is the lair of a scorned devotee - a fanatic certain the potato god slighted him and passed him over for a champion he despises: the Whispered Potato Paladin. He is out chasing the paladin now, as always; as always, he is days behind. The room stands empty.

DC 25 Investigation finds a loose brick - wall or floor, DM's pick - hiding a cache of notes: rants on the paladin's maddening elusiveness, every page ending the same way. If only I could catch him, I could exact some of my revenge!

blocks.text: It is load-bearing whimsy; keep it.

blocks.title: LOCKED SIDE DOORS - THE KEYRING
blocks.sub: generated from the chapter's room registry - picks at DC 15 unless a room says otherwise; the roll button fires the right Side Rooms table for that door

scenes.mechanics: Time pressure is the counterweight to greed: every door searched is another luck check on the tunnels' other users - a patrol of 4 Dark Star Cutthroats (Appendix A) on a 1-4 on a d20 per hour spent looting.

script.text: Doors off the route are optional greed with real rewards: pick a door on the Keyring below - its roll button fires the right Side Rooms table for the door; picks at DC 15 unless the registry says otherwise.

Place two by hand: the POOL OF POISON (DC 10 Con save or 1d4 poison - one dip coats a blade for 1 strike or 3 pieces of ammunition, potency fades in 1 minute), and Room 22 - the POTATO ROOM, one word in a dozen scripts over a scorned devotee's empty lair (DC 25 Investigation finds his revenge notes). It is load-bearing whimsy; keep it.
The counterweight to greed is time: every hour spent looting, 1-4 on a d20 brings a patrol of four Dark Star Cutthroats. Track light sources; let them hear everything before they see it.

scenes.title: The Four-Locked Door
scenes.boxedText: A metal door, watertight at its threshold, wearing four heavy locks in a vertical line - and etched around its frame, glyphs that read as warnings in any language you check.

lines: The party cannot and should not open this yet. Locks 1 and 3: DC 26 to unlock, untrapped. Locks 2 and 4: trapped (DC 27 to disarm), DC 26-27 to unlock. At 5th level those numbers are a message, not a challenge. It becomes the party's obsession in Chapter 7, where a hired master picks it - and what waits behind it (scene 7.6) is worth the wait.

blocks.text: WHERE IT STANDS — the head of corridor 3, the basin room's south door. Behind it: the junction hall (4), the torch store (5), both tablet rooms (13, 15), the pillared hall (17), and the grand ritual chamber (11). Chapter 7 business, every square of it.

scenes.development: Let it loom. Answer no questions. Move on.

script.text: Push the door and read the glyph line slowly.
The numbers are a message, not a challenge: DC 26-27 across four locks, two trapped. At 5th level, the door is telling them 'not yet.'
Let it loom. Answer no questions. Move on - it becomes their obsession in Chapter 7, and what waits behind it is worth the wait.

sq.label: What Rises on a New Day

scenes.title: The Channel Expanse

blocks.title: THE EXPANSE
lines: Roughly 2.5 miles wall to wall and 15 miles end to end. Three doors punctuate each side wall at the same intervals as the bridges above, plus a lock at either end.

The vanes: rough-hewn stone walls thirty feet tall, ten thick, forty to eighty long - tapered to points at both ends and along the crest, so nothing can perch or stand on them. To the party they read as walls in the dark; in truth they run lengthwise with the flow, patterned to speed a flood from lock to lock. With both locks open, this whole chamber drowns.
Dead acoustics: the pattern that smooths the flood smooths sound the same way - no echo, and noise dies fast. That is why the patrol can close unheard (see the battle).

No running water is seen or heard before the far stretch: the floor is damp at most. The fast channel enters the scene only past the battleground and the grade shift - 40 feet across in a 20-foot depression, quick enough to sweep a wader; walking miles south-east to the head of the waters is a legitimate dry solution.

rows.result: (or DC 15 active, traveling alert) hear the patrol before it closes - hushed barking carried flat and low between the vanes. Fail, and the dretches open with surprise.
salt-water marks ring the vanes at one height - a waterline; these channel vast floods through this space. The dwarves built a cavern that breathes.
where the ground grade shifts near the far end: the fresh teleportation point that delivered the fiends - the campaign's third circle.
to resist the fast channel's sweep (post-battle, past the grade shift - water enters the scene only here).

blocks.title: THE VANES - FIGHTING AND CLIMBING
lines: Walls, funnels, and blinds - never platforms. The taper leaves no purchase: DC 12 Athletics scrambles up an end-slope, but there is nowhere to stand at the top, and anything that tries slides off.
Cover: a vane is total cover to anything on the far side; the open lanes between them are the vrocks' killing ground.
Reading the stone: the salt lines ring every vane at the same height. Let a sharp player do the waterline math before the Investigation check hands it over.

blocks.title: ABYSSAL EARS
lines: The dretches hate their orders - 'Always pushed around. Scout over there. Find them. Always orders. I HATE orders!' An Abyssal speaker can work that.

Bait or stall (Abyssal only): a successful DC 12 Charisma (Deception or Persuasion) - commiserate, contradict their orders, claim their handler is dead - delays the vrocks' dive by +1d4 rounds, or splits the dretches: half spend their first round arguing instead of fighting.
Lines to feed a player: 'Who orders you?' / 'The one who orders you is not coming.' / 'Scout somewhere else. You never found us.'
They are still demons: nothing turns them friendly, and 'Found them! Come, come!' ends the parley the moment blood is drawn.

blocks.text: The long walk: the Crossing Ambience table (d10) and Debris Pockets (d8) live in this chapter's roll tables - ambience as often as the silence needs breaking, debris for anyone who digs (DC 10 Investigation to find anything at all).

battle.name: The Demon Patrol
battle.setup: A quarter of the way across: four squat, pale, varicose-veined creatures bickering in Abyssal - 'Always pushed around. Scout over there. Find them. Always orders. I HATE orders!' The vanes kill sound both ways: passive Perception 15 (or DC 15 active) hears them first; fail, and the dretches close with surprise. An Abyssal speaker has an angle - see ABYSSAL EARS. On engagement they scream 'Found them! Come, come!' - and the dark answers.

combatants.name: Dretch
combatants.note: The bait and the noise. Fetid Cloud early, then cower behind it.

combatants.name: Vrock
combatants.note: Dive from the dark 1d4+1 rounds after the dretches scream. Stunning Screech on the clumped.

combatants.name: Hezrou
combatants.note: Ambles in on all fours 1d4+2 rounds after the vrocks, and stands: eight feet of toad-shaped stench.

battle.tactics: The vrocks own the vertical and punish anyone caught in the open lanes between vanes - the tapered crests hold no perch, for them or for you; the hezrou walks straight up the middle trusting its stench to break formations. None of them retreat - demons on this plane have nowhere to go.
battle.adjusting: Weaker party: 1 vrock, and the hezrou arrives only if the fight is going too easily. Stronger party: 6 dretches and both vrocks open with a coordinated screech.
battle.aftermath: Harvest for the bold: ichor vials, ten spines, a claw, and the hezrou's heart - store that heart somewhere; a certain sarcophagus in Chapter 7 gives it meaning if you wish. The first crew won this fight with ground spikes and forced movement, grinding the hezrou at range - honor clever terrain play; the vanes are cover and funnels - walls to fight along, never platforms to hold.

scenes.development: Across the water, through the far Gate Port Door, the manifest's tail plays out: right, left, left door across a basin, double doors... and a corridor ending at a door lined in lead. Chapter 6 begins there. (DM note: the manifest's promised EXIT SHAFT beyond is caved in - the party should not learn this here; they discover it in 6.1 when they walk the manifest's tail and the rubble turns them back.)

script.text: The last corridor opens into nothing - push the Expanse and sell the scale: 2.5 miles wall to wall, 15 end to end, tapered vanes reading as walls in the dark. Damp stone and drifts of debris - no running water anywhere, and no echo: this room eats sound. (DC 18 Investigation on the vanes: salt-water marks - the dwarves built a chamber that floods.)
As they commit to the crossing, push Into the Dark - then let the Crossing Ambience table (d10, chapter roll tables) carry the miles. Debris Pockets (d8) rewards anyone who digs.

A quarter of the way across: passive Perception 15 (or DC 15 active) hears the patrol first; fail, and the dretches open with surprise - the vanes kill sound both ways. An Abyssal speaker can work their resentment (ABYSSAL EARS) before 'Found them! Come, come!' ends it. Roll initiative.

Run the fight on the terrain (battle block): the vanes are cover and funnels, never platforms - the tapered crests hold no perch; the vrocks own the vertical over the open lanes; the hezrou walks the middle trusting its stench. None of them retreat.

Past the battleground, the ground grade shifts steeper - noticeable, easily walkable. DC 15 Perception where it starts: the fresh teleportation point that delivered the fiends, the campaign's third circle.

Only now does water enter the scene: the rush of it, heard again at last - the fast channel, 40 feet across in a 20-foot depression. DC 10 Athletics to resist the sweep, or the legitimate dry walk miles south-east to the head of the waters. Beyond the far door the manifest's tail plays out to a corridor ending at a door lined in lead.

boxed.title: The Expanse
boxed.text: The passage ends and the world simply stops. Your light finds a smooth stone floor running out of reach in every direction, and above - nothing; the ceiling is somewhere the dark keeps to itself. Behind you the wall runs away left and right until it, too, is gone. The air hangs still and damp, tasting faintly of old salt. Drifts of debris scatter the floor: staved barrels, broken boxes, patches of sand and silt, pebbles, half-buried odds and ends. And out in the black your light catches the edge of something immense - a wall of rough-hewn stone, drawn to a point along its crest, running lengthwise into the dark. Beyond it, another. The silence is total; even your footsteps seem to die at your boots.

boxed.title: Into the Dark
boxed.text: The crossing swallows hours. Your circle of light stays the same size while everything inside it repeats - silt, pebbles, a barrel stave, the flank of another vane sliding past like the hull of a sunken ship. Sound refuses to carry: a word spoken here falls flat and is gone. The dark ahead never gets closer, and the dark behind never lets go.

chapters.chapterDevelopment: Milestone: the party reaches 6th level after the Expanse. They now know demons walk beneath the Twins, someone teleported them here, and a lead-lined door stands between them and whatever the fiends were guarding.

chapters.title: The Battle for Oospufmorn
chapters.overview: Behind a lead-lined door, a basin of impossibly still water hides the root of a god-tree. The climb inside it ends on grass in the middle of Yuvl Ilmern - inside a barrier the city cannot see - where signs of battle mark the trunk stair, and at the platform a pitch-black glabrezu and a boring-swarm mage are minutes from the heart. The party fights magnificently, and loses anyway. In-world: roughly two days, hard on the heels of the crossing.
chapters.running: Read the Tone & Safety page's advisory before running this chapter: the heart's loss is SCRIPTED, and your table consented to that at session zero - your job now is to make the fight feel winnable anyway. Every round the party delays the mage is real; every follower dropped is real; the extraction clock is simply shorter than their best. Do not fudge toward false hope and do not rush the loss - run the clock honestly and let the table's fury arrive on its own. The message from the Empress afterward is the pressure release: someone in authority says out loud that it was not their fault.

scenes.title: The Basin Room
scenes.body: The corridor door is lead-lined (DC 10 Investigation for anyone proficient to notice) and locked with a simple loop-and-padlock: DC 20 to pick, or AC 19 and 5 HP to break. Inside: a large inlaid floor basin of clear, potable, unnaturally STILL water.

rows.result: an overwhelming aura floods the basin - abjuration layered over illusion, centered on the water and the etched circle. This is a MAINTAINED ward, not a permanent enchantment: it can be dispelled or suppressed. Say that plainly if they cast it - this is the telegraph.
the water is deep with no visible bottom; faint lines are etched into the wall all the way around.
a ritual circle unlike anything studied, though hints echo other work.
fail - you simply do NOT want to jump in that pool; save - you briefly see a shimmering barrier around the basin, the pool seems to vanish, and something like rough wood waits beyond.

blocks.title: DISPEL MAGIC drops it properly
lines: The shimmer manifests and fades, the water is gone, and before you a giant gnarled root breaches the ceiling and dives into the depths - light above and below, runes (Druidic, Arcane, and Religious) glowing around the walls a few feet down.
A large hole has been HEWN into the root - rotting AND burnt, and now that you see it, the smell arrives.
Push 'The Root Revealed' the moment the veil drops - however they dropped it.

blocks.title: IF NO ONE HAS DISPEL MAGIC
lines: TRACE THE CIRCLE - a character proficient in Arcana, Religion, or Nature can spend 10 minutes working the etched lines around the wall. DC 15 suppresses the barrier for the same one-minute window before the runes reassert.

COMMUNION - a character who meditates in the tree's presence (a short rest or longer spent quietly in this room) may retry the DC 25 Wisdom save with advantage: the reluctance fades the longer they sit with Oospufmorn. On a success while touching the water's surface, the veil parts for one minute - the tree knows its own.

FAILSAFE - if the party takes a long rest here, the veil parts on its own as they wake. The pull is preordained; the Champions were always meant to pass. Do not gate the campaign's pivot behind a spell slot.

blocks.text: RESET: if the hole is not entered, after one minute the water begins rising and the barrier re-opaques; the reset completes in a second minute.

blocks.title: THE ROUTE TAIL - PAST THE BASIN
blocks.sub: keyed to the vault-leg survey - the manifest's last four lines
items: Left door, across the basin, through the corridor - the north door, 7 into 8.
Double doors - west into the torch hall (9).
The alcove (10) - the Exit Shaft: the ladder that should run 380 ft up to Yuvl Ilmern.
Caved in. Floor to ceiling, no gap, no draft. The manifest's last word is a dead end.

rows.result: the collapse is total - not a squeeze-through, not an afternoon's dig. Clearing it is crew-scale work: weeks of labor and gear the party is not carrying. Say nothing of cause - the record doesn't, yet; a crew will be at it come Chapter 7.

blocks.text: THE FUNNEL: a party that follows the manifest as given WILL walk the tail and find the cave-in - that is the design, not a failure state. They come back to the basin with nowhere else to go. That is not a dead end; that is the tree's pull. The room's presence makes it a natural rest site - the party will WANT to camp in this warmth. Let them: every hour spent here feeds the Communion and Failsafe rungs above.

script.text: Before this chapter, reread the Tone & Safety advisory: the heart's loss is SCRIPTED and consented to. Your job is to make the fight feel winnable anyway.
The lead-lined door (DC 10 to notice for the proficient; DC 20 pick, or AC 19 / 5 HP): inside, the basin - push it as the presence hits them.
Run the layers (Mechanics): Detect Magic telegraphs a maintained, dispellable ward; DC 15 the still deep water; DC 18 the unfamiliar ritual circle; the DC 25 jump-in save.

The manifest points them straight past the basin - let them follow it. Walk the tail (Mechanics): the corridor, the double doors, the torch hall - and at the alcove, push the discovery. DC 12 Investigation confirms the collapse is total and crew-scale; say nothing of cause. Then let the walk back land: the only warmth in the dark is the room they left. The pull is honest.
Dispel Magic drops it properly - but if no one has it, work the contingency ladder: trace the circle, communion, or the long-rest failsafe. The veil WILL part; only the route to it varies.
The moment it drops - by spell, ritual, or the tree's own hand - push the reveal. This is the pivot of the campaign: let the room go quiet before you read it.
Watch the reset: one minute of rising water, sealed in the second. Commit or start over.

boxed.title: The Basin Room
boxed.text: The rushing feeling hits you before the door is fully open: the same presence from the mind's-eye tour those days ago - the warmth of a gentle embrace, the certainty of standing WITH Oospufmorn. You can still feel the other trees' directions. But this one is here. The room beyond is lead-lined floor to ceiling - the door was only the first hint - and set into the floor is a large inlaid basin of clear water. It is deep. It is drinkable. And it is STILL - too still. Drop something in and the surface swallows the ripples almost before they form, settling back to glass while you watch.

boxed.title: The Root Revealed
boxed.text: A shimmering barrier flashes into being where the water was - and fades. The pool is gone. The ceiling above it is gone. Before you, a giant gnarled root breaches from above and dives deep into the basin below, filling most of the shaft but not all of it - there is light from above and light from below. Runes - Druidic, Arcane, and Religious intertwined - glow along the walls a few feet down from the surface. And there, hewn into the root's flank, a large hole - the wood around it rotting AND burnt. Now that you see it, the smell arrives, and it does not please the senses.

boxed.title: The Caved-In Shaft
boxed.text: The manifest keeps its word, right up until it doesn't. Through the far door the corridor runs true; the double doors give onto a long hall with cold torch brackets down both walls; and at its end, the alcove - the Exit Shaft, the last line on the list, the ladder that should carry you 380 feet up to open air. What waits there instead is stone. The shaft is choked floor to ceiling with collapsed rock, grit sifting between the slabs when you disturb them, the ladder's lowest rungs vanishing into the rubble. There is no gap to squeeze through, no draft to follow. The way out is not out. Behind you, back down the hall and across the basin, the warmth of the room you left is the only thing in the dark still saying yes.

scenes.title: The Climb
scenes.body: Inside the hole, a rope ladder pinned to the wall, each rung about a foot apart, its top lost in darkness. Tedious more than hard - until just past 100 feet, where the ladder's abrupt end curls over an edge some 60 feet above: DC 10 Constitution save or lose grip. Past the landing, a steep walkable slope winds like a spiral staircase without stairs, rot-smoothed underfoot, the burnt smell constant - then a dim light, a corner, a bright exit.
scenes.boxedText: You step out onto grass. Behind and above you, Oospufmorn stands tall and grand - and something else catches your eye: a huge rune circle surrounds the tree as far as you can see, and a shimmering wall rises twenty feet out, spanning up to the foliage itself. Beyond the wall: the city of Yuvl Ilmern, going about its day. A citizen strolls toward the barrier to your left - touches it - and is simply WALKING AWAY on the far side of the circle, at the same angle, none the wiser.
scenes.mechanics: Any attempt to push out through the barrier meets what feels like a stone wall a hundred feet thick. The party is inside with the tree - and with whatever came before them.

script.text: They step out onto grass inside the rune wall - push the climb's arrival and the barrier.
Let the citizen land: strolls to the barrier, touches it, and is simply WALKING AWAY on the far side, none the wiser.
The ladder in the hole: a foot a rung, its top lost in dark - and just past 100 feet the abrupt curl, DC 10 CON or lose grip. Then the rot-smoothed spiral, and a bright exit.
Any push outward through the barrier meets stone a hundred feet thick. They are inside with the tree - and with whatever came before them.

scenes.title: Signs of Battle
scenes.body: Ascending the trunk stair: scorch and slash marks, fallen arrows, arrows still standing in the wood - old enough to be cold, recent enough to hurry the feet. At three-quarters height, enemy scouts spot the party and sprint upward, shouting the alarm.

battle.name: Race up the Spiral
battle.setup: A running fight on a stair five feet wide with no rail on the outside. The scouts' job is not to win - it is to be loud and die slowly.

combatants.name: Scout
combatants.note: Fire and fall back, always upward. Their warning WILL reach the platform; the question is how much of the mage's clock it buys.

battle.tactics: Fliers can bypass the stair entirely and ferry the slow - hammer-and-anvil vertically. Every round saved here is a round of the extraction clock in 6.4.
battle.adjusting: Weaker party: 2 scouts. Stronger party: 4, and one carries a horn that starts the platform's preparations a round early.
battle.aftermath: Speed matters and the party should feel it in their lungs. Straight into 6.4 - no rest, no regroup.

script.text: Ascending the trunk stair: scorch, slash, arrows cold enough to be old and recent enough to hurry the feet.
At three-quarters height, scouts spot them and sprint upward, shouting the alarm. Roll initiative - a running fight on a stair five feet wide with no outside rail.
The scouts' job is not to win; it is to be loud and die slowly. Fliers can bypass and ferry - hammer-and-anvil vertically. Every round saved here is a round of 6.4's clock.
Straight into 6.4. No rest, no regroup - the party should feel it in their lungs.

scenes.title: The Platform

battle.name: The Heart of Oospufmorn
battle.setup: The mage (Heartbore Mage - use the Mage stat block) concentrates to keep the Heartbore Swarm on task rather than wandering to its preferred food. THE CLOCK: once the party reaches the platform, the mage needs two successful rounds to reach the heart and a third to extract it and hand it to the glabrezu - then both teleport out at the first opportunity via the circle etched beside the bore. Breaking the mage's concentration resets his current round; it does not stop the followers from buying him new ones. PLACEMENT: the bore - and the mage at it - sits on the FAR face of the trunk from the stair's arrival edge; neither is visible until someone moves around the trunk far enough for line of sight.

combatants.name: Glabrezu
combatants.note: Pitch-black, coldly intelligent. Fights to protect the mage's clock, not to kill - power word stun on the party's best interrupter.

combatants.name: Heartbore Mage
combatants.note: Concentration on the swarm; shield and counterspell guard his own clock. See Appendix A: Heartbore Swarm for what he commands.

combatants.name: Heartbore Swarm
combatants.note: Roach-sized, toothy maws: 2 damage per turn to any organic surface it occupies, automatically, while directed.

combatants.name: Cultist
combatants.note: Followers of Essax; they fight to the death as bought time.

combatants.name: Cult Fanatic
combatants.note: Hold person and spiritual weapon aimed at whoever threatens the mage.

battle.tactics: Everything serves the clock. The glabrezu bodies the strongest melee, the fanatics lock down interrupters, the cultists throw themselves between spells and the mage. When the heart comes free, demon and mage step to the circle and are gone - and REMEMBER: anyone standing in the circle when it fires goes along. A player may take that ride. Let them; it is a magnificent, terrible choice - and Contingency C3 (The Ride Taken) solves it generously.
battle.adjusting: Weaker party: 4 cultists, 1 fanatic, and the extraction takes four rounds. Stronger party: the glabrezu opens with confusion into the party's stack, and a second swarm peels off to harass.
battle.aftermath: The followers are corpses; the platform is theirs; the heart is not. Perception DC 10 finds no entry-circle scorch (they did not teleport IN - file that) and no Defender bodies anywhere. Investigation DC 15: 220 gold in the followers' purses. DC 20: each corpse bears a tattoo at the base of the neck running the length of the spine. History on the tattoo - DC 28: it matches a drawing in an ancient, crumbling book, captioned WAND OF KELETHTONRETH. DC 29: Kelethtonreth - goat-legged, ram-horned, bloated, bat-winged; cared for nothing save himself; his wand a skull-topped artifact with the power to slay any living being; his realm DEMONHOLME, frigid, frozen, infested with the undead. Speak with Dead on a follower can additionally reveal where the bore-side circle leads - the answer bank in this scene's mechanics has their voices.

scenes.treasure: 220 gp; the tattoo lore above; and a permanent teleportation circle the party does not yet understand (Chapter 7 teaches it).

script.text: The platform - push it, and start the clock the moment the party arrives: the mage needs two successful rounds to reach the heart, a third to extract and hand it over.

The bore is on the far face of the trunk - invisible from the arrival edge. The moment any party member moves around the trunk far enough for line of sight, push the reveal: the mage and the Heartbore Swarm, the clock made visible. The clock itself starts on arrival regardless - the reveal is discovery, not the timer.
Breaking his concentration resets his CURRENT round only; the followers exist to buy him new ones. The glabrezu bodies the strongest melee; everything serves the clock.

When the heart comes free: demon and mage step to the circle and are gone - and anyone standing in that circle when it fires goes along. A player may take that ride. Let them; it is a magnificent, terrible choice - Contingency C3, The Ride Taken, is the whole road.
Run the clock honestly. Do not fudge toward false hope; do not rush the loss. The table's fury should arrive on its own.

Aftermath forensics: DC 10 - no entry-circle scorch (file that) and no Defender bodies anywhere. DC 15 - the purses. DC 20 - the spine tattoos; the History ladder at 28/29 reaches WAND OF KELETHTONRETH and DEMONHOLME.
Speak with Dead: the followers answer in two voices - the zealot and the spent - and the circle question earns the Master's garden. The full answer bank is in this scene's mechanics.

boxed.title: The Platform
boxed.text: Heavy resistance holds the platform - spellcasters and armed followers of Essax, and not one Defender of the tree to be seen. At their head: a pitch-black demon, fifteen feet of broad muscle, purple piercing eyes cold with intelligence, two pairs of arms - great pincers above, clawed humanoid hands at the stomach - and goat horns crowning a canine head.

boxed.title: The Heartbore
boxed.text: You round the trunk and the sound reaches you before the sight does - a dry, chittering hiss, like fire eating wet paper. A mage stands rapt before a hole bored into Oospufmorn's trunk, hands weaving, lips moving without pause - and the hole is MOVING: a swarm of fiery-necrotic insects, roach-sized and toothy, ember-light crawling through blackened rot, eating toward the heart. The mage does not turn. Whatever holds his attention holds all of it.

blocks.title: SPEAK WITH DEAD - THE FOLLOWERS ANSWER
blocks.sub: five questions, ten minutes - brief, cryptic, and the dead do not stop believing
lines: The corpse knows only what it knew in life, and the spell compels brevity, not honesty - but fanatics do not lie about glory. They brag. Answer in fragments; make the table work the follow-up questions.

Two voices among the dead, and repeat castings should find both: the ZEALOT (rapturous, present tense, as if the cause were still winning) and the SPENT (flat, bitter - they knew exactly what their lives were bought for).
The answer bank below covers the questions tables actually ask. Anything off the bank: the followers were fodder - logistics, names, and the ritual's mechanics were never spent on them.

blocks.title: WHAT THE DEAD KNOW
blocks.sub: answers by question - hand the table fragments, not paragraphs

rows.name: Who sent you?
rows.note: "The Master. He was touched, as we are touched." (A hand would drift to the spine tattoo, if the dead could move.) The spent version: "A man who pays in promises. We were the small coin."

rows.name: Where does the circle lead?
rows.meta: THE REVEAL - both voices give it
rows.note: "To the Master's garden. Where the stolen green grows, behind walls no map holds." DM: this is the circle's blank DEFAULT destination - the walled glade and the cutting of Oospufmorn. Chapter 7 teaches the circle; Chapter 8 opens that door. This answer may accelerate both - let it. The party earning the destination early is the spell working as intended.

rows.name: Where is the heart going? What is it for?
rows.note: "To the working. Three will sing, the door will open, and The One will come through cold." They know the heart is an ANCHOR and that three suffice; they do not know where the working happens or when.

rows.name: Who was the demon?
rows.note: "It has a name. It never spent it on us." Nothing more - the glabrezu did not speak to fodder.

rows.name: Why fight to the death?
rows.note: Zealot: "Bought time is holy time." Spent: "Because the ones worth following had already left."

blocks.text: If a champion stood in the circle when it fired: Contingency C3 - The Ride Taken - is the whole road, all three tracks. The garden the dead describe is where the rider landed.

scenes.title: The Wilting
scenes.boxedText: The foliage turns from bright green to deep red. Leaves loose from the boughs and float down, gently, to their resting places in the streets of Yuvl Ilmern. Below, the magic that hid the sacred tree fails - and two cities look up at once.
scenes.body: With the heart gone, the concealment dies. Some below stand in awe, some in pandemonium; Council Guard rush the tree's base to staunch the flow of people. A sending from the Empress reaches the party's leader - run the exchange below in order: her question, the leader's reply composed live, then her answer. And the far exit shaft, when checked, is caved in - rigged. The way they came is the way back, and the city has found the tree.
scenes.development: By the time the party reaches the ground, the Captain of the Guard is waiting. Chapter 7 begins mid-stride.

script.text: The heart is gone and the concealment dies with it - push the wilting.
Two cities look up at once: awe, pandemonium, Council Guard rushing the base to staunch the flow of people.
Run the sending exchange in order: the Empress's 25-word question, the leader's live 25-word reply, then 'Dire news' as the answer - it lands only after their report.
The far exit shaft is caved in - rigged. The way they came is the way back, and by the time they reach the grass, the Captain of the Guard is waiting. Chapter 7 begins mid-stride.

time.label: The fight crosses into dawn

blocks.title: SENDING I - THE QUESTION
blocks.sub: the Empress, to the party's leader - DM's choice, whoever has emerged as leader in play. Exactly 25 words: she spent the spell's whole cap.
lines: "What's happened? Our wizards informed me of tragedy at Oospufmorn. Our scrying can now penetrate the magic and we see the wilting over the Twins."

blocks.text: THE REPLY - sending grants the recipient 25 words back. Make the leader compose it live at the table; count the words. What they choose to fit into 25 is the scene.

blocks.title: SENDING II - THE ANSWER
blocks.sub: cast only after she hears the reply - never deliver it first; it responds to their report
lines: "Dire news - come home with haste to regroup. This is more dire than we could have believed."

blocks.text: 'More dire than WE could have believed' - the crown misjudged, not the party. Someone in authority saying out loud that it was not their fault is the chapter's pressure release.

chapters.chapterDevelopment: Milestone: 7th level. Heartbreak beats worth engineering: a flier stunned at height and caught one-handed at the railing; the party's melee ace dropping unconscious at the mage's feet as the heart comes free. The loss is scripted; the grief should be earned.

chapters.title: Champions Adrift
chapters.overview: Aftermath as adventure: a gruff captain with hard questions, the Council of Twelve with the Empress already in the room, a gifted mansion with too many basements, eight open mysteries handed to the table - and behind a four-locked door, a chained sarcophagus that promises healing and warns of madness. The campaign's downtime hub: let it breathe as long as the table is having fun. In-world: about eight days of downtime, counted scene by scene at the table.
chapters.running: Structure disappears here on purpose. Scenes 7.1-7.3 are fixed (the institutional response); everything after runs on player initiative against the Eight Mysteries list - hand it over as a physical thing and follow their finger. The original DM closed this arc by asking the table a straight question, and it worked; it is reprinted in 7.3. Whatever identity the party builds in this chapter - a healing house, a company, a name - fund it, staff it, and remember it: the endgame will threaten what they love, and this chapter is where they decide what that is. A recurring nightmare also begins in this downtime: seed scene 7.7 (The Recurring Dream) on the party's first real rest and let it repeat - it is the setup that scene 9.1 pays off, and it must land on the same champion (preferably the Sword of the Palace - see Session Zero 0.5 and the binding, 1.3).

scenes.title: The Captain

boxed.title: The Captain
boxed.text: Far below, Council Guard flood the grass and a cordon locks around the trunk of the tree. One figure detaches from it and starts up the stair alone - and anyone of you at the rail can watch the whole climb: formal, unhurried, taking the steps like a parade ground. A dozen steps shy of the top he halts, and his voice arrives before he does - projected like a man used to being heard across a deck: "Maros Softblossom - Captain of the Guard. I come under the authority of the Council of Twelve." Then he takes the final stair onto the platform: a halfling in a captain's harness, built like a keg, weathered like a hull, looking at your party the way a man looks at a problem he intends to solve before dinner.

boxed.title: The Long Walk
boxed.text: The stair takes longer going down. At the base the cordon opens a corridor through the crowd - and the crowd is a city still looking up, pressed against the guard line, staring at a tree that was not there yesterday. The escort walks you north through Yuvl Ilmern the whole way: streets gone quiet where people stand in doorways with their heads tipped back, knots of pandemonium the guard is still untangling, and behind you, always, the red canopy shedding its leaves. At the northern tip the Palace of the Council of Twelve opens its doors before you reach them - into an antechamber, and a wait, while somewhere beyond the far doors twelve chairs fill one by one.

blocks.text: Maros Softblossom, Captain of the Guard (halfling, he/him, 129) - gruff despite two centuries of general peace, because he earned the gruffness elsewhere: a sellsword for a time on a ship that crossed the ocean, and in those lands to the west. He climbs to the platform alone and announces himself before the final stair - formal, unmistakable, witnessed by anyone at the rail. Below him, his platoon secures the perimeter and starts the inspection climb: thirty minutes of wary, inch-by-inch ascent, and that climb is the scene's time gauge. Two windows, plainly: anything the party wants done unobserved must happen before Maros crests; anything they want done un-inventoried must happen before the platoon tops the stair.
Once Maros is on the platform he refuses the party nothing - cast, dig, search, argue - but he clocks every bit of it, and the platoon arriving behind him is an inspection squad.

blocks.title: THE CAPTAIN'S QUESTIONS
blocks.sub: asked in order, in his own time - he waits out silences longer than most people can stand
lines: "What happened here?" - he asks it looking at the dead guardians, not at the party.
"Who did this - and where did they go?" - the trunk is bored, the heart is gone, and none of the dead are the ones who did it.
"Who are you, and by whose leave were you on this platform?" - the true answer names the Empress's charge, and his posture shifts a degree when it does.
"What is wrong with the tree?" - the question he is actually carrying for the Council; he asks it quieter than the others.
"Is anything up here going to hurt my people when they crest that stair?" - the platoon is mid-climb, and he watches their eyes as they answer.

blocks.title: THE LADDER
blocks.sub: silent DM tally - one mark per question
items: Plain truth: +1, no roll. Truth spoken plainly needs no check, and Maros knows it when he hears it.
Honest but hedged - true, partial, softened: DC 13 Persuasion. Success +1; failure 0 - he notes the seam without pulling at it.
Evasive or false: DC 16 Deception. Success 0 - it lands, but earns nothing; failure -1 - two centuries and a sellsword's ocean behind his eyes.
Silence or refusal: -1. He writes it down, literally, and moves to the next question.
A straight answer to his last question also stands the platoon down from inspection footing when they crest - goodwill no other answer here buys.

blocks.title: THE ESCORT
blocks.sub: pool the marks - every tier arrives at the Council
lines: +3 OR MORE - THE WARM ESCORT: Maros walks beside them and vouches at the palace doors; they arrive as witnesses, and there are seats waiting when the Council convenes.
0 TO +2 - THE FORMAL ESCORT: correct and cold; they arrive as persons of interest and wait on the benches in the antechamber - the worse seating, made literal.
NEGATIVE - THE ESCORT UNDER GUARD: the platoon forms up around them, weapons peace-bonded by request rather than seizure, and the antechamber wait is a watched one. Same doors, same Council.
Detonation at any point - grief spoken, steel drawn, or flight - is Contingency C4, The Handle Flies; every track still reconverges at the Council.

blocks.text: THE WALK - the Palace of the Council of Twelve stands at Yuvl Ilmern's northern tip; the escort is a long one, through a city that has just seen the sky change, and it ends in an antechamber and a short wait while the Council is assembled. Push The Long Walk as the party leaves the grass.

If the party works the platform (now or later), run the full forensics below. If the party detonates instead of answering - grief spoken, steel drawn, or flight - Contingency C4 (The Handle Flies) holds the line generously.

scenes.development: The antechamber wait ends and the far doors open. Scene 7.2.

rows.result: no entry-teleport scorches like previous battles; no Defender bodies at all.
a permanent teleportation circle etched beside the bore-hole under sooty, rotting sawdust; the tree-map symbol still shines with arcane light.
the circle is entwined with Religious and Druidic runes, not merely arcane.
confirms the rune-weave.
the inscriptions teach ACTIVATION: stand the inner circle, utter the incantation while tracing the runes; thereafter DC 15 Arcana to fire it, minus 1 per successful use.

blocks.title: INVESTIGATION
blocks.sub: later, on study

rows.result: the inner ring depicts all the sacred trees with Oospufmorn's position blank.
a sliding ring rotates the blank to another tree's sigil - the circle RETARGETS.

blocks.text: That discovery is Chapter 8's ignition; let it wait until the party goes looking.

script.text: The magic falls, the cordon sets below, and the Captain climbs - push him as he crests.

Maros Softblossom: gruff because he earned it elsewhere - a sellsword across the ocean once. He climbs alone and announces himself before the final stair; his platoon secures the perimeter below and starts the inspection climb - thirty minutes of wary, inch-by-inch ascent. That climb is the scene's clock: unobserved ends when Maros crests, un-inventoried ends when the platoon arrives.
Once on the platform Maros refuses the party nothing - he watches, notes, and lets them work. The platoon behind him is the deadline, not him.
Then his questions - five, in order, in the scene body - and the silent tally. Plain truth needs no roll; the pool decides the escort: warm, formal, or under guard. Every tier arrives at the Council.
If the beat detonates - grief spoken, steel drawn, or flight - Contingency C4, The Handle Flies, solves it generously; every track reconverges at the Council.

Whenever they return to the platform, run the full forensics ladder (Mechanics) - the sliding ring waits at DC 25/27 Investigation for when they go looking. It is Chapter 8's ignition; do not push it at them.
When he has his answers, the long walk - push it: down the stair, north through a staring city to the Palace at the northern tip, and a short wait in the antechamber while the Council is assembled.

scenes.title: The Council of Twelve
scenes.boxedText: The grand receiving hall of the Council of Twelve holds all twelve - and one more. At the far end, in hushed and heated conversation with the First Counsel, stands the Empress of Torrentath herself.

rows.name: First Counsel Frobyn Mossblossom
rows.note: mid-argument with the Empress

rows.name: Steward Unasica Copperglide
rows.note: found, alive, and a locked box on the subject of her missing tenday - looking worse for wear and explaining nothing

rows.result: catches Mossblossom's sterner half: '...we will talk at length of this later - we have more urgent matters to attend to'

blocks.text: The strange politics between First of Twelve and Empress, and the Steward's silence, are mysteries #6 and #6a on the list in 7.4.

blocks.title: WHAT THE COUNCIL OFFERS
lines: Transportation to the imperial capital or any of the three other capitals; requests beyond that meet hesitancy at best - the Empress has called the army to assemble for an invasion on the EASTERN border.

scenes.development: The Empress turns from the First Counsel to the party. Scene 7.3.

script.text: The receiving hall of the Twelve - push it: all twelve, and one more.
DC 15 Perception catches the First Counsel's sterner half: '...we will talk at length of this later.' File it - mysteries #6 and #6a.
The Steward: found, alive, worse for wear, and a locked box on the subject of her missing tenday. Leave it locked.
The Council offers transportation to any capital; beyond that, hesitancy - the Empress has called the army to assemble on the EASTERN border. Then she turns from the First Counsel to the party. 7.3.

scenes.title: The Empress and the Estate

lines: Give each PC one exchange; she remembers everything from Chapter 1 and proves it. (She keeps whatever the party once gave her, however absurd — a ceremonially gifted potato deserves a place of honor. Set the tone you deserve.)

blocks.text: The estate: a mansion, nearly unfurnished, a map of Arret lying haphazard on the study desk.

blocks.title: THE SEVEN DOORS
blocks.sub: bedroom picking · an RP beat, not a die roll
lines: The manor holds UP TO SEVEN bedrooms (br1–br7 on the floor plan) — the requirement is one door per party member, however many sit at the table. br7 is the room at the spiral stair.

Go around the table: each member claims a door and narrates ONE thing they do to make the room theirs — where the bed faces, what goes on the wall, what never leaves the nightstand. No mechanics; this is how a house becomes a home base.
Doors beyond the party's count stay dark and locked until claimed — or don't, if you want a mystery. Spare rooms are guest rooms, shrines, workshops, or arguments waiting to happen.
Expect the party to spread through the wings and jump straight to crafting, scrolling, and shopping — let the claiming slow that down and land the 'this is ours now' beat.

scenes.development: Close the scene the way the original DM closed the arc - pose it to the table straight: 'Essax is out there, in league with something called The One, bringing demons into your lands and killing your sacred trees. Are you loyal to the Empire, or to its people? Do you defend these lands, or do you hunt evil? Now that you're bound together: who ARE you? Our adventure truly begins. What will you do?'

script.text: Push her greeting and give each PC one exchange - she remembers everything from Chapter 1 and proves it. (She keeps whatever they once gave her, however absurd - a ceremonially gifted potato deserves a place of honor. Set the tone you deserve.)
Her word, verbatim - the holding order in the Empress's own voice. Push it and let it land before the escort moves.
Then the holding order, and the estate: Captain Softblossom escorts them to a mansion, nearly unfurnished, a map of Arret lying haphazard on the study desk. Push the walk-in and the floor plan.
The Seven Doors: up to seven bedrooms, one door per party member — each claims a room and narrates one thing that makes it theirs. Spare doors stay dark until claimed.

Close the arc the way the record did - pose it to the table straight: 'Are you loyal to the Empire, or to its people? Do you defend these lands, or do you hunt evil? Now that you're bound together: who ARE you? What will you do?'

time.label: Audiences and the estate — how many days?

boxed.title: The Empress
boxed.text: Our newest band of Champions of the Empire! Tell us of the deeds you've performed thus far on your quest. Know that the loss of the heart of Oospufmorn is a grievous blow - though not a deadly one, and not your fault. I know you fought bravely against insurmountable odds and are still able to be here with us today.

boxed.title: The New Estate
boxed.text: Captain Softblossom leads you through a gate into a front courtyard, past a coach house and a shuttered office, to doors that open on a manor that is, in truth, a mansion. Rooms unfold in every direction — a great dining and living room at its heart, a kitchen and servants' wing standing empty, covered porches wrapping toward a back courtyard, a bar with nothing on its shelves, and bedrooms enough for every one of you. Nearly all of it is bare: a few pieces of furniture scattered through the halls, dust where a household should be. In the study, lying haphazard across the desk, is a map of the continent of Arret.

boxed.title: Her Word
boxed.text: 'Know that we haven't seen any other marks of Essax on the sacred trees, as you might have noticed on Oospufmorn itself. We are investigating all means to unearth how Essax was able to gain access. Until we have more information, we would like you to hold fast in preparation of the needs of the Empire. To ease this passage of time, I have arranged a manner for you - Captain Softblossom will escort you to your new estate.'

blocks.title: WHEN TO PLAY IT
lines: Present this at the END of a session, with the party in the midst of their first real downtime. Push the questions, close the book, and let them stew until next time.

blocks.text: The eighth mystery - the rumored treasure in the middle of the Twins Channel - is WITHHELD from the player list. The rumor itself runs free on both shores (retired bridge guards tell it best), but the PRECISE SPOT is guild knowledge: the thieves guild sells it during this downtime IF the party has gained their trust (Side Quests: The Treasure of the Twins Channel).

mechanics.title: Threads that answer - this chapter's yield

rows.name: THE SHAFT
rows.note: a crew of 15 workers and a full score of sellswords ('We're paid to pay no mind... just ensure these folks get their job done'). The crew: 'Contracted by the Clearwater Co. Worst job yet - dangerous work, clearing rubble. Up in about a week.' Clearwater has warehouses all over the Twins: a standing thread to Essax's local hand - payroll, manifests, and who signs for what - yours to expand if you want it.

rows.name: THE CIRCLE
rows.note: the sliding-ring discoveries in 7.1 (DC 25/27 Investigation).

rows.name: CHAMPIONS
rows.note: DC 15 Persuasion among officials or guard captains: 'There have been several... chosen by the realm itself... old Tegen, the retired Captain of the Bridge Guard, used to speak of it.'

rows.name: THE BOND
rows.note: eyes closed, spin, point: three tugs remain, unerring.

blocks.text: The bridges question pays off in Chapter 10; the sealed door pays off in 7.6; the First-of-Twelve politics belong to the endgame. The withheld treasure thread runs through the thieves guild - the rumor is free, the precise spot is the prize (Side Quests: The Treasure of the Twins Channel).

script.text: End the session here: with the party in the midst of their first real downtime, push 'What next?:' and let them carry the questions home. Then follow their finger next time. Structure disappears here on purpose.
This chapter's yield (Mechanics): the shaft crew and the Clearwater Co. thread; the sliding ring; old Tegen's stories of earlier Champions; eyes closed, spin, point - three tugs remain.

The bridges pay off in Chapter 10; the sealed door pays off in 7.6; the First-of-Twelve politics belong to the endgame. The treasure stays off the list entirely - the rumor runs free, but the precise spot comes through the thieves guild, if trust is earned. Do not spend them early.

time.label: Downtime among the mysteries — how many days?

boxed.title: What next?:
boxed.text:
Are the bridges still shut down?

What waits behind the sealed door in the Underbelly of the Twins?

Why did the exit shaft cave in?

Where does the permanent teleportation circle on Oospufmorn's platform lead?

What passed between the First of Twelve and the Empress - and why the Steward's silent tenday?

'Newest' Champions of the Empire - there were others?

What is this bond with the trees?

scenes.title: The House Below

blocks.title: THE MANSION HAS OPINIONS
lines: Exploring the deep sub-basement finds secret doors, a cavernous chamber, an arcane-locked door (dispellable), a ladder shaft - and a room that IS an elevator: minutes of descent opening into the familiar Junction Rooms of the Underbelly. The mansion was built over the thieves' road.
Who gifted this house, again? File that thought where the party can hear it being filed.

blocks.title: THE HOUSE'S LEVELS
lines: MAIN BASEMENT — the way down hides in the two-square gap below the bar (Perception to notice the seam or draft, Investigation behind the bar - DC 13 defaults). Its north wall carries a secret door, drawn on the levels map. The room is grand enough that a dwarf might call it the finest bedroom in the house.

SMALL BASEMENT — below br1, reached only through that bedroom's closet: a locking sliding panel at the back with a hidden release (Perception to spot the seams DC 13, Investigation to work the mechanism DC 15 - defaults; the checks are set, the numbers are yours).
SECOND FLOOR — the spiral stair at br7 is the only way up; the landing opens onto the upper rooms.

blocks.title: ALSO IN THE POST
lines: A letter from Twins Channel Station Immigration - paperwork is required to keep the abode. Comedy, bureaucracy, and the lawful anchor for the party's base.

The letter's own terms: the group signs by GROUP NAME, or one representative signs with a signed affidavit of leadership from every other member. Thirty days from delivery, or the transfer is null and void.

The hook inside the paperwork: if the party has not yet named itself, the deed CANNOT be signed until it does. The clerk's quill waits. This is the naming ceremony disguised as bureaucracy - do not rush it.

blocks.title: RP HOOKS
blocks.sub: if the play gets stale

rows.name: Lockpick
rows.note: 18 platinum via the clacks (in Thieves' Cant) hired a master lockpick

rows.name: Farm sponsorship
rows.note: 100 gold over 20 months, first payment made

rows.name: Standing patronage
rows.note: a temple of Essa and the farm paid up half a year

blocks.title: THE UNREMARKABLE FLASK — DM
lines: It is exactly what it looks like and nothing like it: a standard iron flask, and the thing sealed inside is Relane — a deva and angel of Essa, corked since the great wall of earth was raised across Arret. The bearer cannot know that. The flask never reads as occupied and never as empty; a Detect Magic or a divination gives up 'a bound creature within' and not one word more. DO NOT reveal the occupant here.

This is a PLANT, not a payoff. Play the finding as loot and nothing else — let a player pocket it and forget it. It comes due in Chapter 12: in Essa's kitchen outside time (12.2), a hero spends one of her granted truths on 'what is in my flask?' and draws the stopper. Freed and grateful, Relane expounds the true properties of the Amulet of Essa.
Full stats and the forward thread: Campaign Items — The Iron Flask, and the side quest What Sloshes in the Iron Flask. Note who carries it out of the Underbelly.

scenes.development: The master lockpick is the bridge to 7.6 - the four-lock door, at last.

script.text: The mansion has opinions: secret doors in the deep sub-basement, an arcane-locked door, a ladder shaft - and a room that IS an elevator, minutes down into the familiar Junction Rooms. The mansion was built over the thieves' road.

The house's other levels, mapped: the main basement under the bar's two-square gap, the small basement behind br1's closet panel, the second floor up the spiral stair. The secret door is drawn on the sheet - push it when found, not before.
'Who gifted this house, again?' - file that thought where the party can hear it being filed.

In the post: the Immigration letter. Comedy, bureaucracy, and the lawful anchor for the party's base. Its terms carry the hook: a group signs by GROUP NAME (or a representative with affidavits) - a party with no name yet cannot sign until it takes one. Thirty days on the clock.
The record's ledger for precedent: 18 platinum via the clacks hired a master lockpick. That lockpick is the bridge to 7.6 - the four-lock door, at last.

sq.label: What Rises on a New Day

script.text: Among the Underbelly haul, one squat iron flask — heavy, stoppered, cool to the touch, and all but silent. Play it as loot. DO NOT reveal what is inside: it is a plant for Chapter 12, where the right question in Essa's kitchen frees the deva Relane and unlocks the Amulet of Essa. Note who pockets it.

time.label: Exploring the house below — how long?

boxed.title: The Iron Flask
boxed.text: Among the haul the elevator-room opens onto — coins gone soft at the edges, a cracked scrying-lens, buckles with no belts — one thing sits wrong in the hand: a squat iron flask, stoppered tight and heavier than its size has any right to be. No maker's mark. No rust worth the name. The metal stays cool no matter how long you hold it. Give it a shake and almost nothing answers — a slow shift somewhere inside, like deep water minding its own weight. Whatever it keeps, it has kept for a very long time.

scenes.title: The Four Locks Open
scenes.boxedText: Behind the four locks: a room thirty feet square, empty save for its center - a sarcophagus of smooth stone, crossed by two heavy chains bolted to the floor and a third across its middle. Runes are cut deep into the lid. They read: RISE, RISE AND COME FORTH TO A NEW DAY.
scenes.body: The runes are Draconic. The chains are warded with 7th-level Abjuration: they absorb force damage and are immune to fire, necrotic, cold, lightning, poison, bludgeoning, and slashing. Identification (ritual study, or a generous Identify): a tool of HEALING - with warnings of madness woven through every layer of the working. It was opened by no one, wisely... and then hauled, whole and chained, into a basement anyway. Of course it was. Full item write-up: Appendix C, the Sarcophagus of the New Day.
scenes.mechanics: If a player asks the obvious question - can we put someone IN it - the honest answer is: the chains say somebody once asked the opposite. What rises on a new day is a Chapter-13 problem, and this book will not solve it for you.
scenes.development: The chapter ends when the party says it does. When they touch the platform circle's sliding ring - or when a new mark blooms on the tree map - Chapter 8 begins.

script.text: The locks open - push the sarcophagus and read the runes aloud: RISE, RISE AND COME FORTH TO A NEW DAY.
Draconic runes; chains warded with 7th-level Abjuration. Identification says HEALING - with warnings of madness woven through every layer of the working (Appendix C: the Sarcophagus of the New Day).

push.label: Appendix C — Sarcophagus of the New Day

script.text: If a player asks the obvious question - can we put someone IN it - the honest answer: the chains say somebody once asked the opposite.
It was opened by no one... and hauled, whole, into a basement anyway. Of course it was. The chapter ends when the party says it does; the sliding ring, or a new mark on the tree map, opens Chapter 8.

time.label: The four locks open

scenes.title: The Recurring Dream

boxed.title: The Dream
boxed.text: You are resting, and then you are not. You step into yourself from the void - a double image: a humanoid you cannot make out, and a great entity looming over it. Four arms - the larger pair ending in claws that pin your shoulders, a smaller pair of human-like hands gripping your torso. Four more shapes hold you to the ground. The thing above you is red, and powerful, and its mouth is moving - it growls and barks in low tones, a language you are certain is meant for you, aimed at you, and not one sound of it means a thing you can hold. It leans closer, as if your not-understanding is the only thing keeping you alive. You wake with your heart slamming, the barks still ringing, and no idea what was said.

blocks.text: THE DREAM STARTS HERE - so that scene 9.1 can pay it off. On the party's first true rest in the new estate, and on recurring nights through this chapter's downtime, the champion the demons have touched most dreams this dream - preferably the Sword of the Palace, taken and wiped by the Princeps right after the Chapter 1 binding (set up at 0.5 / 1.3), else the circle-rider (Contingency C3), the demon-marked, or simply your most roleplay-hungry player. It MUST be the same seat that will receive scene 9.1.

Nothing changes mechanically yet - no Abyssal, no words, no reveal. The dreamer only knows they were pinned, watched, and spoken to in a tongue they could not read. REFUSE every attempt to translate it: the not-understanding IS the mechanism, and it is what makes the words landing in 9.1 a gut-punch instead of a footnote.

SOURCE OPTION: in the original record this is also the night the dreamer's blade takes a small black stone that lets it blink a short distance (bampf). Graft that gift on here only if a champion was actually taken through the circle (C3).

scenes.mechanics: SESSION-ZERO ANCHOR: this dream pays off consent taken at Session Zero - the content-advisory items 'Mind-reading & altered memories' and 'Kidnapping & forced capture' (Tone & Safety). The restraint-and-surveillance imagery is by design, and it echoes Kelethtonreth's psionic touch of the old heroes in Kili's tale (10.3) - the demon reaching into a mind the way Kelethtonreth reached into Bobby's. Offer the X-Card reminder before any push. HOW IT PAYS OFF: run the same images more than once, never translated; then scene 9.1 repeats them verbatim and lets the growl resolve into words, and the dreamer wakes speaking Abyssal.
scenes.development: The dream is banked, not spent. It waits for scene 9.1, The Dream Turns Two-Way.

script.text: SESSION-ZERO ANCHOR - offer the X-Card before pushing. This dream is the consent taken at Session Zero: 'Mind-reading & altered memories' and 'Kidnapping & forced capture' (Tone & Safety). It echoes Kelethtonreth's touch of the old heroes (10.3) by design.

Give the dream to the champion the demons have touched most - preferably the Sword of the Palace (taken and wiped by the Princeps right after the binding; set up in 0.5 / 1.3), else the circle-rider (C3), the demon-marked, or your most roleplay-hungry player. It MUST be the same seat that receives 9.1. Push it on the first real rest in the estate.
Do not translate it - not now, not on request. The barks are a language, but meaningless to the dreamer. The not-understanding is the whole mechanism.
Recur it through the downtime, same images every time. The payoff is banked for 9.1, where the growl finally becomes words and the dreamer wakes knowing Abyssal.
Source option: the same night, the dreamer's blade gains a small black stone that lets it blink a short distance (bampf). Graft it on only if a champion was actually taken through the circle (C3).

time.label: Nights the dream recurs — how many?

chapters.chapterDevelopment: Whatever the party founded here is now a campaign character: name it, staff it, and put it on the map. A House of Healing makes a fine model - beloved local weirdos within a tenday. The endgame lands harder when the heroes have an address.

chapters.title: The Tree Network

sigil.label: The Sacred Trees
sigil.caption: The sigil of the sacred trees

chapters.overview: The platform circle is a door to every sacred tree - and Essax is already through it. A new mark blooms on the tree map; Chanfirch and Vum are hollow when the party arrives; Aedlab is warned in time. And the circle's blank fourth destination leads somewhere no map admits: a walled glade, a living cutting of Oospufmorn, a hedge maze that punishes wrong turns with teleportation - and an archway wearing something that is not moss.
chapters.running: This chapter is a race the party can only half win, and the half they win matters enormously: Aedlab survives Chapter 9's assault AS a battle instead of a fait accompli because they warned it here. Run the circle hops briskly - hollow trees need five minutes of dread apiece, not thirty - and spend the saved time in the glade and maze, where the party is off every map that exists. The Threshold Blight fight teaches the campaign's endgame vocabulary: portals can be OPENED at archways, and closed if you are fast and know how.

scenes.title: The New Mark
scenes.boxedText: On the tree map etched in Oospufmorn's trunk, where the arcane light still shines, something has changed. A dark smudge - almost burnt, almost necrotic - is beginning to etch itself below the Defenders' name-columns of two trees at once: Chanfirch. And Vum. It is the beginning of a letter. Perhaps an E. You have seen where that letter leads - the rotten thumbprint of a finished name still sits beside Oospufmorn. It seems ESSAX, or their minions, have not stopped at one tree...
scenes.body: Whoever checks the platform first sees it (the Champion bond gives everyone a reason to feel it): the beginning of a letter - perhaps an E - growing below Chanfirch and Vum at once, the same rot that finished into ESSAX beside Oospufmorn. The party knows the circle's activation from Chapter 7 (DC 15 Arcana to fire, -1 per successful use); the sliding-ring discovery (Investigation DC 25/27) is now urgent rather than academic: rotate the blank to another tree's sigil, and the circle goes THERE.
scenes.development: Two marks, two trees, one circle. Let the party pick their order - both are already lost, and the order only changes which silence they hear first.

script.text: Whoever checks the platform first sees it - push the new mark. The Champion bond gives everyone a reason to feel it. (The full Map on the Trunk handout remains in App. D if the table wants to re-read the whole etching.)

The circle's activation they already know (DC 15 Arcana, minus 1 per use). The sliding ring (DC 25/27 Investigation) is now urgent rather than academic: rotate the blank to a tree's sigil, and the circle goes THERE.
Two marks, two trees, one circle. Let the party pick the order - both are already lost, and the order only changes which silence they hear first.

scenes.title: Too Late Twice
scenes.body: CHANFIRCH: the circle delivers them to a platform like Oospufmorn's - and a bore-hole with nothing behind it. The heart is extracted, the foliage already turning. VUM: a hole where a heart should be, older by days. At the BASE of each tree stands a moss-covered stone archway - the moss smelly, clinging in patches, faintly wrong (do not name it; the party meets its source in 8.5). No enemies, no bodies, no note. Essax stopped performing for them.
scenes.mechanics: Nature or Arcana DC 15 at either archway: this 'moss' grew in days, not years, and it grew in a PATTERN - radiating from the arch's keystone. DC 20: something passed through these arches recently, repeatedly, and large.
scenes.development: Three hearts lost is the villain's threshold (the party may not know that yet - Kili tells them in Chapter 10). Aedlab is the only surface tree left. Scene 8.3, at speed.

script.text: Run the hops briskly - hollow trees need five minutes of dread apiece, not thirty. CHANFIRCH: a platform like Oospufmorn's, a bore-hole with nothing behind it. VUM: older by days.
At the base of each tree, the moss-covered stone archway - smelly, clinging, faintly wrong. Do NOT name it; the party meets its source in 8.5.
Nature or Arcana DC 15: the moss grew in DAYS, in a pattern radiating from the keystone. DC 20: something passed through recently, repeatedly, and large.
No enemies, no bodies, no note - Essax stopped performing for them. Aedlab is the only surface tree left. 8.3, at speed.

time.label: Racing the network — how many days lost?

scenes.title: Aedlab Warned
scenes.boxedText: The wall around Aedlab is light made solid - a shimmer twenty feet out from the trunk, rising all the way to the foliage. With the alert called, the Defenders cycle their patrols: a scout walks at the barrier and is through it before your eyes agree it opened - a green flash at her wrist, a ripple, gone. Another returns the same way an hour later. To those who live here it is nothing: a Key Bracelet piercing the wall, the known sight of a Defender coming home. Nothing else gets in. Nothing, they tell you, ever has.
scenes.body: At Aedlab the Defenders have noticed NO mark - the party's warning lands before the blow. The tree goes to high alert; if any PC has a Defender parent (the Warden's Child hook), this is a reunion scene worth five real minutes - pride, fear, and a bracelet with a green gem that will matter terribly in Chapter 9. If the party informs the Empress - and Champions who just saved a sacred tree usually do - run it as a live sending exchange: their 25-word report composed at the table, then her 25-word reply back through the same casting. Three replies are provided in the Mechanics block; choose the register the moment needs - gratitude, command, or the mask slipping. Underneath any of them, dread. Either way, the party must LEAVE THIS SCENE KNOWING WHAT A KEY BRACELET IS - the alert itself provides the RP. WITH the hook: Zontif walks her child the barrier's length and opens the wall for a returning patrol - the same gesture that opened the meadow in 0.4 - and names it. WITHOUT it: any Defender proudly explains the shimmer the party keeps seeing - one bracelet per Defender, bonded, undetectable as spellwork, the only keys that exist. This is deliberate setup: 9.2 opens on this exact sight, and its dread depends on the party knowing what it means.
scenes.development: The party has done everything right. Chapter 9 will hurt anyway - that is not their failure, and the book will say so again when it matters.

script.text: At Aedlab the Defenders have noticed no mark - the party's warning lands BEFORE the blow. The tree goes to high alert.
If any PC has a Defender parent (Warden's Child), this reunion is worth five real minutes: pride, fear, and a bracelet with a green gem that will matter terribly in Chapter 9.

Establish the KEY BRACELET on-screen - push the shimmer. With the Warden's Child in play, Zontif herself opens the wall for a returning patrol (the same gesture that opened the meadow in 0.4) and names the bracelet; without it, any Defender proudly explains: one bracelet per Defender, bonded, the only keys that exist. 9.2 opens on this exact sight - let them learn it here so the dread lands there.

If the party informs the Empress, run the sending exchange: their 25-word report composed live at the table, then ONE of her three replies from the Mechanics block - gratitude, command, or the mask slipping. Underneath whichever she sends: dread.
The party has done everything right. Chapter 9 will hurt anyway - that is not their failure, and the book will say so again when it matters.

time.label: Warning Aedlab — how long does it take?

blocks.text: THE REPORT - this time the party speaks first: a sending to the Empress (their own casting, or a Defender wizard at Aedlab lends the spell and the party dictates). 25 words, composed live at the table - count them. What they choose to fit into 25 is the scene. Her reply rides back through the same casting: 25 words, no more.

blocks.title: HER REPLY - GRATITUDE
blocks.sub: exactly 25 words - she spends the spell's whole cap on them
lines: "You did what Our Empire could not - you were in time. Aedlab lives because of you. Whatever you need is yours. Come home to Us."

blocks.title: HER REPLY - COMMAND
blocks.sub: 24 words - logistics first; the crown as war-machine
lines: "Hold Aedlab. A wing of Defenders and two war-wizards teleport to you by dusk; the nearest garrison marches tonight. Report each hour. Well done."

blocks.title: HER REPLY - THE MASK SLIPS
blocks.sub: 23 words - the pressure release: authority saying out loud what the party will need to hear again in Chapter 9
lines: "Thank you - Aedlab holds because of you. But three trees are gone, and We fear heroes alone could never stop this. Come home."

blocks.text: Choose ONE reply - the register the table has earned: gratitude if they need warmth, command if they need momentum, the mask if they need to hear the weight of it. Whichever she sends, read it evenly and let it sit - the dread lives under the words, never in them.

scenes.title: The Blank Destination
scenes.boxedText: The squeeze between planes releases, and the first thing you notice is the PULL - faint, familiar, diminishing: a cutting of Oospufmorn, three feet tall, an exact replica of its mother, gnarled roots spread wide in a shallow stone pot on a three-tiered stand. Around you: a thirty-foot glade walled in stone, thirty feet high, cloudy sky above, an iron-bound double door opposite - and the teleportation circle under your feet.
scenes.body: Only Oospufmorn's circle offers this fourth, BLANK option - and it is the default. The cutting is too small to have a heart of its own but still connected to its mother somehow; Speak with Plants earns politeness, not intelligence. Flight meets a magical barrier at wall height. DC 15 Arcana: this is a RETURNING circle, same activation, one rune of difference pointing home.
scenes.mechanics: The door is held by Arcane Lock (DC 10 Arcana or Insight to identify from its placement). Ways through: Knock; Dispel Magic; or brute force - AC 25, 100 HP.
scenes.development: Beyond the door: hedges. Scene 8.5.

script.text: Only Oospufmorn's circle offers the blank fourth destination - and it is the default. Push the glade on arrival.
The cutting: too small for a heart of its own, still connected to its mother somehow. Speak with Plants earns politeness, not intelligence. Flight meets the barrier at wall height.
DC 15 Arcana: this is a RETURNING circle - same activation, one rune of difference pointing home.
The door is held by Arcane Lock (DC 10 to identify from placement): Knock, Dispel Magic, or AC 25 and 100 HP. Beyond it - hedges. 8.5.

If a champion rode the circle in 6.4 (Contingency C3 - The Ride Taken): this glade is where they landed. Track Two means they may still be here - run the reunion before the door. Track Three means the trail continues past the door and through the archway; the rescue can be this chapter's second half.

scenes.title: The Maze
scenes.body: A hedge maze in a small forest on the great plains of Aria - and the party is coming from the INSIDE OUT, center door to outer wall. Any wrong turn warps the offender (wall-hopping counts as a wrong turn) to the maze's TRUE beginning: its outer entrance, outside the walls, on the stone walkway beneath the three archways. Which is exactly where the trouble is. Every warp is a FULL ejection - all five teleports, one destination, no partial setbacks. The true route, traced on the map with north up, every step one 5-foot square (diagonals are true diagonals): from the center door - the open gap on the northwest of the inner circle - 1 northwest, 2 southwest, 3 west, 2 southeast, 1 northeast to JUNCTION 1 (left warps); 2 east to JUNCTION 2 (right warps); 2 east to JUNCTION 3 (right warps); then 5 northeast, 1 west, 1 north, 2 northeast to JUNCTION 4 (left warps); 4 south and out the exit to the EAST - and striding past that exit is JUNCTION 5, the fifth warp: The Long Way Down. Run it from the MAZE RUNNER below - it tracks every runner square by square so you never lose your place; every warp pays out one entry from the New Knowledge table. Failure is progress here - and the middle archway is enshrouded.

route.start: The center chamber's door - the open gap on the northwest of the inner circle. North is up on the map.
route.note: Cardinal walkthrough traced on the DM map, north up. Every step is one 5-foot square; diagonal steps are true diagonals. Junctions sit at the END of their leg - the party arrives, then the call is made. The correct call at each junction is simply the next leg's heading; the named wrong direction is the warp.
route.flavorNote: Fey-touched corridor flavor - optional, one per corridor, read after the turn that opens it. The maze IS fey; let it show. Works in either direction - the corridor does not care which way you are walking it.

reverse.start: The break in the east wall - the maze's outer entrance, off the archway walkway. They step in heading west and are standing at Junction 5 immediately: the true way is NORTH; south is The Long Way Down, walked inward.
reverse.note: The return run - outside back to the center - walks the same squares backward: same junctions, same numbers, same wrong directions, same destination for every warp (the archway walkway, which on this run means back where they started). The correct call at each junction is simply the outbound heading reversed. Junction read-alouds were written outbound; mirror them freely.

legs.flavor: The corridor is a single breath long, and the hedge leans in to look at you. Dew hangs on the yew in perfect spheres that do not fall.
Foxglove blooms out of season along the roots, nodding in the windless air. Somewhere a small bell rings twice, sweet and pleased with itself, then is embarrassed into silence.
The long westward run smells of crushed thyme, though no one has stepped here in years. The shadows fall the wrong way - toward the sun.
Red-capped toadstools stand in a half-ring across the path like a gate left open. Every instinct says step around them. Stepping around them turns out to be impossible.
One square of green silence. The birdsong stops mid-phrase here, as if the singer forgot the tune - or was paid not to finish it.
Tiny white moths rise at every footfall and settle behind you - precisely, deliberately - into your exact bootprints.
The hedge walls here are woven - actually woven, over-under, like basketry. Nothing that grows does this. The corridor is very proud of it.
Honeysuckle drips through the yew and the air goes syrup-sweet. Laughter runs along the top of the hedge, always exactly one square ahead, always one voice too many.
A single square that is somehow uphill in both directions. A stone sits in the middle of it, mossy, and warm as a sleeping cat.
One pace and the season hiccups: a square of deep autumn, gold leaves ankle-deep, while every hedge around it stays high summer. The leaves are always freshly fallen.
Cobwebs strung with dew-lights span the passage at shoulder height. They part politely as you approach and re-knit behind you, slightly neater than before.
The corridor runs straight and solemn, and the hedges bow as you pass - actually bow, a slow ripple of green. Whether it is honor, farewell, or apology, the maze will not say.

maze.warp: A wrong turn warps the OFFENDER only - the one who called it - and every warp lands in the same place: full ejection to the maze's outer entrance, on the archway walkway. All five teleports, one destination; no partial setbacks. Wall-hopping is a wrong turn. Invite every victim to narrate the half-second of indignity. Ejections are not a bug: the more warps, the more of the party is standing under the archways when the middle one flashes purple.

modes.name: Full team
modes.text: The group moves as one; only the character who called the wrong turn is warped. The rest stand at the junction, suddenly one voice short.

modes.name: Solo runner
modes.text: One scout runs it while the rest hold the glade and the returning circle. Ejected or waiting characters may shout remembered directions through the hedges: DC 10 Intelligence to relay accurately - a failed relay arrives confidently WRONG, and it is absolutely the party's fault.

decisions.read: The corridor rights itself out of the long western sweep and forks: to the left an opening curves back northwest, cool and shaded, arching invitingly toward the heart of the maze; ahead the passage runs on east, hugging the bend of the wall.
decisions.wrong: Turning LEFT (northwest) is WARP 1 - full ejection to the archway walkway.
