decisions.read: Two squares on, a gap opens to the right - south, wide and sunlit, breathing open plains air. It sounds like outside. The true path runs straight on east, narrow and unconvinced.
decisions.wrong: Turning RIGHT (south) is WARP 2 - full ejection to the archway walkway. Yes, the wrong way SOUNDS like outside. The maze's favorite joke.

decisions.read: The maze repeats itself: two more squares east and another southern gap, wider than the last and twice as confident. The true path bends away northeast beneath a clipped arch - the longest run in the maze, five squares of it.
decisions.wrong: Turning RIGHT (south) is WARP 3 - full ejection to the archway walkway. The same joke, told louder.

decisions.read: The long northeast climb ends in a jog - one square back west, one north, two more northeast between older, woodier hedges - and then the split: left, northwest, the hedge opens generous and green; south, the passage tightens to shoulder width.
decisions.wrong: Turning LEFT (northwest) is WARP 4 - full ejection to the archway walkway. Generous and green is how the maze says goodbye.

decisions.miss: STRAIGHT ON - south, past the exit
decisions.read: Four squares south down the tightening corridor, a break opens in the outer wall to the EAST - plains light, wind, worked stone beyond. The way out. It is entirely possible to stride right past it.
decisions.wrong: Missing the exit and walking on is WARP 5 - The Long Way Down (below). Full ejection, eventually.

trap.name: The Long Way Down
trap.text: The fifth warp is a patience trap: the exit is a break in the east wall four squares down the final corridor, and a confident party can stride right past it. Let them. The corridor beyond is long, generous, utterly convincing - let the mapper sketch it boldly. The warp waits until the moment they realize and turn back, and takes each victim exactly as they turn. Full ejection; invite them to narrate the walk of shame that never finishes.

maze.exit: Junction 5's break in the east wall delivers them through the outer hedge and onto the stone walkway - three archways between them and the open plains, the middle one enshrouded, and every warped companion already standing beneath it. The battle block takes it from here.

hints.note: One entry per warp, drawn by the map or chosen by you - cumulative; repeat earned hints on request. Failure is progress: every trip through the warp teaches the maze. The pool is shared across both directions - outbound and return warps draw from the same six entries until all are earned; after that, repeat freely. NO MAP? Roll d6 and re-roll anything already earned - the draw is what the tool does and the re-roll is how you do it by hand.
entries: The true first turn smells faintly of lavender - the only hedge in the maze that blooms.
Along the correct path the boughs overhead are clipped square; every wrong opening grows wild.
The true path is worn - a pale thread of trodden grass. Wrong corridors are lush and unstepped.
Warp-light lingers a half-second on the hedge that punished you: glance back on re-entry and the offending wall still glows faintly.
Birds nest only over dead ends. Song ahead means stop.
The yank comes from BELOW - the runes are under the sod at each junction. DC 15 Perception at any junction spots the mown seam before a foot lands on it.

maze.valve: After the table's THIRD total warp, offer the montage: one group Intelligence (Survival) check, DC 13. Success narrates them out to the walkway; failure costs exactly one more warp (and one more hint) and then narrates them out anyway. The maze is a bit, not a wall - it may never hard-stall the table. The valve is direction-blind: it counts the table's TOTAL warps, outbound and return alike, and works the same both ways.

battle.name: The Archway
battle.setup: The 'moss' on the middle archway is a THRESHOLD BLIGHT (Appendix A) - the same species whose leavings marked Chanfirch and Vum. As combat nears it, the archway FLASHES PURPLE: a portal opening. Will-o'-wisps wander through as it widens.

combatants.name: Threshold Blight
combatants.note: Merged with the arch (DC 15 Nature/Arcana to read it as a creature before it moves). The portal completes in 1d4+3 rounds unless it dies first.

combatants.name: Will-o'-Wisp
combatants.note: Drift through the widening portal from round 2; more each round the portal stands open, if you are feeling honest.

battle.tactics: The Blight does not chase - it IS the objective, and it knows it. Wisps harry casters to protect the Blight's timer. If the portal completes, closing it requires Dispel Magic against DC 18, or a dispel cast at 8th level or higher.
battle.adjusting: Weaker party: portal completes in 1d4+5 rounds, 2 wisps. Stronger party: the portal disgorges 2 dretches (Appendix A) the round it completes, every round, until closed.
battle.aftermath: Arcana DC 25 studying the closed (or closing) portal's far side: cold, dark, undead-thick - DEMONHOLME. The party now knows where the war comes from, and where it must eventually go. The fight sings when the table splits three ways - maze mappers, portal guards, outside fighters. Encourage it. Then let the adrenaline drain on-screen: the scene's true exit is WHERE DO YOU SLEEP TONIGHT (script beats below; the full lever set and the fallback wait in 9.1's THE ROADS TO AEDLAB).

script.text: They are solving the maze from the INSIDE OUT - center door to outer wall, five junctions. A wrong call at any of them warps the offender to the outer walkway beneath the archways: every warp a full ejection, no partial setbacks. Run it from the MAZE RUNNER below - one click per square, junction calls and warps handled in place, every runner tracked so you never lose your place. Read one New Knowledge entry per warp. Let the mapper suffer beautifully.

The fifth warp is the cruelest: the exit is a break in the east wall four squares down the final corridor, and a confident party strides right past it. The Long Way Down: let them walk, let the mapper sketch, and the warp takes each victim the moment they turn back. Invite them to narrate the walk of shame that never finishes.

Their exit walkway carries three stone archways; the middle one is enshrouded - and every ejected character is already standing beneath them. As combat nears it, the arch FLASHES PURPLE - a portal opening, wisps wandering through as it widens (battle block: the Blight does not chase; it IS the objective and knows it).
If the portal completes: Dispel Magic against DC 18, or a dispel at 8th level or higher. Encourage the three-way split - mappers, portal guards, outside fighters; it sings.
Aftermath, DC 25 Arcana on the far side: cold, dark, undead-thick - DEMONHOLME. The party now knows where the war comes from, and where it must eventually go.

When the portal closes, do not cut away - let the adrenaline drain on-screen and push the exhale. Then ask the table, in so many words: WHERE DO YOU SLEEP TONIGHT? This scene's real exit is a decision, not a door.

Let their own reasons do the walking - deal these as needed, never all at once: TRIAGE (they are burned, bruised, and spell-spent; the glade is no bed, and the way home passes Oospufmorn's platform - heartless, autumn-struck, no wall around any of it). The BOND (close your eyes, turn, point: three of the four pulls now end in hollow places; only Aedlab's still feels ALIVE). The REPORT OWED (Zontif stands watch on their word, and they now know what the moss is, where the portals go - and that an archway stood at the foot of BOTH hollow trees. Is there one near Aedlab? Let a player ask it). The STANDING ORDER (only if HER REPLY - COMMAND was the 8.3 sending: 'Hold Aedlab... Report each hour' - returning is compliance). FAMILY (the Warden's Child seat: after a brush with Demonholme, you go where your mother is).

When they name Aedlab - and nearly every table will - do not wink, do not foreshadow, do not linger: 'the only wall that has never been broken' is Chapter 9's job. Cut on the decision. The full DM logic, voice samples, and the fallback if they bed down anywhere else: THE ROADS TO AEDLAB, in 9.1.

time.label: Time in the maze — how long?

boxed.title: The Wrong Place to Sleep
boxed.text: The portal dies, and the glade exhales. The archway is only stone again - but the cold it let through has not left; it pools at your ankles like water that remembers being ice, and the wisp-ash drifts across the walkway without any wind to carry it. Behind you the maze holds its hedges still; somewhere at its heart, faint and familiar, the cutting's small pull still reaches you - three feet of borrowed life, leaves drawn in tight. The adrenaline goes out of you all at once, the way it does - and every burn and bruise the maze collected files its complaint. Somewhere beyond these walls the sun is going down. You are off every map that exists, standing beside a door Demonholme knows how to knock on. Whatever gets decided tonight will not be decided here - and it will not be slept on here, either.

chapters.chapterDevelopment: Milestone: 8th level. The party ends this chapter holding the whole board: the network, the archway weapon, the Demonholme address, and one tree still standing. Chapter 9 begins with the retreat to Aedlab (9.1) - and the breach lands at most four hours into the rest they take there.

chapters.title: The Fall of Aedlab
chapters.overview: Essax stops sneaking. A stolen Key Bracelet pierces Aedlab's barrier; a PC's recurring dream turns out to be a two-way wiretap; two glabrezu, six red hoods, and a forty-foot collared colossus come through the hole. The party fights on two fronts, wins almost everything - and the tree falls anyway, revealing a heart larger than any other. Then the dwarves arrive, an elf troop follows, and the word KNOBDIMMON is finally spoken above ground.
chapters.running: Check the Tone & Safety advisory again before this one: memory violation (Zontif), kidnapping (the Defenders), a possible PC exit (Nika Blackthorn's portal), and the fall of a beloved place are all live here. The battle runs on one iron rule, stated in the logic sidebar of 9.3: EACH ENEMY STRIKE TEAM SERVES ITS OWN MISSION AND ABANDONS EVERYTHING ELSE. Play the demons as professionals with a shopping list, not as fighters with pride, and the horror arrives on its own. The dream scene (9.1) belongs to whichever PC the demons have touched most - preferably the Sword of the Palace (the Princeps tie makes it seamless), else the circle-rider, the demon-marked, or simply your most roleplay-hungry player; it must be the seat that first dreamed in 7.7. AND THE PULL-ASIDE COMES FIRST: at the top of the session, before any dice, take the likely chaser aside - out of character - and say it plainly: going through a portal alone, with enemies obviously on the other side of it, can take your character out of the campaign. This is why the table built backup characters (0.1). Warned is warned; 9.5 resolves on it.

scenes.title: Retreat to Aedlab — The Dream Turns Two-Way

boxed.title: The Last Wall Standing
boxed.text: The circle releases you onto Aedlab's platform, and the first thing you feel is the wall: light made solid, twenty feet out from the trunk and rising all the way to the foliage - wrapped around the last surface tree in the Empire that still holds its heart. High alert has not slackened since your warning. The patrols still walk the barrier's edge, weapons worn openly, and word of your arrival runs down the boughs faster than you do. The Warden meets you at the circle and looks over what the maze left of you - the burns, the bruises, the map still clutched in someone's hand - and hears everything: the cutting, the maze, the archway portal forced shut. When the telling is done she gives the only order that makes sense tonight: rest. You are inside the only wall that has never been broken. Nothing gets in. Nothing ever has.

boxed.title: The Dream
boxed.text: As you rest, your head begins to nod - just a bit - and you step into yourself from the void: the old dream, the double image: a humanoid you cannot make out, and a great entity - four arms, the larger pair ending in claws, pinning your shoulders while human-like hands grip your torso. Four others hold you down. And this time it changes. The demon comes into focus - red, and powerful - and its growl becomes language inside your head: 'Ah, our connection is strong. You must be close, whelp. We will take the heart, and your pitiful defenses will be destroyed.' You wake standing.

scenes.body: WHY THE PARTY IS HERE - THE CALL TO ACTION IS THEIR OWN: at the end of 8.5, battered from the maze and the archway battle, the party teleports to Aedlab to rest, heal, and decide what comes next - and every reason is a good one. It is the last surface tree still holding its heart. It stands on high alert BECAUSE OF THEIR WARNING (8.3). Its barrier has never been breached - the safest bed in the Empire. And the Warden who greets them at the circle (a parent, if the Warden's Child is seated) wants their report: give the greeting and the telling of the maze battle a few real minutes before anyone lies down. They came here to sleep, not to fight; the tragedy of this chapter is that they carried the wiretap with them. Mid-rest - at most four hours in - the dream turns two-way. From this night, that PC UNDERSTANDS ABYSSAL - and can speak back into the dream if they dare. The wiretap runs both ways: everything they say in it is heard, and everything they hear is true. What they just heard is a declaration of war with a timestamp - and the timestamp is NOW: the dream is one moment, not a string of nights, and the battle cry follows it before the dreamer's eyes are fully clear. (The full lever set, voice samples, and the fallback if they bed down anywhere else: THE ROADS TO AEDLAB, in Mechanics below.)

blocks.text: SESSION-ZERO ANCHOR: this beat pays off consent taken at Session Zero - the content-advisory items 'Mind-reading & altered memories' and 'Kidnapping & forced capture' (Tone & Safety). It is the second half of the recurring dream first seen in scene 7.7 (The Recurring Dream), and the images echo Kelethtonreth's psionic touch of the old heroes (10.4) by design. This is surveillance and bodily restraint imagery on purpose - offer the X-Card reminder before running it if your table runs sensitive. TIMING: the dream fires ONCE, mid-rest at Aedlab - at most 4 hours into a long rest, or just after a short one - and 9.2's breach follows immediately on Zontif's cry. Do not run it across multiple nights: the demon's 'you must be close' is true because the party is AT Aedlab when the connection wakes.

THE ROADS TO AEDLAB - TWO CLOCKS, ONE NIGHT: the breach was scheduled the night the bracelet left Zontif's wrist (9.2) - the enemy is not reacting to the party and is not luring them; the demon's 'you must be close' is SURPRISE. The party's retreat is their own choice - 'to take some time to rest and heal from combat,' as the original table's log has it - and the collision of the two clocks is coincidence. And the coincidence is the MERCY: because their own good sense carries the wiretap to the target, Aedlab gets the only advance warning it will ever have, and 9.2 opens as a battle instead of a fait accompli. NEVER make it a summons. The tragedy needs the party to have chosen the safest bed in the Empire and been right about everything - except the thing they carried. The cards below are the levers - deal them as needed in 8.5's closing beats or at the circle here; never all at once.

blocks.title: THE TRIAGE
blocks.sub: any PC's own tally - let a player say it first if they will
lines: "Between us we have one healing spell, no slots worth naming, and a door Demonholme knows how to knock on. Not here."

blocks.title: NO BED AT OOSPUFMORN
blocks.sub: the way home crosses its platform: autumn leaves underfoot, crowds below, no barrier since the heart was taken
lines: Voice (a Council guard at the stair): "You're welcome to rest here, Champions - we'll keep watch. We just can't promise what we're watching for."

blocks.title: THE BOND
blocks.sub: the Champion boon, put to work
lines: "Close your eyes. Turn. Point. Three pulls end in hollow places - you feel the difference now, like reaching for a hand and finding a glove. Only Aedlab still pulls warm."

blocks.title: THE REPORT OWED
blocks.sub: Zontif stands watch on their word (8.3) - and they hold what she needs
lines: "You left Zontif standing watch on your word. You now know what the moss is, where the portals lead - and that an archway stood at the foot of both hollow trees. She knows none of it."
Is there an archway near Aedlab? Let a player ask it.

blocks.title: THE STANDING ORDER
blocks.sub: only if HER REPLY - COMMAND was the 8.3 sending
lines: Voice (the sending, remembered): "Hold Aedlab... Report each hour." They have been away from their post.

blocks.title: FAMILY
blocks.sub: Warden's Child only
lines: Voice (the seat's own gut): "You have seen what is left of a tree that had no warning. Your mother is standing under the last one that got one."

blocks.text: IF THEY BED DOWN ANYWHERE ELSE: do not force it, and do not punish it - the breach fires on schedule wherever they sleep. The dream still comes (the connection is the ritual's, not the geography's) but distant: the growl never resolves into words except one, AEDLAB, said the way a thing names a place it is already inside. Swap the demon's line for 'Too far to matter, whelp.' Zontif's alarm follows by sending if anyone can receive one. The circle they know (DC 15 Arcana, minus 1 per use) puts them on the platform mid-battle: run 9.2 already in motion, the forward force already engaged, and let arriving late be its own scar - the original table once re-entered a fight by circle in under thirty seconds. The door swings both ways.

script.text: Check the Tone & Safety advisory before this chapter, and offer the X-Card reminder if your table runs sensitive - this scene is surveillance and restraint imagery by design, consented to at Session Zero ('Mind-reading & altered memories'; 'Kidnapping & forced capture'). It pays off the recurring dream first seen in 7.7 - give it to the SAME seat. Then the PULL-ASIDE (9.5 Mechanics): before any dice, take the likely chaser aside, out of character - a portal taken alone, with enemies obviously on the other side of it, can take a character out of the campaign; that is why the table built backup characters (0.1).

The party chose this. At the end of 8.5, battered, they teleport to the last surface tree still holding its heart - on high alert from THEIR OWN warning (8.3), behind the only barrier that has never been breached, with the Warden waiting at the circle. Push the arrival, then take the report RP: she hears everything about the maze and the archway portal, and if the Warden's Child is seated this is family - give it the minutes it deserves.

Let them bed down believing it: nothing has ever come through that wall. They came here to rest, not to fight - the wiretap came with them. At most four hours into the rest (Mechanics), the dreamer's head begins to nod.

Give the dream to the PC the demons have touched most - preferably the Sword of the Palace (Princeps tie; set up in 0.5 / 1.3 and first seen in 7.7), else the circle-rider, the demon-marked, or your most roleplay-hungry player - the SAME seat as 7.7. Push it.
From this night, that PC UNDERSTANDS ABYSSAL - and can speak back into the dream if they dare. Everything said in it is heard; everything heard in it is true.
What they just heard is a declaration of war with a timestamp - and the timestamp is NOW. Run the dream once; there is no second night.

Before the dreamer can say what they saw, Zontif's cry rings from the canopy: 'They are here, to arms! To arms, something is coming to steal the heart of Aedlab!' Straight into 9.2 - no scene break; the shimmer is already opening.

time.label: Retreat and broken rest — how long?

scenes.title: The Breach
scenes.body: DM ONLY - THE RITUAL BEHIND THE BREACH: the green-gem KEY BRACELET that pierces Aedlab's barrier is missing from its Defender's wrist (Zontif's, if the Warden's Child hook is in play). Like the dreamer, she was taken and put through a ritual: her mind read, an idea planted AS IF HER OWN - leave the bracelet outside the barrier after using it - and the event wiped. The breach is an inside job that nobody committed. When this surfaces (during or after the battle), it should land as violation, not as blame. SESSION-ZERO ANCHOR: Zontif's violation is the same consent item as the dreamer's - 'Mind-reading & altered memories' (Tone & Safety), flagged at Session Zero; it is the ritual twin of scene 7.7 / 9.1. Play it as violation, never blame. THE SURFACING IS BUILT IN: the seed at 9.5 (the way that stands open for Nika Blackthorn, and Zontif's bare wrist) and the reveal at 9.6 (the bracelet found in the grass, outside the line the barrier held).
scenes.boxedText: A shimmer in the protective barrier - to those who dwell here, the well-known sight of a Key Bracelet piercing the wall: a Defender coming home. Any other day they would barely look up. Today, warned, every weapon is already out. Through the hole step two muscular figures, both over ten feet, both four-armed: one jet black, one hide-red. Six figures in dark red hooded cloaks fan out behind them. Then the ground rumbles like heavy cavalry - and with a roar, a massive creature knuckle-runs through the opening, bending it to fit. It stands to its full height - forty feet - a leering bison's head with carnivorous teeth and horns curving upward, bear-muscled arms wide as old oaks, sickly purple-green hide, a bronze collar at its neck, carvings etched into its horns.
scenes.mechanics: TIMING: at most 4 hours into a long rest, or just after a short one; the remaining hours can be finished after the fight for full benefit (mercy with a straight face). Abyssal-speakers hear the giant's bellows as words: 'Fuck this stupid small hole' - 'Fucking right!' Zontif dives from the canopy, feather-light at the last instant, yelling in Abyssal: 'MY DREAMS ARE MY OWN! STAY OUT OF MY MIND!'

script.text: Timing (Mechanics): at most four hours into a long rest, or just after a short one - the remainder can be finished after the fight, mercy with a straight face. Push the breach. The party KNOWS this shimmer - it was established at the wall in 8.3 (and in 0.4, for the Warden's Child). Give them the half-second of recognition before what steps through.

DM only: the Key Bracelet that pierced the barrier is missing from Zontif's wrist - taken, mind read, an idea planted AS IF HER OWN, the event wiped. The breach is an inside job that nobody committed. When it surfaces, land it as violation, not blame.
Abyssal-speakers hear the colossus' bellows in the raw - the dreamer gets the whole indignity of it.
Zontif dives from the canopy, feather-light at the last instant, yelling in Abyssal: 'MY DREAMS ARE MY OWN! STAY OUT OF MY MIND!'

scenes.title: Two Fronts
scenes.body: Zontif, landing: 'You must defend the heart of the tree at all costs!' - and the Defender crew dives from the boughs to meet the ground assault. The party must split its attention or split itself; either hurts, on purpose. Heart-wrenching screams from below punctuate the platform fight. When the last standing Defender falls, the ground force rewards the platform with a barrage of fireballs - a tactical retreat through the platform circle to Oospufmorn is the right call, and the door should stand open for it.

battle.name: The Breach - Above and Below
battle.setup: TWO FRONTS, ONE MAP. ABOVE (the platform): the red glabrezu, two hooded mages, one fanatic - mission: TAKE THE HEART. BELOW (the roots): the black glabrezu, three hooded fanatics, the colossus - mission: KIDNAP THE DEFENDERS (the colossus' mission is the TRUNK). The Defenders (treat as 4 Scouts + Zontif as a Knight with feather fall) hold the ground as NPCs; they will lose without help, and may lose with it.

combatants.name: Glabrezu (red - above)
combatants.note: The dreamer's demon. Flies direct for the heart; abandons any grapple the moment a path opens.

combatants.name: Glabrezu (black - below)
combatants.note: Coordinates the kidnappings; power word stun on whoever shepherds the Defenders.

combatants.name: Cult Fanatic
combatants.note: One above, three below. Hold person on Defenders; fireball barrage (treat as Mage slots if you upgrade one) when the ground is won.

combatants.name: Heartbore Mage
combatants.note: Above. One bores; one guards with counterspell.

combatants.name: Horned Colossus of Demonholme
combatants.note: Ignores creatures unless they damage it twice in a round; its war is with the trunk.

tree.name: Aedlab - the trunk
tree.modes: HORNS ONLY (the fiction - it slams its horns into the trunk): 2x(4d10+9), average 62 a round, about ten working rounds. FULL MULTIATTACK (horns + slam, both doubled by Siege Monster): 2x(4d10+9) + 2x(4d8+9), average 116 a round, about six working rounds. At +14 against a trunk it misses only on a natural 1 - the tracker rolls that check per attack. Or roll at the table and type the damage in; the tracker is bookkeeping, not the boss.
tree.valve: Three release valves, DM-only. DISTRACTED: the party dealt it damage twice this round (Mission Discipline) - the clock pauses, no trunk damage. REINFORCE: quietly add hit points mid-fight - druidic resilience nobody sees, the invisible thumb on the scale. FELL IT NOW: drop the tree on the dramatic beat regardless of the number - the fall lands where the story needs it.
tree.canon: The fall is canon: the clock controls WHEN, never IF. However the dice land, 9.6 - The Tree Falls - fires as written: everyone aboard braces, the demon steps aside to keep fighting, and the protective magic dies with the fall.

battle.tactics: THE IRON LOGIC (say it in your head every round): the fight below exists to kidnap the Defenders; the fight above exists to take the heart. The demons fly direct, take the objective if ever possible, and abandon anyone out of position. NEITHER STRIKE TEAM HELPS THE OTHER. Each teleports away the moment its mission completes - the black glabrezu with captured Defenders, the red with the heart if it can get it.
battle.adjusting: Weaker party: drop one fanatic below and the second mage above; the colossus needs three cumulative trunk-rounds more. Stronger party: the red glabrezu opens with confusion into the platform stack, and both mages carry shield. (With the tree clock in play, the same knob in hit points: three trunk-rounds ≈ +350 HP at full output, +190 at horns-only - or just pull REINFORCE live and nobody ever knows.)
battle.aftermath: However the fronts resolve, scene 9.4 offers the counter-punch and 9.5 explains the hooded figure who is NOT on anyone's side.

scenes.development: If the party retreated to Oospufmorn: scene 9.4. If they held the platform: run 9.4's dwarven arrival at Aedlab directly and skip the rally.

script.text: Zontif, landing: 'You must defend the heart of the tree at all costs!' - the Defenders dive to meet the ground assault. The party must split its attention or split itself; either hurts, on purpose.

THE IRON LOGIC - say it in your head every round: below exists to KIDNAP THE DEFENDERS, above exists to TAKE THE HEART, the colossus works the TRUNK. Neither strike team helps the other. Each teleports away the moment its mission completes.
Heart-wrenching screams from below punctuate the platform fight. When the last standing Defender falls, the ground force rewards the platform with fireballs.
A tactical retreat through the platform circle to Oospufmorn is the right call - leave that door open. Then 9.4, or straight to the dwarven arrival if they held.

scenes.title: The Counter-Charge

boxed.title: The City Below the Bare Tree
boxed.text: The circle sets you down on Oospufmorn's platform, and the first thing you notice is the quiet - no barrier hum, no canopy overhead: bare boughs, and autumn leaves drifting across boards that once held a heart. The city saw you arrive. Word runs down the great stair faster than you ever could - the Champions are back, and they came through at a run. Below, along the avenues and the tree-green, faces turn upward: the tree watch on the stair, dock hands, shopkeeps, families who stood in these same streets the day the leaves turned and could do nothing but watch. They are not afraid of you. They are waiting. The whole city feels like a held breath - like tinder, waiting for one voice to strike.

scenes.body: AN IF, NOT A STOP: this scene fires ONLY if the party took 9.3's open door - the tactical retreat through the platform circle to Oospufmorn. (If they held the platform, skip the rally entirely: Knight Ordran Dwokhumilin and his advance Knights teleport straight onto Aedlab's field, answering the request sent at the battle's onset, and the chapter loses nothing but the speech.) A party that runs is buying respite - and, if they think of it, reinforcement - but a table that just fled a losing field may not see what running made possible. The DM's job is to hint, never to hand: THE HINTS (Mechanics) are five doors to open softly. And the city is ripe for the asking - since the day the heart was carried away, Oospufmorn stands bare over the Twins with no barrier and no secrets, and every soul below knows exactly what a demon can take from them. One rousing speech from a PC can win that crowd, and the guards standing in it: THE RALLY roll decides how many rise. In the record this is precisely what happened - a speech recruited every available guard, the debate on timing got tense, and mid-debate the dwarven ADVANCE Knights teleported in, the answer to a request sent at the battle's onset, the main support still on schedule. Then everyone squeezes onto the circle: re-entry at Aedlab in under thirty seconds, landing at an angle that tumbles the careless (DC 10 DEX or arrive prone, weapons everywhere, dignity nowhere).

blocks.text: THE IF: 9.4 exists for the party that RAN. Retreat is not defeat - it is the beat where the table catches its breath and the world offers help to those who ask. Nothing here fires on its own: if nobody reaches for any of it, hint - an NPC voice, a guard's question, a moment of quiet. If the party held the platform at Aedlab, run only the Knights' arrival, there, and skip the rest of this scene.

blocks.title: THE HINTS
blocks.sub: five doors a running party may not see - open them softly, one at a time
lines: TRIAGE - the breather is real: bind wounds, drink the potions, count who is still standing. (The clock still runs - every minute away is trunk damage. Say so once, and only once.)
THE CROWD - the city watched them arrive at a run. Let a guard of the tree watch ask it for them: 'Champions - what's happened? What do you need?' That question is the door to the speech.
THE REQUEST SENT - remind whoever sent word to the dwarves at the battle's onset: an answer may yet come. (It does - mid-debate.)
THE AMBUSH - the circle lands where they left it. The enemy knows where the door is, but not WHEN it opens: coming back is an entrance the party gets to choose.
THE TIMING DEBATE - let it get tense. Rest longer and return stronger, or return now and save more? There is no right answer; the debate itself is the scene - and the Knights interrupt it.

blocks.title: THE SPEECH
blocks.sub: the city is ripe - hand it to a PC and let them win the crowd
lines: Stage it: the platform rail or the great stair, the crowd upturned, the tree watch in earshot. The player gives it in their own words - a single sentence is enough if it lands.
The crowd is primed by canon: they stood in these streets the day the heart was carried away, with nothing to swing at. This is the first time anyone has offered them a way to swing back.

Then THE RALLY: Charisma (Persuasion or Performance) by the speaker; one other PC can Help by standing with them. Intimidation can force bodies onto the circle, but caps the result at the 10-14 row - fear follows orders; it does not volunteer.
Advantage if the speech names the day the leaves turned - the wound this city already carries.

blocks.title: THE RALLY - WHO RISES
blocks.sub: one roll; read the row it reaches. This is the crowd's answer, not the DM's

rows.note: The shamed few: 1d6+2 guards step forward anyway - every one of them stood the tree watch the day the heart was taken. No officers.
A squad: twelve guards and a corporal of the tree watch. The rest hold the tree - someone must.
The watch empties: two dozen guards, both corporals, and a sergeant who takes the charge; a skeleton crew stays on the boards.

The record's outcome: EVERY available guard, the full watch with its officers - and Captain Maros Softblossom takes the charge himself, sword drawn, the crowd roaring them onto the circle. Armed citizens push forward too; whether any are taken is the party's call, made out loud, with the city listening.

blocks.text: Faces for the rally, from the record's own muster list - rename freely: ALAS PAWRAEK, NEREMYN VADI, MARIONA CARKAS, AYDA OLOLAMIN. Stat: Guard (officers: Veteran; Softblossom: Knight). Below a 20, Captain Softblossom holds the tree - someone must - but gives the watch leave to choose, which is its own small speech.
Town guards charging down the ramp to stab at a forty-foot demon, knowing exactly what it costs, is the emotional center of this chapter. Name two of them. One should survive.

scenes.development: However many rise, the return is the same door: the platform circle, the tumble of the landing, and the fight exactly as they left it - back into 9.3's field, with 9.5 (Nika Blackthorn) waiting for the moment the battle goes to ground. If the party never ran, none of this fired: the Knights arrive at Aedlab, and the chapter loses nothing but the speech.

script.text: AN IF, NOT A STOP: run this scene only if the party retreated to Oospufmorn. If they held the platform, the advance Knights teleport straight onto Aedlab's field - skip the rally and rejoin at the landing. A party that ran bought respite and maybe reinforcement; they may not see it. Hint, never hand - THE HINTS (Mechanics) are five doors: triage, the crowd, the request sent, the ambush, the timing debate.
Push the arrival: the bare tree, the held-breath city, the faces turning up. The city is ripe - let a guard of the tree watch ask, 'Champions - what's happened? What do you need?'

push.label: The City Below the Bare Tree

script.text: Hand the speech to a PC and let them give it in their own words. Then THE RALLY (Mechanics): Charisma (Persuasion or Performance), one Helper; read the row the roll reaches - that is the crowd's answer. Give the risers faces: Alas Pawraek, Neremyn Vadi, Mariona Carkas, Ayda Ololamin.
Mid-debate on timing, the dwarven advance Knights teleport in - Knight Ordran Dwokhumilin, answering the request sent at the battle's onset; the main force is still on schedule.
Everyone squeezes onto the circle: re-entry at Aedlab in under thirty seconds, DC 10 DEX or arrive prone, weapons everywhere, dignity nowhere.
Town guards charging down the ramp at a forty-foot demon, knowing what it costs, is the emotional center of this chapter. Name two of them. One should survive.

scenes.title: Nika Blackthorn
scenes.body: DM ONLY. The seventh hooded figure - NIKA BLACKTHORN - is NOT Essax's. When the battle goes to ground she slips in, collects the unconscious Defenders, moves them out through the very hole the enemy entered by - no bracelet on her own wrist, no Defender's hand-motions; the way simply stands open - HEALS them (visibly - let the party SEE the healing land; it is the only mercy on this field), then triggers a teleportation pyramid and is gone. Her parting line, if pursued or hailed: 'I am trying to SAVE them, you idiot. Retrieve them at Terrid Hall if you're so daring. Come to the Bronze Storm empire and see what you've done.' THE SEED: a party that learned the bracelet at 8.3 should be allowed to notice two wrongnesses here, unprompted - the hole that never closes, and (Perception DC 13, automatic for the Warden's Child) Zontif's wrist, BARE as she is carried through. Describe; do not explain. 9.6 pays it.
scenes.mechanics: THE EXIT VALVE: her portal is a door out of the campaign, and the warning already happened - the pull-aside at the top of the session (chapter running note / 9.1), out of character: going through a portal alone, with enemies obviously on the other side of it, can take your character out of the campaign; this is why the table built backup characters (0.1). So if a PC squeezes through her closing portal anyway, do not stop the scene - resolve it straight: the character exits the campaign's stage, carried with Nika Blackthorn and the Defenders to the Bronze Storm empire, and the player comes back in on their BACKUP character (0.1). The Terrid Hall thread keeps a timed return on the table if the story reaches for it - but the backup holds the seat, and the warned dive is the player's own.

script.text: DM only. The seventh hooded figure - NIKA BLACKTHORN - is NOT Essax's. When the battle goes to ground she collects the unconscious Defenders, moves them out through the hole the enemy came in by, and HEALS them - visibly. Let the party SEE the healing land; it is the only mercy on this field.

THE SEED: let a watcher notice (Perception DC 13; automatic for the Warden's Child) that the way stands OPEN for her - no bracelet, no hand-motions - and that Zontif's wrist, as she is carried through, is BARE. Describe; do not explain. 9.6 pays it.
Her parting line if pursued or hailed: 'I am trying to SAVE them, you idiot. Retrieve them at Terrid Hall if you're so daring. Come to the Bronze Storm empire and see what you've done.'

THE EXIT VALVE: the pull-aside at the top of the session already said it plainly - a portal taken alone, with enemies obviously on the other side, can take a character out of the campaign. If a PC dives through anyway, do not stop the scene: they are gone with Nika Blackthorn to the Bronze Storm empire, and the player comes back in on their backup character (0.1). The Terrid Hall thread keeps a timed return on the table.

scenes.title: The Tree Falls
scenes.body: Spellcasters dispatched, the black glabrezu slain (somebody at your table just earned the title DEMON SLAYER - say it out loud), the colossus keeps slamming its horns into the trunk. The tree is felled even in victory: everyone aboard braces, the demon steps aside to keep fighting, and the protective magic dies with the fall. Its heated bronze collar finishes it as the party lands the killing blows (see the stat block - below half HP the collar sears it berserk, and the collar itself becomes the kill). When the field settles, the breach point should be walked: Zontif's Key Bracelet lies in the grass OUTSIDE where the wall stood - the reveal 9.2 promised, and the party's to assemble (see the script).

blocks.text: Rosters, for texture: dwarven troop - 95 soldiers; mages/clerics Dubida Mudfoot and Snagnoud Bonebringer; veteran Moggar Brightbuckle; Knight Ordran Dwokhumilin. Elven troop - 24 scouts, the Druid Luvon Trisbalar at their head.

blocks.title: RP - THE PROCLAMATION AT THE STUMP
blocks.sub: play it, don't narrate it - pick a route, let an officer say the word out loud
lines: THE SHAPE OF THE MOMENT (source-true): introductions to the Knight - the tense peace with the elven troop - counsel WITH the party - the decision - the word. The proclamation is the dwarves' payment of trust: the party gave the Empire a heart; the realm answers with its oldest secret.

ROUTE 1 - THE KNIGHT'S WORD (default). Ordran, fewest words possible: 'The heart cannot stay under open sky. It goes below - to the Grand Vaults of Bhindarul, in Knakknthazn.' A beat. 'That name is not spoken up here. Neither is the next, and I will say it once, so you know what manner of door we offer: the trees are not four. A fifth stands, untouched, below the world - KNOBDIMMON. Every dwarf in our realm would die before either is taken. That is the vault we offer.'

ROUTE 2 - THE CLERICS' RITE. Dubida and Snagnoud ward the heart as they trade lines like one speaker: 'Four the surface counts-' '-and four the surface keeps.' 'One the deep holds-' '-and the deep has never lost.' Together, the name: 'KNOBDIMMON.' Ordran, flat, to the party: 'Now you carry a secret of the dwarven realm. We guard it like a fifth heart. So will you.'

ROUTE 3 - THE VETERAN'S OBJECTION (can precede either route). Moggar, low, eyes on twenty-four surface bows: 'Twenty-four elven bows, and we speak of it HERE?' Ordran's ruling carries the Thane's own logic: 'The name was never the lock, Brightbuckle. The realm is the lock.' (If a player later asks why the secret could be spoken at all - that line is the answer.)

KIN AT THE STUMP (conditional): if the Thane's-Grandchild seat is in play, Ordran's gauntlet comes off before rank does - a forearm clasp first, the proclamation after. 'Your grandmother will want this tale from your own mouth. Come home and tell it.' Skip cleanly if the seat is empty.

THE SEAL, SHOWN (optional, either route): Snagnoud produces the vault warrant - wax the color of forge-slag, pressed with a sigil on no surface map: a fifth tree. And IF the dwarven-made brooch from the underbelly desk is in anyone's pack, one of the pair goes still mid-rite: 'Where did you come by this?' Held beside the wax, the match is exact.

HOW THE CONTINGENCY ACTS: Ordran shows, never explains (the record has him stepping onto a circle and vanishing wordless); the mage-cleric pair finish each other's sentences; Moggar posts where he can watch the treeline and the portal-scar both, and counts the elves twice; the ninety-five hold ranks in silence until the word is spoken - then the whole contingency turns as one to face the stump.

blocks.title: RP - SAVING THE TREE
blocks.sub: 'to no avail,' with dignity
lines: THE PRINCIPLE: let every idea be tried and answered honestly by the right voice - no stonewalling; each no teaches the world. The brainstorm is canon: the party tried to save the mighty tree, to no avail.
HEALING MAGIC - Snagnoud, hand flat on the bark: 'I can close a wound. This is not a wound. The life has gone out from under it - there is nothing left to knit to.'

THE DRUID'S VERDICT (Luvon arrives mid-discussion; his no lands hardest): he kneels, palm to the heartwood, the longest silence of the scene, then - 'You cannot save the tree. You already saved what the tree was for.' The mercy line: it reframes 'saved' for the whole table.

REPLANT IT? GROW A NEW ONE FROM THE HEART? - Dubida: 'A cutting grows a tree. A heart is not a cutting. What a heart grows - none living have seen it tried.' (Deliberately does not foreclose the future; keeps the mystery.)
THE VETERAN'S SUMMARY - Moggar, measuring the stump while the casters debate: 'Save what can be carried.' The pivot line, straight into the council.
DM NOTE: if the table reaches for miracle-tier magic, the officers go quiet - this is above every pay grade at the stump; that question belongs to bigger powers, later chapters.

blocks.title: THE CIRCLE IN THE GRASS
blocks.sub: the platform's portal - down, not out
lines: If the PCs search the aftermath, they come upon it with NO CHECK: the platform's permanent teleportation circle, knocked off WHOLE when the tree came down, lying slanted on the rocky, grassy ground where it landed.
DC 17 Arcana: it is still usable - sound, and it will activate with the proper incantation, slant and all.
DC 10 Arcana: it resists any movement away from the center of the stump. It CAN be moved with great force - but force begins eroding the sigils and the combined magics that make it work.

blocks.text: FOOTNOTE - A DOOR FOR NEW BLOOD: the arrivals are the cleanest entrance in the book for a replacement character (the backup rule, 0.1) - a hero who fell in the battle, or who chased the portal in 9.5 and sits imprisoned beyond it, is succeeded here. The new character marches with the ninety-five, walks among the twenty-four, or arrives on the column's heels with business of their own at the stump. One introduction at the council, and they are inside the secret with everyone else.

scenes.development: Council at the stump: the Tree Heart of Aedlab goes to the GRAND VAULTS OF BHINDARUL, Knakknthazn - and with that decision, in front of the party, the word is spoken above ground and the seal explained: a FIFTH sacred tree. KNOBDIMMON. Teleport with a Council-of-Twelve guard detail; exit a cave outlet into Bhindarul proper - open dark above, a city outlined in candlelit windows and blue street lamps; a 'Transportation' building with no vehicles, just a small circle under an archway that Knight Ordran steps onto and vanishes from. The Low Keep's marble entrance hall; apartments for the party; and the best sleep anyone has had in a month.

script.text: Spellcasters down, the black glabrezu slain - somebody at your table just earned the title DEMON SLAYER; say it out loud - and the colossus keeps slamming its horns into the trunk.

The tree falls even in victory: everyone aboard braces, the demon steps aside to keep fighting, the protective magic dies with the fall. Below half HP, the heated collar sears it berserk - and the collar itself becomes the kill.
Push the fall: the heart exposed and whole in the burst trunk, LARGER than the others, the horns from the treeline, ninety-five dwarves, twenty-four elven scouts with a druid at their head.

THE BRACELET IN THE GRASS: when the field settles, anyone walking where the breach opened finds it OUTSIDE the line the barrier held - Zontif's green-gem Key Bracelet, unbroken, lying exactly where its Defender left it and cannot remember doing so. The party has every piece: a bracelet no Defender removes (8.3), a wrist that was bare (9.5), and one of their own who was taken, read, and wiped the same way (7.7/9.1). Let THEM assemble it - an inside job that nobody committed. Land it as violation, never blame; the council at the stump can confirm the ritual's shape. Then the bracelet goes home: to the Warden's Child if that seat is in play - or held for Zontif, against Terrid Hall.

SAVING THE TREE: the brainstorm is canon - the party tried to save the mighty tree, to no avail. Let every idea be tried and answered honestly by the right voice - no stonewalling; each no teaches the world. RP - SAVING THE TREE (Mechanics) has the voices, and the druid's verdict lands hardest.

THE CIRCLE IN THE GRASS: if they walk the field they come upon it with no check - the platform's teleportation circle, knocked off whole, slanted where it landed. DC 17 Arcana confirms it still works; DC 10 Arcana learns the price of moving it away from the stump. The card has the rest.

Council at the stump: the heart - freed from the wreck and borne to the tree's grave - goes to the GRAND VAULTS OF BHINDARUL - and in front of the party, Knakknthazn is spoken above ground and the seal explained: a FIFTH sacred tree. KNOBDIMMON. Play the proclamation, don't narrate it - pick a route from RP - THE PROCLAMATION AT THE STUMP (Mechanics), let an officer say the word out loud - and push the word as it lands.
Teleport with a Council guard detail; the cave outlet, the Low Keep, apartments, and the best sleep anyone has had in a month.

boxed.title: The Fallen Giant
boxed.text: The tree did not break clean. The length of it lies across the field, and where the platform rode the trunk - where they bored and clawed to reach what it held - the fall has finished what they started: that whole section has burst open, heartwood splintered wide to the sky. And deep in the break, something catches the light: a tree heart, exposed and WHOLE - and it is LARGER than the others. Then horns, from the treeline: the promised main force arrives from the dwarven realm, ninety-five soldiers in ordered ranks - and behind them, quiet as weather, an elven troop of twenty-four scouts with a druid at their head.

boxed.title: The Word Below the World
boxed.text: The ninety-five have stood in silence since the horns. Now, on no order you can hear, the whole contingency turns as one to face the stump. Iron creaks; a standard dips. When the word comes, it comes quiet - a name the surface has never spoken, set down before you like something heavy laid gently on stone: KNOBDIMMON. The trees are not four. They never were. And below the world, one still stands untouched. Ninety-five fists strike ninety-five chests, once - like a door closing.

chapters.chapterDevelopment: Milestone: 9th level. The scoreboard is brutal and honest: one tree standing (hidden), one heart saved (the largest), Defenders alive but TAKEN, a demon slayer named, and the party inside the one realm Essax cannot touch. Chapter 10 is the breath before the plunge.

chapters.title: Bhindarul
chapters.overview: The hidden realm, at last: a 250-mile stone dome under a lake, a grandmotherly Thane with a beard to her belt and a story that reframes the entire war, a goddess who answers three questions badly - and a captured portal-demon whose archway is the road to Hell. In-world: the days immediately after Aedlab's fall; the clock says SEVEN DAYS.
chapters.running:
Chapter 10 is the campaign's second downtime hub wearing a countdown. The Commune answers in 10.2 set the tempo - seven days - and everything else is the party choosing how to spend them. (The number is BUILT before it is confirmed: 10.2's war-count argues it at maps, and the goddess hardens it - never let seven arrive from nowhere.) Kili's tale (10.3) is the chapter's heart: deliver it as a monologue, trim to your table's patience, and do not paraphrase the Bobby material - the campaign's villain becomes a person in this scene, and the war becomes a family tragedy. The treasure dive now lives in SIDE QUESTS (The Treasure of the Twins Channel): open the moment the rumor lands, and if the table spends one of the seven days on it, schedule it before the tale so the tonal drop lands.

THE HONEST-TIME KIT: the truth that Demonholme keeps Material time is available twice before the gate — the Commune's one straight answer (10.2) and the Thane's line about the old war (10.3). Start the console's SEVEN DAYS clock when the Commune lands; the banner counts down as the calendar advances, and the date push carries the count to the players.

scenes.title: The Hidden Fifth

boxed.title: The Hidden Fifth
boxed.text: The cave outlet opens and Bhindarul opens with it: a dark that is not empty but INHABITED - a city outlined in candlelit windows and blue street lamps, streets that glitter faintly with worked stone, and far overhead, where a sky should be, the honest black of a mountain's heart. Two hundred and fifty miles of dome, and every foot of it is home to someone.

boxed.title: The Court's Other Guest
boxed.text: The Low Keep's marble hall is not quite empty. By the great hearth, tuning a lute with unhurried patience, sits a half-elf in traveling clothes a shade too worn for the room - and when he looks up, the smile arrives before the accent does, and the accent is from the wrong side of the border. 'They let me in the front door,' he says, reading your faces exactly right. 'Which should tell you something about the people who did the checking. Alias - storyteller, collector of roads. The court keeps me for the tales the mountain cannot grow on its own.'

scenes.body: Realm mechanics the party experiences immediately (from the world lore, now firsthand): no scrying reaches this realm; the climate is unreasonably pleasant; and every citizen is baptized-sealed against revealing Knobdimmon - which makes the party, who were TOLD, honored guests of a specific and heavy kind. The Low Keep hosts them; the vault holds two hearts now (Aedlab's giant heart beside the realm's own reserve); and word comes that the Thane will see them tomorrow. One more introduction waits at the Low Keep: ALIAS, a half-elf storyteller out of the Bronze Storm Empire - vetted by the court, vouched reputable, and inside the realm's trust before the party ever arrived. His contacts reach roads the realm cannot walk (10.2), and his rumors are good (10.4). Some at the table will trust him instantly; some will call him spy. Both are right to wonder - 10.2's Commune answers UNCERTAIN, and the book keeps it that way. If the table takes to him, the long play lives in CONTINGENCY C5.
scenes.development: Errands first (10.2), audience after (10.3) - or reverse it if your table runs impatient. The seven-day clock starts at the Commune.

script.text: The cave outlet opens - push Bhindarul, and give the dome its due: two hundred and fifty miles, every foot of it home to someone.

The realm firsthand: no scrying reaches here; the climate is unreasonably pleasant; every citizen is baptism-sealed against revealing Knobdimmon - which makes a party who was TOLD honored guests of a specific and heavy kind.
The Low Keep hosts them; the vault holds two hearts now; word comes that the Thane will see them tomorrow.

The Low Keep holds one more guest: ALIAS, the court's storyteller - Bronze Storm-born, vetted and found reputable by a realm that never lets anyone in. Push him introducing himself. Some will trust him instantly; some will call spy. Both are right to wonder - and if he attaches himself to the party, the long play is CONTINGENCY C5.
Errands first, audience after - or reverse it if your table runs impatient. The seven-day clock starts at the Commune.

time.label: The road to the hidden fifth

scenes.title: Commune, and Errands of the Almost-Doomed

boxed.title: The Rite of Three Questions
boxed.text: The clerics do not take you to a temple. They take you DOWN - past the vault doors, to a worked hollow where roots run through the living stone like veins of silver, and every root runs toward the deep tree. Snagnoud Bonebringer sets three candles on the altar stone. 'The goddess grants three questions,' he says, 'and she answers plainly - which is worse.' Dubida Mudfoot lights the first candle and finishes the thought the way the two of them always do: 'Most who stand here spend a year choosing. You have tonight. Ask what you cannot afford to guess.'

scenes.body: The chapter's hinge, run as a sequence, not a verdict: the realm argues SEVEN DAYS out loud at maps (THE WAR-COUNT), the goddess is asked to confirm it (THE RITE - the players phrase the questions themselves), and the answers come back verbatim from the record: WILL ESSAX TRY TO CLAIM ANOTHER TREE HEART WITHIN 7 DAYS? - YES. IS ALIAS TO BE TRUSTED? - UNCERTAIN. SHOULD THE CHAMPIONS RESCUE THEIR LOST MEMBER? - NO. Sit with that last one; it stings on purpose - and then, unlike the record, walk the table to the WHY (THE PROOF OF SAFETY): they can reach their lost member, and the answer is still no, and those two facts together are the lesson. Logistics attach themselves: escort Gagnot Axeborn is assigned to the party; the wizard Dalothun Gravelbreaker teleports errands. In Yuvl Ilmern the deed office recognizes the party's name - fame has beaten them home. (Gelf's diamond store, two blocks east of Go Figure, for the arcane-focus shoppers.)

blocks.text: RUN IT AS A SEQUENCE: 10.2 is four beats wearing one scene key. (1) THE WAR-COUNT - the realm argues the number in front of the party. (2) THE RITE - the players phrase the three questions and the goddess answers. (3) The fallout - TALKING WITH ALIAS and THE PROOF OF SAFETY, spread across the days that follow. (4) The errands. Run them in that order the first time; the SEVEN DAYS clock starts when the Commune lands, and everything after happens with the banner counting.

blocks.title: THE WAR-COUNT
blocks.sub: where SEVEN DAYS comes from - the players hear it argued before any goddess confirms it
lines: The pieces the court lays on the table (Snagnoud, Dubida, and Knight Ordran, maps out, the night the party arrives - or fold it into 10.3 if the audience runs first): Essax holds THREE hearts, and three are enough to raise the lesser crossing - the plane-shift that carries Kelethtonreth, his minions, and a piece of his realm across. Kili says it plainly in 10.4; here it is the war-masters' working assumption.
The deep watch at the far-side camp (10.4) reports the ritual fires were lit the night Aedlab fell - and when the crossing stands, the only hearts left outside his hand sit in THIS vault.

Three days are already spent - the fall, the road, the arrival - and the clerics admit their count is soft: 'A tenday from first fire, if his ritualists were men. They are not.' The honest window could be seven days; it could be less. The court needs to KNOW.

So the first question is not scripted, it is NEEDED: the court asks the party to put the sharp version to the goddess - WITHIN SEVEN DAYS? When YES comes back, the soft estimate hardens into the campaign's clock. Count it on your fingers in front of the players: ten from first fire, three gone, and the goddess just confirmed the remainder.

blocks.title: THE RITE
blocks.sub: the players phrase the questions - staging and steering
lines: Who casts: Snagnoud Bonebringer officiates at the deep altar of Essa, Goddess of All That Grows - the trees are hers. A party cleric or druid may hold the rite instead; the realm provides the incense and the candles either way, and Snagnoud stands second without a flicker of pride.

Three questions, yes-or-no form, one casting. Do NOT hand the players the record's list - let them argue it. The officiant coaches phrasing ('The goddess answers the question you ASK, not the one you meant'), and the table choosing what it cannot afford to guess is the whole RP of the beat.

The steer, if they drift: the court openly needs the war-count tested (question one asks itself); Alias is the only stranger inside a realm that admits no strangers (someone will want question two); and the empty chair at their own fire asks question three without a word from you.

Off-script questions: answer in the goddess' voice - short, true, unhelpful at the edges. Anything the book answers elsewhere may be confirmed here; anything it does not, UNCERTAIN is always honest. If the table spends a question on Demonholme time, give the TIME BELOW answer and count it a mercy.

IF NO MEMBER WAS LOST (a table where nobody took the 9.5 portal): the third question becomes the taken Defenders - SHOULD THE CHAMPIONS RESCUE THE DEFENDERS OF THE TREES? - and the answer is the same NO, for the same arithmetic.

blocks.title: THE ANSWERS
blocks.sub: verbatim from the record - and how to land each one
lines: WILL ESSAX TRY TO CLAIM ANOTHER TREE HEART WITHIN 7 DAYS? - YES. Land it as confirmation, not news: the room exhales, Ordran starts writing orders. The estimate the party heard argued is now a fact with their names on it.

IS ALIAS TO BE TRUSTED? - UNCERTAIN. The goddess is not being coy - the man is genuinely unresolved (C5). Do not let the table shrug it off: UNCERTAIN, from a goddess who answers plainly, is itself information. It should send them straight to TALKING WITH ALIAS.

SHOULD THE CHAMPIONS RESCUE THEIR LOST MEMBER? - NO. It stings on purpose - but do not leave it as divine cruelty. The goddess is doing arithmetic the party can check themselves: THE PROOF OF SAFETY is how they check it.

blocks.title: TALKING WITH ALIAS
blocks.sub: UNCERTAIN is an invitation - conversations that must be available, not optional
lines: He knows what was asked - the Low Keep keeps no secrets from its own hearth - and he does not dodge: 'UNCERTAIN. I have been called worse, by better.' He makes himself available all seven days: at meals, on errands, tuning the lute by the vault stair. Every conversation the table wants, he grants.

Asked point-blank whose side he is on: 'The story's. It is the only side that has ever taken me.' - and he means it (C5, PLAYING THE UNCERTAIN: Insight reads him sincere because he IS sincere; detection magic finds no fiend, no charm, no lie - the ambiguity is biographical, not magical).

Give both camps ammunition on schedule: for every kindness that looks like proof, one detail that does not add up - a border checkpoint he knew too well, a Bronze Storm marching song he stopped humming mid-bar. Ten missing years he will not explain, deflected with a true story about a different decade.

What the conversations BUY, either way: his contacts carry letters where no realm road runs - including toward Terrid Hall (THE PROOF OF SAFETY) - and his rumor pays out in 10.4 (CAL NAI). If the table takes to him and he asks to walk their road, that is CONTINGENCY C5, and it starts in these seven days.

blocks.title: THE PROOF OF SAFETY
blocks.sub: why the answer is NO - lead the table to it, do not tell them
lines: Let them try to reach their lost member - encourage it. A SENDING gets through, and an answer comes back in the member's own voice (twenty-three words; the spell allows twenty-five - rewrite it in the voice of the character your table actually lost): 'Alive. Unhurt. Held at Terrid Hall - guest and prisoner both. They watch me always. Do not come. Save the tree. I will keep.'

A SCRY works too - Bhindarul's veil turns eyes coming IN, not eyes cast OUT (say so plainly if a caster hesitates). The water shows a high window, bronze banners, books, a guard who never leaves the door - and the lost member alive, unhurt, pacing like someone keeping their own count. Comfort that is also custody.

Now the NO is arithmetic the table can do without the goddess: their member is SAFE and the tree is not. Terrid Hall is an empire away; seven days spent marching at it are seven days handed to Essax - and the crossing, once raised, comes for the vault their member would want held. The goddess did not forbid the rescue. She priced it, for THIS week.

SAY THE QUIET PART AT THE TABLE (out of character, once): the empty chair is empty because its player chose the portal with eyes open - the 9.5 pull-aside and the backup rule (0.1) were the warning, given and taken. The NO is the campaign agreeing with the table's own rules, not punishing them. And the door is not closed: the rescue keeps.

THE THREAD HELD OPEN: Terrid Hall is a place on the map now, with a named prisoner in it. Beside Nika Blackthorn's standing invitation (12.5) and Alias' road home (C5), it is the third thread into the campaign after this one - or a side quest the moment your table refuses to leave it alone. If they go back for their own, that is not a failure of this book; it is the next one.

blocks.text: LOGISTICS: escort Gagnot Axeborn is assigned to the party for the realm's roads; the wizard Dalothun Gravelbreaker teleports errands. In Yuvl Ilmern the deed office recognizes the party's name - fame has beaten them home. (Gelf's diamond store, two blocks east of Go Figure, for the arcane-focus shoppers.) Letters go out by Alias' contacts if the party writes them; reports to Kili get a grandmother's reply: thank you - keep the reports coming.

TIME BELOW: if anyone asks about time on Demonholme (a later Commune, a prayer, or plain worry), the answer comes back unnervingly straight — because it is the cruelest answer available: 'BELOW, THE DAYS ARE THE SAME DAYS. THE TREE WILL NOT WAIT FOR YOU.' If nobody thinks to ask, any divine caster may make a DC 12 Religion check to recall that planar time on Demonholme runs lockstep with the Material — no slippage, no mercy.

scenes.development: The NO is a door held open, not closed: Terrid Hall now has a name, a window, and a prisoner keeping their own count. Beside Nika Blackthorn's invitation (12.5) and Alias' road (C5), it is a standing thread for a side quest or the next campaign - whenever the table comes back for their own.

script.text: The war-count first, at maps: Essax holds three hearts, three raise the lesser crossing, the deep watch saw the ritual fires lit the night Aedlab fell - and the clerics' tenday is soft. Count it on your fingers: ten from first fire, three gone. Let somebody doubt the seven out loud; that doubt is exactly what the rite is for.
Down past the vault doors to the deep altar - push the rite. Three candles, three questions, and the PLAYERS phrase all three; the record's list is your steer, not their script.

The answers, verbatim from the record: WILL ESSAX TRY WITHIN 7 DAYS - YES. IS ALIAS TO BE TRUSTED - UNCERTAIN. SHOULD THE CHAMPIONS RESCUE THEIR LOST MEMBER - NO. The first lands as confirmation, the second as an invitation, the third stings on purpose - and this time the book explains it.
UNCERTAIN sends them to the hearth: Alias grants every conversation, reads sincere because he is, and hands both camps ammunition on schedule. If the table takes to him, Contingency C5 starts here.

Let them reach for their lost member and SUCCEED: the sending answered, the scry clear - alive, unhurt, held at Terrid Hall. Then let the table do the arithmetic the goddess did. The rescue is not refused; it is deferred - and the thread stays open past the last page.
Logistics attach: escort Gagnot Axeborn, the wizard Dalothun for teleport errands, and a deed office in Yuvl Ilmern that already knows their name - fame has beaten them home.
Seven days. Say the number out loud and keep saying it.

time.label: Errands of the almost-doomed — how many days spent?

scenes.title: The Thane's Tale
scenes.boxedText:
A hundred twenty-nine years ago, Arith - our fair Empress - was nineteen. Abra, father of the Steward of Pand, was a strapping barbarian of twenty-two. El was about as old as I am now. Lebby was there of course - grandfather of the Lord of Teg, so much grandeur. Lid joined the world late, from the monastery, an adult at sixty-five.

We were just a group of adventurers - a troop of friends fastened together by the will of the universe. We were Kaddrin Vurrath - the Banner of the Red Hawk.

And we were THERE. There when Kelethtonreth stepped through the portal onto our plane and began the devastation of Arret. Before the great wall was erected and split the land as a barrier against his armies. Before he was pushed back into Demonholme to sit, and stew, and plot.

Essax was there too. Not Essax then - young Bobby. Robert when they were testy. A gaunt young tiefling with a chip on their shoulder, but a nice enough person, most days.

We were all there when Kelethtonreth was sealed - but not before he reached out with his mind and touched each of us, telling us he knew who we were, and how he would gain his revenge.

It drove young Bobby insane. Drove them to terrible things to gain favor with Kelethtonreth - perhaps to stay their own punishment. Sad, truly. Though we never thought it would come to this.

blocks.title: KILI DWOKHUMILIN, THANE OF KNAKKNTHAZN
lines: A grandmotherly dwarf with a luscious gray beard curled to her belt, thanking the party like family - then telling them the truth.

blocks.title: THE STRATEGY
blocks.sub: after the tale
lines: The heart stones serve arcane work as batteries or FOCAL POINTS - here, anchors for a massive plane-shift ritual.
With three hearts Essax can run a lesser version: shift to Demonholme and anchor Kelethtonreth, his minions, and a PIECE of his realm for the crossing.

The fifth heart is safe: 'Every dwarf in this cave system would die to defend it. Essax cannot compete with the arcane and martial might of our realm. Unlike the lands above, we have kept ever vigilant.'

blocks.text: TIME BELOW (folded into the tale, available just by listening): one companion from the old war went through the archway and came back. Kili, without being asked: 'Nine days by his count. Nine days by ours. The dead keep honest time.'

scenes.development: Essax HAS their three hearts. The ritual is not a threat; it is a schedule. The only question left is where the party stands when it fires - and Kili has an answer for that too: 10.4.

script.text: Kili thanks the party like family - then tells them the truth. Push the tale and deliver it as a monologue; trim to your table's patience, but do NOT paraphrase the Bobby material. The villain becomes a person in this scene, and the war becomes a family tragedy.
Let silence do its work after 'we never thought it would come to this.'

Then the strategy: heart stones are batteries and FOCAL POINTS - anchors for a massive plane-shift. With three, Essax runs a lesser version: shift to Demonholme and anchor Kelethtonreth, his minions, and a PIECE of his realm for the crossing.
The fifth heart is safe, and she means every word: 'Every dwarf in this cave system would die to defend it.' Essax HAS their three. The ritual is not a threat; it is a schedule.

scenes.title: The Way Down

blocks.title: THE WAY DOWN
lines: The dwarves captured a THRESHOLD BLIGHT creeping up from the deep and LET it open its archway-portal - to Demonholme, no coincidence - then built a small fortified base camp on the FAR side.
Kili: 'You are welcome to take that route, if you so dare. It will be a hard one.'
Rumor for the road (Alias, DC 15 History or Insight to confirm): a resistance inside the Bronze Storm empire opposes Essax's iron-fist rule. They call themselves CAL NAI - the Red Knife.

scenes.development: Milestone: 10th level. The party stands at a held-open door to Hell with seven days on the clock. Chapter 11 begins when they step through - and the book assumes they do.

script.text: The way down: the dwarves captured a Threshold Blight and LET it open its archway - to Demonholme, no coincidence - then built a fortified base camp on the FAR side. Kili: 'You are welcome to take that route, if you so dare. It will be a hard one.'
Rumor for the road (Alias; DC 15 History or Insight to confirm): a resistance inside the Bronze Storm empire - CAL NAI, the Red Knife.
Milestone: 10th level. A held-open door to Hell, seven days on the clock. Chapter 11 begins when they step through - and the book assumes they do.

time.label: To the archway, and through

chapters.chapterDevelopment: If the party refuses the Demonholme route, the campaign still works: Essax completes the ritual unopposed and Chapter 12's final battle relocates to Arret at catastrophic scale. But the saga's own road went down - and the book is built for the brave.

chapters.title: Demonholme
chapters.overview: Demonholme: blinding snow with no north, worms the size of siege engines that explode when they die, a lava chasm with chaos rules, a cheerful multiversal potion salesman - and at the end of a goddess' directions, a shallow gargantuan bowl where nine mages raise a burning heart inside an invisible fortress. Break one anchor here and the ritual weakens; the party learns Demonholme fights back with geography.
chapters.running:
Demonholme is a character, not a backdrop: it is cold, hostile, and it CHEATS (the Spites in 11.3 exist to prove it). Track exhaustion visibly - the CON saves are the plane's ante, and resource attrition is the real difficulty of this chapter, not any single fight. Bognil (11.4) is the pressure valve: let the table laugh, shop, and overpay before the Bowl. The Bowl itself (11.5) is a puzzle wearing a battle: the Cube of Force's charge pool is the boss's hit points, and the heart's altitude is the timer.

HONEST TIME: every day below burns one of the seven — the gate closing (11.1) and Essax's ritual run on the same clock. There is no sun on Demonholme, so the Pendant is the calendar: at each surface dawn it gives one warm pulse (first pulse boxed in 11.1) — automatic, no check, the tree's pull reaching all the way down. A party that ignored every warning still feels the days being spent; a party that knows exactly what each pulse means gets to sweat. Run the scene time chips and the New Day travel button as normal; the SEVEN DAYS banner decrements itself.

scenes.title: Through the Gate
scenes.boxedText: The archway's cold is a lie about the cold beyond it. You step through into a blinding snowstorm - white in every direction, wind like a grudge - and understand immediately what the dwarves meant when they said there is no north here. There is no anything here. There is only forward, if you can decide what forward means.
scenes.body: Arrival: each PC makes a DC 15 CON save or arrives with one level of exhaustion (cold gear and magic grant advantage - reward preparation loudly). The dwarven base camp at the archway's far side is the last friendly ground: resupply, a garrison of twelve very calm dwarves under Warden-Captain Kadrun Stillhammer, and a standing rule - the gate stays open seven days, then Stillhammer's twelve dispel it themselves, with or without you.
scenes.mechanics:
DIRECTIONS FROM ESSA (a prayer at the camp is answered - with, the cleric swears, a giggle: 'tehe'): 'Since no north and no south exist: walk forward from where you stand now for two days, then traverse the crevasse and follow it for one day to the left. There you will find your quarry.' Scrying confirms: the heart-thief mage is on this plane. The party now owes a goddess a conversation - Chapter 12 collects.

THE PENDANT KEEPS THE COUNT: at each surface dawn, the Pendant of Torrentath pulses once against its bearer — warm, brief, certain. One pulse = one of the seven days spent. Automatic, no check: it is the Champions' boon reaching all the way down.

THE FAITHFUL FEEL IT TOO: at that same prayer, one devoted PC's holy symbol (or a trinket they hold dear) answers Essa's giggle and, from here on, pulses once each surface dawn exactly as the Pendant does. Pick the bearer by precedence — a CLERIC OF ESSA first; failing that a FOLLOWER OF THE SMALL POTATO GOD from Scrapps' wake (their potato-carved token counts, and a potato-god follower takes precedence over a lay worshipper when there is no cleric); failing both, any PC who venerates Essa. Same warm pulse, same honest count — Essa, Goddess of All That Grows, and her small potato-god friend keeping time for their own.

script.text: Push the storm the moment they cross - the cold beyond the archway is worse than the archway's cold, and there is no north here.
Demonholme's ante: DC 15 CON on arrival or one level of exhaustion - cold gear and magic grant advantage; reward preparation loudly. Track exhaustion visibly from here on.

The base camp is the last friendly ground on the plane, and it has faces to bargain with. WARDEN-CAPTAIN KADRUN STILLHAMMER commands the twelve - unhurried, flat, calm the way people get once they have made their peace. QUARTERMASTER VOZMI BACKSTOCK keeps the stores and will sell the party whatever is left in the crates right up until they march - cold-weather gear (advantage on the cold saves), rations, oil, torches, a healing potion or two. HEDDA COALVOW at the forge-wagon patches a weapon or trades a warm cloak for a good story. Let them resupply; the white punishes the unprepared.

Stillhammer delivers the standing order the moment they arrive, flat as slate: 'It has been determined that the portal must be closed in seven days. We will be dispelling it ourselves.' And to anyone who worries about the way home: 'It is not like it would be easy to find your way back here anyway.' Seed it hard - no north, no sun, no landmark; they are in the middle of NOWHERE, and a question put to a god may be the only way to get a direction. Literally.

Take the hint and pray: a plea for bearings at the camp is answered - with, the cleric swears, a giggle: 'tehe.' Two days forward, traverse the crevasse, one day to the left. Scrying confirms the heart-thief mage is on this plane. The party now owes a goddess a conversation; Chapter 12 collects.

THE FAITHFUL FEEL IT TOO: at that same prayer, a devoted PC's holy symbol warms with a pulse of its own and keeps the count from here on, once each surface dawn, like the Pendant. Pick ONE bearer by precedence - a cleric of Essa first; if none, a potato-god follower from Scrapps' wake (their potato token, or a trinket they hold dear); if neither, any PC who venerates Essa. Push 'The First Pulse — the Faithful' to that player.

boxes.title: The First Pulse
boxes.text: There is no morning here. But against your chest, the Pendant beats once — warm, brief, certain — like something far above counting on its fingers.

boxes.title: The First Pulse — the Faithful
boxes.text: There is no morning here. But your holy symbol — or the small dear thing you carry — warms once in your hand, and under it you would swear you catch the faint echo of a giggle: 'tehe.' Something that loves growing things is counting the days right alongside you.

scenes.title: Frost Worms
scenes.body: Day two: ice rubble in the distance, then great holes in the ground - then the ground itself rumbles.

battle.name: The Worms
battle.setup: Two maws crest the ice from opposite quarters. Gargantuan, shrieking, and - the party will learn - volatile.

combatants.name: Frost Worm
combatants.note: Stunning shriek on first emergence; they EXPLODE on death (see the block). Stagger the kills or eat both blasts.

battle.tactics: They burrow between strikes and target whoever is loudest. A moment worth handing over whole: a PC swallowed and spat back out burning by a perfectly timed rebuke - if a player earns it, give it to them.
battle.adjusting: Weaker party: one worm, and the second circles but does not commit. Stronger party: the second worm times its emergence under the party's back line.
battle.aftermath: Nothing worth harvesting but ick, and two craters of frozen ichor. Half a day on: warmth in the air that has no business here. Scene 11.3.

script.text: Day two: ice rubble in the distance, then great holes in the ground - then the ground itself rumbles. Two maws crest from opposite quarters. Roll initiative.
They burrow between strikes and target whoever is loudest - and they are volatile; the party will learn.
A moment worth handing over whole: a PC swallowed and spat back out burning by a perfectly timed rebuke. If a player earns it, give it to them.
Nothing worth harvesting but ick and two craters of frozen ichor. Half a day on: warmth in the air that has no business here. 11.3.

time.label: The march — Essa said two days forward

frostworms.note: A 500-ft square of open snow (100x100). Place the worms hidden (players see nothing), let the party choose where they stand, then Breach (worm surfaces) or Burrow (worm submerges) to punch a 10-ft-wide crater centered on its footprint. Every crater is 30 ft to the first bend - a creature moved into one takes 3d6 falling and the drop applies for the rest of the fight. Spite attacks: Quake (DC 18 DEX or prone + 1 sq random), Stunning Shriek (DC 16 CON, stunned to end of next turn), Maw Snatch & Spit (DC 16, dragged toward the nearest open crater).

scenes.title: The Chasm
scenes.boxedText: Fog envelops you slowly. Brushes of warmth on your cheeks; brimstone in your nostrils. At the crevasse's lip you see what you were feeling: a river of lava, a hundred feet down, three hundred across. Then the snow turns heavy - rain and snowstorm at once, freezing on skin the instant it lands.
scenes.body: Drop the interactive crossing (below) between the party and the far side: one continuous plain of stone tiles and columns over the flow, scrolled left to right. The storm, the winds, the tiles, and Demonholme itself are the opposition - there is no monster here, only the plane. Mirror the ~50-square focus window to the player screen (hazards stay hidden until a tile actually bursts) and let them sweat.

mechanics.title: Crossing the lava - every rule the plane throws

blocks.text: Run it on the interactive map below. Add a token per crosser, drag them across the plain, and let the tools arm tiles, roll the bursts, open the gaps, and fire the Spites.
