The map tracks each crosser's Speed (the highlighted squares are their reach) and Strength (their long jump for clearing gaps); everything the party sees mirrors to the player screen, and everything that can kill them does not. The plain always offers at least two ways across its full length - collapse a lane with bursts or a Spite if you want to force the party single-file.

blocks.title: THE STORM - the ante
lines: Rain and snow at once, freezing on anything warm. Each hour exposed on the crossing: DC 18 CON save or gain a level of exhaustion.
Track it visibly - exhaustion is the real cost of the chasm. A party that dawdles arrives at the Bowl already bleeding levels.

blocks.title: THE LAVA - the ladder (per round in the flow)
lines: Fall onto the surface: 2d10+5 fire.
Sink in: 4d10+10.
Wade: 10d10.
Fully submerged: 18d10.

WATER WALK (a real spell, and it names lava): the target treads the surface and takes NO damage from the crossing at all - no ladder, no fall damage, nothing. The single hardest counter to this whole scene; let a prepared caster feel clever.

blocks.title: FLIGHT - the wind fights you
lines: The storm halves flying speed.
DC 18 Insight or Perception to read the erratic winds above the lava.
A creature that ENDS its move airborne: DC 22 DEX save or wind shear slams it down to surface level - the lava, unless a tile sits under it.

blocks.title: THE TILES - Lava Bursts (rolled on the map below)
lines: Nothing on the plain is armed at the start - it is a creature's weight that sets a tile. At the START of each round, every tile a PC is standing on flips: an unarmed tile arms into a Lava Burst, and an already-armed tile is released by that same weight. (On the map, Start Round does this for the whole party at once; Shift-click sets or releases any stone tile by hand.)

At the END of the round, every PC still standing on an armed tile rolls the tile's Lava Burst (d20, on the map): 10-20 it holds, 1-9 it BURSTS - DC 20 DEX, 5d10 fire (half on a save); miss the save by 10+ and you are thrown one tile in a random direction (d4: 1 forward, 2 right, 3 back, 4 left).
A tile that bursts is GONE - a gap opens where it stood. Cross it with a running long jump (Athletics), or find another route. The map opens and tracks every gap for you.

blocks.title: CREATING FOOTING - the party's own trick
lines: Let clever players make their own path: a bucket of water tipped from a bag of holding, Shape Water, Create or Destroy Water, or an ice spell freezes a square of the flow into standing footing.
On the map, the ❄ Ice tool drops a temporary ice tile over the lava - it holds for a few rounds (you set how many) then melts back into the river. Reward the ingenuity, but keep the clock ticking.

blocks.title: THE SPITE - five times, Demonholme rearranges
lines: FIVE times across the crossing (once per zone), at a moment of your cruel choosing, the plane shifts. Press ▧ Spite on the map and it lifts a SCATTER - a random 16-28% of that zone's standing stone, spread across the whole zone rather than in a line, and never the lava, so a Spite always lands on real footing. The banner names the zone and counts the tiles that went up.

NO MAP? Roll it by hand: d4 for the column (1 Left, 2 Middle, 3 Right, 4 the whole width) and d6 for the row band (1-4, 5-8, 9-12, 13-16, 17-20, 21-24) - that strip flips instead. It is a coarser cut than the map's scatter and a band CAN fall entirely on open lava; re-roll the row if it would flip nothing. Everything below is the same either way.
Flips one through four are armed for a single round - creatures caught on the flip make a DC 15 DEX save or fall prone - then settle back to safe stone if nobody sets them off.
The FIFTH flip does not settle: it ERUPTS on the spot. Every tile it lifted blows into a gap; anyone standing on it makes a DC 20 DEX save for 5d10. Save the cruelest zone for last.

blocks.text: And once - exactly once, at the far lip - let the plane take a free swing: a sourceless psychic lash at the most exhausted PC (4d6 psychic, DC 15 WIS for half, no explanation ever). Demonholme does not owe anyone fairness.

scenes.development: A half-day beyond the chasm, the machinations of Demonholme culminate in... commerce. Scene 11.4.

script.text: Fog, warmth, brimstone - push the chasm at the crevasse lip.
Put the battle map down and let them sweat: the tiles, the columns, the storm, and Demonholme itself are the opposition.

Run the numbers (Mechanics) without mercy: hourly DC 18 CON in the storm, the lava damage ladder, flight at half speed with the DC 22 wind-shear slam, the tile Lava Bursts - and the Spites five times, once per zone, the fifth one erupting where it lands.

At the far lip, once and only once, the plane takes its free swing: a sourceless psychic lash at the most exhausted PC - 4d6, DC 15 WIS half, no explanation ever. Demonholme does not owe anyone fairness.

time.label: Along the crevasse — a day to the left

chasm.note: One continuous plain, left to right: each pale stone is one 5-ft walkable tile, everything else is the lava river. Five zones of ~50 squares each - the Near Lip (the two solid lip squares, then a crumbling apron), the Braid (three woven strands), the Columns (the ONLY zone with rock pillars - clusters of three in an L), the Shattered Field (scattered debris around two jagged lanes), and the Far Lip (the scatter narrows to a single point that meets the far ledge). The players' focus window shows ~50 squares at a time. Legend in the grid strings: S/E ledges, T tiles, C columns, . lava.

scenes.title: Bognil
scenes.body: A cheerful multiversal being, alone on the ice with a laden cart and no visible fear, selling potions: BOGNIL (Appendix A - a bognil, and yes: if your table met a bognil potion-seller on the trade road tables of Chapter 2, it is DEFINITELY the same guy, and he remembers their custom fondly). Stock him with what they will need - healing, fire resistance, one thing they cannot afford - and overcharge them kindly. He does not explain how he is here. He never explains how he is anywhere.
scenes.mechanics: Robbing a bognil is its own punishment (see the stat block's Bognilism). Those who try it pay. Wisely.

script.text: A half-day on, the machinations of Demonholme culminate in... commerce. BOGNIL, cheerful and alone on the ice with a laden cart and no visible fear - and yes: if the table met a bognil potion-seller on the Chapter 2 trade roads, it is DEFINITELY the same guy, and he remembers their custom fondly.
Stock him with what they will need - healing, fire resistance, and one thing they cannot afford - and overcharge them kindly. He never explains how he is anywhere.
Robbing a bognil is its own punishment (Bognilism). Those who try it pay. Wisely. Let the table laugh here - it is the pressure valve before the Bowl.

scenes.title: The Bowl of the Nine
scenes.boxedText: Cresting a ridge: a faint light. Below, a shallow, gargantuan bowl scooped from the ice - and at its center, nine hooded figures working an arcane circle. At ITS center, a tree heart, glowing dark red. Rising.

bowl.note: A 320-ft bowl (64x64). Nine Abyssal Ritualists ring the Tree Heart inside a Cube of Force (charges start 24/31; attacks drain it — Disintegrate 1d12, Horn of Blasting 1d10, Passwall 1d6, Prismatic Spray 1d20, Wall of Fire 1d4). Two Stormbone Giants hammer from opposite rims; two Mindwithers are the anvil. The party starts in the Trap Set Zone (room for 8). THREE CLOCKS, ONE BATTLE: the ambush, the cube's charge pool, and the Heart (300 HP / AC 14) climbing 30 ft a round out of reach. Drop the cube to 0 and the shield falls; shatter the Heart and the anchor breaks.

battle.name: The Anchor Ritual
battle.setup: As the party descends, the trap closes: the anvil comes from four directions at once while the nine mages work on, untouchable behind an invisible fortress. DC 18 Arcana reads it: a CUBE OF FORCE, running on a charge pool (the record's stood at 24 remaining of 31). ATTACKS DRAIN IT - spells and effects striking the cube burn charges: Disintegrate 1d12, Horn of Blasting 1d10, Passwall 1d6, Prismatic Spray 1d20, Wall of Fire 1d4 (extrapolate for other effects by spell level). At zero, the shield drops and the mages are meat.

combatants.name: Stormbone Giant
combatants.note: The hammer, from opposite rims.

combatants.name: Mindwither
combatants.note: The anvil. Mind Blast into whoever coordinates.

combatants.name: Abyssal Ritualist
combatants.note: Inside the cube, working. They do not fight until the shield falls; then they fight like the doomed.

battle.tactics: THE HEART IS THE REAL TARGET: 300 HP, AC 14 (revised down from 20 - the lower number plays better; keep it), starting 30 feet up and rising 30 feet per round. Shatter it and the anchor breaks - and the mages 'draw a gruesome mortal fate for failing' (narrate; do not roll). The party must split attention between the ambush, the cube's charge pool, and the climbing heart - three clocks, one battle.
battle.adjusting: Weaker party: one giant, one mindwither, cube at 18 charges. Stronger party: cube at 31, and the heart accelerates to 40 ft/round once above 90 feet.
battle.aftermath: One anchor broken. Two remain - and at the bowl's far rim, an active stone archway. Scene 11.6.

scenes.treasure: Ritual paraphernalia worth 800 gp to the right buyer; a mage's notebook in Abyssal (troop movements, a supply schedule, and one line the dreamer PC recognizes from their own dream).

script.text: Cresting the ridge - push the Bowl and let them count the nine.

As they descend, the trap closes: the anvil comes from four directions while the mages work on behind an invisible fortress. DC 18 Arcana reads it - a CUBE OF FORCE running a charge pool; attacks striking it burn charges (Disintegrate 1d12, Wall of Fire 1d4, extrapolate by level). At zero, the shield drops and the mages are meat.
THE HEART IS THE REAL TARGET: 300 HP, AC 14 - keep the revised number - starting 30 feet up and rising 30 per round. Three clocks, one battle: the ambush, the pool, and the climb.
Shatter it and the anchor breaks - and the mages draw a gruesome mortal fate for failing. Narrate; do not roll.
Aftermath: the paraphernalia, and the notebook in Abyssal - troop movements, a supply schedule, and one line the dreamer PC recognizes from their own dream.

time.label: From Bognil to the Bowl — how long?

scenes.title: The Portal at the Rim
scenes.body: A stone archway, active. DC 15 Perception: through it, at the right angle, another distant point with a red glow - in fact TWO of them (the other heart rituals, running NOW). DC 20: a third option at a third angle - an INVITING one: forest, then meadow, then a patch of overgrown mushrooms, ever-changing, green with life. Enter at different angles for different destinations. Two promise battle without rest. One promises the unknown.
scenes.development: Milestone: 11th level. A beat worth planting: the party rolls the dice on the green door - and one companion quietly does NOT step through, staying behind in Demonholme. If the court's storyteller walks with the party, ALIAS is the plant (Contingency C5); failing him, any suitable NPC serves. The reunion in Chapter 12 lands beautifully.

script.text: At the bowl's far rim, an active stone archway. DC 15 Perception: through it, at the right angle, another distant red glow - in fact TWO. The other heart rituals, running NOW.
DC 20: a third angle, and an INVITING one - forest, meadow, mushrooms, green with life. Enter at different angles for different destinations.
Two doors promise battle without rest. One promises the unknown. The choice is theirs - and the book, like the goddess, assumes green.

A beat worth planting: one companion quietly does NOT step through, staying behind in Demonholme. If Alias walks with the party, he is the plant (Contingency C5); failing him, any suitable NPC serves. The Chapter 12 reunion lands beautifully. Milestone: 11th level.

chapters.chapterDevelopment: The party leaves Demonholme with one anchor down, two burning, and a choice made. Chapter 12 opens on the other side of whichever door they took - and the book, like the goddess, assumes green.

chapters.title: Essa's Grace
chapters.overview: Through the green portal, each hero wakes alone in the safest place their memory owns. A goddess pours tea, trades one truth per hero, and grants the band a single boon - the only way to beat two ritual clocks at once. The split assault succeeds by half: one heart shatters clean; one ritual completes in a blinding white flash. The campaign ends where the record ends - over a flat, icy desert where the world they knew should be, asking the question the next campaign will answer.
chapters.running: Three movements: QUIET (12.1-12.2, the happy places and the tea - run them slow, one beat per player, no dice), COUNCIL (12.3, truths and the boon - budget one revelation per player and make at least one a bomb with a long fuse), and WAR (12.4-12.5, the split assault - two initiative counts, no reinforcements, and an ending that is a cliffhanger ON PURPOSE). Do not resolve the icy desert. The record didn't, and the mystery is the campaign's bequest to whatever you run next.

scenes.title: The Happy Places
scenes.body: Each PC wakes ALONE, somewhere they once felt perfectly safe, exactly as they remember it - the kitchen that fits two, the forest clearing, the barracks bunk, the workshop at the good hour. Run one quiet beat per player before anything else: what do they touch first? Who do they expect to walk in? Give each of them ninety seconds of peace. They have earned it, and the chapter spends it deliberately.
scenes.mechanics: Safety note: 'the safest place in your memory' can be tender territory. The prep-card answers from Session Zero (scene 0.3, 'your element') are your map of where each player wants this to go.

script.text: No dice in this scene. Each PC wakes ALONE, somewhere they once felt perfectly safe, exactly as they remember it. Run one quiet beat per player before anything else: what do they touch first? Who do they expect to walk in?
Ninety seconds of peace apiece. They have earned it, and the chapter spends it deliberately.
Safety note: 'the safest place in your memory' can be tender territory. The session-zero prep cards - 'your element' - are your map of where each player wants this to go.

scenes.title: Tea with Essa
scenes.boxedText: She sets down her cup as if she'd poured it knowing the exact moment you would arrive. 'Hello, my children. I have watched you from very far away - farther than you have ever walked - and I am so proud of what you've grown into. Sit. Drink. I owe each of you one true answer, and your band a single gift... and you all owe me some conversation.' A huge, inviting smile.
scenes.body: In the kitchen sits a figure in living green - skin like leaf and vine in soft gradients, ears drawn to points, every line of her regal and kind - sipping tea. This is a god's own realm, and the rules here are hers: each hero's Happy Place gives way like a held breath let go, and the whole band coalesces around the one table at the same moment, however far apart their safe places were. The tea grants the benefit of a long rest (the record delivered it alongside a fifteen-hour potato dish from a small potato god - honor your table's equivalents; every campaign has a potato). Essa explains she has tracked their doings, and SHE cracked the rift in the portal they used. A scrying pool is offered for planning the assault - hide one or two oddities in its image for sharp-eyed players to bank.

blocks.text: THE TRUTHS: one true answer per hero. Budget one revelation per player; make at least one a bomb with a long fuse, and let one be small and kind. Worked example: 'What is in my Iron Flask?' - a DEVA, trapped since the raising of the great wall that marred Arret; poured out on the spot, RELANE, angel of Essa (Appendix A: Deva), grateful, who can expound the true properties of a certain amulet.

blocks.title: IN ESSA'S VOICE - a bank for the table
blocks.sub: short lines to speak as her, by the moment they're needed
lines: Wary - 'are you real, or a trick of Demonholme?': 'Demonholme cannot make a place smell of rain on turned earth. It has never grown a thing in its life. ...I have. Feel the difference?'
A hero grieves / the Happy Place cut deep: 'I know. I brought you here soft on purpose. Even soldiers are allowed a kitchen. Breathe. This hour is yours, and nothing in it can reach you.'

Why she helped / cracked the rift: 'I have been in your story since the first tale-teller in the first village said your names by a fire. I could not fight beside you - but a door left ajar? That I can manage. ...You are very welcome.'
Framing a truth: 'Ask me one true thing. Not what you hope - what is. I will not dress it kindly, but I will not lie to you either.'
The heavy truth (a bomb with a long fuse): '...You did not want that answer. I'm sorry. I told you I wouldn't lie. Carry it gently; it will matter later, and you'll be glad you knew.'
The small, kind truth: 'There. A little one, to balance the scales. Not every true thing has to weigh a stone.'
If they push for more than one: 'One each, my child. Greed is a weed - pull it early. ...Though I do like that you tried.' (tehe)

Asked about the taken companion (the lost Champion - kept, and known safe; a PC's role or an NPC): 'They are alive, and known safe - sendings are answered, the scrying holds. They are kept, not lost. That door is not closed to you. But it is not tonight's door.'

Asked about Essax - she knew him before he fell: '...Bobby. A frightened boy with a chip on his shoulder, before the Demon put its thumb on his mind. I mourn what he was. That does not mean I will let you lose to what he is.'
Asked for a bearing / directions: 'Tehe. Two days forward from where you stand. Cross the burning crevasse. Then a day to your left. The rest, you already know how to do.'
If they fear the plan ahead: 'You are asking whether it can be done. Wrong question. You've been doing the impossible since Oospufmorn. The only question left is how you'd like to.'
Nudging the scrying pool (without spoiling): 'Look closely. The pool shows true - but truth is crowded, and it does not point. What you notice is yours to keep.'
Farewell / benediction: 'Go and grow something out of all this ruin. I'll keep the kettle warm. ...And I'll be counting the days right alongside you - you know I will.'

blocks.title: THE LITTLE POTATO GOD - hand the scene to the believer
blocks.sub: the dish grants a long rest; let the follower author their god
lines: ARRIVAL (the pushed card is the players' read): a second cup is not what appears at the believer's place - a dish does, steaming, smelling of the single best thing their childhood kitchen ever made, and riding that steam, small enough to stand on the table's edge, is someone. Their god. Here. Delighted.

HAND OVER THE PEN: ask the potato-god's follower to describe the little god exactly as their mind's eye lays it over the steam - its size, its face, how it moves, what it wears, the dish it sets down. Their version is canon at your table.

SEEDS (only if they want a nudge): a palm-high figure in a spud-brown travel cloak; a warm, cheerful potato with stubby arms and root-whisker hair; something that rides the steam and bows; something that just radiates 'eat - you've earned it.' Let them cook.

THE PROPERTY: the dish grants the benefit of a long rest in a few bites - the same rest the tea gives the others, by a smaller, dearer hand. (Callback: the blessed seed potato from the whispered-paladin side quest is this same little god's work.)

A KEEPSAKE - the Warm Potato: the little god leaves one behind. It stays warm for 24 hours; once, before it cools, its bearer may reroll any one die. (It can also stand in as the Faithful's pulse-bearer trinket - see 11.1.)

script.text: This is her realm - each hero's Happy Place gives way and the whole band coalesces around one table at the same moment, however far apart their safe places were. Push Essa.

The tea grants a long rest. For the potato-god's believer, the fifteen-hour dish arrives with the little god itself - push the card, then hand that player the pen to describe their god (Mechanics has the prompt and the Warm Potato keepsake).
She has watched their struggle, and SHE cracked the rift in the portal they used. The scrying pool goes up for planning - hide one or two oddities for sharp-eyed players to bank.

THE TRUTHS: one true answer per hero. Budget one revelation per player; make at least one a bomb with a long fuse, and let one be small and kind. Lean on the voice-bank in Mechanics for what she says.

boxes.title: The Little Potato God
boxes.text: A second cup is not what appears at your place. Steam climbs from a dish that smells like the single best thing your childhood kitchen ever made - and riding that steam, small enough to stand on the table's edge, is someone. Your god. Here. Delighted.

scenes.title: The Boon and the Plan
scenes.body: Time runs long in her realm - a kindness. Argue, plan, rest; the hourglass on the far side of that door does not turn until you open it, and once you do it runs fast. Essa raises the scrying pool as a living map: two bowls, two circles of nine, both hearts already rising - 'They will not wait for one another. Strike one, and the other finishes while you travel. That is the arithmetic.' Let the players read the racing clocks and reach the answer themselves. The boon the math demands is the SPLIT - she can set the band in two places at once (see the boon menu). She grows; she does not slay: the boon can put you where you need to be, but it will not swing a blade for you.
scenes.development: Marching orders are the players' to give - team composition AND who takes which door. Two teams, two locations. Scene 12.4 runs both on one Bowl map.

script.text: Time runs long here - a kindness. Plan, rest, argue; the hourglass beyond the door does not turn until you open it, and then it runs fast.
Raise the scrying pool as a racing clock: two bowls, two hearts already rising. 'They will not wait for one another.' Let the table do the math and reach the split themselves.

The boon menu is in Mechanics. She grants exactly what is asked, with its edges named - but only the SPLIT beats both clocks. Limits: one boon for all, TWO locations only, she grows and does not slay.
Marching orders are the players' to give - who goes, and which door. Two teams, two locations. 12.4 runs both on one Bowl map.

blocks.title: THE BOON - what she can grant, and its edges
blocks.sub: she grants exactly what is asked; only the split beats both clocks
lines: * TWO PLACES AT ONCE (the split) - the band divides; both teams act in the same slice of time, the goddess holding the thread. The ONLY boon that beats both clocks. Limit: exactly TWO locations, no more; no PC, item, or spell crosses between teams; it ends when both rituals resolve.
A BLESSING OF GROWTH / HASTE - one team fights as if hasted, or with advantage on the cube-casters. Limit: one site only - it does not split time, so the other ritual completes. She'll say so.
A CHAMPION AT YOUR SIDE - Relane the Deva fights with one team. Limit: one site only; mighty, but not two places at once.

FOREKNOWLEDGE - she shows the exact cheat waiting at the snag site (a Spite, a cube's second wind, an accelerating heart) so they can prep. Limit: information only - deadly WITH the split, useless as a substitute for it.
BRING THEM HOME - she spends the gift fetching the taken companion instead of aiding the assault. Limit: a heart choice, not a tactical one - both rituals may run. Legitimate all the same.
RESTORATION - clears exhaustion, a pool of healing, sets them whole for the fight. Limit: sustains, does not split.

blocks.title: HER LIMITS - set these out loud
blocks.sub: there are things a goddess will not be asked twice
lines: ONE boon for the whole party - the truths are one each; the gift is one for all.
TWO locations, no more. She can place anyone anywhere - but only across two separate places. Ask her to scatter seven heroes to seven doors and she will only pour you more tea.
She grows; she does not slay. No boon directly kills a foe or fills a clock for them.
Whatever is chosen ends when they leave the kitchen. Out there, the hourglass runs fast.

blocks.title: HOW TO REACH THE SPLIT - without railroading
blocks.sub: four levers, gentlest first
lines: 1. LET THE POOL TEACH. Run it as a live visual - both hearts visibly rising, too far apart to reach in turn. Players who see racing clocks reach 'we have to hit them at once' on their own.
2. NAME THE CONSTRAINT, NOT THE ANSWER. 'There are two. They will not wait for each other.' Then wait - let a player propose the split.
3. MAKE THE MENU EXPLICIT. Reading the options invites them to CHOOSE the split. Agency, not instruction.
4. OFFER IT LAST, AS HER SUGGESTION. Only if they're stuck: 'I have one gift that answers two doors.' She proposes; they decide.

scenes.title: Two Hearts, One Clock
scenes.body: Run BOTH assaults on one map. Reuse the Bowl of the Nine (scene 11.5) here: play the team you're actively running on the live bowl - full mechanics, the ambush, the cube, the climbing Heart - while the OTHER team rides alongside as Clock 4 - The Other Bowl, a heart you climb and chip in step. Strike-team style: the record's two-hero team dispatched their gem fast and plane-shifted home to somewhere unrecognized - a plain of sickly grass, a purple-hued forest, an active volcano. Each site carries a resolution valve: mark it shattered (that team wins the race) or ritual-completes (the white flash lands there). The fail can land on EITHER side - set it as the table earns it. Whichever site completes, a blinding white flash plane-shifts that team home along with a slab of Demonholme; the other team watches their sky go white in the same instant.
scenes.mechanics: Structural honesty: the record scripts one clean success and one completion - but WHICH is which is the players' to earn. Their read of the pool (12.2's banked oddities), their team split, and who carries the cube-breaker decide it. If a team beats a clock it was 'supposed' to lose, honor it and move the completion to a third site off-screen. The white flash happens either way; what it delivered is the point - do not resolve it (12.5).

bowl.note: Two hearts, one map. Reuse the Bowl of the Nine (11.5): run the team you're playing on the live bowl - the nine behind the Cube of Force, two Stormbone Giants, two Mindwithers, the Heart climbing out of reach - and keep the OTHER team as Clock 4 - The Other Bowl, a heart you climb and chip in step. Each site has a resolution valve: mark it shattered (that team wins the race) or ritual-completes (the white flash lands there). The fail can land on EITHER side.

battle.name: The Split Assault (one map, two hearts)
battle.setup: One Bowl map, two hearts. Run the live team on the map (nine Abyssal Ritualists behind the Cube of Force, two Stormbone Giants, two Mindwithers); track the other team on Clock 4. Cut between them on initiative like a film editor - one shared initiative order across both, and cut mid-scene on cliffhangers.

combatants.name: Stormbone Giant
combatants.note: One pair per site - placed on the live bowl, abstract on Clock 4.

combatants.name: Mindwither
combatants.note: The anvil, per site. Split or double to taste.

combatants.name: Abyssal Ritualist
combatants.note: Nine per bowl, behind their cubes; the live map seeds one bowl's nine.

battle.tactics: The live site plays fair or cheats to taste; the tracked site is a clock you advance to match the fiction. LEVERS THAT MATTER (set in 12.3's plan): who carries the cube-breaker (Horn of Blasting 1d10 drains fastest - split your nukes and both cubes fall; stack them on one team and that site flies while the other stalls behind an intact shield); who goes where (the team sent to the snag site meets the Spite / cube second-wind / accelerating heart - their read vs. reality); which truths they cashed in; and the starting resources the tea and the dish set.
battle.adjusting: Tune each site to the team that chose it - the split is the players' own difficulty slider. Weaker overall: lower one heart's effective HP, or skip the snag. Stronger: accel on both hearts, and the snag site's cube regenerates 1d6 charges once.
battle.aftermath: White light - on one side by the shatter-race, on the other by completion. Set each site's valve, then 12.5.

script.text: One map, two hearts. Reuse the Bowl (11.5): run the live team on the map, and keep the other team as Clock 4 - The Other Bowl, climbing and chipping in step. Cut between them on one shared initiative like a film editor.

The plan decides it: who carries the cube-breaker (split the nukes and both cubes fall; stack them and one site stalls), who takes which door, which truths they cashed. Their read of the pool vs. what's really waiting is the tension.
TEAM ONE's clean run ends in a strange arrival - sickly grass, a purple-hued forest, an active volcano. TEAM TWO hits the snags - a Spite, a cube regenerating 1d6 once, an accelerating heart.

Set each site's resolution valve - shattered or ritual-completes. The fail can land on either side. Whichever completes, the white flash takes that team home with a slab of Demonholme; the other watches their sky go white. Do not resolve it - 12.5.

time.label: Two hearts, one clock — how much time slips?

scenes.title: The Icy Desert
scenes.boxedText: Reunited and airborne, you look down on a land transformed: an icy desert where the world you knew should be. It is FLAT. And there is no army. No Kelethtonreth. Nothing at all to be seen.
scenes.body: The campaign-turning question, verbatim from the record's final line: DID THE SPELL FAIL - OR IS SOMETHING HIDDEN HERE? Do not answer it. End the session, the chapter, and the campaign's first saga right here, in the cold air, with the party staring down at a blank page wearing snow.
scenes.development: Milestone: 12th level, and the title CHAMPIONS OF THE EMPIRE meaning something new. Scene 12.6 is the drawer of parts for whoever runs onward.

script.text: Reunited and airborne - push the icy desert, and let the silence run.
The campaign-turning question, verbatim from the record's final line: DID THE SPELL FAIL - OR IS SOMETHING HIDDEN HERE? Do not answer it.
End the session, the chapter, and the saga's first arc right here, in the cold air, with the party staring down at a blank page wearing snow.
Milestone: 12th level - and the title CHAMPIONS OF THE EMPIRE meaning something new.

time.label: Crossing the icy desert — how long?

scenes.title: Beyond the Record - Threads to Continue
scenes.body: Everything the saga leaves loaded: the flat icy desert and what hides beneath it. The lost Champion, taken from Aedlab - and Nika Blackthorn's standing invitation: 'Retrieve them at TERRID HALL... come to the Bronze Storm empire and see what you've done.' CAL NAI, the Red Knife resistance. The possessed Princeps, still unexposed - the campaign's longest fuse, still burning. Koth'Tavuth and Thron, still unbanished. The Clearwater Co.'s paymasters. The sarcophagus in the basement, still chained. The great wall that split Arret. And Essax - Bobby - somewhere on the far side of a white flash.

blocks.title: PLANNING FRAGMENTS
blocks.sub: loose threads, for whoever runs onward
lines: A meeting with 'Wyoh'.
'Advantage over Essax or Kelethtonreth - quest of the super weapon?'
'They are fighting so we might find out how to beat him.'
'The highlander is now canon.'
A Library.

blocks.title: VERBRECHEN ['fair-breken']
blocks.sub: one scene, ready to run
lines: Stone keeps ringed by mud-brick hovels, dirt roads, no guards, everyone in the same cut of tunic.

On the main road a man in a rice-paddy hat and brown robes boils water over a precise little fire, an unfamiliar curved sword at his hip: 'Greetings, fair travelers - can you spare some food? Perhaps I can be your guide in these lands, for compensation?'
He knows the way to the VERBOTEN mines, two days north.

blocks.text: Somewhere in this arc: a ring of three wishes, and the words ALL MAGIC ITEMS GONE.

scenes.development: Treat this scene as a drawer of parts, not a script. The saga is complete; the world is not. That is the point of worlds.

script.text: This scene is a drawer of parts, not a script. Read the threads aloud only as the table reaches for them - the desert, Terrid Hall, Cal Nai, Clearwater, the sarcophagus, the wall, and Essax somewhere past a white flash.
The longest fuse is still burning: the Princeps, still unexposed. Guard it to the last.
Stars & Wishes (Tone & Safety) makes a fitting final ritual - and the last Wish at the table is the seed of the next campaign.

chapters.chapterDevelopment: The book ends where the chronicle ends: mid-mystery, on purpose. Stars & Wishes (Tone & Safety) makes a fitting final ritual - and the last Wish at the table is the seed of the next campaign.

traits.t: The goblin can take the Disengage or Hide action as a bonus action on each of its turns.

actions.t: Melee Weapon Attack: +4 to hit, reach 5 ft., one target. Hit: 5 (1d6 + 2) slashing damage.
Ranged Weapon Attack: +4 to hit, range 80/320 ft., one target. Hit: 5 (1d6 + 2) piercing damage.

creatures.name: Goblin Rag-Crown

traits.t: As a bonus action on each of its turns, a rag-crown can take the Disengage or the Hide action. It is the first thing it learned and the reason it is still wearing the crown.
While at least three other goblins are within 30 feet of it and conscious, the rag-crown has advantage on saving throws against being frightened. Count them as they drop; the trait goes with them.

actions.t: The rag-crown makes two scimitar attacks, or one scimitar attack and one thrown javelin.
Melee Weapon Attack: +5 to hit, reach 5 ft., one target. Hit: 6 (1d6 + 3) slashing damage.
Melee or Ranged Weapon Attack: +5 to hit, reach 5 ft. or range 30/120 ft., one target. Hit: 6 (1d6 + 3) piercing damage.

The rag-crown names one creature it can see within 60 feet. The first goblin ally to hit that creature before the start of the rag-crown's next turn deals an extra 3 (1d6) damage. It does not have to be a good plan; it has to be loud.

reactions.t: When a creature the rag-crown can see targets it with an attack, the rag-crown swaps places with a goblin within 5 feet of it and that goblin becomes the target instead. The goblin does not get a say and has never once complained afterwards.

creatures.alternate: Substitute any CR 1 goblin captain that can shove a subordinate into an incoming attack.

actions.t: Melee or Ranged Weapon Attack: +3 to hit, reach 5 ft. or range 20/60 ft., one target. Hit: 4 (1d6 + 1) piercing damage, or 5 (1d8 + 1) piercing damage if used with two hands to make a melee attack.

traits.t: The knight has advantage on saving throws against being frightened.

actions.t: The knight makes two melee attacks.
Melee Weapon Attack: +5 to hit, reach 5 ft., one target. Hit: 10 (2d6 + 3) slashing damage.
Ranged Weapon Attack: +2 to hit, range 100/400 ft., one target. Hit: 5 (1d10) piercing damage.

actions.n: Leadership (Recharges after a Short or Long Rest)
actions.t: For 1 minute, the knight can utter a special command or warning whenever a nonhostile creature that it can see within 30 feet of it makes an attack roll or a saving throw. The creature can add a d4 to its roll provided it can hear and understand the knight.

reactions.t: The knight adds 2 to its AC against one melee attack that would hit it. To do so, the knight must see the attacker and be wielding a melee weapon.

traits.t: The dog has advantage on Wisdom (Perception) checks and on saving throws against being blinded, charmed, deafened, frightened, stunned, or knocked unconscious.

actions.t: The dog makes two bite attacks.

Melee Weapon Attack: +4 to hit, reach 5 ft., one target. Hit: 5 (1d6 + 2) piercing damage. If the target is a creature, it must succeed on a DC 12 Constitution saving throw against disease or become poisoned until the disease is cured. Every 24 hours that elapse, the creature must repeat the saving throw, reducing its hit point maximum by 5 (1d10) on a failure. This reduction lasts until the disease is cured. The creature dies if the disease reduces its hit point maximum to 0.

creatures.name: Polewight
creatures.resistances: bludgeoning, piercing, and slashing from nonmagical attacks
creatures.immunities: poison; charmed, exhaustion, frightened, paralyzed, poisoned, unconscious
creatures.languages: understands whoever lashed it to the pole; does not answer

traits.t: While a polewight hangs still it is indistinguishable from a bundle of wet sacking lashed to a post, and nothing short of touching it says otherwise.

A polewight ignores difficult terrain caused by water, ice, or a pitching deck, and is never knocked prone by the movement of the thing it is standing on. Everyone else on that deck is rolling for it.
A polewight that takes fire damage keeps burning, taking 3 (1d6) fire damage at the start of each of its turns until it or another creature spends an action to smother it. It does not try.

actions.t: The polewight makes two hook attacks.

Melee Weapon Attack: +4 to hit, reach 5 ft., one target. Hit: 7 (2d4 + 2) slashing damage. If the target is a creature, it must succeed on a DC 12 Wisdom saving throw or be frightened of the polewight until the end of the polewight's next turn.

The polewight turns its head to one creature it can see within 30 feet. If the target can see the head turn, it must succeed on a DC 12 Wisdom saving throw or be frightened until the end of the polewight's next turn. While frightened this way the target is also paralyzed — the fear is the kind that arrives before the thought does.

creatures.alternate: Substitute any CR 1 Medium construct that passes for an inanimate object and paralyses with a look.

creatures.name: Shadow
creatures.skills: Stealth +4 (+6 in dim light or darkness)
creatures.resistances: acid, cold, fire, lightning, thunder; bludgeoning, piercing, and slashing from nonmagical attacks
creatures.immunities: necrotic, poison; exhaustion, frightened, grappled, paralyzed, petrified, poisoned, prone, restrained

traits.t: The shadow can move through a space as narrow as 1 inch wide without squeezing.
While in dim light or darkness, the shadow can take the Hide action as a bonus action.
While in sunlight, the shadow has disadvantage on attack rolls, ability checks, and saving throws.

actions.t: Melee Weapon Attack: +4 to hit, reach 5 ft., one creature. Hit: 9 (2d6 + 2) necrotic damage, and the target's Strength score is reduced by 1d4. The target dies if this reduces its Strength to 0. Otherwise, the reduction lasts until the target finishes a short or long rest. If a non-evil humanoid dies from this attack, a new shadow rises from the corpse 1d4 hours later.
Melee Weapon Attack: +3 to hit, reach 5 ft., one target. Hit: 4 (1d6 + 1) slashing damage.
Ranged Weapon Attack: +3 to hit, range 80/320 ft., one target. Hit: 5 (1d8 + 1) piercing damage.
The captain makes three melee attacks: two with its scimitar and one with its dagger. Or the captain makes two ranged attacks with its daggers.
Melee Weapon Attack: +5 to hit, reach 5 ft., one target. Hit: 6 (1d6 + 3) slashing damage.
Melee or Ranged Weapon Attack: +5 to hit, reach 5 ft. or range 20/60 ft., one target. Hit: 5 (1d4 + 3) piercing damage.

reactions.t: The captain adds 2 to its AC against one melee attack that would hit it. To do so, the captain must see the attacker and be wielding a melee weapon.

creatures.name: Imp
creatures.resistances: cold; bludgeoning, piercing, and slashing from nonmagical attacks that aren't silvered

traits.t: The imp can use its action to polymorph into a beast form that resembles a rat (speed 20 ft.), a raven (20 ft., fly 60 ft.), or a spider (20 ft., climb 20 ft.), or back into its true form. Its statistics are the same in each form, except for the speed changes noted. Any equipment it is wearing or carrying isn't transformed. It reverts to its true form if it dies.
Magical darkness doesn't impede the imp's darkvision.
The imp has advantage on saving throws against spells and other magical effects.

actions.t: Melee Weapon Attack: +5 to hit, reach 5 ft., one target. Hit: 5 (1d4 + 3) piercing damage, and the target must make on a DC 11 Constitution saving throw, taking 10 (3d6) poison damage on a failed save, or half as much damage on a successful one.
The imp magically turns invisible until it attacks or until its concentration ends (as if concentrating on a spell). Any equipment the imp wears or carries is invisible with it.

traits.t: As a bonus action, the orc can move up to its speed toward a hostile creature that it can see.

actions.t: Melee Weapon Attack: +5 to hit, reach 5 ft., one target. Hit: 9 (1d12 + 3) slashing damage.
Melee or Ranged Weapon Attack: +5 to hit, reach 5 ft. or range 30/120 ft., one target. Hit: 6 (1d6 + 3) piercing damage.

traits.t: The worg has advantage on Wisdom (Perception) checks that rely on hearing or smell.

actions.t: Melee Weapon Attack: +5 to hit, reach 5 ft., one target. Hit: 10 (2d6 + 3) piercing damage. If the target is a creature, it must succeed on a DC 13 Strength saving throw or be knocked prone.

traits.t: The owlbear has advantage on Wisdom (Perception) checks that rely on sight or smell.

actions.t: The owlbear makes two attacks: one with its beak and one with its claws.
Melee Weapon Attack: +7 to hit, reach 5 ft., one creature. Hit: 10 (1d10 + 5) piercing damage.
Melee Weapon Attack: +7 to hit, reach 5 ft., one target. Hit: 14 (2d8 + 5) slashing damage.

creatures.name: Veteran

actions.t: The veteran makes two longsword attacks. If it has a shortsword drawn, it can also make a shortsword attack.
Melee Weapon Attack: +5 to hit, reach 5 ft., one target. Hit: 7 (1d8 + 3) slashing damage, or 8 (1d10 + 3) slashing damage if used with two hands.
Melee Weapon Attack: +5 to hit, reach 5 ft., one target. Hit: 6 (1d6 + 3) piercing damage.
Ranged Weapon Attack: +3 to hit, range 100/400 ft., one target. Hit: 6 (1d10 + 1) piercing damage.

creatures.flavor: Ket, First Mate of the River Serpent, uses this block - and has the scars to justify every line of it.

creatures.name: Berowl

traits.t: The berowl has advantage on Wisdom (Perception) checks that rely on sight or smell.
The berowl has advantage on attack rolls against a creature if at least one other berowl is within 5 feet of that creature and isn't incapacitated.
A berowl interrupted while feeding has disadvantage on initiative but deals an extra 3 (1d6) damage with its claws until the end of its second turn in combat.
The berowl will not willingly enter water deeper than its knees.

actions.t: The berowl makes two attacks: one with its beak and one with its claws.
Melee Weapon Attack: +7 to hit, reach 5 ft., one creature. Hit: 10 (1d10 + 5) piercing damage.
Melee Weapon Attack: +7 to hit, reach 5 ft., one target. Hit: 14 (2d8 + 5) slashing damage.

creatures.flavor: Owlbear-kin bred and teleport-seeded as hunting packs by the servants of Essax; a group is called a sleuth.

creatures.name: Sleapless
creatures.speed: 30 ft. (fly 50 ft. in raven and hybrid form)

traits.t: The Sleapless can use its action to polymorph into a raven-humanoid hybrid or into a raven, or back into its true form, which is humanoid. Its statistics, other than its size and flying speed, are the same in each form. Any equipment it is wearing or carrying isn't transformed. It reverts to its true form if it dies.

The Sleapless regains 5 hit points at the start of its turn. If the Sleapless takes damage from a silvered weapon, or from an improvised weapon of cold-worked iron (a ship's hull nail, a pry bar, a length of anchor chain), this trait doesn't function at the start of the Sleapless's next turn. The Sleapless dies only if it starts its turn with 0 hit points and doesn't regenerate.
The Sleapless can mimic simple sounds and humanoid voices it has heard. A creature that hears the sounds can tell they are imitations with a successful DC 14 Wisdom (Insight) check.

The Sleapless has advantage on saving throws against being charmed or frightened. It fights with fanatic devotion and will die before betraying its master willingly - interrogators need magic AND genuine kindness (see Chapter 3, scene 3.6).

actions.t: The Sleapless makes two shortsword attacks.
Melee Weapon Attack: +5 to hit, reach 5 ft., one target. Hit: 6 (1d6 + 3) piercing damage.
Melee Weapon Attack: +5 to hit, reach 5 ft., one target. Hit: 5 (1d4 + 3) piercing damage.

creatures.flavor: Soldiers of the Bronze Storm Empire granted corvid lycanthropy by Essax themself. The soldiers call themselves the Sleapless - they claim to need no rest while the Storm is owed a debt - and a flight of six is an Unkindness.
creatures.alternate: Substitute any CR 2 Medium humanoid shapechanger that takes the form of a raven - intelligent, organised, and run as a flock rather than as a beast.

creatures.name: Dark Star Cutthroat

traits.t: Once per turn, the cutthroat deals an extra 3 (1d6) damage to a creature it hits with a weapon attack if an ally of the cutthroat is within 5 feet of that creature and isn't incapacitated.

actions.t: Melee Weapon Attack: +4 to hit, reach 5 ft., one target. Hit: 5 (1d6 + 2) piercing damage.
Melee or Ranged Weapon Attack: +4 to hit, reach 5 ft. or range 20/60 ft., one target. Hit: 4 (1d4 + 2) piercing damage.

creatures.flavor: The Dark Star guild's disposable blades - recruited fast, spent faster. Members bear a solid black seven-pointed star tattooed on the left side of the neck (DC 15 Insight to place it).
creatures.alternate: Substitute a Thug, or a Bandit for a lighter table.

creatures.name: Dark Star Agent

traits.t: On each of its turns, the agent can use a bonus action to take the Dash, Disengage, or Hide action.

The agent deals an extra 7 (2d6) damage when it hits a target with a weapon attack and has advantage on the attack roll, or when the target is within 5 feet of an ally of the agent that isn't incapacitated and the agent doesn't have disadvantage on the attack roll.

actions.t: The agent makes two shortsword attacks.
Melee Weapon Attack: +5 to hit, reach 5 ft., one target. Hit: 6 (1d6 + 3) piercing damage.
Ranged Weapon Attack: +5 to hit, range 30/120 ft., one target. Hit: 6 (1d6 + 3) piercing damage.

reactions.t: The agent halves the damage that it takes from an attack that hits it. The agent must be able to see the attacker.

creatures.flavor: Ranked guild muscle; a First-Mate in Dark Star parlance. Identified by a ring worn on the inside of the belt.
creatures.alternate: Substitute a Spy, or a Bandit Captain for a heavier one.

creatures.name: Dark Star Captain

traits.t: The captain has disadvantage on Wisdom (Insight) checks against creatures that flatter or challenge his skill. A creature can exploit this with a DC 14 Charisma (Deception or Intimidation) check as an action, baiting the captain to move up to his speed toward it.

actions.t: The captain makes three melee attacks: two with his scimitar and one with his dagger.
Melee Weapon Attack: +5 to hit, reach 5 ft., one target. Hit: 6 (1d6 + 3) slashing damage.
Melee or Ranged Weapon Attack: +5 to hit, reach 5 ft. or range 20/60 ft., one target. Hit: 5 (1d4 + 3) piercing damage.

reactions.t: The captain adds 2 to his AC against one melee attack that would hit him. To do so, the captain must see the attacker and be wielding a melee weapon.

creatures.flavor: A full Captain of the Dark Star - blue coat, orange bandana at the temples, the guild's seven-pointed star at his neck. His identification rings - his own and his crew's - are sewn inside his belt.

creatures.name: Doman Bail, Captain of the River Serpent

traits.t: Doman has advantage on any ability check made to pilot, navigate, or handle a water vehicle, or to read the moods of a river and of those who work it.

When an ally within 30 feet of Doman that can hear him makes an attack roll, Doman can bark an order: the ally gains advantage on that roll. The Serpent's crew always count as allies - and so does anyone he has decided to pull out of a fight.

actions.t: Doman makes three melee attacks: two with his scimitar and one with his dagger.
Melee Weapon Attack: +5 to hit, reach 5 ft., one target. Hit: 6 (1d6 + 3) slashing damage.
Melee or Ranged Weapon Attack: +5 to hit, reach 5 ft. or range 20/60 ft., one target. Hit: 5 (1d4 + 3) piercing damage.
Ranged Weapon Attack: +5 to hit, range 30/120 ft., one target. Hit: 6 (1d6 + 3) piercing damage. At the Bowl he leads with this - crossbows first, terms later.

reactions.t: Doman adds 2 to his AC against one melee attack that would hit him. To do so, Doman must see the attacker and be wielding a melee weapon.

creatures.flavor: Captain of the fastest smuggler on the Trenlem, ally of the Moonlight Strategy, and no friend at all of the Dark Star. He fights the way he bargains: fast, loud, and finished before anyone agrees on terms. If he draws steel at the Bowl, he counts the survivors, says nothing, and walks - the rest of that sentence waits at the gangplank. ('Aye, I be the capton of the River Serpant.')

creatures.name: Dretch
creatures.languages: Abyssal, telepathy 60 ft. (works only with creatures that understand Abyssal)

actions.t: The dretch makes two attacks: one with its bite and one with its claws.
Melee Weapon Attack: +2 to hit, reach 5 ft., one target. Hit: 3 (1d6) piercing damage.
Melee Weapon Attack: +2 to hit, reach 5 ft., one target. Hit: 5 (2d4) slashing damage.

A 10-foot radius of disgusting green gas extends out from the dretch. The gas spreads around corners, and its area is lightly obscured. It lasts for 1 minute or until a strong wind disperses it. Any creature that starts its turn in that area must succeed on a DC 11 Constitution saving throw or be poisoned until the start of its next turn. While poisoned in this way, the target can take either an action or a bonus action on its turn, not both, and can't take reactions.

creatures.name: Vrock
creatures.resistances: cold, fire, lightning; bludgeoning, piercing, and slashing from nonmagical attacks

traits.t: The vrock has advantage on saving throws against spells and other magical effects.

actions.t: The vrock makes two attacks: one with its beak and one with its talons.
Melee Weapon Attack: +6 to hit, reach 5 ft., one target. Hit: 10 (2d6 + 3) piercing damage.
Melee Weapon Attack: +6 to hit, reach 5 ft., one target. Hit: 14 (2d10 + 3) slashing damage.

A 15-foot-radius cloud of toxic spores extends out from the vrock. The spores spread around corners. Each creature in that area must succeed on a DC 14 Constitution saving throw or become poisoned. While poisoned in this way, a target takes 5 (1d10) poison damage at the start of each of its turns. A target can repeat the saving throw at the end of each of its turns, ending the effect on itself on a success. Emptying a vial of holy water on the target also ends the effect on it.

The vrock emits a horrific screech. Each creature within 20 feet of it that can hear it and that isn't a demon must succeed on a DC 14 Constitution saving throw or be stunned until the end of the vrock's next turn.

creatures.name: Hezrou
creatures.resistances: cold, fire, lightning; bludgeoning, piercing, and slashing from nonmagical attacks

traits.t: The hezrou has advantage on saving throws against spells and other magical effects.

Any creature that starts its turn within 10 feet of the hezrou must succeed on a DC 14 Constitution saving throw or be poisoned until the start of its next turn. On a successful saving throw, the creature is immune to the hezrou's stench for 24 hours.

actions.t: The hezrou makes three attacks: one with its bite and two with its claws.
Melee Weapon Attack: +7 to hit, reach 5 ft., one target. Hit: 15 (2d10 + 4) piercing damage.
Melee Weapon Attack: +7 to hit, reach 5 ft., one target. Hit: 11 (2d6 + 4) slashing damage.

creatures.name: Glabrezu
creatures.resistances: cold, fire, lightning; bludgeoning, piercing, and slashing from nonmagical attacks

traits.t: The glabrezu's spellcasting ability is Charisma (spell save DC 16). The glabrezu can innately cast the following spells, requiring no material components: At will: darkness, detect magic, dispel magic. 1/day each: confusion, fly, power word stun.
The glabrezu has advantage on saving throws against spells and other magical effects.

actions.t: The glabrezu makes four attacks: two with its pincers and two with its fists. Alternatively, it makes two attacks with its pincers and casts one spell.

Melee Weapon Attack: +9 to hit, reach 10 ft., one target. Hit: 16 (2d10 + 5) bludgeoning damage. If the target is a Medium or smaller creature, it is grappled (escape DC 15). The glabrezu has two pincers, each of which can grapple only one target.
Melee Weapon Attack: +9 to hit, reach 5 ft., one target. Hit: 7 (2d4 + 2) bludgeoning damage.

creatures.flavor: Two named glabrezu serve Essax: Thron, their field commander, and Koth'Tavuth, who wears the Princeps. The pitch-black one at Oospufmorn is a third - the party will learn what that implies.

creatures.name: Mage

traits.t: The mage is a 9th-level spellcaster. Its spellcasting ability is Intelligence (spell save DC 14, +6 to hit with spell attacks). The mage has the following wizard spells prepared: Cantrips (at will): fire bolt, light, mage hand, prestidigitation. 1st level (4 slots): detect magic, mage armor, magic missile, shield. 2nd level (3 slots): misty step, suggestion. 3rd level (3 slots): counterspell, fireball, fly. 4th level (3 slots): greater invisibility, ice storm. 5th level (1 slot): cone of cold.

actions.t: Melee or Ranged Weapon Attack: +5 to hit, reach 5 ft. or range 20/60 ft., one target. Hit: 4 (1d4 + 2) piercing damage.

creatures.flavor: The Heartbore Mage of Chapter 6 uses this block, his concentration devoted to the swarm at his side.

creatures.name: Cultist

traits.t: The cultist has advantage on saving throws against being charmed or frightened.

actions.t: Melee Weapon Attack: +3 to hit, reach 5 ft., one creature. Hit: 4 (1d6 + 1) slashing damage.

creatures.flavor: Followers of Essax bear a spine-length tattoo at the base of the neck (DC 28 History: Wand of Kelethtonreth).

traits.t: The fanatic has advantage on saving throws against being charmed or frightened.

The fanatic is a 4th-level spellcaster. Its spellcasting ability is Wisdom (spell save DC 11, +3 to hit with spell attacks). The fanatic has the following cleric spells prepared: Cantrips (at will): light, sacred flame, thaumaturgy. 1st level (4 slots): command, inflict wounds, shield of faith. 2nd level (3 slots): hold person, spiritual weapon.

actions.t: The fanatic makes two melee attacks.
Melee or Ranged Weapon Attack: +4 to hit, reach 5 ft. or range 20/60 ft., one creature. Hit: 4 (1d4 + 2) piercing damage.

traits.t: The scout has advantage on Wisdom (Perception) checks that rely on hearing or sight.

actions.t: The scout makes two melee attacks or two ranged attacks.
Melee Weapon Attack: +4 to hit, reach 5 ft., one target. Hit: 5 (1d6 + 2) piercing damage.
Ranged Weapon Attack: +4 to hit, range 150/600 ft., one target. Hit: 6 (1d8 + 2) piercing damage.

creatures.name: Heartbore Swarm
creatures.immunities: fire, necrotic, poison; charmed, frightened, grappled, paralyzed, petrified, poisoned, prone, restrained, stunned

traits.t: The swarm can occupy another creature's space and vice versa, and the swarm can move through any opening large enough for a Tiny insect. The swarm can't regain hit points or gain temporary hit points.

While a creature within 60 feet of the swarm concentrates on directing it (as if concentrating on a spell), the swarm automatically deals 2 damage at the start of each of its turns to one organic surface or unattended object in its space - wood, root, rope, leather, flesh left too still. If the director's concentration ends, the swarm spends its turns seeking its preferred food instead: the nearest living creature.
A creature that ends its turn in the swarm's space takes 2 (1d4) fire damage from the heat of the swarm's bodies.

actions.t: Melee Weapon Attack: +4 to hit, reach 0 ft., one target in the swarm's space. Hit: 10 (4d4) piercing damage plus 4 (1d8) necrotic damage, or 5 (2d4) piercing damage plus 2 (1d4) necrotic damage if the swarm has half of its hit points or fewer.

creatures.flavor: Conjured boring insects the size of large cockroaches, each with an oversized toothy maw - fiery to the touch, necrotic in the wound. A mage of Essax directs them like a chisel.
creatures.alternate: Substitute a Swarm of Insects, with fire or necrotic flavor to taste.

creatures.name: Will-o'-Wisp
creatures.resistances: acid, cold, fire, necrotic, thunder; bludgeoning, piercing, and slashing from nonmagical attacks
creatures.immunities: lightning, poison; exhaustion, grappled, paralyzed, poisoned, prone, restrained, unconscious
creatures.languages: the languages it knew in life

traits.t: As a bonus action, the will-o'-wisp can target one creature it can see within 5 feet of it that has 0 hit points and is still alive. The target must succeed on a DC 10 Constitution saving throw against this magic or die. If the target dies, the will-o'-wisp regains 10 (3d6) hit points.
The will-o'-wisp can't wear or carry anything.
The will-o'-wisp can move through other creatures and objects as if they were difficult terrain. It takes 5 (1d10) force damage if it ends its turn inside an object.
The will-o'-wisp sheds bright light in a 5- to 20-foot radius and dim light for an additional number of feet equal to the chosen radius. The will-o'-wisp can alter the radius as a bonus action.

actions.t: Melee Spell Attack: +4 to hit, reach 5 ft., one creature. Hit: 9 (2d8) lightning damage.
The will-o'-wisp and its light magically become invisible until it attacks or uses its Consume Life, or until its concentration ends (as if concentrating on a spell).

traits.t: The shark has advantage on melee attack rolls against any creature that doesn't have all its hit points.
The shark can breathe only underwater.

actions.t: Melee Weapon Attack: +9 to hit, reach 5 ft., one target. Hit: 22 (3d10 + 6) piercing damage.

creatures.name: Water Elemental
creatures.resistances: acid; bludgeoning, piercing, and slashing from nonmagical attacks
creatures.immunities: poison; exhaustion, grappled, paralyzed, petrified, poisoned, prone, restrained, unconscious

traits.t: The elemental can enter a hostile creature's space and stop there. It can move through a space as narrow as 1 inch wide without squeezing.
If the elemental takes cold damage, it partially freezes; its speed is reduced by 20 feet until the end of its next turn.

actions.t: The elemental makes two slam attacks.
Melee Weapon Attack: +7 to hit, reach 5 ft., one target. Hit: 13 (2d8 + 4) bludgeoning damage.

Each creature in the elemental's space must make a DC 15 Strength saving throw. On a failure, a target takes 13 (2d8 + 4) bludgeoning damage. If it is Large or smaller, it is also grappled (escape DC 14). Until this grapple ends, the target is restrained and unable to breathe unless it can breathe water. If the saving throw is successful, the target is pushed out of the elemental's space. The elemental can grapple one Large creature or up to two Medium or smaller creatures at one time. At the start of each of the elemental's turns, each target grappled by it takes 13 (2d8 + 4) bludgeoning damage. A creature within 5 feet of the elemental can pull a creature or object out of it by taking an action to make a DC 14 Strength check and succeeding.

creatures.name: Deva
creatures.resistances: radiant; bludgeoning, piercing, and slashing from nonmagical attacks

traits.t: The deva's weapon attacks are magical. When the deva hits with any weapon, the weapon deals an extra 4d8 radiant damage (included in the attack).

The deva's spellcasting ability is Charisma (spell save DC 17). The deva can innately cast the following spells, requiring only verbal components: At will: detect evil and good. 1/day each: commune, raise dead.
The deva has advantage on saving throws against spells and other magical effects.

actions.t: The deva makes two melee attacks.
Melee Weapon Attack: +8 to hit, reach 5 ft., one target. Hit: 7 (1d6 + 4) bludgeoning damage plus 18 (4d8) radiant damage.
The deva touches another creature. The target magically regains 20 (4d8 + 2) hit points and is freed from any curse, disease, poison, blindness, or deafness.

The deva magically polymorphs into a humanoid or beast that has a challenge rating equal to or less than its own, or back into its true form. It reverts to its true form if it dies. Any equipment it is wearing or carrying is absorbed or borne by the new form (the deva's choice). In a new form, the deva retains its game statistics and ability to speak, but its AC, movement modes, Strength, Dexterity, and special senses are replaced by those of the new form, and it gains any statistics and capabilities (except class features, legendary actions, and lair actions) that the new form has but that it lacks.

creatures.flavor: Relane, angel of Essa, spent a century inside an Iron Flask - trapped since the raising of the great wall. Freed in Chapter 12, deeply grateful, and very well informed about a certain amulet.

creatures.name: Threshold Blight
creatures.resistances: cold, fire, lightning; bludgeoning, piercing, and slashing from nonmagical attacks

traits.t: While the blight remains motionless and merged with a doorway, archway, or window frame, it is indistinguishable from foul greenish moss or slime. A creature that studies it can identify it as a living thing with a successful DC 15 Intelligence (Nature or Arcana) check.

While merged with a doorway, archway, or window frame, the blight slowly attunes the opening to Demonholme. When combat begins within 60 feet of it, the archway flashes purple: a planar portal begins to open, completing in 1d4 + 3 rounds. If the blight dies before completion, the working collapses. Once complete, the portal remains open until targeted by Dispel Magic against DC 18, or by Dispel Magic cast using a spell slot of 8th level or higher.
The blight can move through a space as narrow as 1 inch wide without squeezing.

actions.t: The blight makes three tendril attacks.

Melee Weapon Attack: +9 to hit, reach 10 ft., one target. Hit: 12 (2d6 + 5) slashing damage, and the target must succeed on a DC 16 Constitution saving throw or be wracked by a vile itching until the end of its next turn - while so wracked, it has disadvantage on Constitution saving throws to maintain concentration.

creatures.flavor: The portal-demons of Essax's network: they enshroud archways like moss and quietly turn them into doors to Demonholme. Their leavings marked the bases of Chanfirch and Vum; the dwarves of Bhindarul keep one captive with its archway held open - on purpose.
creatures.alternate: Substitute any CR 11 Medium fiend that is a spreading corrosive growth rather than a body - rooted where it sits, harmful to touch, and unable to speak.

creatures.name: Frost Worm
creatures.senses: blindsight 30 ft., tremorsense 60 ft., passive Perception 10

traits.t: The frost worm can burrow through solid ice and frozen earth, leaving a 10-foot-diameter tunnel in its wake.

When the frost worm dies, its frozen core detonates. Each creature within 20 feet of it must make a DC 16 Dexterity saving throw, taking 14 (4d6) cold damage and 14 (4d6) piercing damage from ice shards on a failed save, or half as much damage on a successful one.

actions.n: Stunning Shriek (Recharges after a Short or Long Rest)
actions.t: When the frost worm first emerges, it shrieks. Each creature within 60 feet of it that can hear it must succeed on a DC 16 Constitution saving throw or be stunned until the end of the worm's next turn.

Melee Weapon Attack: +10 to hit, reach 10 ft., one target. Hit: 25 (3d12 + 6) piercing damage plus 9 (2d8) cold damage. If the target is a Large or smaller creature, it is grappled (escape DC 16) and restrained until the grapple ends; the worm can grapple one creature at a time, and takes no bite actions against other targets while doing so. A grappled creature takes 9 (2d8) cold damage at the start of each of the worm's turns. The worm can spit a grappled creature up to 20 feet away as a bonus action.

creatures.flavor: Siege engines of the frozen plane. They hunt sound through the ice - and their deaths are as dangerous as their lives. Stagger the kills or eat both blasts.
creatures.alternate: Substitute a Remorhaz, inverting its heat to cold.

creatures.name: Stormbone Giant
creatures.immunities: lightning, poison; charmed, exhaustion, frightened, poisoned

traits.t: Arcs of lightning crawl the giant's bones. A creature that touches the giant or hits it with a melee attack while within 5 feet of it takes 4 (1d8) lightning damage. The giant's weapon attacks deal an extra 9 (2d8) lightning damage (included below).

If damage reduces the giant to 0 hit points, it must make a Constitution saving throw with a DC of 5 + the damage taken, unless the damage is radiant or from a critical hit. On a success, the giant drops to 1 hit point instead.

actions.t: The giant makes two greatsword attacks.
Melee Weapon Attack: +12 to hit, reach 10 ft., one target. Hit: 29 (6d6 + 8) slashing damage plus 9 (2d8) lightning damage.

The giant slams its blade into the ground, discharging its marrow. Each creature within 20 feet of it must make a DC 17 Dexterity saving throw, taking 27 (6d8) lightning damage on a failed save, or half as much damage on a successful one.

creatures.flavor: The raised bones of storm giants who died far from any storm - lightning still remembers them.
creatures.alternate: Substitute a Storm Giant animated with the Skeleton's undead nature.

creatures.name: Mindwither
creatures.resistances: cold, lightning, necrotic; bludgeoning, piercing, and slashing from nonmagical attacks
creatures.immunities: poison; charmed, exhaustion, frightened, paralyzed, poisoned

traits.t: The mindwither has advantage on saving throws against spells and other magical effects.
The mindwither has advantage on saving throws against any effect that turns undead.

The mindwither is a 12th-level spellcaster. Its spellcasting ability is Intelligence (spell save DC 16, +8 to hit with spell attacks). It has the following wizard spells prepared: Cantrips (at will): chill touch, mage hand, prestidigitation, shocking grasp. 1st level (4 slots): detect magic, magic missile, shield. 2nd level (3 slots): invisibility, mirror image. 3rd level (3 slots): counterspell, lightning bolt. 4th level (3 slots): confusion, greater invisibility. 5th level (2 slots): cone of cold, wall of force. 6th level (1 slot): globe of invulnerability.

actions.t: Melee Spell Attack: +8 to hit, reach 5 ft., one creature. Hit: 10 (3d6) necrotic damage, and the target can't regain hit points until the start of the mindwither's next turn.

The mindwither emits psychic energy in a 60-foot cone. Each creature in that area must succeed on a DC 16 Intelligence saving throw or take 22 (4d8 + 4) psychic damage and be stunned for 1 minute. A creature can repeat the saving throw at the end of each of its turns, ending the effect on itself on a success.

creatures.flavor: Withered lich-minds in Kelethtonreth's service: undead spellcasters whose skulls hum like struck bells. They coordinate the Bowl ambushes and save their counterspells for whoever coordinates back.
creatures.alternate: Substitute any CR 10 Medium undead aberration - a psionic horror that bought its own lichdom, with a mind blast, a phylactery, and no intention of joining anything larger.

creatures.name: Horned Colossus of Demonholme
creatures.resistances: cold, fire, lightning; bludgeoning, piercing, and slashing from nonmagical attacks

traits.t: The colossus deals double damage to objects and structures - including living trees.

The colossus ignores creatures unless they deal damage to it twice in the same round; its war is with its assigned objective. When it drops below half its hit points, its HEATED BRONZE COLLAR sears it into a berserk fury: it attacks the nearest creature each round, and the collar becomes exposed.

While the colossus is berserk, its bronze collar can be targeted: AC 20, 30 hit points, immune to poison and psychic damage. Destroying the collar kills the colossus in a spectacular convulsion at the start of its next turn. A creature grappling or climbing the colossus near its neck takes 10 (3d6) fire damage at the start of each of its turns.

actions.t: The colossus makes two attacks: one with its horns and one with its slam.
Melee Weapon Attack: +14 to hit, reach 15 ft., one target. Hit: 31 (4d10 + 9) piercing damage. Against an object or structure, this attack deals double damage (Siege Monster).

Melee Weapon Attack: +14 to hit, reach 15 ft., one target. Hit: 27 (4d8 + 9) bludgeoning damage, and if the target is a Huge or smaller creature, it must succeed on a DC 19 Strength saving throw or be knocked prone.

If the colossus moves at least 20 feet in a straight line, it can move through the spaces of Large or smaller creatures; each such creature must make a DC 19 Dexterity saving throw, taking 22 (4d10) bludgeoning damage and falling prone on a failure, or half damage on a success.

creatures.flavor: Forty feet of bison-headed muscle in a heated bronze collar, carvings etched into its horns, bellowing complaints in Abyssal. It did not choose this war; the collar chose for it - and the collar is its death.
creatures.alternate: Substitute any CR 17 demon built like a horned bull, scaled up to Gargantuan - charge, trample, and a gore that takes walls down.

creatures.name: Bognil the Peddler
creatures.languages: Common, Goblin, and an unsettling smattering of everything else

traits.t: Any creature that attempts to damage Bognil must first succeed on a DC 12 Charisma saving throw or be charmed until the end of its next turn. A creature charmed this way must use its action praising Bognil. (Robbing a bognil is its own punishment.)
Bognil's innate spellcasting ability is Charisma. He can innately cast the following spells, requiring no material components: At will: mage hand, prestidigitation. 1/day: hideous laughter.

Once per turn, when a creature within 30 feet of Bognil compliments him, his wares, or his prices, Bognil regains 5 hit points and knocks a little something off the total. He can hear a compliment through any language barrier.

actions.t: Melee Weapon Attack: +4 to hit, reach 5 ft., one target. Hit: 4 (1d4 + 2) bludgeoning damage. He is genuinely sorry about it.

creatures.flavor: A traveling potion-seller on a 10-day circuit that apparently includes Demonholme. If the party met a bognil peddler on the trade roads of Chapter 2, it is DEFINITELY the same guy, and he remembers their custom fondly. He never explains how he is anywhere.
creatures.alternate: Bognil is homebrew - substitute any CR 1 goblin whose nature runs backwards: healed by the damage it takes, harmed by the healing it is given, and impossible to hit while somebody at the table is laughing.

traits.t: The wolf has advantage on Wisdom (Perception) checks that rely on hearing or smell.
The wolf has advantage on an attack roll against a creature if at least one of the wolf's allies is within 5 feet of the creature and the ally isn't incapacitated.

actions.t: Melee Weapon Attack: +5 to hit, reach 5 ft., one target. Hit: 10 (2d6 + 3) piercing damage. If the target is a creature, it must succeed on a DC 13 Strength saving throw or be knocked prone.

traits.t: The tiger has advantage on Wisdom (Perception) checks that rely on smell.

If the tiger moves at least 20 feet straight toward a creature and then hits it with a claw attack on the same turn, that target must succeed on a DC 14 Strength saving throw or be knocked prone. If the target is prone, the tiger can make one bite attack against it as a bonus action.

actions.t: Melee Weapon Attack: +6 to hit, reach 5 ft., one target. Hit: 10 (1d10 + 5) piercing damage.
Melee Weapon Attack: +6 to hit, reach 5 ft., one target. Hit: 12 (2d6 + 5) slashing damage.

traits.t: The bear has advantage on Wisdom (Perception) checks that rely on smell.

actions.t: The bear makes two attacks: one with its bite and one with its claws.
Melee Weapon Attack: +7 to hit, reach 5 ft., one target. Hit: 9 (1d8 + 5) piercing damage.
Melee Weapon Attack: +7 to hit, reach 5 ft., one target. Hit: 12 (2d6 + 5) slashing damage.

traits.t: If the elk moves at least 20 feet straight toward a target and then hits it with a ram attack on the same turn, the target takes an extra 7 (2d6) damage. If the target is a creature, it must succeed on a DC 13 Strength saving throw or be knocked prone.

actions.t: Melee Weapon Attack: +5 to hit, reach 5 ft., one target. Hit: 6 (1d6 + 3) bludgeoning damage.
Melee Weapon Attack: +5 to hit, reach 5 ft., one prone creature. Hit: 8 (2d4 + 3) bludgeoning damage.

creatures.name: Glimmerkin
creatures.languages: Sylvan, and every language spoken near it for long enough to get bored

traits.t: A glimmerkin that has been told a creature's true name, formally and to its face, has advantage on all checks made to charm, find or aggravate that creature — and will not lie to it. This is the whole reason to give one your name, and the whole reason not to.
A glimmerkin has advantage on saving throws against spells and other magical effects.
As a bonus action, the glimmerkin turns invisible until its concentration ends, as if concentrating on a spell. Anything it wears or carries turns with it.

The glimmerkin's innate spellcasting ability is Charisma (spell save DC 13). It requires no material components. At will: druidcraft, dancing lights. One each per day: entangle, phantasmal force, sleep.

actions.t: Melee Weapon Attack: +7 to hit, reach 5 ft., one target. Hit: 1 piercing damage, and the target must succeed on a DC 13 Wisdom saving throw or drop one held object of the glimmerkin's choice.

The glimmerkin repeats, exactly, something a creature within 60 feet said earlier today, in that creature's own voice. Any creature that hears it and knows the speaker must succeed on a DC 13 Wisdom saving throw or spend its reaction turning to look.

creatures.alternate: Substitute any CR 1/4 Tiny fey trickster with innate spellcasting and at-will invisibility. It should be unkillable in practice rather than on paper — the encounter is a conversation.

traits.t: The owlbear has advantage on Wisdom (Perception) checks that rely on sight or smell.

actions.t: The owlbear makes two attacks: one with its beak and one with its claws.
Melee Weapon Attack: +7 to hit, reach 5 ft., one creature. Hit: 10 (1d10 + 5) piercing damage.
Melee Weapon Attack: +7 to hit, reach 5 ft., one target. Hit: 14 (2d8 + 5) slashing damage.

creatures.name: Night Hag
creatures.resistances: cold, fire; bludgeoning, piercing, and slashing from nonmagical attacks not made with cold iron weapons

traits.t: The hag's innate spellcasting ability is Charisma (spell save DC 14, +6 to hit with spell attacks). She can innately cast detect magic and magic missile at will, and each of the following twice per day: plane shift (self only), ray of enfeeblement, sleep.
The hag has advantage on saving throws against spells and other magical effects.

A night hag carries two very rare magic items that she must craft for herself: a heartstone (which lets her become ethereal and cures disease at a touch) and a soul bag (which can trap the soul of an evil humanoid dying within 30 feet of her).

actions.t: Melee Weapon Attack: +7 to hit, reach 5 ft., one target. Hit: 13 (2d8 + 4) slashing damage.

The hag magically polymorphs into a Small or Medium female humanoid, or back into her true form. Her statistics are the same in each form. Any equipment she is wearing or carrying isn't transformed. She reverts to her true form if she dies.
The hag magically enters the Ethereal Plane from the Material Plane, or vice versa. To do so, the hag must have a heartstone in her possession.

While on the Ethereal Plane, the hag magically touches a sleeping humanoid on the Material Plane. A protection from evil and good spell cast on the target prevents this contact, as does a magic circle. As long as the contact persists, the target has dreadful visions. If these visions last for at least 1 hour, the target gains no benefit from its rest, and its hit point maximum is reduced by 5 (1d10). If this effect reduces the target's hit point maximum to 0, the target dies, and if the target was evil, its soul is trapped in the hag's soul bag. The reduction to the target's hit point maximum lasts until removed by the greater restoration spell or similar magic.
The giant makes two greataxe attacks.
Melee Weapon Attack: +9 to hit, reach 10 ft., one target. Hit: 25 (3d12 + 6) slashing damage.
Ranged Weapon Attack: +9 to hit, range 60/240 ft., one target. Hit: 28 (4d10 + 6) bludgeoning damage.

traits.t: The dryad's innate spellcasting ability is Charisma (spell save DC 14). The dryad can innately cast druidcraft at will, and each of the following spells 3/day: entangle, goodberry; 1/day each: barkskin, pass without trace, shillelagh. It requires no material components.
The dryad has advantage on saving throws against spells and other magical effects.
The dryad can communicate with beasts and plants as if they shared a language.

Once on her turn, the dryad can use 10 feet of her movement to step magically into one living tree within her reach and emerge from a second living tree within 60 feet of the first tree, appearing in an unoccupied space within 5 feet of the second tree. Both trees must be Large or bigger.

actions.t: Melee Weapon Attack: +2 to hit (+6 to hit with shillelagh), reach 5 ft., one target. Hit: 2 (1d4) bludgeoning damage, or 8 (1d8 + 4) bludgeoning damage with shillelagh.

The dryad targets one humanoid or beast that she can see within 30 feet of her. If the target can see the dryad, it must succeed on a DC 14 Wisdom saving throw or be magically charmed. The charmed creature regards the dryad as a trusted friend to be heeded and protected. Although the target isn't under the dryad's control, it takes the dryad's requests or actions in the most favorable way it can. Each time the dryad or its allies do anything harmful to the target, it can repeat the saving throw, ending the effect on itself on a success. Otherwise, the effect lasts 24 hours or until the dryad dies, is on a different plane of existence from the target, or ends the effect as a bonus action. If a target's saving throw is successful, the target is immune to the dryad's Fey Charm for the next 24 hours. The dryad can have no more than one humanoid and up to three beasts charmed at a time.

creatures.name: Young Silver Dragon
creatures.senses: blindsight 30 ft., darkvision 120 ft., passive Perception 18

actions.t: The dragon makes three attacks: one with its bite and two with its claws.
Melee Weapon Attack: +10 to hit, reach 10 ft., one target. Hit: 17 (2d10 + 6) piercing damage.
Melee Weapon Attack: +10 to hit, reach 5 ft., one target. Hit: 13 (2d6 + 6) slashing damage.

The dragon uses one of the following breath weapons. Cold Breath: the dragon exhales an icy blast in a 30-foot cone. Each creature in that area must make a DC 17 Constitution saving throw, taking 54 (12d8) cold damage on a failed save, or half as much damage on a successful one.
