Paralyzing Breath: the dragon exhales paralyzing gas in a 30-foot cone. Each creature in that area must succeed on a DC 17 Constitution saving throw or be paralyzed for 1 minute. A creature can repeat the saving throw at the end of each of its turns, ending the effect on itself on a success.

creatures.name: Hollowmourn
creatures.resistances: acid, fire, lightning, thunder; bludgeoning, piercing, and slashing from nonmagical attacks
creatures.immunities: cold, necrotic, poison; charmed, exhaustion, frightened, grappled, paralyzed, petrified, poisoned, prone, restrained
creatures.languages: Common, and whatever tongue it was grieving in

traits.t: A hollowmourn is fixed to the place its grief happened and cannot travel more than 60 feet from it by any means, willing or forced. Everything it can do, it can do only there. Cross the ground and you have beaten it.
A hollowmourn knows the number and rough bearing of every living creature within 5 miles. It does not know what they are, only that they are still going.
A hollowmourn moves through creatures, walls and stone as though they were deep snow. It takes 5 (1d10) force damage if it finishes its turn inside something solid.

actions.t: Melee Spell Attack: +6 to hit, reach 5 ft., one target. Hit: 14 (4d6) necrotic damage, and the target cannot regain hit points until the end of its next turn.

Each living creature within 60 feet that can see the hollowmourn must succeed on a DC 14 Wisdom saving throw or be frightened for 1 minute, repeating the save at the end of each of its turns. A creature that succeeds, or whose fright ends, cannot be affected by that hollowmourn's face again for 24 hours.

Out of direct sunlight, the hollowmourn lets go of the sound it has been holding. Constructs and undead do not hear it. Every other creature within 30 feet that can hear must make a DC 13 Constitution saving throw, dropping to 0 hit points on a failure and taking 11 (2d10) psychic damage on a success. A creature that has already been reduced to 0 by a keening this year has advantage on the save — the body learns.

creatures.alternate: Substitute any CR 4 incorporeal undead whose signature action is a killing scream; give it the Bound to the Turning trait or the encounter stops working.

traits.t: The wolf has advantage on Wisdom (Perception) checks that rely on hearing or smell.
The wolf has advantage on an attack roll against a creature if at least one of the wolf's allies is within 5 feet of the creature and the ally isn't incapacitated.
The wolf has advantage on Dexterity (Stealth) checks made to hide in snowy terrain.

actions.t: Melee Weapon Attack: +6 to hit, reach 5 ft., one target. Hit: 11 (2d6 + 4) piercing damage. If the target is a creature, it must succeed on a DC 14 Strength saving throw or be knocked prone.

The wolf exhales a blast of freezing wind in a 15-foot cone. Each creature in that area must make a DC 12 Dexterity saving throw, taking 18 (4d8) cold damage on a failed save, or half as much damage on a successful one.

traits.t: If the mammoth moves at least 20 feet straight toward a creature and then hits it with a gore attack on the same turn, that target must succeed on a DC 18 Strength saving throw or be knocked prone. If the target is prone, the mammoth can make one stomp attack against it as a bonus action.

actions.t: Melee Weapon Attack: +10 to hit, reach 10 ft., one target. Hit: 25 (4d8 + 7) piercing damage.
Melee Weapon Attack: +10 to hit, reach 5 ft., one prone creature. Hit: 29 (4d10 + 7) bludgeoning damage.

creatures.name: Rimewalker
creatures.languages: understands Giant but does not speak

traits.t: While a rimewalker holds still in snow it is indistinguishable from a snowbank, and a creature must succeed on a DC 18 Wisdom (Perception) check to tell otherwise. It has advantage on Dexterity (Stealth) checks in snow whether it is holding still or not.
A rimewalker that takes fire damage has disadvantage on attack rolls and ability checks until the end of its next turn, and will not willingly end its turn within 10 feet of an open fire.
A rimewalker has advantage on Wisdom (Perception) checks that rely on smell, and can smell a warm-blooded creature through a closed tent at 200 feet.

actions.t: The rimewalker uses Frostgaze if it is available, then makes two claw attacks.
Melee Weapon Attack: +10 to hit, reach 10 ft., one target. Hit: 15 (2d8 + 6) slashing damage plus 7 (2d6) cold damage.

The rimewalker fixes on one creature it can see within 30 feet. If the target can see it back, the target must succeed on a DC 17 Constitution saving throw or take 21 (6d6) cold damage and be paralyzed for 1 minute, unless the target is immune to cold damage. The target repeats the save at the end of each of its turns. A creature that succeeds, or whose paralysis ends, cannot be frostgazed by that rimewalker again for 1 hour.

The rimewalker breathes out a 30-foot cone of driving ice. Each creature in it makes a DC 17 Constitution saving throw, taking 44 (8d10) cold damage on a failure or half as much on a success. The area is heavily obscured until the end of the rimewalker's next turn — which is the point of it.

creatures.alternate: Substitute any CR 9 Huge cold-country brute with a freezing gaze and a cone of cold breath.

traits.t: The roc has advantage on Wisdom (Perception) checks that rely on sight.

actions.t: The roc makes two attacks: one with its beak and one with its talons.
Melee Weapon Attack: +13 to hit, reach 10 ft., one target. Hit: 27 (4d8 + 9) piercing damage.

Melee Weapon Attack: +13 to hit, reach 5 ft., one target. Hit: 23 (4d6 + 9) slashing damage, and the target is grappled (escape DC 19). Until this grapple ends, the target is restrained, and the roc can't use its talons on another target.

traits.t: While the treant remains motionless, it is indistinguishable from a normal tree.
The treant deals double damage to objects and structures.

actions.t: The treant makes two slam attacks.
Melee Weapon Attack: +10 to hit, reach 5 ft., one target. Hit: 16 (3d6 + 6) bludgeoning damage.
Ranged Weapon Attack: +10 to hit, range 60/180 ft., one target. Hit: 28 (4d10 + 6) bludgeoning damage.

The treant magically animates one or two trees it can see within 60 feet of it. These trees have the same statistics as a treant, except they have Intelligence and Charisma scores of 1, they can't speak, and they have only the Slam action option. An animated tree acts as an ally of the treant. The tree remains animate for 1 day or until it dies; until the treant dies or is more than 120 feet from the tree; or until the treant takes a bonus action to turn it back into an inanimate tree. The tree then takes root if possible.

creatures.name: Adult Silver Dragon
creatures.senses: blindsight 60 ft., darkvision 120 ft., passive Perception 21

traits.t: If the dragon fails a saving throw, it can choose to succeed instead.

actions.t: The dragon can use its Frightful Presence. It then makes three attacks: one with its bite and two with its claws.
Melee Weapon Attack: +13 to hit, reach 10 ft., one target. Hit: 19 (2d10 + 8) piercing damage.
Melee Weapon Attack: +13 to hit, reach 5 ft., one target. Hit: 15 (2d6 + 8) slashing damage.
Melee Weapon Attack: +13 to hit, reach 15 ft., one target. Hit: 17 (2d8 + 8) bludgeoning damage.

Each creature of the dragon's choice that is within 120 feet of the dragon and aware of it must succeed on a DC 18 Wisdom saving throw or become frightened for 1 minute. A creature can repeat the saving throw at the end of each of its turns, ending the effect on itself on a success. If a creature's saving throw is successful or the effect ends for it, the creature is immune to the dragon's Frightful Presence for the next 24 hours.

The dragon uses one of the following breath weapons. Cold Breath: the dragon exhales an icy blast in a 60-foot cone. Each creature in that area must make a DC 20 Constitution saving throw, taking 58 (13d8) cold damage on a failed save, or half as much damage on a successful one. Paralyzing Breath: the dragon exhales paralyzing gas in a 60-foot cone. Each creature in that area must succeed on a DC 20 Constitution saving throw or be paralyzed for 1 minute. A creature can repeat the saving throw at the end of each of its turns, ending the effect on itself on a success.

Detect: the dragon makes a Wisdom (Perception) check. Tail Attack: the dragon makes a tail attack. Wing Attack (Costs 2 Actions): the dragon beats its wings. Each creature within 10 feet of the dragon must succeed on a DC 21 Dexterity saving throw or take 15 (2d6 + 8) bludgeoning damage and be knocked prone. The dragon can then fly up to half its flying speed.

creatures.name: Ancient Silver Dragon
creatures.senses: blindsight 60 ft., darkvision 120 ft., passive Perception 26

traits.t: If the dragon fails a saving throw, it can choose to succeed instead.

actions.t: The dragon can use its Frightful Presence. It then makes three attacks: one with its bite and two with its claws.
Melee Weapon Attack: +17 to hit, reach 15 ft., one target. Hit: 21 (2d10 + 10) piercing damage.
Melee Weapon Attack: +17 to hit, reach 10 ft., one target. Hit: 17 (2d6 + 10) slashing damage.
Melee Weapon Attack: +17 to hit, reach 20 ft., one target. Hit: 19 (2d8 + 10) bludgeoning damage.

Each creature of the dragon's choice that is within 120 feet of the dragon and aware of it must succeed on a DC 21 Wisdom saving throw or become frightened for 1 minute. A creature can repeat the saving throw at the end of each of its turns, ending the effect on itself on a success. If a creature's saving throw is successful or the effect ends for it, the creature is immune to the dragon's Frightful Presence for the next 24 hours.

The dragon uses one of the following breath weapons. Cold Breath: the dragon exhales an icy blast in a 90-foot cone. Each creature in that area must make a DC 24 Constitution saving throw, taking 67 (15d8) cold damage on a failed save, or half as much damage on a successful one. Paralyzing Breath: the dragon exhales paralyzing gas in a 90-foot cone. Each creature in that area must succeed on a DC 24 Constitution saving throw or be paralyzed for 1 minute. A creature can repeat the saving throw at the end of each of its turns, ending the effect on itself on a success.

Detect: the dragon makes a Wisdom (Perception) check. Tail Attack: the dragon makes a tail attack. Wing Attack (Costs 2 Actions): the dragon beats its wings. Each creature within 15 feet of the dragon must succeed on a DC 25 Dexterity saving throw or take 17 (2d6 + 10) bludgeoning damage and be knocked prone. The dragon can then fly up to half its flying speed.

dramatis.name: Empress Arith Tezaibel Kethith
dramatis.tags: Half-Elf, she/her - Empress of Torrentath
dramatis.text: Fifty years on the throne; a century and a half of memory. Once the young sword of Kaddrin Vurrath, now the anchor of an empire. PLAY HER: warm to the brave, surgical to the evasive, and never surprised twice. She speaks the word Knakknthazn aloud exactly once in this campaign and the court gasps.

dramatis.name: Princeps Ontavex Kethith
dramatis.tags: Tiefling, they/them - heir presumptive
dramatis.text: Tall, sleek, purple horns combed back with long black hair; ceremonial purple and gilded boots. PLAY THEM: flawlessly gracious, one beat too composed - the only figure on the dais still standing when the shot cracks (DC 25 Insight). DM SECRET, both layers: the Princeps STRUCK A BARGAIN - tricked by Essax with the promise of the Empire once the ritual of the trees completes, they sold the knowledge of the Aria tree as payment - and the glabrezu KOTH'TAVUTH possessing them is the collateral Essax took on the deal. Every audience is a report to the enemy; every smile is two people smiling.

dramatis.name: Rodsonn
dramatis.tags: The Empress' personal guard
dramatis.text: The one who moved before the crack finished echoing - taking the shot through the shoulder that the Empress' warded cape might have turned anyway. PLAY HIM: economy itself; he has said perhaps forty words in fifty years of service and every one of them was load-bearing. He heals; he resumes his post; he notices who checks on him. Those people have a friend at court.

dramatis.name: Lislanis
dramatis.tags: Half-Elf, she/her - clerk of the Mayor's manor, Kitetown
dramatis.text: The front desk of Hurdatin Underfall's manor, and the keeper of his appointment book (three slots: half an hour, two hours, four hours). PLAY HER: professional warmth with a bureaucrat's memory - she recalls every visitor, which makes her quietly one of the best-informed people in Kitetown.

dramatis.name: The Farm Families of Kitetown
dramatis.tags: The breadbasket south of the wall
dramatis.text: Four households in a row of thatch roofs: the SIDES (Hors, half-orc, 50; Eswyn, half-elf, 75; Xanral, 14; little Pulri, 7), the JOFILLS (old Wiphar, 102; May, human, 53; daughters Maaris, Bridrin, Vicsula), the SEWELLS (Batkin and Isot; Matilda, 15; Joss, 10; Hob, 6), and the FERNHARES (mothers Xina and Zefda; Kasdon, 22). They trade river knowledge for cheese, adopt polite strangers instantly, and are the faces the endgame will put on the word EMPIRE.

dramatis.name: Ru
dramatis.tags: Watcher of the Dark Star - Kitetown rooftops
dramatis.text: The reason the Bowl ambush exists: she watched the drop point, read the party's message, resealed it (DC 25 Perception to catch the tampered wax), and sold the route. PLAY HER (if the party ever finds her): unrepentant, professional, and genuinely impressed by anyone who traces the ambush back to a rooftop. The record leaves her at large - a loose end with excellent eyesight.

dramatis.name: Devan Runewhirl
dramatis.tags: Human - Mayor of Yririe
dramatis.text: Welcoming, overworked, and entirely uninformed - Yririe's mayor governs a dock town from a hall behind the warehouse district and likes it that way. PLAY HIM: helpful about everything that doesn't matter.

dramatis.name: Serell 'the Kicker'
dramatis.tags: Human, he/him - keeper of the Quiet Star, Yririe; retired Knight of the Empire
dramatis.text: An inn on the north edge, run by a man who once wore plate for the crown and now polishes tankards with the same discipline. PLAY HIM: he clocks the party's bearing instantly, asks nothing, and - if treated with respect - offers exactly one piece of soldier's advice per stay. It is always good advice.

dramatis.name: The Crew of the River Serpent
dramatis.tags: Doman Bail's people
dramatis.text: KET, First Mate - half-orc, he/him, a Veteran with a quartermaster's glare. OKTUX (they/them) and THUSH (he/him), half-orc deckhands. LIGART, ANDREU, GIB, WILL, TOMAS, and SANSON, human crewmates who play cards badly and sing worse. And KEYA, elf scout, the eyes in the crow's nest - she spots the scarecrow poles, she reads the clear water, and nothing gets close to the Serpent before she has named it. Defend any of them unasked, and the ship becomes family.

dramatis.name: Essax (born Robert 'Bobby'; true name Amurt Sselkcer)
dramatis.tags: Tiefling necromancer - the villain
dramatis.text: A gaunt young tiefling driven insane by the psionic touch of Kelethtonreth 129 years ago; now the mist-shrouded iron fist of the Bronze Storm Empire. He appears in this campaign first as a NAME - a rotting mark, a fanatic's prayer - and should stay offstage for a long, long time. His army calls his patron The One.

dramatis.name: Thron
dramatis.tags: Glabrezu - Essax's field commander
dramatis.text: Performs the teleportation rituals that deliver hunters onto the party's trail. Named aloud for the first time by the Sleapless captive (scene 3.6). Four arms, cold intelligence, and a professional's patience.

dramatis.name: Wispa Sweetcup
dramatis.tags: Fairy, she/her - mentor
dramatis.text: An old fairy who has collected favors and friends across half the Empire. PLAY HER: endearments as punctuation, steel underneath. Anyone she sponsors is 'her very best' and had better act like it.

dramatis.name: Hurdatin Underfall
dramatis.tags: Dwarf, he/him - Mayor of Kitetown
dramatis.text: A dwarf who chose to represent his kin ABOVE ground - which cost him family standing below it; to any dwarf PC he is a friend of the family, albeit an estranged one, and they likely never heard he was elected. His study is scaled to him and nothing else (save the weapons rack: a crossed war hammer and battle axe), and the SEVEN CONJOINED SILVER RINGS of the mayoral office hang at his chest on a chain. Honest to a fault; his help is real, paper-shaped, and comes with wine, bread, cheese, and both of the Empress' proclamations. PLAY HIM: hospitality first, logistics second, gossip never - and if a dwarf walks in, eyes wide and twenty years younger for one sentence: 'Do my eyes deceive?'

dramatis.name: Doman Bail
dramatis.tags: Human, he/him - Captain of the River Serpent
dramatis.text: The best smuggler on the Trenlem and proud of the distinction. PLAY HIM: professional warmth that hardens instantly when his crew is threatened - and melts permanently for anyone who defends them unasked. HIS VOICE: the rolling 'do be' cadence his greeting sets ('I be the capton... do you be the party...'), oaths sworn on his own fortune, and blunt bargaining with no second price - an honest smuggler who holds a bought bargain sacred and reads a passenger the way he reads the river. Nothing on the water rattles him; only threats to his people do. His year-of-ports map is a standing favor the campaign can cash anywhere. DM ONLY - CROSSED PATHS: Corben Vash, the wolf-team guide of the Dragonspine race, has ridden this deck; how their paths crossed is a story all this world's own, and each man tells it differently. It matters only if your table has run (or will run) the one-shot - a shared name, a raised mug, nothing more.

dramatis.name: Diana
dramatis.tags: Human, she/her - Paladin of Teg
dramatis.text: A border-tribe paladin carrying eyewitness testimony to the Empress: the four-armed demon, the kobold sniper, the rend in space. PLAY HER: measured, exact, allergic to embellishment - which makes her account terrifying. Whether she arrives safely is a thread the DM controls.

dramatis.name: The Kobold Sniper
dramatis.tags: Kobold - the trigger finger
dramatis.text: Fired the shot at the Empress through a rend in space using a slender long pipe, then melted through senior rangers like fog. Never caught; never named. A recurring cameo for later chapters if you want the players to develop a very personal grudge.

dramatis.name: Maros Softblossom
dramatis.tags: Halfling, he/him, 129 - Captain of the Guard, Yuvl Ilmern
dramatis.text: Gruff despite two centuries of general peace, because he earned it elsewhere: a sellsword for a time on a ship across the ocean, and in the lands to the west. PLAY HIM: economical, unimpressed, fair - he asks hard questions once and listens completely to the answers. Respect is his currency and he pays promptly.

dramatis.name: Frobyn Mossblossom
dramatis.tags: Halfling, she/her, 188 - First Counsel of the Twelve
dramatis.text: The most powerful person in Aria who is not the Sovereign - and, when the party first sees her, mid-argument with the Empress herself. PLAY HER: velvet procedure over iron opinion. Whatever she and the Empress disagree about is never stated in this record - it is yours to invent, and worth inventing well.

dramatis.name: Unasica Copperglide
dramatis.tags: Halfling, she/her, 190 - Sovereign's Steward
dramatis.text: Missing for a tenday; found worse for wear; explaining nothing. PLAY HER: composed the way porcelain is composed. The record never says where she was. If your table pulls the thread, the answer should touch the manhunt, the lockdown, and someone's secret - build it from what your party fears.

dramatis.name: Sovereign Liddamacin Rufius
dramatis.tags: Halfling, they/them, 194 - Sovereign of Aria
dramatis.text: Greater-among-equals over the Council of Twelve; once Lid of Kaddrin Vurrath, a monastery adult at sixty-five who joined the world late. PLAY THEM: stillness that outranks noise. They were THERE when Kelethtonreth was sealed - and they know exactly what a wilting sacred tree means.

dramatis.name: Valfer Keenlade
dramatis.tags: Halfling, he/him, 165 - Mastermind, the Moonlight Strategy
dramatis.text: The mind of the Twins' native guild. PLAY HIM: soft-spoken, precise, always two questions ahead - he prices everything said in the room and never haggles twice.

dramatis.name: Elielle Nimblesurge
dramatis.tags: Halfling, she/her, 123 - Ringleader, the Moonlight Strategy
dramatis.text: Operations. PLAY HER: brisk warmth, a docker's vocabulary, and the only person who interrupts Valfer. If the party earns a friend in the guild, it is her.

dramatis.name: Ruglal Vuzrubor
dramatis.tags: Dark Elf, she/her, 200 - Captain, the Moonlight Strategy
dramatis.text: Muscle, discipline, and a long memory. PLAY HER: fewest words in the room, first to be obeyed. DM NOTE: a dark elf captain in a city hunting 'a Dark Elf' is a coincidence the table will chew on - the record never resolves it. Decide for yourself whether Johnny saw her, her people, or something wearing the rumor.

dramatis.name: Rinys Glowseeker
dramatis.tags: Proprietor of Ebony Camp, Ru Ailmen
dramatis.text: Innkeep of the treetop lodge and the guild's front door. PLAY HER: hospitality with excellent hearing. Tenday discounts for guests she likes; directions to a hideout for guests who prove out.

dramatis.name: Halwrick Twilightcheeks
dramatis.tags: Halfling, he/him, 86 - warehouse 'worker', Banminster Co.
dramatis.text: The elevator man. Does not want to give his name (he will, if the party insists, with a sigh). PLAY HIM: pass phrases delivered like weather reports, and one genuine kindness at the bottom of the shaft: 'Be on your guard - those you are affiliated with are not the only ones who use these tunnels.'

dramatis.name: Bresira Deepwind
dramatis.tags: Innkeeper, the Ancient Blossom, Ru Ailmen
dramatis.text: Good rooms, better counsel. PLAY HER: the innkeeper every party adopts - she notices who comes in limping and sends up the good stew unasked. A safe interlocutor for players thinking out loud.

dramatis.name: Kili Dwokhumilin
dramatis.tags: Dwarf, she/her - Thane of Knakknthazn; once of Kaddrin Vurrath
dramatis.text: A grandmotherly dwarf with a luscious gray beard curled to her belt, who thanks heroes like family and delivers history like a bedtime story with a knife in it. PLAY HER: warmth first, then the tale (Chapter 10, scene 10.3 - deliver it whole). She was THERE. She remembers Bobby fondly. That is the tragedy.

dramatis.name: Zontif
dramatis.tags: Tiefling, she/her - Defender of Aedlab
dramatis.text: A Defender of the sacred tree and, if the Warden's Child hook is in play, that PC's mother. Dressed to fade into the forest; never without her green-gem Key Bracelet - until Chapter 9, when it is missing and the reason is a violation she cannot remember. PLAY HER: competence as love language. Her dive from the canopy, yelling 'MY DREAMS ARE MY OWN' in Abyssal, is the chapter's war cry.

dramatis.name: Nika Blackthorn
dramatis.tags: Tiefling, she/her - hooded operative of the Bronze Storm - allegiance: her own
dramatis.text: The seventh hood at Aedlab, on nobody's side but the Defenders'. Under the hood: a red-skinned tiefling, frost-pale eyes, quicker than the eye wants to allow, and haunted by something she has never named at any table. She heals the fallen VISIBLY, extracts them by teleportation pyramid, and leaves an invitation shaped like an insult: 'Retrieve them at Terrid Hall if you're so daring. Come to the Bronze Storm empire and see what you've done.' PLAY HER: fast, furious, and right about at least one thing. The next campaign's door, wearing a hood.

dramatis.name: Alias
dramatis.tags: Half-Elf bard, he/him - storyteller of the Bronze Storm Empire
dramatis.text: The court's other guest: a Bronze Storm-born storyteller the court of Bhindarul vetted and found reputable before the party ever arrived - introduced at the Low Keep in 10.1, lute case and all. His contacts carry letters no realm road can (10.2), and his rumors are good (10.4). Commune says UNCERTAIN and the book keeps it that way. PLAY HIM: genuinely charming, genuinely useful, genuinely evasive about exactly one decade of his life. He is optional at every step - he travels only if the table takes him (the long play is Contingency C5). If he goes: he stays behind in Demonholme in Chapter 11 - quietly, without telling anyone - and the reunion in Chapter 12 is either heartwarming or damning. Decide only when your table forces you to.

dramatis.name: Luvon Trisbalar
dramatis.tags: Elf druid, he/him - leader of the elven troop
dramatis.text: Twenty-four scouts move like weather; he moves like the season changing. PLAY HIM: few words, all of them load-bearing. The elves came for Aedlab and stayed for the grief - he treats the stump like a grave, because it is one.

dramatis.name: Knight Ordran Dwokhumilin
dramatis.tags: Dwarf knight - the advance force
dramatis.text: Leads the dwarven Knights who teleport into the counter-charge. PLAY HIM: parade-ground crisp until the fighting starts, then joyful in a way that worries people. Demonstrates the Transportation circle in Bhindarul by stepping onto it mid-sentence.

dramatis.name: Gagnot Axeborn & Dalothun Gravelbreaker
dramatis.tags: Dwarf escort & realm wizard, Bhindarul
dramatis.text: The party's assigned logistics in Chapter 10: Gagnot walks with them, Dalothun teleports for them. PLAY THEM as a double act - Gagnot answers every question with directions, Dalothun answers every direction with questions.

dramatis.name: Relane
dramatis.tags: Deva, angel of Essa - a century in an Iron Flask
dramatis.text: Trapped since the raising of the great wall; freed in a kitchen outside time by a hero asking the right question. PLAY HER: gratitude with a long memory and precise information - she can expound the true properties of a certain amulet, and she remembers exactly who corked the flask. Stat block: Appendix A, Deva.

dramatis.name: Essa
dramatis.tags: Goddess of All That Grows - CG - the tea-pourer
dramatis.text: She has been watching from afar; she cracked the rift the party used; she answers prayers with directions and, once, a giggle. PLAY HER: a goddess doing an aunt impression and not quite hiding the divinity - every mundane gesture lands one degree too perfectly. Grants each hero one true answer and the band one boon, and asks for nothing. That, too, should worry the wise.

dramatis.name: The Rice-Hat Guide
dramatis.tags: Verbrechen, the Bronze Storm Empire - epilogue thread
dramatis.text: A man in a rice-paddy hat and brown robes, boiling water over a precise little fire on the main road of Verbrechen, an unfamiliar curved sword at his hip: 'Greetings, fair travelers - can you spare some food? Perhaps I can be your guide in these lands, for compensation?' He knows the way to the Verboten mines, two days north. Everything else about him is the next campaign's business.

magicItems.name: The Pendant of Torrentath
magicItems.text: Worn by the reigning sovereign. When presented to worthy souls in the Empire's need, the pendant chooses Champions - the selection made by the Empire itself, not the wearer. The chosen glow faintly, and on kneeling are bound: each Champion gains permanent unerring awareness of the direction of the four surface sacred trees, and the authority of the crown. The bond cannot be removed while the Champion lives; whether it can be refused twice has never been tested.

magicItems.name: Dark Star Identification Ring
magicItems.text: A plain iron band with a seven-pointed black star inlay, worn on the inside of the belt, never the finger. Proof of Dark Star rank. In the Twin Cities, showing captured rings to the right people opens doors that gold cannot (Chapter 4: the Moonlight Strategy) - and marks the bearer to Dark Star loyalists.

magicItems.name: The Empress' Shield-Cape
magicItems.text: The ceremonial cape of the reigning sovereign, warded by the court's finest abjurers. Once per scene, as a reaction, the cape can turn one hit against its wearer into a miss - a shimmer like heat off stone, gone before most eyes register it. At the fiftieth-anniversary celebration it was never tested: Rodsonn's shoulder got there first. (Reconstructed from a margin note - tune the trigger to taste.)

magicItems.name: One-Way Teleportation Wristband
magicItems.text: A leather band with a single destination woven into it. Snapping the band teleports the wearer to the keyed circle. Recovered examples are spent and inert - but they prove someone is manufacturing retreat for expendable troops.

magicItems.name: The Sarcophagus of the New Day
magicItems.text: A smooth stone sarcophagus found behind four locks and a watertight threshold in the Underbelly, crossed by three floor-bolted chains warded with 7th-level Abjuration (the chains absorb force damage and are immune to fire, necrotic, cold, lightning, poison, bludgeoning, and slashing). Draconic runes on the lid read: RISE, RISE AND COME FORTH TO A NEW DAY. Identification reveals a tool of profound HEALING - laced, at every layer of the working, with warnings of madness. The record deliberately leaves its function unresolved: it was opened by no one and moved into a basement. Suggested handling if a table commits: a creature sealed within for a full night is restored - hit points, diseases, curses, even death within a tenday - and rises changed, carrying something of whoever was healed in it before. The chains say somebody once asked the opposite question. What rises on a new day is yours to answer. Full side quest - the room, the chains, the engine, and the price: Side Quests > What Rises on a New Day.

magicItems.name: Painter's Wells of Making
magicItems.text: A fine one-pound wooden box with an almost seamless sliding top: three inlaid, stoppered wells of primary-color paint, and a beautifully crafted metal-handled brush. Anything painted with the wells becomes real as the last stroke finishes - up to 1,000 square feet of two-dimensional surface (a door, a pit, a window) or 10 cubic feet of three-dimensional objects (a boat, a ladder, a chest). Painted objects are nonmagical and mundane once created. The wells hold enough pigment for 10 uses. ALTERNATE: substitute Marvelous Pigments.

magicItems.name: Tree Heart
magicItems.text: The living core of a sacred tree: a heartwood stone, warm to the touch, faintly luminous, humming at the edge of hearing. Extracted, a heart serves great arcane work as a battery or FOCAL POINT - most terribly, as an anchor for plane-shifting ritual at continental scale (three suffice for a lesser working; see Chapter 10). A heart has 300 hit points and AC 14 for the purposes of being shattered mid-ritual, and shattering one breaks any working anchored to it. Aedlab's heart, pulled whole from the burst trunk where the tree fell, is LARGER than the others - the record never says why, and the vaults of Bhindarul are in no hurry to find out.

magicItems.name: Key Bracelet of the Defenders
magicItems.text: A woven band set with a single green gem, keyed to a sacred tree's barrier. With an intricate set of hand motions - no arcane warping, nothing detectable as spellwork - the wearer opens a passage through the tree's protections for themselves and those they lead. A bracelet answers only its bonded Defender... which is why the theft that breaches Aedlab required not a thief but a RITUAL: the bearer's mind read, an idea planted as her own, the event wiped (Chapter 9, scene 9.2). Hers is found in the grass outside the fallen barrier when the field settles (9.6) - unbroken, and heavier than it looks.

magicItems.name: Teleportation Pyramid
magicItems.text: Nika Blackthorn's exit from Aedlab — a cut-ruby pyramid, three goat eyes at its apex, keyed to a distant circle written on no map the party owns: Terrid Hall, in the Bronze Storm Empire. She had only one charge to spend, so it looked like a one-and-done. Full stats: Campaign Items — the Ruby Pyramid of Teleportation.

magicItems.name: Stormcleave
magicItems.text: Khulgroubelynn Koboldaxe's own work and the one piece on the Garage's board he will not haggle over: a broad dwarven battleaxe, a haft of blued iron, and a bead of storm-glass set behind the bit that hums when weather is coming. You gain a +1 bonus to attack and damage rolls made with this magic weapon. When you score a critical hit with it the bead discharges - the target and each creature of your choice within 5 feet of it take an extra 2d6 thunder damage, and the crack carries 300 feet. Once between long rests, as a bonus action, you can call the storm up early: the next attack you hit with before the end of your next turn deals that same extra 2d6 thunder whether or not it is a critical. 2,000 gp in The Storm Hammer Garage, and Khulgroubelynn will quote a matching pair to a party that asks. ALTERNATE: substitute any +1 battleaxe.

handouts.name: Proclamation of the Empress (Public)
handouts.text:
BY ORDER OF HER IMPERIAL MAJESTY, ARITH TEZAIBEL KETHITH, EMPRESS OF TORRENTATH - posted by criers in every town and holding of the Empire:

Let it be known that we are at war with those that dwell beyond the Sinuous World Spine Mountains, the great eastern barrier raised by the four gods themselves to protect us.

To the north and to the south our sister nations are in peril. Refugees are pouring in on the borders of Pand and Teg.

With this influx of people in hardship we have seen banditry on the rise, looting and pillaging at our furthest outpost towers and strongholds.

The four sacred trees, though hidden and guarded by great magics, may be in peril.

We must stabilize our Empire, for if we do not and prepare for the coming evil, we will all perish.

I call to all citizens of Torrentath. Join in to keep the peace we have known for generations. Do what you can by seeking out your steward, panarch, lord or sovereign's service.

Given under Our hand and the Great Seal of the Empire, at the Sovereign Palace in Ru Ailmen, in the fiftieth year of Our reign.

ARITH TEZAIBEL KETHITH
By Grace of the Pendant, Empress of Torrentath

Let no hand deface this notice, under penalty of the crown's justice.

handouts.name: Proclamation of the Empress (Official Channels)
handouts.text:
UNDER SEAL. NOT FOR POSTING. Circulated to stewards, panarchs, lords, and sovereigns of the Empire, and to no other hand.

You have read the notice We set upon your town posts. Read now what it does not say.

Let it be known that upon the fiftieth celebration of the reign, cowardly violence was attempted against the crown and answered by the courage of common and noble blood alike. Let it be known that the Pendant of Torrentath has chosen, and CHAMPIONS OF THE EMPIRE walk the roads once more, about the Empire's business. Render them aid as you would the crown itself.

Let every citizen be watchful. Report to your local guard any stranger asking after the old places, any mark of decay upon living wood, and any teleportation worked without a wizard to claim it.

These three signs are not to be criered. A frightened Empire is a stampeding one, and We have no wish to learn what a stampede does to a road Our Champions must travel. Watch. Report. Say nothing.

The Empire endures.

Given under Our hand and the Great Seal of the Empire, at the Sovereign Palace in Ru Ailmen, in the fiftieth year of Our reign.

ARITH TEZAIBEL KETHITH
By Grace of the Pendant, Empress of Torrentath

handouts.name: The Tile Code of the Twins
handouts.text:
Learn a building by its roof:
INNS blue
TAVERNS red
GENERAL STORES yellow
MAGIC purple
APOTHECARIES green
WAREHOUSES brown
OFFICIAL CITY BUILDINGS gray
MARKETS orange

Respect the gray ones. - Doman Bail

handouts.name: The River Serpent - Year of Ports
handouts.text: Keep this close to your chest. Where the Serpent and her crew will be, by month: trading up the Irricam through high summer; the Trenlem coves in the turning seasons; home to the North Docks of Ru Ailmen for Deepwinter. Show this paper at any slip we hold and passage is yours. Should you need us for travel, we will assist you. - D.B. (DM: place specific coves and dates to suit your table's map.)

handouts.name: The Bottle
handouts.text:
A small, heavy glass bottle, warm to the touch. Its surface is crowded with the same three words, repeated in a dozen languages and alphabets - and once more, larger than all the rest:

DO NOT OPEN

handouts.name: Shipping Manifest - the 'Green Star'
handouts.text:
MANIFEST OF LADING - the GREEN STAR, out of Yririe. Owner: Banminster Co. Master: Cpt. L. Wright.
To the Dock Master, for offload and claim:
1 crate lanterns, LEFT-handed fittings
2 bolts canvas, RIGHT weave, OVER-strength BRIDGE cord
1 cask pitch, LEFT of hold
4 coils rope, RIGHT lay
2 casks nails, RIGHT drawn
1 pallet timber, OVER-cut for BRIDGE work
6 crates saltfish, DOWN-salted, WATERFALL-cured, STAIRS-stacked
3 casks lampoil, FOLLOW standing FLOW order
1 chest fittings, RIGHT-threaded
1 chest fittings, LEFT-threaded
sundries for the GATE PORT warehouse, DOOR-side.
Balance of cargo to cross the CHANNEL for the EXPANSE consignment, opposite GATE PORT, DOOR-side. Then: 1 crate RIGHT-angle braces (CORRIDOR grade)
1 crate LEFT-hinge sets
1 crate LEFT-hinge sets, across-BASIN stock, CORRIDOR grade
2 DOUBLE-DOOR frames
EXIT hardware, SHAFT-mounted.
Signed: L. Wright, Master. (A Thieves' Cant reader extracts the route at a glance; everyone else sees paperwork.)

handouts.name: The Map on the Trunk
handouts.text: Etched in living bark, glowing faintly with arcane light: five trees arranged across a continent's silhouette - four you have seen in your mind's eye, and a fifth whose place is marked but whose name refuses to be read. Beside each tree, a column of names in a fluid script: the Defenders. Beside one tree, below the list of venerable names, a smudge - dark, rotten, dabbed there like a thumbprint of decay. It is a name. You know it the way you know a burn: ESSAX.

charOptions.name: The Standing Order
charOptions.summary: A soldier does not fight by inspiration. He fights by orders — called out loud, on the beat, the way the line regiments of Torrentath have drilled them for two hundred years. Most veterans come off the muster roll remembering three.

features.t: You have four order dice, each a d8. You regain all expended order dice when you finish a short or long rest. Your order DC is 8 + your proficiency bonus + your Strength or Dexterity modifier, chosen when you take this archetype and fixed thereafter.

Once on each of your turns, when you hit a creature with a weapon attack, you may spend one order die, add it to that attack's damage, and call one order you know. You know three: Hold the Line, Called Shot and Sweep the Legs.

This order is called out of turn. When a creature you can see misses you with a melee attack, you may spend an order die as a reaction and make one melee weapon attack against it, adding the die to the damage.
You may spend the die after you have rolled the d20 and before the DM tells you whether it hit, adding the die to the attack roll rather than to the damage.
The target must succeed on a Strength saving throw against your order DC or be knocked prone. A creature more than one size larger than you has advantage on the save.

You can spend one minute talking a willing creature through an order you know. Until your next long rest that creature may call that order once, spending one of your order dice to do it. You cannot teach an order you have already taught to somebody who still has it.

charOptions.higher: At 7th level your order dice become d10s and you learn a fourth order. At 10th you may call one order per short rest without spending a die. At 15th the dice become d12s. At 18th you regain one spent die whenever you roll initiative.
charOptions.alternate: Substitute any fighter archetype built on a pool of manoeuvre dice. Four d8s, refreshed on a short rest, against a DC of 8 + proficiency + Strength is the shape this sheet assumes.

charOptions.name: The Long Sight
charOptions.summary: Every wizard reads the future badly. The Long Sight's discipline is to read it early — to take two numbers out of tomorrow at dawn, before they have gone stale, and then to be stuck with them all day.

features.t: At the end of each long rest, roll two d20s and write both numbers down where the table can see them. These are your omens. When you, or a creature you can see within 60 feet, makes an attack roll, an ability check or a saving throw, you may replace that roll with one of your omens. You must choose before the roll is made.

Omens are a reading, and a reading is taken in order: you must spend the LOWER of your two omens before you may spend the higher. A 3 you cannot get rid of is a 3 you have to find a use for, which is the Long Sight's whole reputation in one sentence.
When you spend your second omen you regain one expended spell slot of 1st level or higher, up to a maximum slot level equal to half your wizard level rounded down.
The gold and the time you must spend to copy a divination spell into your spellbook are halved.

charOptions.higher: At 6th level you roll three omens and still read them lowest first. At 10th, one omen per long rest may be re-rolled at the moment you write it down. At 14th you may spend an omen after the roll it replaces, provided the DM has not yet said whether it succeeded.
charOptions.alternate: Substitute any wizard tradition that grants pre-rolled d20s to replace later rolls; two dice per long rest is what this sheet assumes.

charOptions.name: The Anvil
charOptions.summary: Torrentath keeps four great forges and a hundred small ones, and every one of them has a shrine in the corner with soot on it. The Anvil's clerics hold that a god is best praised by making something that outlasts the maker.
charOptions.domainSpells: 1st — identify, shield of faith · 3rd — heat metal, magic weapon · 5th — elemental weapon, protection from energy · 7th — fabricate, stoneskin · 9th — animate objects, creation

features.t: You gain proficiency with heavy armor and with smith's tools, and you add double your proficiency bonus to any Intelligence (History) check you make to work out who made a metal object, where, and how long ago.

At the end of a long rest you may touch one nonmagical weapon, suit of armor or shield and bless it until you use this feature again. A blessed weapon gains a +1 bonus to attack and damage rolls; blessed armor or a blessed shield gives +1 AC. The blessing also holds one measure of the god's patience: the first time its bearer drops to 0 hit points while carrying it they drop to 1 instead — and the blessing is spent, and the item is plain again.

Starting at 2nd level, you can use your Channel Divinity to work metal. Over 10 minutes at a forge, a fire, or a stone hot enough to spit on, you turn raw metal worth at least half the finished value into one nonmagical object worth no more than 100 gp — a tool, a weapon, a set of shoes for a sled dog. The object carries your maker's mark, plainly and permanently, and there is no way to make it not.

charOptions.higher: At 6th level, a creature that hits you with a melee attack while you are wearing blessed armor takes fire damage equal to your Wisdom modifier. At 8th you gain Divine Strike (1d8 fire, rising to 2d8 at 14th). At 17th your Hammer-Blessing may rest on two items at once.
charOptions.alternate: Substitute any cleric domain built on making and mending — heavy armor, smith's tools, a +1 blessing renewed at each long rest, and a Channel Divinity that creates a mundane object.

charOptions.name: Circle of the Second Skin
charOptions.summary: Some druids wear a beast the way you wear a coat: quickly, and in weather. The Second Skin does not study animals. It borrows them, and it is very careful about giving them back.

features.t: You can use a bonus action rather than an action to assume a beast's shape.
You may take the shape of a beast with a challenge rating as high as 1. Your other limits on beast shapes are unchanged.

While you are in a beast's shape you keep your own Wisdom saving throw bonus, and you can speak one word each round in a language you know. One word is enough for a name, a direction, or RUN. You also always have speak with animals prepared, and it does not count against the number of spells you may prepare.

When you leave a beast's shape you may choose one creature within 30 feet other than yourself; it regains hit points equal to your druid level. You may not choose yourself, and the Circle is very clear that this is the point.

charOptions.higher: At 6th level your beast shapes' natural attacks count as magical, and you may take the shape of a beast of CR 2 or lower. At 10th, CR 3. At 14th, once per long rest, you may take the shape of a beast that died within the last minute and that you touched while it lived.
charOptions.alternate: Substitute any druid circle that grants a bonus-action shapechange and CR 1 beast forms from 2nd level.

charOptions.name: Path of the Pack
charOptions.summary: The mountain's wolves have no strongest. They have a direction, and whoever is nearest the front sets it. A barbarian of the Pack rages the way a pack runs — outward, and with everybody.

features.t: Your walking speed increases by 10 feet.

While you are raging, your allies have advantage on melee attack rolls against any creature within 5 feet of you, and the first ally to hit that creature on a given round adds your rage damage bonus to the hit.
You can cast speak with animals and beast sense as rituals. You do not need to be raging, and you cannot cast them any other way.

charOptions.higher: At 6th level you and every ally within 30 feet ignore difficult terrain made of snow, ice or scree. At 10th, while raging, you may use your reaction to move up to half your speed when an ally within 30 feet drops to 0 hit points. At 14th, a creature you knock prone while raging cannot stand until the start of its next turn.
charOptions.alternate: Substitute any barbarian path that grants a pack-tactics aura while raging and ritual beast-speech; +10 feet of walking speed is folded into this sheet's Speed.

charOptions.name: The Ghosthand
charOptions.summary: A school with exactly one lesson, taught in the back of a Zethel fur-house for the price of whatever you can lift on the way in: the hand you can see is not the one doing the work.

features.t: You know the mage hand cantrip and it does not count against any limit on cantrips known. Your spectral hand is invisible, and you can use it as a bonus action to stow an object in a container another creature is carrying, take one out, pick a lock, or disarm a trap at range — using your Dexterity (Sleight of Hand) check wherever a check is called for.

You learn two cantrips and three 1st-level spells from the short list the school teaches: the cantrips minor illusion, prestidigitation and message; the spells charm person, disguise self, expeditious retreat, find familiar, silent image and sleep. Intelligence is your spellcasting ability. You have two 1st-level spell slots and regain them on a long rest. You learn one further spell from the list at 7th, 13th and 19th level.
When a creature you can see hits you with an attack, you may use your reaction to halve the damage it deals to you. Once per short or long rest.

charOptions.higher: At 9th level, once per short or long rest, you may cast a spell you know with no verbal or somatic component whatsoever — nobody watching sees you do anything at all. At 13th your invisible hand can draw a creature's own weapon out of its scabbard. At 17th, Not Where You Struck reduces the damage to none instead of half.
charOptions.alternate: Substitute any rogue archetype that grants Intelligence spellcasting from 3rd level and an invisible, larcenous mage hand.

charOptions.name: Stonewrought Dwarf
charOptions.summary: The dwarves of the high shelves, who quarry in weather that kills valley clans and consider that the valley clans' problem. The free rules give you your dwarf; this gives you your shelf.

features.t: Your Strength score increases by 2.
You have proficiency with light and medium armor. Over a short rest, with smith's tools, you can repair one battered suit of armor or one shield back to its full effect.
You have advantage on saving throws made to resist exhaustion caused by cold weather, and you can sleep in it without shelter and wake up merely furious.

charOptions.alternate: Substitute any dwarf subrace granting +2 Strength and light and medium armor training. Take the base dwarf traits from the free rules; only the subrace is ours.

charOptions.name: Ridgewood Elf
charOptions.summary: The elves of the tree line, who live in the last hundred feet of forest before the rock starts and regard everything below them as farmland.

features.t: Your Wisdom score increases by 1.
Your walking speed is 35 feet.
You have proficiency with the longsword, shortsword, shortbow and longbow.
You can attempt to hide even when you are only lightly obscured by falling snow, mist, rain or heavy foliage.

charOptions.alternate: Substitute any elf subrace granting +1 Wisdom, a 35-foot speed, martial weapon training and hiding in light obscurement. Take the base elf traits from the free rules; only the subrace is ours.

charOptions.name: Hollowroot Gnome
charOptions.summary: Gnomes who keep their doors in the root-hollows under the pines, on the reasonable grounds that a door nobody can find is a door nobody knocks on.

features.t: Your Dexterity score increases by 1.
You know the minor illusion cantrip. Intelligence is your spellcasting ability for it.

You can speak simply with any beast of Small size or smaller. Once per long rest you may ask one such beast a single question about what it has seen since dawn, and it answers as truthfully, and as badly, as a squirrel can.

charOptions.alternate: Substitute any gnome subrace granting +1 Dexterity, a known illusion cantrip and speech with small beasts. Take the base gnome traits from the free rules; only the subrace is ours.

charOptions.name: Wayborn Human
charOptions.summary: Torrentath is a road with towns hung off it, and some people are born on the road rather than in the towns. A wayborn child is registered in whichever town the wagon reached first, which is why so many of them are owed things.

features.t: Two ability scores of your choice increase by 1. You do not gain the free rules' +1 to every ability score.
You gain proficiency in one skill of your choice.
You gain one charter — this book's word for a feat — of your choice.
You begin play knowing, by name, one person in each town along the Dragonspine road who owed your family a favour. Whether any of them honour it is between you, them, and the DM.

charOptions.alternate: Substitute any human variant granting +1 to two abilities, one skill and one feat at 1st level.

charOptions.name: First to Move
charOptions.summary: The charter of somebody who has been ambushed enough times to have stopped finding it surprising.

features.t: You gain a +5 bonus to initiative.
You cannot be surprised while you can hear.
When you roll initiative you may trade places in the order with one willing ally who rolled lower than you. You each keep your own roll for anything that reads it later.

charOptions.alternate: Substitute any feat granting a large initiative bonus and immunity to surprise.

sideQuests.title: In the Wake of the Whispered Paladin
sideQuests.tags: Side quest - Chapters 2-12 - The goodwill economy
sideQuests.figure: Scrapps, the Whispered Potato Paladin. Plate dented and honest, a sack of seed potatoes over one shoulder, sworn to a small potato god no temple records. He asks no bed but a barn, pays in labor and seed stock, and preaches the glories of potatoes with a sincerity no one can withstand. He caught a falling friend one-handed once, they say. Most folk never learn his name - they know his wake: new potato rows, and farmers still laughing.
sideQuests.hook: Scene 2.2, the farms south of Kitetown: a fresh-turned seed row in the Sewell field, tended like a shrine; a warm welcome for armored strangers; and a name spoken half in jest and wholly in love - the Whispered Potato Paladin.
trail: He is always ahead of the party, always days gone - and always on the same roads the tree's pull draws them down.
Kitetown: a market farmer remembers him charming a week's lodging out of a barn and leaving the yard planted.
Yririe's outskirts: new potato rows in the gentle, steady wake of the whispered paladin.

The Underbelly, Room 22 (5.3): the dark mirror - a scorned devotee's empty lair, one word in a dozen scripts, and a loose-brick cache of revenge notes (DC 25). He hates the champion he cannot catch; the wake teaches what the god's love plants, the lair teaches what curdles without it.
Place a trace wherever the party lingers: a carved tuber sigil on a barn beam, an innkeeper still full from the sermon-dinner, a child's wooden holy symbol shaped suspiciously like a potato.
sideQuests.payoff: Scene 12.2, Tea with Essa: when the fifteen-hour potato dish arrives from a small potato god, any hero who followed the wake understands exactly whose god set this table.
sideQuests.resolution: They never catch him. Three days gone is the closest anyone gets - his work is the meeting.
sideQuests.reward: The goodwill economy: farms along the wake offer shelter, food, and small kindnesses to those who speak well of him. Optionally, Batkin Sewell gifts a blessed seed potato (one use: a creature that eats it as an action gains the benefit of a short rest).

sideQuests.title: The Flower Carnival
sideQuests.tags: Side quest - Chapter 4+ - The honest midway
sideQuests.figure: A small traveling carnival camped outside the Ru Ailmen wall - wagons set as trade stalls, canvas shades on poles, barkers calling the games. Petalla Vance's flowers, Lareth's rings, Hans & Frans in their leotards, Quick Odo's shells. Every game is honest, which is the strangest thing about it.
sideQuests.hook: Doman Bail's third parting gift (scene 3.7): a small carnival sits outside the city wall, for anyone who needs joy. Street Talk of the Twins, roll 4, points the same way. In a locked-down city holding its breath, the midway is the one place still laughing.
trail: Lareth flutters up before anyone speaks - the rings she holds are nearly as big as she is. Let her adopt whichever hero throws worst; she coaches them loudly and without mercy.
Hans announces every hold before he attempts it. Frans never speaks at all. The pot of 22 gp 8 sp sits in plain view on a stool - that is the marketing.
Quick Odo rolls his sleeves to the elbow and narrates his own shuffle. A player who takes three of five gets the face paint and a job offer he does not mean.

Petalla builds the wrapped 1 gp bouquet slowly and asks questions that are none of her business - a quiet channel for any confession a player has been sitting on. For the coin, she learns one true thing.
The lockdown reaches even here: a guard pair drifts the midway's edge, watching the crowd, not the games. Anyone who watches them back notices they are off duty - and losing at the shell game.
Run every game from Run the Table > Carnival Games: push the barker's rules first, take the table's dice or let the console roll, and let each play land on the player screen as it happens.
sideQuests.payoff: The Wand of Smiles - once only, tied into a bouquet for the sharpest count in the Twins. And the carnival is a traveling fixture: it may not be in the same place, or the same city, on a return visit. Wherever the party finds it again, the folk remember who played.
sideQuests.resolution: There is nothing to solve - that is the point. In a chapter of locked doors and polite refusals, the carnival is the one door that opens. Spend it when the table needs joy.
sideQuests.reward: Prizes as won: the glimmerdust (fly your speed, 1 minute), the adorned wooden shortsword, Frans' pot, the face paint (disguise self, 1 hour), bouquets - and the once-only Wand of Smiles.

people.name: Petalla Vance
people.note: Human, she/her, 58 - the carnival's matriarch; wraps every bouquet herself and ties the secret flower round the stems

people.name: Lareth
people.note: Glimmerkin - sits on a cloth-draped wooden box dangling her legs, holding three brass rings almost as big as she is; flutters up to greet you

people.name: Hans & Frans
people.note: Two humans in leotards - Hans the apprentice (+2), Frans the master (+4)

people.name: Quick Odo
people.note: Halfling, he/him, 77 - the fastest hands on the circuit; honest, which is the part nobody believes

people.name: Ilvin Marsh
people.note: Half-elf, he/him, 130 - charcoal to the elbows; catches a likeness in an hour, a soul on commission

people.name: Bibb & Tatta
people.note: Gnome sisters, she/her, 140 and 137 - finish each other's sales pitch

people.name: Old Cormun
people.note: Dwarf, he/him, 190 - carves the "dragon" horn pipes himself and will not say from what

people.name: Marla Two-Spoons
people.note: Human, she/her, 44 - the second spoon is for whoever looks hungriest

people.name: Sugar Wen
people.note: Halfling, she/her, 90 - dusts every apple twice and counts children as regulars

voice.cue: “Hello! I am Lareth and this is the Ring Toss! Three silver for three rings! You have to stand on the rug and ring the post! One point for each ring on the post. Three levels of prizes!”
“Hello, I am Hans and this is Frans and we are here to… pin you. The price is two silver but the prizes differ, for I am Hans the apprentice and he is Frans the master. Which do you choose?”
“Three shells, one pebble, one silver. Eyes open, coin down - I shuffle honest, which is the part nobody believes.”
Builds the 1 gp personalized bouquet slowly, asking questions that are none of her business - and for the coin, she learns one true thing about the buyer.

items.name: Flowers
items.note: Cut fresh from the wagon beds

items.name: Personalized bouquet
items.note: Wrapped, with vase - Petalla builds it while she talks. The stall hosts the Flowers in the Bouquet game

items.name: Black & white portrait
items.note: Up to 3 people, one hour per person; larger or color on commission

items.name: Trinkets!
items.note: Red stocking cap · wizard-tower salt & pepper shakers · green-tinted glass monocle · wind-up clockwork dragonfly (beats its wings, cannot fly) · glossy bell-capped mushroom that jingles · tiny sundial that casts a shadow only in moonlight

items.name: Tibac pipes
items.note: Gnarled root, "dragon" horn, bone

items.name: Candied delights
items.note: Strawberries 2 cp · honeyed strawberries 3 cp · apples 3 cp · caramel apples 5 cp · honeyed apples 4 cp

sideQuests.title: What Rises on a New Day
sideQuests.tags: Side quest - Chapters 5-7 and beyond - DM's discretion
sideQuests.figure: The Sarcophagus of the New Day. Smooth stone behind four locks and a watertight threshold in the Underbelly, crossed by three floor-bolted chains warded with 7th-level Abjuration. Draconic runes cut deep into the lid: RISE, RISE AND COME FORTH TO A NEW DAY. Identification says HEALING - laced, at every layer of the working, with warnings of madness. The record deliberately leaves its function unresolved; this page arms a table that decides to resolve it anyway.
sideQuests.hook: Scene 5.4, the four-locked door: a metal door, watertight at its threshold, four heavy locks in a vertical line, warning glyphs in every language you check. At 5th level the DCs are a message, not a challenge. Let it loom.
trail: 5.4 - the door says no. Locks 1 and 3: DC 26, untrapped. Locks 2 and 4: trapped (DC 27 to disarm), DC 26-27 to unlock. The party's wisest voice reads the glyphs and counsels walking away. They walk away. It follows them.
7.4-7.5 - the obsession pays for help: 18 platinum via the clacks hires a master lockpick, the bridge to the door at last.
7.6 - the four locks open. A room thirty feet square, empty save for its center. The RP moments below carry the unlocking, the seal, the room, and - if a table commits - the lid.
The identification: a tool of profound HEALING, with warnings of madness woven through every layer of the working. The chains say somebody once asked the opposite question.
The move: it was opened by no one... and the entire sarcophagus was relocated into a basement. Of course it was. Where it sits now is wherever your party put it.

boxed.title: The Fourth Lock
boxed.text: The master's hands are quick and quiet - one lock, then two, a long pause at the third, and the trapped fourth surrenders with a sound like a held breath let go. Four locks that outlasted every name in this city, open in an afternoon. The door waits to be pushed.

boxed.title: When the Seal Breaks
boxed.text: The watertight threshold parts with a sigh - air moves here for the first time in an age. It smells of cold stone and still water, of a dark that has never known a torch - and beneath all of it, faint as a memory, something sweet. Not flowers. Not rot. Something that has no business smelling gentle this far down.

boxed.title: The Room
boxed.text: Thirty feet by thirty of nothing at all, arranged around one thing. No dust. No debris. The stillness is not empty - it is kept, the way a shrine is kept. Or a cell. Every step toward the center feels watched by something patient enough to have waited this long.

boxed.title: If the Lid Opens
boxed.text: The lid is smooth as riverstone and warmer than this room has any right to make it. It moves - slow, balanced, quieter than stone should be - and the air that rises from inside is warm, sweet, and terribly clean. Whatever this box was built to do, it is still ready to do it.

blocks.text: DM'S DISCRETION, FORMALLY — the record leaves the sarcophagus unresolved on purpose, and 7.6 keeps that promise to the players. This page exists for the table that commits anyway: the chains, the engine, and the price. Everything below the chains is suggested handling, not canon.

blocks.title: THE CHAINS — HOW THEY COME OFF
lines: THE SANCTIONED DOOR: the ward was set against exactly this - Dispel Magic ends a chain's warding outright from a 7th-level slot or higher; from a lower slot, the ability check is DC 17. One casting per chain. Three chains.

THE GAPS: the warding absorbs force damage and ignores fire, necrotic, cold, lightning, poison, bludgeoning, and slashing - which leaves acid, radiant, and thunder with teeth. A warded chain: AC 19, HP 40 (defaults - tune to taste; the immunity list is canon, the numbers are not).

THE BOLTS: the ward lives in the chains, not the floor. Four mundane floor bolts anchor the assembly - masonry work, prybars, and patience free the sarcophagus still wearing its chains. It was moved once before; the record never says how. This is the honest guess.

blocks.title: THE ENGINE — IF A TABLE COMMITS
lines: A creature sealed within for a full night (the lid closed the whole while) is restored: hit points to maximum, diseases cured, curses ended - and a creature dead no longer than a tenday rises alive.

The box sustains what it holds. A creature sealed inside does not age, starve, or suffocate - a full night, or a hundred years. The chains say somebody once asked the opposite question: it holds as well as it heals.
The runes do not lie. Whatever goes in comes forth to a new day. The question the record refuses to answer is what else comes forth with it.

blocks.title: THE PRICE — WHAT RISES CHANGED
lines: Everyone who rises carries something of whoever was healed in it before: a borrowed mannerism, a taste they never had, a half-memory that is not theirs. Let the player choose one - or choose for them and let it surface at the worst table moment.

THE CRAVING (defaults - the warnings of madness are canon, the numbers are not): the first use is free. Each later use by the same creature within a year forces a Wisdom save, DC 12 + 2 per prior use; on a failure, an indefinite madness flavored as the box's own gravity - euphoria in its presence, grandeur out of it, and the quiet certainty that every wound deserves a new day.
A creature that dies of the craving denied is a story, not a rule. Use sparingly.

blocks.text: A LEDGER WORTH ALLOWING — a party may identify it, fear it, open nothing... and still move the entire sarcophagus into the basement of their own house. Let the wisest voice at the table counsel against every step of that sentence, and let it happen anyway.
What rises on a new day is a question this book hands to your table unanswered - by design. If nobody ever climbs in, the box in the basement is a better story than any rule on this page.

sideQuests.payoff: Whenever a table finally commits - a dying friend, a tenday-old corpse, a desperate night - every warning on this page comes due at once. The healing is real. So is the price.
sideQuests.resolution: Deliberately unresolved. It was never opened; the chains say somebody once asked the opposite question; the answer belongs to whoever asks it next.
sideQuests.reward: The most powerful healing engine on the continent, chained in the party's own basement - and the slow discovery of what it costs.

sideQuests.title: The Treasure of the Twins Channel
sideQuests.tags: Side quest - Chapter 3 onward - open the moment the rumor lands
sideQuests.hook: The rumor runs free on both shores, and retired bridge guards tell it best: something old and rich sleeps at the dead center of the Twins Channel. The PRECISE SPOT - the Sea of Radjure - is guild knowledge; the thieves guild sells it in the Chapter 7 downtime if trust is earned (7.4). The quest is open the moment the table has the rumor and a way to breathe water.
trail: 3.7 onward - the crossing plants the rumor: retired bridge guards tell it best, and it circulates on both shores. Any tavern on either shore can echo it.

7.4, the Chapter 7 downtime - the thieves guild sells the precise spot (the Sea of Radjure, dead center of the channel) IF the party has earned their trust. The rumor is free; the location is the prize.
Water Breathing or its equal gets the party down - past the light, past the cold shelf. No spot, no spell: no dive.

The TIDE decides the fight. Dock urchins and dock workers know the tide table (a coin, or a DC 12 Persuasion / Investigation), and the thieves guild gives it up free once trust is earned - time the dive for Ebb (easy), High or Low (standard), or Flood (hard, best loot). Dive without the read and the tide is rolled blind at the table.

boxed.title: The Dive
boxed.text: The Sea of Radjure, dead center of the Twins Channel, where the rumor has always pointed. Water Breathing settles over the party like a second skin. Down you go - past the light, past the cold shelf, to where a patch of seaweed grows too thick and too deliberate.

blocks.text: The withheld eighth mystery from Chapter 7, paid in full. The seaweed parts on a temple older than the empire: a wide, rune-etched circle glows on the sea floor, crescent-moon stones set around its heart, where a tiered altar bears a purple chest.

blocks.title: Purple Chest Quirks & Secrets
lines: The trigger — anyone breaching the perimeter of the circle toward the chest activates a homing signal for the giant sharks that roam the channel and summons two water elementals.
The chest is magically sealed to the altar (easily dispelled), trapped, and locked. Identify reveals it is a magic item, plus the complexity of the trap and the lock and their 24-hour reset.

blocks.title: The Trap — a puzzle box
blocks.sub: Lift the box off the altar to work it. Everything resets 24 hours after the last attempt.

rows.note: Spot the trap.
Read it as a puzzle box; the box must come off the altar to work it. Allows a help action, or a separate proficient Insight to assist.
Grants advantage on the disarm.
Disarm the box. +2 to the DC on each retry until the 24-hour reset.

blocks.text: Trap springs on: unlocking before the trap is disarmed, or a disarm roll of 14 or lower. Effect — a 20-ft blast: DC 17 Dexterity save for half; 6d6 lightning within 10 ft, half beyond.

rows.note: Thieves' tools. +2 to the DC on each attempt until the 24-hour reset.

battle.name: The Drowned Temple
battle.setup: Any non-sea creature breaching the circle toward the chest springs the trap: the temple's guardians rise in joined force. Three-dimensional combat; remind martial players that water hates them (slashing/bludgeoning at disadvantage without a swim speed or magic).

combatants.name: Giant Shark
combatants.note: Blood Frenzy makes first blood a strategic event.

combatants.name: Water Elemental
combatants.note: Whelm the concentrating caster; the water IS the terrain.

battle.tactics: The elementals herd; the sharks hit whatever bleeds. Vanquish or rout them - routing counts.
battle.adjusting: Difficulty is set by the TIDE (run it on the Drowned Temple dive map below). Ebb tide - easy: 1 Giant Shark, 1 Water Elemental. High or Low tide - standard: 2 and 2. Flood tide - hard: 2 Giant Sharks and 3 Water Elementals, the third rising from the temple floor when the treasure box is touched. Muster the count to match the tide the party dove.
battle.aftermath: The purple chest IS the treasure. Dispel its seal, beat the puzzle-box trap (DC 20 to spot, DC 25 to disarm; 6d6 lightning on a bungle) and the DC 25 lock, and it opens on one hoard - the same three signature pieces every dive: Red Dragon Scale Mail (Medium humanoid), the Aria Stone (an Ioun Stone of Strength - a relic of Aria, Goddess of Sciences and Innovation; tracked in Campaign Items), and a Rod of Absorption. Only the coin scales with the tide the party braved: 400 gp at Ebb, High, or Low; at Flood, 1,000 gp in gems (a 500 gp diamond among them) AND a Portable Hole. The full trap/lock furniture and the 24-hour reset are laid out above, under Purple Chest Quirks & Secrets.

sideQuests.resolution: One dive, one fight, one chest. The party learns the tide table in the Twin Cities - dock urchins and dock workers sell it cheap, the thieves guild gives it up free once trust is earned (7.4) - and times the dive to choose the fight; dive blind and the tide is rolled at the table. If it falls inside Chapter 10's seven days it costs one of them: schedule it BEFORE the Thane's tale, so the tonal drop lands harder - pure joy, then the knife.
sideQuests.reward: One chest, all three magic items every dive: Red Dragon Scale Mail (Medium humanoid), the Aria Stone (Ioun Stone of Strength; a relic of Aria - tracked in Campaign Items), and a Rod of Absorption. Coin by tide: 400 gp at Ebb / High / Low; at Flood, 1,000 gp in gems (a 500 gp diamond among them) plus a Portable Hole.

chest: The Aria Stone - Ioun Stone of Strength

flood.label: Flood tide
flood.coin: 1,000 gp in gems (incl. a 500 gp diamond)

sideQuests.title: What Sloshes in the Iron Flask
sideQuests.tags: Side quest - Chapters 7 to 12 - a plant that pays off in Essa's kitchen
sideQuests.figure: An iron flask, stoppered and standard, turned up among the Underbelly haul beneath the party's own house. Unremarkable by every test — no maker's mark, cool to the touch, never reading as full or as empty. Sealed inside, unknown to whoever carries it, is Relane: a deva and angel of Essa, corked since the great wall of earth was raised across Arret. The flask keeps its occupant hidden until the right question is asked and the stopper is drawn.
sideQuests.hook: Scene 7.5, the Junction Rooms the mansion's elevator opens onto: among coins and oddments, one squat iron flask that sits wrong in the hand. Let a player pocket it as loot. Say nothing. The whole point is that it rides forgotten.
trail: 7.5 — found among the Underbelly treasures and pocketed. It never reads as occupied; Detect Magic and divination give up 'a bound creature within' at best, and the flask offers no more than that. Let it gather dust in a pack.

Chapters 8-11 — it simply travels. Resist every urge to foreshadow; the flask earns its payoff by being ignored. If a player uncorks it early, the standard flask rules apply — Relane emerges willing and grateful, and the reveal below simply happens here instead of in the kitchen. That is allowed; the record merely had it wait.

Chapter 12, Essa's kitchen (12.2-12.3) — the goddess grants each hero one true answer. A bearer who spends theirs on 'what is in my flask?' learns of the deva, draws the stopper, and frees him. This is where the plant blooms.

boxed.title: The Iron Flask
boxed.text: Among the haul the elevator-room opens onto — coins gone soft at the edges, a cracked scrying-lens, buckles with no belts — one thing sits wrong in the hand: a squat iron flask, stoppered tight and heavier than its size has any right to be. No maker's mark. No rust worth the name. The metal stays cool no matter how long you hold it. Give it a shake and almost nothing answers — a slow shift somewhere inside, like deep water minding its own weight. Whatever it keeps, it has kept for a very long time.

sideQuests.payoff: Chapter 12: a hero spends one of Essa's truths on the flask and draws the stopper. Relane rises with a century's gratitude behind him and — bound to Essa as he is — expounds the true properties of the Amulet of Essa (Campaign Items). A forgotten piece of loot becomes the key to the party's own signature relic.
sideQuests.resolution: Opened in Essa's kitchen by the right question. Relane, freed, acts of his own will — grateful, precise, and very well informed about a certain amulet. See the deva's stat block in Appendix A and his entry in the cast.
sideQuests.reward: The deva Relane, freed and thankful; and through him, the full, spoken properties of the Amulet of Essa.

sideQuests.title: The Dragonspine "Dog" Sled Race
sideQuests.tags: Side quest · the far north · any winter · downtime or detour
sideQuests.figure: A crumpled broadsheet, passed hand to hand down every trade road out of the north: ANNUAL WINTER RACE — REGISTRATION NOW OPEN.
sideQuests.hook: Every winter the Zethel Racing Commission runs its five-day sled race over the Dragonspine pass to Cornell — 10,000 gold to the winning team and a mysterious magical bonus prize the rumor mill dresses up as vorpal blades and wish spells. The broadsheets travel farther than the racers do: taverns, bridge posts, and market stalls across the realms carry word of it by midwinter.
trail: The rumor runs free — any tavern keeper, caravan master, or bridge guard can tell it in winter, and a broadsheet handout can land wherever the party drinks.

Getting there is the adventure: overland it is a hard northern road into the Dragonspine range — or a party with a teleport (the Amber Chunk, the Ruby Pyramid) can be at the Zethel bonfire in a heartbeat of downtime.
Registration closes at the deadline horn: four racers and one licensed guide with a sled team. Arriving late means finding the one guide nobody else would sign.

boxed.title: The Broadsheet
boxed.text: THE DRAGONSPINE MOUNTAINS "DOG" SLED RACE — ANNUAL WINTER RACE, REGISTRATION NOW OPEN. Route: Town of Zethel to Cornell via the Dragonspine Mountain Pass, five days. First place: 10,000 gold pieces, plus a mysterious magical bonus prize. All finishers: safe-passage certificate from the Dragonspine Guild. Registration before the deadline horn. — ZETHEL RACING COMMISSION

blocks.text: The race itself — scenes, days, encounters, the town of Zethel, the pregens, and the race rules — lives in its own part of this book: III · The "Dog" Sled Race. This page is the campaign-side door.

blocks.title: RUNNING IT AS A DETOUR — DM
lines: The race is tuned as written for level 3 and weighted toward RP, racing calls, and the mountain itself — a stronger campaign party wins the fights more easily but the positions, the pace, the wolves, and the passengers of the pass (the hag, the dragon, the hollowmourn) play exactly the same.

It costs the campaign five in-world days plus travel — or a downtime window and a teleport. The date advances like any other travel; nothing in the main plot waits on it, so schedule the detour where the table wants the breather.

sideQuests.payoff: A winter of racing stories, 10,000 gold on the line, a bonus prize worth the rumor mill’s breath — and the north opened as a place the party has friends in.
sideQuests.resolution: Run the race from Part III. Win or lose, the Dragonspine Guild’s safe-passage certificate and the friends made on the trail (a guide, a commissioner, a wolf pack) are the party’s to keep.
sideQuests.reward: 1st place: 10,000 gp split per the guide’s contract (the guide takes 20%), plus the bonus prize. All finishers: the Dragonspine Guild safe-passage certificate.

contingencies.title: The Lithgow - The Long Way Down
contingencies.tags: Contingency C1 - Chapters 2-3 - If the party takes the honest route
contingencies.framing: The pull runs downriver either way. The party was not offered a shortcut so much as a fork they could not see - and the honest road keeps its receipts quietly.
contingencies.boxedText: The Lithgow takes her passengers the way a manor takes its guests - a broad-beamed river queen in white and brass, three decks of lacquered rail and lamplight, her paddle-boxes trimmed in the colors of the Brimwater line. Porters take your bags before you think to hold them. Somewhere above, a string quartet is tuning.

blocks.title: THE PRICE THEY PAID
blocks.sub: DM only - never announced
lines: Three days. That is the whole bill, and they pay it without ever seeing it.

No Death Dog fight: the stalker shadows the Brimwater shore at dawn and is left behind, its purpose unspent. The party sails without the suspicion that something is placing monsters in their path - let that arrive later, and let it land harder for the delay.
Do not reveal that the river road existed. The book keeps that receipt folded.

blocks.title: THE CREW OF THE LITHGOW
blocks.sub: well manned - stat references in Appendix A where it matters

rows.name: Odell Farwater
rows.note: thirty years on the Trenlem; runs her deck like a ledger - everything accounted for, nothing forgiven twice

rows.name: Brenna Coppergill
rows.note: Kitetown-born; handles the crew and the cargo manifests

rows.name: Silvo Quenn
rows.note: master of the salon; knows every passenger's name and net worth by the second evening

rows.name: Yliette
rows.note: reads the river at night by the sound of it

rows.name: Deckhands
rows.note: Pold, Ammer, Rusk, Jonna, Teff, and Old Grum the cook (half-orc - feeds the crew first and apologizes to no one); a dozen more hands below, Commoners with good river legs

rows.name: Passengers of note
rows.note: a Drrosh ore magnate, a silk factor from the Twins, and Diana - a Paladin of Teg of the south-eastern border tribes, traveling to the capital, who does not gamble

blocks.title: THE SALON
blocks.sub: gambling for posh folk - buy-ins in gold, the house takes one coin in twenty
lines: Lamplight, lacquer, and money that has never been counted in public. The magnate holds court at the back table; the silk factor loses gracefully and often; Silvo Quenn glides between them remembering everything.
The salon is texture, marks, and cover - for the party, and for passengers less friendly than they appear.

rows.result: the card game of the propertied class, named for the rings of civic office. 5 gp table; 25 gp back table. Each round: opposed Wisdom (Insight) vs. Charisma (Deception). Once per sitting, Intelligence (Investigation) DC 15 reads the table and grants advantage on the next round.
pure chance, 1 gp a spin. Roll a d20: 1-10 lost, 11-17 doubled, 18-19 tripled, 20 the wheel pays five and the salon applauds.
