dice and bluff, the loud table. Deception vs. Insight each round, stakes agreed before the throw.
Sleight of Hand DC 15 against the pit boss's passive Perception 16. Caught once: confined to cabin. Caught twice: put ashore at the next landing, mid-wilderness, fare unrefunded.

blocks.title: NIGHT ONE - THE ATTEMPT
blocks.sub: the heart of the contingency
lines: Dark Star watchers in Kitetown clocked the Champions the moment they walked through guild territory - proclamation-famous faces get reported whether or not any message ever drops. A cell booked passage among the salon crowd.
Past the midnight bell, one of them fumbles in the passenger corridor - a serving tray left outside a cabin door goes skittering across the boards.

blocks.title: THE CELL
blocks.sub: stat references in Appendix A

rows.name: 1 Dark Star Agent
rows.note: the leader - carries the rings

rows.name: 3 Dark Star Cutthroats
rows.note: working the cabins in pairs; they fight quiet and break for the rail when it turns

blocks.title: RUNNING THE ATTEMPT
items: Roll openly for one random PC: they wake to the noise. Any other PC with passive Perception 12+ wakes as well.
The woken PC has the choice the scene is built on: raise the party, or investigate alone into a dark corridor.
Run the cell as sketched - quiet blades, cabin by cabin, the rail their exit. The crew is well manned but slow to wake; the first shout brings deckhands in one round, Brenna Coppergill in three.
AFTERMATH: inside the Agent's boot, DARK STAR IDENTIFICATION RINGS (Appendix C) - the same rings, the same Chapter 4 door. Keep them visible in play.
IF NOBODY WAKES: they strike the most isolated PC first - one round of surprise, then the scream wakes the ship. A fighting chance, never a free kill.

blocks.title: REJOINING THE BOOK
lines: Chapter 3 travels with the party, not the ship. From night two, roll the UNKINDNESS LUCK CHECK each dusk as written (never night one); the scarecrow poles and the Berowl shore lie on the Lithgow's water too.
Diana boarded at Brimwater - run her scenes aboard the salon deck instead of below the Serpent's. The captive's THRON confession rides with the Unkindness boarding, exactly as written.
Arrival at the Twins: three days behind the Serpent's schedule. Carry it on the calendar and say nothing.

blocks.text: They chose the honest road. Honor the choice: a gentler voyage, one hard night, and a bill they never see itemized.

contingencies.title: The Guild Burns - The Channel Without the Moonlight Strategy
contingencies.tags: Contingency C2 - Chapter 4 - If the party makes an enemy of the guild
contingencies.framing: The pull does not care who the party offended - Yuvl Ilmern waits across the water either way. The book's paved road runs through the guild's sewers; when that road burns, the channel is still crossable, but every alternative charges more and tells someone.
contingencies.boxedText: The channel has never looked wider. Gulls ride the wind between the Twins like it costs nothing, and the middle bridge stands guarded at both ends. Somewhere under all that water, they say, the dwarves built a road. Nobody who would show it to you is speaking to you.

blocks.title: THE PRICE THEY PAID
blocks.sub: DM only - never announced
lines: Burning the guild costs the paved road, not the destination. All three routes below land the party where the guild's bargain would have: the Underbelly, wet dark, and Chapter 5 within reach. The chapter's shape survives; the party's reputation in the Twins does not.
Do not soften the freeze-out. The Rare Coin still pours their ale and stops talking; tattooed thumbs close against forefingers wherever they walk. The city should feel like a held breath.

blocks.title: ROUTE ONE - THE THAW
blocks.sub: restitution · the guild re-opens for a price
items: The guild's price is a service, not gold. Pick one: recover something Dark Star took from the club, or embarrass the immigration station on the Yuvl side badly enough to be deniable - and the Dark Star rings are surrendered for keeps either way.
Approach through any tattooed thumb; a Footpad carries terms back within a day. The guild was always going to answer - curiosity is its oldest vice.
On completion the original bargain resumes - the NAME, the TIME, the PASS PHRASE - at half again Ruglal's original price.

blocks.title: ROUTE TWO - THE HARBOR CHAIN
blocks.sub: smuggler's water · coin and nerve
items: DC 16 Investigation along the north docks turns up a harbor pilot who runs the chain gap at slack tide - 100 gp a head, half up front, no questions asked and none answered.
The crossing is a group DC 13 Stealth. Failure means a Twins Channel Station patrol lamp and very official questions - the immigration station's page in The World has the faces they'll meet.
The pilot lands them at a Yuvl-side sea cave that meets the Underbelly's outfall: a wet, unfriendly back door into the same tunnels the guild would have sold them politely.

blocks.title: ROUTE THREE - THE DWARVES' OWN DOOR
blocks.sub: the legal road · slow, and it writes their names down

rows.result: The sanitation system was commissioned by the Twins and dwarf-carved - and the city keeps a maintenance registry. Any dwarf PC knows this without a roll.
Honest words or honest coin gets the party keyed through a sanitation work-gate into the Underbelly - legal, slow, and their names go in a ledger the Council of Twelve can read.

blocks.text: Whichever route, land them where the guild's ladder would have: the Underbelly, and Chapter 5 within reach. The pull is patient. The guild's memory is longer - the Moonlight Strategy resurfaces in later chapters as weather: cold if burned, warm if mended.

contingencies.title: The Ride Taken - Through the Circle with the Heart
contingencies.tags: Contingency C3 - Chapter 6 - If a champion rides the escape circle
contingencies.framing: The book invites this: anyone standing in the circle when it fires goes along, and the tactics line says let them. Here is the generosity that line promised. The circle fires to its blank DEFAULT destination - the walled glade of Chapter 8 - so the rider lands somewhere the campaign already knows intimately, with three honest roads out.
contingencies.boxedText: The world squeezes and releases. Underfoot: the circle, still warm. Around you: a thirty-foot glade walled in stone, thirty feet high, cloudy sky far above - and a pull you know, faint and small. A cutting of Oospufmorn, three feet tall, an exact replica of its mother, roots spread in a shallow stone pot. The mage does not look back; he is already at an iron-bound double door, the heart's glow leaking between his fingers. The demon looks back. It has all the time in the world, and it spends a long moment of it on you.

blocks.title: THE ROOM WHERE THEY LAND
blocks.sub: the glade of scene 8.4, met two chapters early
lines: Everything 8.4 says is already true: the walled glade, the flight barrier at wall height, the cutting too small for a heart of its own but still connected to its mother, the iron-bound double door held by Arcane Lock (AC 25, 100 HP; Knock or Dispel Magic opens it), and - under the rider's feet - a RETURNING circle: same activation, one rune of difference pointing home (DC 15 Arcana).
The enemies do not linger. The mage speaks a word to the door and is through with the heart; the glabrezu goes last, walking backward, watching. The door closes on its lock behind them.
Push the boxed text to the player screen for the rider alone if your setup allows - the rest of the table should hear silence.

blocks.title: THE DEMON'S CALCULUS
blocks.sub: DM only - why the rider is not simply killed
lines: The glabrezu is a professional with a shopping list, and the heart's delivery outranks a corpse. Killing a Champion of the Empire without orders is a DECISION, and demons in Essax's hierarchy do not make unpaid decisions.
So it offers one long, cold look - pricing the rider for later - and leaves. If the rider forces the fight anyway: power word stun, and Track Three begins.
This is also the tracking engine at work: within a day, Essax knows a champion rode the circle. What they do with that knowledge is Track Three's fuel.

blocks.title: TRACK ONE - THE WAY HOME
blocks.sub: the mercy built into the floor
items: A rider who keeps their head is standing on the way back: DC 15 Arcana identifies the returning circle - same activation, one rune pointing home. Grant advantage if they watched the mage work the platform circle at any point.

Home within the hour, carrying treasure no roll could buy: the glade exists, a cutting of the sacred tree grows in it, and an iron-bound door leads somewhere the enemy walks freely. Chapter 8's discovery is now banked foreshadowing instead of a cold open.
Cost honesty: the heart is still gone, and the rider watched it leave twice. Let that land.

blocks.title: TRACK TWO - GONE TO GROUND
blocks.sub: through the door on the enemy's heels
items: If the rider slips through the door before it locks: hedges (scene 8.5). The maze punishes pursuit exactly as it punishes intrusion - wrong turns teleport to the maze's start, which for a hiding rider is survivable geometry: the enemy cannot easily corner what the maze keeps relocating.

The rider lives on the glade's edge - water from the cutting's pot, stolen quiet, days measured in patrol rhythms through the archway. Play it in short cuts between the main party's scenes; never let the separated player sit dark for a full hour.

Reunion is Chapter 8: when the party learns the circle (Chapter 7) and takes the blank default, run 8.4 with the rider already inside - a guide who knows the geography and none of its meaning. The Speak with Dead reveal (this scene's answer bank) can pull that timeline in hard; let it.

blocks.title: TRACK THREE - TAKEN
blocks.sub: the enemy encampment - a rescue the campaign can carry
items: If the rider fights, fails a hide, or simply gets unlucky: stunned, bound, and carried through the maze to the enshrouded archway - and through it, to a border staging camp in the eastern shadow of the World Spine, Bronze Storm side. The same camp rhythm Thron's rituals feed: cultist guards, a fanatic warden who quotes the Master, supply arrivals on a cadence a patient prisoner can learn.

The rider is leverage, not a corpse: Essax trades in fear, and a living Champion proves the Empire's chosen can be taken. Interrogation is questions about the bond, the Empress, and the other trees - and the rider knows the campaign's real secret defense: they genuinely know almost nothing yet.

The rescue trail is already in the party's hands: Speak with Dead names the garden; Chapter 7 teaches the circle; Chapter 8 opens the door and the Threshold Blight fight teaches that archways can be OPENED - and closed. Run the rescue as Chapter 8's second half or as its own session between 8 and 9.

Alternative pressure valve: the Empire's channels. The Empress's reach (or the dwarves' vigilance) can surface proof of life and a location - useful if the table stalls, at the cost of the party owing the favor.
Session-zero check before running this track: kidnapping and forced capture is on the Tone & Safety advisory, and a possible PC exit doubly so. Confirm the dials; the veil can drop in one sentence.

blocks.title: WHAT THE CAMPAIGN BANKS - EVERY TRACK
blocks.sub: the ride always pays
lines: The circle has a DEFAULT destination, and the enemy uses it: the single most important fact about the platform circle, learned chapters early.
A living cutting of Oospufmorn exists behind walls no map holds - the party will feel the weight of that in Chapter 8 either way.
The endgame vocabulary arrives early: circles have destinations, archways carry portals, and both can be learned. Nothing in Chapters 7-8 breaks; it arrives pre-loaded.

blocks.text: Whichever track: do not punish the choice. The tactics line called it a magnificent, terrible choice, and the book means both words - the ride should cost something real and pay something real, in that order.

THE DREAM SEED: a rider the demon prices and touches here is the natural dreamer for the recurring nightmare - seed scene 7.7 (The Recurring Dream) on that champion, and pay it off at 9.1. Session-Zero anchor: 'Mind-reading & altered memories' and 'Kidnapping & forced capture' (Tone & Safety).

contingencies.title: The Handle Flies - Grief at the Bottom of the Stair
contingencies.tags: Contingency C4 - Chapter 7 - If the party detonates at the Captain
contingencies.framing: Scene 7.1 hands a grieving party to a gruff stranger with hard questions - an invitation to detonate, and some tables will accept it. The beat may fire on the platform, where Maros stands alone, or at the grass, with the cordon at his back - the contingency holds in both. This is the emotional beat working, not breaking. The Empire cannot afford to fight its Champions, Maros has seen grief before, and every road below reconverges at the Council of Twelve: the beat survives anything the table throws at it.
contingencies.boxedText: The Captain does not reach for his blade. One hand comes up - flat, unhurried - and at his signal the cordon shifts, at his back or far below at the rail's edge of sight: shields forward, spears grounded, not one edge pointed your way. "That's fair," he says, in the voice of a man who has buried friends and filed the paperwork after. "Say it all. I'll wait. And then you're coming with me - because the Empress is waiting too, and she'll want it said to her face."

blocks.title: THE BEAT UNDERNEATH
blocks.sub: DM only - it is grief, not defiance
lines: The party fought magnificently and lost anyway. Anger at Maros is anger at the wilting with nowhere else to go - read every outburst through that lens before pricing it.
Pace it, do not punish it. Let players say the ugly thing; the NPC absorbs it. The scene's job is to move the grief through the room, not to win an argument with it.
Watch the table, not just the characters: if a PLAYER is the one running hot, that is a pause, not a track.

blocks.title: THE CAPTAIN'S CALCULUS
blocks.sub: DM only - why Maros will not escalate
lines: He was a sellsword across the ocean; he has watched grief wear armor before and knows it burns out faster when nothing pushes back.

The Empress has called the army to mobilize for the eastern border. A dead or jailed Champion is a strategic catastrophe, and Maros refuses to author one over hard words at the foot of a dying god-tree.
The crowd is watching. The Council Guard is barely holding a city in pandemonium; a captain brawling with the heroes on the grass is a story he will not let the Twins tell.

On the platform he is alone and knows it - he counted that cost on the climb. The party could throw him off the tree; he is betting his rank and his read of grief that they will not, and the bet itself is the message.

blocks.title: TRACK ONE - GRIEF SPOKEN
blocks.sub: the outburst is words
items: Maros takes it standing. He answers what is asked with hard honesty, corrects nothing that is merely unfair, and waits out the rest - push the boxed text when the storm crests.
The escort proceeds. "Worse seating" becomes literal here: an honored escort walks the party in; a hostile one waits on benches in the antechamber while the Council is assembled.
Reconverge at 7.2 unchanged. Grief spent on the grass is grief that does not detonate in the Council chamber - that is this track paying for itself.

blocks.title: TRACK TWO - STEEL DRAWN
blocks.sub: shields, not swords
items: Push the boxed text the moment a weapon clears. The guard answers with shields, grapples, and numbers - Maros orders no killing blows against Champions, full stop.

If the party presses to real bloodshed, the cordon WIDENS instead of closing: Maros falls back and lets them stand alone in a ring of grounded spears with a city watching. He will not spend guards' lives to subdue people the Empress needs whole.

Reconverge at 7.2 under a cloud: the party arrives escorted-in-fact-if-not-in-name, the hushed conversation stops when they enter, and the Empress intervenes on their behalf - because she needs them, and everyone in the room knows it.
Charge a fair price and no more: injured guards are remembered in the Twins, and Maros's later courtesies (he is their escort again to the estate) cool by exactly that much.

blocks.title: TRACK THREE - FLIGHT
blocks.sub: let them go
items: No chase. A city in pandemonium hides no one for long, and Champions carry a pull that cannot be outrun - let the escape succeed completely and feel briefly like relief.
The summons finds them within a day: a sending in the Empress's voice, guards at every gate already on manhunt footing, or the bond's own quiet weight - DM's choice by tone.

Reconverge at 7.2 with the room already knowing they ran. Nothing is withheld - the audience, the answers, even the estate still come - because the Empire's answer to flight is generosity with a ledger, and the party should feel the ledger.

blocks.title: WHAT EVERY TRACK BANKS
blocks.sub: the beat always pays
lines: The party learns the Empire will not fight them - true information about their own leash, and the chapter's quiet thesis stated in action.
Maros becomes a known quantity before 7.3 hands him back to them as the estate escort: whatever happened on the grass walks into that scene with him.
The grief gets spent somewhere survivable. Chapters 7's downtime works better in a party that has already said the ugly thing out loud.

blocks.text: This contingency exists so the emotional beat can run hot safely. Do not punish grief; charge fair prices only for steel - and if the heat is at the table rather than in it, that is a Tone & Safety pause, not a track.

contingencies.title: The Storyteller - The Long Play
contingencies.tags: Contingency C5 - Chapters 10-12 - If the court's storyteller attaches himself to the party
contingencies.framing: Alias is canon as a voice and optional as a companion. The court of Bhindarul found him reputable; the Commune found him UNCERTAIN; the book refuses to break the tie. This contingency exists for the table that takes him along - and for the DM who wants the long game his missing decade is hiding.
contingencies.boxedText: He does not ask your leader. He asks the fire, the night before you leave. 'Every road I ever collected ran the wrong way - toward home, away from the story. Yours runs INTO it.' He turns the lute case so you can see it is already packed. 'Take me along and I will carry the parts too heavy to sing. Leave me, and I will wave you off from the door like an honest man - and you will never know which of us that made me.'

blocks.title: THE CANON POSITION
blocks.sub: DM only - what is true even if he never leaves the Keep
lines: The court's vetting is real. Bhindarul does not let anyone in - Alias got IN, which means the realm's own scrutiny looked at him and found his word good. Say that plainly if the party asks; it is the realm's answer and the realm believes it.

His information is pivotal and it is GOOD: his contacts carry letters where no realm road runs (10.2), and his rumor of CAL NAI - the Red Knife, the resistance inside the Bronze Storm empire - checks out (10.4).
The Commune's UNCERTAIN (10.2) is not a plot hole; it is the point. The god is not being coy - the man is genuinely unresolved, and what he does in Chapter 12 may be undecided even in HIM.
If the party leaves him behind, he stays the court's voice: letters, rumors, a face at the Low Keep hearth every time they return. The campaign loses nothing - this contingency simply stays folded.

blocks.title: THE LONG PLAY
blocks.sub: if the table takes him
lines: THE ASK: the night before the party leaves for the gate, he asks - push the boxed text. He asks the whole fire, not the leader; a storyteller knows where decisions actually live.
ON THE ROAD: make him earn the seat daily - tongues nobody else speaks, roads nobody else knows, a song at the cold camps exactly when the table needs one. The better he is, the harder 11.6 lands.

THE DECADE: he is genuinely evasive about exactly ten years of his life. Never explain them. If pressed, he deflects with a true story about a different decade - charming, complete, and not an answer.
THE QUIET EXIT (11.6): at the green door he simply is not in the line that steps through. No note, no speech. If a player counts heads, let them notice; do not flag it otherwise.
THE REUNION (Chapter 12): heartwarming or damning - decide only when your table forces you to, and not one scene sooner. Both endings must stay possible until the moment one of them is true.

blocks.title: PLAYING THE UNCERTAIN
blocks.sub: how to keep the tie unbroken, honestly
lines: Never cheat the mechanics: Insight reads him sincere, because he IS sincere. Detection magic finds no fiend, no charm, no lie - the ambiguity is biographical, not magical.

Give both camps ammunition on schedule: for every kindness that looks like proof, one detail that does not add up - a border checkpoint he knew too well; a Bronze Storm marching song he stopped humming mid-bar.
If a player asks him point-blank whose side he is on: 'The story's. It is the only side that has ever taken me.' - and he means it, whatever else is true.
The DM's private compass: do not decide what the missing decade holds until Chapter 12 demands it. An undecided secret cannot be leaked by accident.

blocks.text: THE DOOR AFTER: whichever way the reunion breaks, Alias is a road into the Bronze Storm empire - beside Nika Blackthorn's standing invitation (12.5), he is the second thread the next campaign can pull.

campaignItems.name: Amulet of Essa
campaignItems.attunement: Requires attunement by a ritual of receiving with a fairy courier of Essa
campaignItems.description: A god-gift — conjured and given in a waking dream as a direct present from Essa, Goddess of All That Grows. Bestowed only on clerics a fairy courier of Essa deems worthy. A clear crystal cut in the shape of the Empire's Sacred Tree, on a thin chain; it is found around the neck after the ritual, and always sizes itself to sit comfortably in a closed palm and hang at the heart.
properties: While you wear it, you are hidden from divination magic — you can't be targeted by such magic or perceived through magical scrying sensors.

When all your other spell slots are spent, the amulet grants one more slot, channeled through it, at up to your highest current slot level. You know this the instant your last slot is gone: the amulet pulses with white light like a heartbeat.
After you cast a spell through the amulet, its glow dims but does not fade for one hour, granting +2 AC for that hour.
Once per day, when you are reduced to 0 hit points, you are instead healed 10 hit points. You know this the instant you drop: the amulet flares with a blinding white shine, pulsing like a heartbeat.

campaignItems.name: Amber Chunk of Teleport
campaignItems.description: A rough, unrefined chunk of amber about four inches across, a single eye held at its center — an eye that once belonged to a goat.
properties: You can use the chunk to cast the teleport spell, requiring no components.
Once used, the amber clouds over and the eye is obscured; it cannot be used again until three days pass, when the amber clears.

campaignItems.name: Pendant of Teg
campaignItems.attunement: Requires attunement during the receiving ritual
campaignItems.description: A god-gift — conjured and given in a waking dream as a direct present from Teg, exactly as the Amulet of Essa is given by Essa. Bestowed only on those a fairy courier of Teg deems worthy. (A distinct item from the Pendant of Torrentath.)
properties: When all your other spell slots are spent, the pendant grants one more slot, channeled through it, at up to your highest current slot level. You know this the instant your last slot is gone: the pendant pulses with light like a heartbeat.
After you cast a spell through the pendant, its glow dims but does not fade for one hour, granting +2 AC for that hour.

campaignItems.name: Ruby Pyramid of Teleportation
campaignItems.attunement: Requires attunement by 3 hours of meditation, which may be split across up to three sessions within 24 hours
campaignItems.description: A cut ruby carved as a pyramid six inches tall, three goat eyes stacked one above another at its apex. It is resistant to ranged attacks, holds a pool of charges, and recharges at dusk each day. At Aedlab, Nika had only a single charge available — which is why her escape there looked like a one-and-done. (This is the tracked item behind the "Teleportation Pyramid" noted in Appendix C.)
properties: 1 charge — teleport: a ritual circle up to 15 feet in radius forms wherever the attuned wills; everything inside is teleported (resolve the destination as the teleport spell).
3 charges — temporal rend in spacetime: a rift opens for up to 1 minute at the location and angle the attuned directs, from 1 foot up to 10 feet across. Resolve its far end as the teleport spell.

campaignItems.name: The Iron Flask
campaignItems.description: An iron flask, stoppered and unremarkable to the eye — and, unknown to whoever carries it, it is not empty. Bound inside is Relane, a deva and angel of Essa, sealed away since the great wall of earth was raised across Arret. The occupant stays hidden until the right question is asked and the flask is opened. Freed, Relane can expound the true properties of the Amulet of Essa.
properties: On command, the flask can draw in a targeted aberration, celestial, elemental, fey, or fiend within 60 feet (a DC 17 Wisdom save resists), or release the creature already sealed within.
A creature released from the flask serves the one who freed it for 1 hour — or acts of its own will if it was already willing (as Relane, grateful, is).

campaignItems.name: The Aria Stone
campaignItems.description: A pale blue rhomboid, small and cool and faintly humming, recovered from the drowned temple at the dead center of the Twins Channel. It is a relic of Aria, Goddess of Sciences and Innovation - one of her Ioun stones. Like all Ioun stones, once attuned it orbits within a few feet of its bearer's head of its own accord, moving to stay near them; struck for, it can be caught (roughly AC 24, 10 HP) and returns to orbit when recovered.
properties: Your Strength score increases by 2, to a maximum of 20, while this stone orbits your head.

To attune, hold it near your head for the first hour; thereafter it orbits on its own and travels with you. If several Ioun stones ever surface, a fair table rule is that only one benefits a creature at a time.

sledRace.title: The "Dog" Sled Race
sledRace.tagline: An annual winter race — Zethel to Cornell, five days over the Dragonspine pass.
sledRace.canon: The race is an annual winter event of the northern Dragonspine. Any year, in the dead of winter, the Zethel Racing Commission opens registration: four adventurers, one licensed guide with a sled team, five days through the mountain pass to Cornell. A campaign party can reach it by traveling north to the Dragonspine range instead of following the plot, or in downtime by teleport — the Amber Chunk or the Ruby Pyramid both know the way. It can equally be run alone as a self-contained adventure for a fresh table, tuned as written for four level-3 racers; the fight is with the mountain and the clock more than the monsters, so a stronger party changes the flavor, not the frame.
sledRace.overview:
This 4-hour one-shot is a race + roleplay hybrid. The combat is largely encounter-based (random on the trail), not dungeon-crawl. The dramatic tension comes from:
1. Time pressure (registration deadline)
2. Negotiation with Corben
3. Daily race decisions (speed vs. safety)
4. Encounter outcomes affecting position PACING GUIDE (4 Hours):
• 0:00–0:30 — Arrival in Zethel, wagons, bonfire scene, Bethalyn
• 0:30–1:00 — Finding Corben, negotiation, meeting the wolves
• 1:00–1:15 — Day 1 setup, race mechanics briefing
• 1:15–2:00 — Days 1 & 2 (narrated fast with dice rolls)
• 2:00–2:30 — Day 3 (Fey forest, long rest, major RP moment with Glimmerkin)
• 2:30–3:15 — Day 4 (Hag negotiation, Frost Giant toll — big setpiece)
• 3:15–3:50 — Day 5 (Silver Dragon test, Hollowmourn finale)
• 3:50–4:00 — Finish line at Cornell, results, reward KEY DM TIPS:
• Use the LUCK CHECK as a dramatic dice roll — describe what happens on fail/success cinematically
• Corben should feel like a beloved character — brash but reliable
• The Paladin from scene 1 can reappear as a rival racer throughout
• If combat goes long, skip to outcome — this isn't a combat one-shot
• The Silver Dragon on Day 5 should feel like a BOSS moment even if no combat occurs
sledRace.running:
4-HOUR TIMING CHEAT SHEET SCENE 1 — ARRIVAL (30 min)
□ Wagon arrival, describe Zethel + bonfire
□ Allow PC introductions in wagon
□ Bethalyn scene — registration tent
□ Reveal: need a 4th member + one guide left
□ [Optional] Shopping at Zethel if party asks SCENE 2 — FIND CORBEN (30 min)
□ Navigate to SE tents — hear growling
□ Paladin argument in progress
□ Corben's pitch + wolf introduction
□ Animal Handling rolls (DC 15, advantage with ranger/druid/etc.)
□ Negotiation — Corben's terms (20% cut)
□ Agreement → registration → camp prep SCENE 3 — THE RACE (2.5 hours for all 5 days)
Each day roughly: 25-30 min
□ Speed declaration (slow/regular/fast)
□ Switchback encounter — narrate and roll
□ Rank update — tell players where they stand
□ Camp scene — brief RP moment each night Day 3 (Fey Forest) — EXPAND to 35-40 min
The Glimmerkin encounter should be a roleplay highlight — she's curious about the wolves and can grant a small boon (advantage on one Day 5 check) if the party plays along. Day 4 (Hag) — EXPAND to 35-40 min
The hag wants something strange: a secret, a memory, a name. Classic deal-with-the-devil moment. SCENE 4 — FINALE (10 min)
□ Cornell finish line
□ Announce final positions
□ Prize distribution (10,000gp split + bonus item)
□ Corben and the wolves epilogue
sledRace.levels: Tuned as written for four racers of level 3 (RP-weighted — see the canon note for stronger parties).

scenes.title: Scene 1 — The Road to Zethel
scenes.flavor: Zethel at nightfall: a huddle of snow-roofed roofs, one enormous bonfire throwing amber light across the drifts, and thirty teams' worth of adventurers waiting for a five-day race up the Dragonspine.

blocks.title: RUNNING THE SCENE — DM
lines: Party arrives by wagon. The town is visibly tired of adventurers. Locals move quickly, eyes down. If the party tries to chat up a local: short answers and pointed directions toward the registration tent.

blocks.text: Rumors about the prize: 'Ten thousand gold and something else — nobody agrees what. Last year it was wish spells. Year before that a vorpal blade. I heard this year it's a relic from the mountain itself.' Let players speculate. The uncertainty is part of the hook.

boxed.title: The Road to Zethel
boxed.text: The covered wagon rocks and creaks beneath you as it pushes through the last stretch of snow-packed road. The pines on either side have grown thick and heavy with frost, their branches sagging white in the dead of winter silence. Through the gap in the canvas behind the driver's bench, you can just make out the faint orange glow of something burning ahead — warm and enormous against the pale grey sky. Wenn, the wagon driver, calls back through the cover: 'Looks like we are about 30 minutes out. We'll be there soon.'

boxed.title: As The Wagon Approaches Zethel
boxed.text: The town of Zethel rises out of the treeline ahead of you — a cluster of snow-roofed buildings crammed together against the cold. But what catches your eye first isn't the buildings. It's the bonfire. It stands in the center of town, enormous and roaring, throwing amber light across the snow in every direction. Around it, dozens of people move — adventurers, from the look of them, laden with gear, talking too loud, moving with the restless energy of people who have been waiting too long. Next to the fire, a large painted sign — the kind meant to be seen from a distance. And beside that, a canvas tent with a door flap. The sign reads, simply: REGISTRATION. Wenn slows the wagon: 'End of the line, friends. Most go directly to REGISTRATION to get the checklist of what's required for your party to register. Good luck in there — you'll need it.'

script.text: Party arrives by wagon. The town is visibly tired of adventurers.

Allow time for introductions — ask each player what their character does during the last stretch. What drew them to Zethel? Let the rumors about the prize come out naturally: vorpal blades, wish spells, wands of untold power. Nobody agrees on what the bonus prize is, and that's the point.
Continue when the table is ready.

scenes.development: Zethel at nightfall: a huddle of snow-roofed roofs, one enormous bonfire throwing amber light across the drifts, and thirty teams' worth of adventurers waiting for a five-day race up the Dragonspine.

scenes.title: Scene 2 — Registration / Bethalyn
scenes.flavor: The registration tent — ink, candle wax, and Bethalyn behind the desk, who has run this race eleven years and can see your next question coming before you do.

blocks.title: RUNNING THE SCENE — DM
lines:
Bethalyn runs registration with terrifying efficiency. Check your party size in the RDT setup tab before this scene — she will ask for it directly. Key beats:
1. She asks for party size (4-6 required) and sled name — both go on the official record
2. Sled name moment: if they don't have one, she says their guide filed a provisional. They can keep it or change it now. Once filed it's locked. This is the moment to set the name in the RDT.
3. She mentions the gentleman who just left (Vane) — he was trying to register his servants as party members. She declined.
4. She sends them south-east past the sled kennels to find their guide. Allow all questions. She knows the race rules better than anyone alive. Vane walks out as the party walks in — first impression before he has a name. Bethalyn's visible relief at seeing real adventurers tells you everything about how that conversation went.

blocks.text: Vane walks past as the party approaches — full plate, two servants, the expression of a man who has been told no and has decided not to accept it. Bethalyn does not mention him by name unless asked. If asked: a long pause, then: He was attempting to register his household staff as racing partners. That is all she will say.

boxed.title: Registration / Bethalyn
boxed.text: Just as you approach the registration tent, the canvas flap opens from the inside. A man steps out. He is tall, expensively dressed for the cold — travelling gear that costs more than most teams' sleds, fur-lined and immaculate despite the snow. He moves with the particular posture of someone who has never seriously considered the possibility that a room might not be arranged for his benefit. Two servants trail behind him, both of them carrying equipment that belongs to someone who intends to win. He looks at your group with the brief, assessing glance of a man who files people quickly under categories. Whatever category he places you in, it is not a flattering one. He says nothing. His expression does it for him. He passes you without acknowledgment and continues down the street.

boxed.title: Registration / Bethalyn — continued
boxed.text: You push through the canvas flap and step into warmth. A small brazier glows in the corner. The tent is sparse — a folding table, stacks of parchment, a camp stool behind the desk — but it smells of ink and candle wax, which feels almost civilized after the cold outside. The woman behind the desk is bent over a form, her head shaking slowly back and forth in what looks very much like frustration. She looks up — gives a small start — and immediately straightens into a warm, professional smile. Oh! Hello — my apologies, I did not see you come in while our last racer was on his way out. I am Bethalyn. I am here to register racers for the Dragonspine Mountains Dog Sled Race. Are you here to register? I assume so — you do not look like locals. She sets a form on the table and uncaps her pen without waiting for an answer. I will need a few things from you. First — your party size. We require between four and six adventuring members per registered sled, not including your guide. Second — your sled name. This goes on the official record, the betting boards, and the Cornell Scrying Pool feed. Choose carefully. You will be hearing it announced for the next five days. That is fine. Your guide will have filed a provisional name to hold the slot. You may keep it or change it now. Once I file this form it is locked until Cornell. Ah. Now that is where things get interesting. You are arriving very late. Most guides secured their parties on the first day. However — you are fortunate. There is one guide remaining with a full sled team. You will know it when you get there. Listen for the growling. Excellent. South-east of the market stalls — last tent on the left past the sled kennels. You will know it when you get there.

script.text: Bethalyn runs registration with terrifying efficiency. Check your party size in the RDT setup tab before this scene — she will ask for it directly.
If players ask who that was — nobody in earshot seems keen to answer. A nearby competitor just shakes their head slightly. This is Lord Aldric Vane. The party will come to know that expression well.
IF THEY HAVE NO NAME YET IF ASKED ABOUT GUIDE AS THEY TURN TO LEAVE

scenes.development: The registration tent — ink, candle wax, and Bethalyn behind the desk, who has run this race eleven years and can see your next question coming before you do.

scenes.title: Scene 3 — Finding Corben / The Argument
scenes.flavor: Past the market stalls and the empty kennels, an argument and a low chorus of growling — several animals, not one — coming from the last tent with a team still to spare.

blocks.title: RUNNING THE SCENE — DM
lines: The party follows Bethalyn's directions south-east, past the market stalls and sled kennels, toward growling and raised voices. They walk in on Corben patiently refusing Vane — who is trying to register his servants as racers. Corben notices the party mid-argument and uses them as his exit line: three walking up who could fill the open spots. Vane's exit is the scene's punctuation — he needs to leave with something. He will not mention this conversation again. Key beats: (1) Corben introduces himself, genuinely pleased — not desperate. (2) If asked why he's the last guide: the wolves. He's the reason they added the quotes to 'Dog' Sled Race. Zero apology. (3) The fourth-member problem — he's already counted three; rules are rules. He won't pick the party's fourth for them, but Vane is still around and desperate. Sled name: if the party still has no name and asks Corben, he thinks for exactly one second and says 'The Wolves.' Not Dire Wolf Pack. Not Fang and Thunder. Just The Wolves. Because that is what they are. He does not explain further — he is already checking the harnesses.

blocks.text: If asked why he's the last available guide: 'You've seen the sign — ‘Dog’ Sled Race, with the quotes? I'm the reason they had to add the quotes. My team is all dire wolves. Every single one. They've brought me to the finish line every year I've entered.' Said with complete sincerity and zero apology. Fourth member: 'I noticed. You'll need a fourth — rules are rules, and I won't be disqualified on a technicality after seven years.' He won't choose for them, but whatever fool they bring needs to pull their weight: 'I'm not a rescue service.'

blocks.title: VOICE & KEY LINES
lines: "I be Corben Vash. The best of the best of guides — if my track record does show."
"Fenra's ears are forward. That do be meaning what you think it do be meaning."
"Not bad. For your first time."
"Stay exactly where we stop. The wolves know the way. But they will not run it without me."

boxed.title: Finding Corben / The Argument
boxed.text: You follow Bethalyn's directions south-east through town, past the edge of the market stalls and a line of sled kennels. Most of the kennels are empty now — the guides have their teams sorted and ready. But from the last cluster of tents, you can hear raised voices. And beneath the raised voices — low, resonant, and deeply unsettling — you can hear growling. Not one animal. Several. As you get closer, the argument resolves into two parties. The first is a tall man in traveling clothes — well-worn, practical, with the easy posture of someone completely unbothered by the cold. Short beard, arms folded, head tilted slightly, as if the man he's talking to is mildly amusing. The second you may recognize from the registration tent: full plate, two servants at a careful distance, and the expression of someone accustomed to getting what he wants.

boxed.title: The Argument — In Progress
boxed.text: The man in traveling clothes says, with great patience: 'Respectfully, sir — we are not in your neck of the woods. And on top of that, I don't make the rules. I just have to enforce them.' The paladin's voice rises: 'This is an outrage. My companions are more than capable—' 'Your companions are servants. Good ones, I'm sure. But servants.' He unfolds his arms and glances past the paladin — straight at you. A slow grin crosses his face. 'Though the light may be shining down on you, sir — there be three walking up behind you who could fill the spots. That is, if they have not already out-bid another party, and if they are only three.'

boxed.title: Corben Vash — Introduction
boxed.text: The man steps around the paladin and extends a hand. 'I be Corben Vash. The best of the best of guides — if my track record does show.'

script.text: The party follows Bethalyn's directions south-east, past the market stalls and sled kennels, toward growling and raised voices. They walk in on Corben patiently refusing Vane — who is trying to register his servants as racers.
Continue when the table is ready.
Continue when the table is ready.

scenes.development: Past the market stalls and the empty kennels, an argument and a low chorus of growling — several animals, not one — coming from the last tent with a team still to spare.

scenes.title: Scene 4 — Meeting the Wolves
scenes.flavor: Six dire wolves in a rope pen, watching you arrive with steady amber eyes. Slow movements. Let them come to you. Whatever you do — don't run.

blocks.title: RUNNING THE SCENE — DM
lines: Corben leads the party behind the tent to the wolf enclosure. This is the Animal Handling gate — the pack must accept the party before the trail, not on it. Run the checks individually. Success: the wolf sniffs and accepts, maybe leans into a hand. Failure: it pulls back or growls. Fail by 5+: it snaps — 1d4 piercing, and Corben sighs deeply. He is not surprised. He is also not happy. Runt is most likely to snap. Tusk is most likely to be enthusiastic. Fenra decides last, and her acceptance matters most.

blocks.text: Animal Handling DC 15 (advantage for Ranger / Druid / Path of the Pack Barbarian). If someone gets bit, Corben: 'And that is why we practice before the trail and not on it.' Not mean — just a man who has seen this exact thing happen many times.

boxed.title: Meeting the Wolves
boxed.text: Corben leads you around the back of the tent, and the growling gets louder. In a large rope enclosure — far more substantial than you might have expected — six dire wolves stand watching you arrive. They are enormous. Even at rest, the smallest one is eye-level with a tall human's chest. Their breath comes out in great plumes of steam. They do not bark. They do not lunge. They simply watch — with amber eyes that catch the firelight from town and hold it, steady and unblinking. Corben steps into the enclosure without a moment's hesitation.

boxed.title: Introducing The Pack
boxed.text: 'This is Fenra.' He rests a hand on the largest wolf, a grey female who regards him with what you might almost call tolerance. 'She's the alpha. Smartest thing on four legs on this mountain, and she knows it. Best to let her know you know it too.' He moves down the line. 'Greyback. Shadowfoot. Blizzard. Tusk — he's the young one, don't let the enthusiasm put you off. And that last one is Runt.' Runt is, indeed, the smallest. He is also the only one currently showing his teeth. 'They need to know you're not prey. Slow movements. Let them come to you first. And whatever you do — do not run.'

script.text: Corben leads the party behind the tent to the wolf enclosure. This is the Animal Handling gate — the pack must accept the party before the trail, not on it.
Continue when the table is ready.

scenes.development: Six dire wolves in a rope pen, watching you arrive with steady amber eyes. Slow movements. Let them come to you. Whatever you do — don't run.

scenes.title: Scene 5 — Corben's Terms & Camp Briefing
scenes.flavor: A hand-drawn map on the camp table: twenty percent of the purse, the bonus prize nobody can name yet, and five days of trail between here and Cornell.

blocks.title: RUNNING THE SCENE — DM
lines: Corben lays a hand-drawn map on the camp table and talks business, then rules, then runs a camp-breakdown drill. The cut (20%): negotiable down to 15% if pressed hard, no lower. He provides the team, the expertise, five years of trail knowledge. That has a price. The three rules don't bend: (1) Keep me alive — without me you're lost, and lost in the Dragonspine in winter is a short story. (2) If I go down, stay exactly where we stop; wait for another guided party and follow them to base camp — the wolves stay with you but won't run without me. (3) Each base camp is a waypoint; transports back to Zethel or Cornell exist from every camp, but once you board you're out of the race. Speeds: Slow (lose ground, safe) / Regular (hold position) / Fast (gain ground, trail pushes back — push too long and the runners crack). Corben calls the speed each morning; the party backs him.

blocks.text: Camp-breakdown drill: a fast, meticulous montage — partly functional, partly characterization. 'The faster we break camp once the horn blasts, the better our position. Every minute fumbling with ropes is a minute another team is ahead. So we don't fumble.' Closes by extending a hand: 'Do we have a deal?' Then he strides off to register the party before the deadline horn. He makes it back before the horn blows.

boxed.title: Corben's Terms & Camp Briefing
boxed.text: Once everyone has met the pack, Corben pulls the group into the tent proper and lays a hand-drawn map of the route on the camp table. 'All right. Now that you've met the family — let's talk business.' He looks each of you in the eye. 'I'll be taking twenty percent of any purse we win. The four of you split the rest, along with whatever fool prize they have as the bonus this year. Last year there was a grand wizard waiting at the top — granted each party member a wish spell.' He shrugs. 'Who knows what it'll be this year. Could be nothing. Could be something that changes your life. Either way, we have to finish to find out.'

boxed.title: Corben's Terms & Camp Briefing — continued
boxed.text: 'My rules. There are three and they don't bend. One: keep me alive. Two: if I go down, stay exactly where we stop — wait for another party with a guide and follow them to the next base camp. The wolves will stay with you. They know the way. But they won't run it without me. Three: each base camp is a waypoint. Transports back to Zethel or Cornell run from every camp — but once you're on one, you're out of the race. Got it?'

script.text: Corben lays a hand-drawn map on the camp table and talks business, then rules, then runs a camp-breakdown drill. The cut (20%): negotiable down to 15% if pressed hard, no lower.
THE RULES — once terms are agreed, his tone shifts. Still warm — but this is the part he means.

scenes.development: A hand-drawn map on the camp table: twenty percent of the purse, the bonus prize nobody can name yet, and five days of trail between here and Cornell.

scenes.title: Scene 6 — Day 1: The Start & First Night
scenes.flavor: The horn goes up over Zethel and thirty teams break for the pass at once — five days out, the whole mountain ahead, and the crowd in Cornell already gathered at the pool.

blocks.title: RUNNING THE SCENE — DM
lines: Roll starting position (d20 + modifier) and tell players where they sit in the pack. Day 1 climbs without mercy — switchback after switchback. Regular is the right call; Corben will say so if asked. Night camp: DC 10 Luck Check. Fail = a saber-toothed tiger enters the firelight (size of a draft horse, never learned to be afraid). Drive it off without a fight: Intimidation DC 14 / Animal Handling DC 16. Corben stays back — this is a party test. He's watching how they handle it, and he is not helping.

blocks.text: If the night Luck Check fails: in the fourth hour, the wolves wake as one, ears forward. Something enormous moves through the trees uphill — breathing too large, too slow. The saber-toothed tiger steps into the firelight with arrogant confidence, amber eyes sweeping the camp. It is looking at the wolves. Or possibly at you. It's genuinely hard to tell.

boxed.title: Day 1: The Start & First Night
boxed.text: Dawn. The bonfire has burned to coals. Zethel is as quiet as it gets with thirty sled teams lined up at the southern edge of town — wolves and dogs and strange hybrid creatures straining against their harnesses, filling the cold air with steam and noise. Corben has you in position. The wolves are harnessed, pacing with coiled energy. Runt keeps looking back at you like he's checking you're still there. Ahead — the mountain trail, climbing steeply, vanishing into pine shadow within a hundred yards. Five days away is Cornell. And the prize. The racing horn sounds — a long, clear blast that echoes off the mountain face and sends every bird in the trees exploding upward in a white cloud. And you're moving.

boxed.title: Day 1: The Start & First Night — continued
boxed.text: 'The horn ending the racing day comes as the light fails. Corben halts at a flat, well-used campsite — old fire rings, worn snow. The wolves collapse into a loose pile, exhausted and content. Camp goes up in eight minutes. Corben watches with his arms crossed and says nothing, which you're beginning to understand is his version of a compliment.'

script.text: Roll starting position (d20 + modifier) and tell players where they sit in the pack. Day 1 climbs without mercy — switchback after switchback.
MAKING CAMP — end of Day 1

push.label: Day 1: The Start & First Night — continued

scenes.development: The horn goes up over Zethel and thirty teams break for the pass at once — five days out, the whole mountain ahead, and the crowd in Cornell already gathered at the pool.

scenes.title: Scene 7 — Day 2: The First Climb
scenes.flavor: Above the treeline the cold gets an edge to it. Bear country by morning, an open meadow the herds run through — and at the end of the day, the ice that's ended races before.

blocks.title: RUNNING THE SCENE — DM
lines: Two encounters, each gated by a DC 10 Luck Check. 1st switchback — Polar bear (fail = it's on the trail; pass = tracks only + bear on a distant ridge). It's a sow with cubs: Nature DC 12 / Animal Handling DC 14 to identify and back away slowly. Running past at Fast speed: DC 13 DEX save or the bear swipes the sled. 3rd switchback — Elk crossing (fail = full panicked herd pours over the ridge). Tusk will want to chase. Athletics / Animal Handling DC 14 to hold the wolves. Fail: sled veers off path → DC 12 DEX save → fail = −2 positions and a repair.

blocks.text: Polar bear (1st switchback, failed check): 'As the sled comes around, the polar bear is just... there. Standing in the middle of the trail, enormous and pale, regarding your operation with mild irritation. You woke it. It does not look pleased.' End of Day 2, Corben tallies position against the field: 'Not bad,' which you're certain is the highest praise he gives.

boxed.title: Day 2: The First Climb
boxed.text: The second day bites harder. The trail narrows as it gains elevation, and the cold has a different quality up here — drier, thinner, with an edge that gets into your lungs on every breath. The wolf pack runs hard, the sled rails singing over packed snow. Corben points out the switchback ahead — a sharp left where the trail doubles back on itself, climbing again. 'First switchback,' he says. 'Keep your weight low.'

boxed.title: Day 2: The First Climb — continued
boxed.text: You hear them before you see them — a rumbling felt through the sled runners before it registers as sound. Then the elk pour over the ridge above you, panicked, paying no attention to the race path. Corben grabs the harness lines: 'Hold the wolves! Do NOT let them chase—' Too late. Tusk has already noticed.

script.text: Two encounters, each gated by a DC 10 Luck Check. 1st switchback — Polar bear (fail = it's on the trail; pass = tracks only + bear on a distant ridge).
ELK — 3rd switchback, on a failed check

scenes.development: Above the treeline the cold gets an edge to it. Bear country by morning, an open meadow the herds run through — and at the end of the day, the ice that's ended races before.

scenes.title: Scene 8 — Day 3: The Fey Stretch
scenes.flavor: The trail turns sideways into old silver wood where the record shows things that don't get explained. Vash's advice on the fey stretch is the same every year: just get through it.

blocks.title: RUNNING THE SCENE — DM
lines: EXPAND THIS SCENE. The trail turns sideways into ancient old-growth — silver light, roots frozen in almost-deliberate shapes. Corben and the wolves go quiet. Glimmerkin (1st switchback): contacts regardless of the roll; the DC 10 Luck Check sets her mood. She's fascinated by a six-wolf sled team and finds it both incredible and mildly offensive to her fey sensibilities. Engage genuinely and name all six wolves → she's delighted and gives a silver bell tied to the lead harness: 'Ring it at the worst moment.' (advantage on one Luck Check in Days 4–5). Shoo or rush her → tangled harness: DC 15 Investigation / Sleight of Hand DC 13, and −1 position for the day. Do not fight the glimmerkin. Owlbear (3rd switchback): DC 10 ±5 Luck Check. Success: Fenra plants herself and stares it down until it reconsiders. Fail: combat.

blocks.text: The Glimmerkin wants: each wolf's name, to understand why humans direct wolves at all, and to be acknowledged as significant. She does NOT want to be ignored, rushed, or lied to (she'll know). Owlbear: 'It announces itself with a sound that's both a screech and a growl, bouncing off the mountain in every direction. Territorial, enormous, astride the trail.' Corben, quietly: 'Don't look it in the eye.' End of Day 3 is a LONG REST in a sheltered vale — intentional, because Day 4 is the hardest day.

boxed.title: Day 3: The Fey Stretch
boxed.text: The third day's trail takes an unexpected turn — not upward, but sideways, into an old-growth section the other trail sections simply don't have. The trees here are ancient. Their roots have cracked through the snow and frozen in shapes that look almost deliberate. The light comes through in shafts of pale silver rather than gold. Corben goes quiet. The wolves go quiet too, which is somehow more unnerving. 'Fey stretch,' Corben says, after a moment. 'Every year. Just get through it.'

boxed.title: The Glimmerkin
boxed.text: The wolves stop. All six, simultaneously, as though someone cut their strings. Corben frowns. Then — from near Tusk's left ear — a voice the size of a bird's: 'You have twelve wolves in your party and none of them are properly introduced. This is rude.'

script.text: EXPAND THIS SCENE. The trail turns sideways into ancient old-growth — silver light, roots frozen in almost-deliberate shapes.
Continue when the table is ready.

scenes.development: The trail turns sideways into old silver wood where the record shows things that don't get explained. Vash's advice on the fey stretch is the same every year: just get through it.

scenes.title: Scene 9 — Day 4: The Valley of Giants
scenes.flavor: The hardest day. The trail goes down, into a silent white valley ringed by peaks — a place with an owner, a toll, and rules Vash states plainly: don't stop, don't talk, and don't point at the rocks.

blocks.title: RUNNING THE SCENE — DM
lines: EXPAND THIS SCENE — the hardest day. The trail goes DOWN into a vast, wind-blocked, almost-silent valley of blinding white snow. Corben is the most serious you've seen him: 'Keep moving. Don't stop unless I say stop. Don't talk to anyone unless I say talk. And whatever you see in the rocks — don't point at it.' The Hag (valley floor, DC 10 Luck Check): fail = she's in the path; pass = she approaches anyway. She wants a secret, a name, a memory, or a year of life — NOT gold (she finds gold boring). In exchange: safe passage, intel on the Frost Giant's name and price, or a minor boon. Night Hag HP 112 if attacked — but she is not the final boss; don't let it become full combat unless the party insists. The Frost Giant (2nd switchback, DC 10 ±5): blocks the trail, demands a toll regardless of mood. Accepts gold (500gp+), a story he hasn't heard (Persuasion DC 15), an arm wrestle (Athletics DC 22, two tries if amusing), something beautiful for his wife, or — if the Hag gave them his name — uses it for free passage. Combat costs −2 positions minimum and risks sled damage.

blocks.text: Frost Giant (2nd switchback): 'The switchback is blocked by a pair of boots the size of boats, attached to a frost giant sitting with his chin in one enormous hand, bored. Behind him, sled-runner ruts where other teams already paid the toll.' His voice rolls down like distant thunder: 'Small people. Many of them today. What do you have?' End of Day 4 is a SHORT REST only. Corben, to Fenra or to all of you: 'One more day. Last push tomorrow. Everything we have.'

boxed.title: Day 4: The Valley of Giants
boxed.text: The fourth day's trail does something none of the others have: it goes down. Steeply. The mountain opens into a wide valley, bowl-shaped and vast, ringed by peaks that block the wind so completely the valley is almost silent. The snow is undisturbed and blindingly white. Corben's expression is the most serious you've seen it. 'Keep moving. Don't stop unless I say stop. Don't talk to anyone unless I say talk. And whatever you see in the rocks on the valley walls — don't point at it.'

boxed.title: The Hag
boxed.text: She appears from behind a boulder the size of a house. For a moment your brain tries to make her into something normal — an old woman, a traveler. Then the details settle: too tall, fingers too long, a smile too wide with too many teeth, all pointing the wrong direction. 'Racing folk,' she says — gravel and cold honey. 'So many things they carry that they don't know the value of.'

script.text: EXPAND THIS SCENE — the hardest day. The trail goes DOWN into a vast, wind-blocked, almost-silent valley of blinding white snow.
Continue when the table is ready.

scenes.development: The hardest day. The trail goes down, into a silent white valley ringed by peaks — a place with an owner, a toll, and rules Vash states plainly: don't stop, don't talk, and don't point at the rocks.

scenes.title: Scene 10 — Day 5: The Final Push
scenes.flavor: Cornell's smoke is somewhere below the last ridge. Three switchbacks left, everything still on the table, and Vash calling one speed all day: fast, and make up the cost at the finish.

blocks.title: RUNNING THE SCENE — DM
lines: Three switchbacks decide the race. Corben calls Fast speed all day: 'Whatever it costs us, we make it up at the finish.' Dryad (DC 10 Luck Check): success blesses passing (advantage on next Luck Check); she can't stop them by force. Dismiss her rudely and Corben looks slightly ashamed — he's passed her many times and never found the right answer either. Silver dragon: appears regardless; DC 10 ±5 Luck Check affects her mood. Engaged seriously: +2 positions. Do NOT let players attack — her breath is a DC 23 CON save for 12d8 cold. Please talk them out of it. Hollowmourn (3rd / final switchback): Cornell is less than a mile below, smoke visible. DC 13 CON save for ALL party + Corben; failure drops to 0 HP. She cannot leave the switchback; Turn Undead works. If Corben falls, the wolves keep running — DC 14 Animal Handling to take the reins, then the party decides: stabilize Corben or push for the finish.

blocks.text: Hollowmourn: DC 13 CON save — everyone, including Corben — failure to 0 HP. She cannot leave the switchback; Turn Undead works. If Corben fails he goes down, the wolves keep running, the sled keeps moving: DC 14 Animal Handling to take the reins, then stabilize Corben or push for the finish. Silver dragon attack = DC 23 CON save, 12d8 cold — please talk them out of this.

boxed.title: Day 5: The Final Push
boxed.text: The fifth morning has a different quality. The cold is the same, the light the same pale grey of mountain dawn — but the trail ahead feels charged, like the air before a lightning strike. The wolves feel it too: on their feet before Corben's command, pulling at the harnesses, eager in a way they haven't been all week. Corben looks at your group. He looks at the trail. He looks back at you. 'Fast speed today,' he says. 'All of it. Whatever it costs us, we make it up at the finish.'

boxed.title: The Last Switchback
boxed.text: The 3rd switchback. The last one. Cornell is less than a mile below — you can see the smoke from the town fires rising in the valley below the ridge. The finish line.

script.text: Three switchbacks decide the race. Corben calls Fast speed all day: 'Whatever it costs us, we make it up at the finish.' Dryad (DC 10 Luck Check): success blesses passing (advantage on next Luck Check); she can't stop them by force.
Continue when the table is ready.

scenes.development: Cornell's smoke is somewhere below the last ridge. Three switchbacks left, everything still on the table, and Vash calling one speed all day: fast, and make up the cost at the finish.

scenes.title: Scene 11 — The Finish Line at Cornell
scenes.flavor: Down the last slope into Cornell, the wolves howling, the town lining the road — five days of Dragonspine behind them and the line crossed.

blocks.title: RUNNING THE SCENE — DM
lines: Announce final positions based on all tracked rank modifiers. First place: 10,000gp + the bonus item (decide it, roll a table, or use last year's wish-spell precedent). Any finishing position: the completion purse plus the story. The wolves howl coming down the last slope — actually howling, as if they've saved it for this moment. Corben's expression is, for the first time, completely open: not confident, not calculating, just purely, completely alive.

blocks.text: Optional epilogue: that night in Cornell's only inn the prize is distributed, hands shaken, stories already changing and getting better. Through the window you can just make out Corben in the wolf pen with Fenra, his hand on her head, the mountain black against a sky full of stars behind them. The Dragonspine Mountains 'Dog' Sled Race is over. You survived.

boxed.title: The Finish Line at Cornell
boxed.text: You come down the last slope into Cornell like a controlled avalanche — the sled loud and fast, the wolves howling now, actually howling, as if they've been saving it for exactly this moment. The town is ready. People line the trail where it becomes Cornell's main road, shouting — not for any specific team, just shouting, the way people shout when something that has been building for five days finally arrives. Corben is upright on the sled runners behind you, one hand on the harness, and for the first time since you met him his expression is completely open.

boxed.title: Final Words
boxed.text: The wolves stop, sides heaving, steam pouring off them. Corben steps down and crouches in the snow — and Tusk is on him, then Greyback, then all six at once, and he is laughing, actually laughing, buried under half a ton of dire wolf. He surfaces. Looks at your group. 'Not bad,' he says. 'For your first time.'

script.text: Announce final positions based on all tracked rank modifiers. First place: 10,000gp + the bonus item (decide it, roll a table, or use last year's wish-spell precedent).
Continue when the table is ready.

scenes.development: Down the last slope into Cornell, the wolves howling, the town lining the road — five days of Dragonspine behind them and the line crossed.

finishVariants.first: Down the last slope into Cornell like a controlled avalanche, the wolves howling, the whole town on its feet — and the pool holds on Vash's team crossing first.
finishVariants.any: Down the last slope into Cornell, the wolves howling, the town lining the road — five days of Dragonspine behind them and the line crossed.
finishVariants.last: Last across, but across — the wolves howling all the same, and Cornell giving the applause that isn't about position but about making it at all.

scenes.title: Scene 12 — After the Line
scenes.flavor: The morning after the line: the prize table in the Hall, the certificate stamped and sealed, the wolves asleep in a heap in the pen, and every road out of Cornell pointing somewhere.

blocks.title: RUNNING THE SCENE — DM
lines: This is the quarter hour after the line — the settlement, the goodbyes, and the doors out. Run it in that order: what they won, what they carry, who they leave, and where the mountain points.
The finish has already been played on the scene before this one. Do not re-announce positions here. Open the prize table and let the table talk.
It closes a YEAR, never the event. Everything settled in this scene is what a returning party comes back holding when the horn sounds again next winter — so settle it, then bank the year.

blocks.title: THE SETTLEMENT — WHAT THEY WON
lines: The purse is the party's tier, not the broadsheet's. The four bands are on the Race Rules page and the winning figure runs from 10,000 gold to 100,000 — read the tier's figure, never the number on the poster.

The guide's contract takes twenty percent off the top — fifteen if it was argued down at the camp table, no lower. The remainder splits equally among the racers who actually rode, which is four by contract and may be more or fewer at your table.

The bonus prize is ONE item and it goes to a party vote. It is never divided and it is never sold for coin at the ceremony. What happens to it afterward is the party's business, and it is frequently the best argument of the night.
A team that finished and did not win is paid the completion purse. Cornell has never sent a finisher home with nothing and has no intention of starting.

blocks.title: THE CERTIFICATE — EVERY FINISHER, WITHOUT EXCEPTION
lines: Every sled that crosses is entered on the register and issued a safe-passage certificate under the Dragonspine Guild's seal — stamped at the Prize Hall the morning after, naming the sled and its crew, and it does not expire.

What it is worth: the northern passes read it. A party carrying one is not stopped on the mountain road, is quartered at any waystation with room to spare, and is owed help by anyone flying the Guild's seal. It is the one thing every finisher walks out with, win or lose, and most of them do not understand it on the day.
Hand it over on the page. It has been promised on the broadsheet since registration opened, and the finish is where it finally arrives.

blocks.title: CORBEN AND THE WOLVES
lines: The contract was for one race and it ends at Cornell. Corben will say so plainly if asked — he does not assume, and he does not angle.

Whether it ends there is the table's. He is a licensed guide with a team and seven years of the pass, and a party that kept his three rules, kept him alive, and never made him regret signing will find a standing arrangement is his to offer rather than theirs to argue for. He names a fair rate and means it.

The wolves decide separately and are not subtle. Runt in particular has opinions. If a racer spent five days earning one of them, that is the wolf that crosses the pen and leans on them, and Corben notices and says nothing at all.
If the guide went down on the trail, this is where that lands. The wolves go to whoever handled them. The Guild stamps the certificate anyway. Cornell buys the round anyway.

blocks.title: WHAT IS STILL OWED
lines: Vestri's ledger does not close at the finish line. Whatever the pool stood at when she gave the Landlord's Farewell is what she remembers them by — a debt, a courtesy, or a grudge — and the valley is hers every winter. She sends no collectors. She simply waits.

The chalk travels. A racer who fought in Sable's basement before the horn and in the Prize Hall undercroft after it has ONE record, kept by one office and honored in both towns. Finish week is when the Iron Scales sends word to the inn.
Anyone who left the race at a base camp is in Zethel or Cornell, cold and intact, and is at the celebration. The pass takes people and hands most of them back.

blocks.title: WHERE THE MOUNTAIN POINTS — the three roads out
lines: EAST OF THE MOUNTAIN. The Commissioner's sealed chest came in from the east, on a horse with mountain mud on its shoes, and Cornell is west. Trollgranite has been filling an unexplained eastern-alloy order for the Thig Dural Thane for two seasons running. Both point off the race route entirely, at the other side of the range — and nobody in either town has set the two beside each other.

YEAR FOUR. The race records upstairs in the Prize Hall carry three days that say only that conditions precluded normal recording. The fight register downstairs carries three nights of bouts those records do not have, and a charter suspension entered beside them. Two ends, one floor apart, and the office that keeps them both is the office that just stamped the party's certificate.

THE ROAD SOUTH. Cornell is the northern end of the kingdom's main trading road and the race brings traffic. There is work in the square that has nothing to do with sleds, money that would very much like to know what the party knows — and a figure who has sat at the same corner table in the Cracked Tusk for four race seasons, standing in the Cornell square right now, nodding across it and not approaching.

blocks.text: The two towns' pages hold the whole of it — the folk who offer the work, the register that will not discuss Year Four, and the line the Iron Scales is holding open. This scene is where they all come due at once.

boxed.title: After the Line
boxed.text: That night in Cornell's only inn the prize is distributed, hands are shaken, and the stories are already changing and getting better in the telling. Somebody buys a round for a team that came in twenty-second. Somebody else is still arguing about Day Three and will still be arguing about it next winter. Through the window you can just make out Corben in the wolf pen with Fenra, his hand flat on her head, the mountain black against a sky full of stars behind them — not celebrating, just standing with them, the way a person stands with the ones they came back with. In the morning the Prize Hall will stamp your safe-passage under the Guild's seal and the road south will be open. The Dragonspine Mountains "Dog" Sled Race is over. You survived it — and not everybody does, and everybody in this room knows which of those two things is the achievement.

script.text: Settle first: the tier's purse, the guide's cut off the top, the rest split among the racers who rode, the bonus item to a party vote — then the certificate, stamped at the Hall in the morning, for every sled that crossed.
Then the goodbyes. The contract ends at Cornell unless Corben offers otherwise; the wolves choose for themselves; anyone who left at a base camp is at the celebration.
Then the doors out — east of the mountain, Year Four, and the road south. Name them and leave them standing. The party decides which one they are already walking toward.
When the table is done talking, bank the year. The race opens again next winter, and the mountain remembers who came over it.

scenes.development: The year is closed, not the event — the purse settled, the certificate sealed, the contract ended or renewed, and three roads out of Cornell that were not there five days ago.

days.label: Day 1 — Leaving Zethel
days.intro: The race begins at dawn. Thirty sled teams line up at the southern edge of Zethel. Corben has the wolves harnessed and ready. The mountain trail climbs steeply ahead, vanishing into pine shadow within a hundred yards. Five days away is Cornell — and the prize.

switchbacks.title: Switchback 1 — The Starting Climb
switchbacks.dmNotes: Opening switchback. Trail is wide and well-packed from race traffic. This is the party's first chance to find their pace. Corben will be watching how they handle the wolves — trust-building moment. Rival teams are bunched up; lots of early jostling but nothing dangerous yet. Roll for starting position: d20 + appropriate modifier. Tell players where they sit in the pack as the trail swallows them up.
switchbacks.readAloud: The trail climbs steeply out of Zethel's shadow, the town falling away behind you as the wolves find their stride. The snow is packed hard by a hundred previous races. The pack stretches ahead and behind — sleds weaving for position in the grey morning light. Corben Vash hasn't spoken since the horn.
switchbacks.flavor: The pool opens on thirty teams pouring out of Zethel into the pass — sleds weaving for the first bend, the field still one tangled knot in the grey morning light.

switchbacks.title: Switchback 2 — The Rocky Narrows
switchbacks.dmNotes: Trail narrows between two rock faces. Still early in Day 1 but teams start to separate here. Lord Vane's Regiment is already using the narrows to push slower teams wide. Good moment to introduce bully squad behavior through narration even if the mechanic hasn't triggered yet. Regular pace is the right call here — Corben will indicate as much through his body language.
switchbacks.readAloud: The trail squeezes between two walls of dark granite, the wolves' breath steaming in the cold air. Teams are thinning out — the gap between the leaders and the stragglers already opening. Somewhere behind you, you hear the crack of wood on wood. Someone is already making contact.
switchbacks.flavor: The trail pinches to a seam between two walls of dark granite. The pack is stretching thin now — and somewhere in it, the first crack of wood on wood carries up the mountain.
switchbacks.encounter: Lord Vane's Regiment likely in this area. If bully check fires, narrate them forcing a rival wide at the narrows before the sled can react.

switchbacks.title: Switchback 3 — First Camp, Nightfall
switchbacks.dmNotes: Final switchback before the first overnight camp. Teams are spreading out into a race shape now. Good opportunity for Corben to say something cryptic about tomorrow's conditions. NIGHT CAMP — SABER-TOOTHED TIGER: Short rest at camp. If they fail DC 10 Luck Check, the tiger enters. If they pass, it's out there in the dark but decides they're not worth it. Combat or: Intimidation DC 14 / Animal Handling DC 16 to drive it off without a fight. Corben stays back — this is a party test. He's watching to see how they handle it.
switchbacks.readAloud: The first day's light is failing as the trail opens onto a broad shelf of rock and snow — the first base camp, smoke already rising from a dozen cook fires. The wolves slow without being told. They've done this before. Corben surveys the field without expression, then begins unhooking the traces. [IF SABER-TOOTH TRIGGERS] Somewhere in the fourth hour of the night, one of the wolves raises its head. Then all six of them are awake, ears forward, bodies still. From the darkness beyond the firelight comes a sound like breathing — but too large. Too slow. Something enormous is moving through the trees on the uphill side of camp. The saber-toothed tiger steps into the ring of firelight with the slow, arrogant confidence of a creature that has never learned to be afraid. It is the size of a draft horse. Its amber eyes sweep the camp. It is looking at the wolves. Or possibly at you. It's genuinely difficult to tell.
switchbacks.flavor: The pool holds on the first camp as the light dies — cook-fires on the shelf, the wolves bedded down in a loose pile, and the dark past the firelight going very still.
switchbacks.encounter:
SABER-TOOTHED TIGER (optional) AC 12 | HP 52 | Speed 40ft
Str 18 (+4) | Dex 14 (+2) | Con 15 (+2) | Int 3 (−4) | Wis 12 (+1) | Cha 8 (−1)
Bite +6, 1d10+4 | Claw +6, 1d6+4
Pounce: if moves 20ft+ before claw, DC 13 STR or knocked prone + bonus bite Intimidation DC 14 or Animal Handling DC 16 to drive off without combat.
Corben stays back. He is watching. He has opinions. [ON SUCCESS WITHOUT COMBAT]
The night passes without incident. Whatever was out there in the dark decided you weren't worth the trouble. The wolves settle. The fire burns low. Morning comes cold and grey.

days.startAloud: Dawn. The bonfire has burned down to coals. The town of Zethel is quiet — or as quiet as it gets with thirty sled teams lined up at the southern edge of town, wolves and dogs and strange hybrid creatures all straining against their harnesses, filling the cold air with steam and noise. Corben has you in position. The wolves are harnessed and ready, pacing with coiled energy. Runt keeps looking back at you like he's checking to make sure you're still there. Ahead of you — the mountain trail. It climbs steeply, vanishing into pine shadow within a hundred yards. Somewhere up there, five days away, is the town of Cornell. And the prize. The racing horn sounds — a long, clear blast that echoes off the mountain face and sends every bird in the trees exploding upward in a white cloud. And you're moving.

days.label: Day 2 — Polar Bear Country
days.intro: The second day enters the high wilderness above the treeline. The cold has a different quality up here — drier, thinner, with an edge to it that gets into your lungs. Polar bear tracks were spotted near camp overnight. The elk herds migrate through this stretch every year. The ice field at the end of Day 2 has claimed three sleds in the last five races.

switchbacks.title: Switchback 1 — Something Crossed the Trail
switchbacks.dmNotes: DC 10 Luck Check. On failure: polar bear is on the trail. On success: tracks only — the bear is visible on a distant ridge. The bear is a sow with cubs nearby. Nature DC 12 or Animal Handling DC 14 to identify this and back away slowly. Running past at Fast speed: DC 13 DEX save or the bear swipes the sled. Corben will have read the tracks already — his hint here is unusually confident.
switchbacks.readAloud: The morning light catches the trail ahead and reveals something that stops your breath — paw prints. Each one the size of a dinner plate, pressed deep into the snow, crossing the race line and disappearing into the white. Corben crouches, touches the edge of one print without comment, and straightens. The wolves are very quiet. [IF BEAR APPEARS] As the sled comes around the switchback, the polar bear is just... there. Standing in the middle of the trail, enormous and pale, regarding your entire operation with mild irritation. It had been sleeping in the lee of the rock face. You have woken it. It does not look pleased.
switchbacks.flavor: Prints the size of a dinner plate track across the race line and vanish into the white. Vash reads them without a word. The wolves have gone quiet.
switchbacks.encounter:
