POLAR BEAR (if check fails) AC 12 | HP 42 | Speed 40ft, Swim 40ft
Str 20 (+5) | Dex 10 (+0) | Con 16 (+3)
Multiattack: Bite + Claw
Bite +7, 2d6+5 | Claw +7, 2d6+5 Sow with cubs nearby — Nature DC 12 or Animal Handling DC 14 to read this.
If read correctly: backs away when given space. If cornered or cubs threatened: full combat.

switchbacks.title: Switchback 2 — The Elk Meadow
switchbacks.dmNotes: DC 10 Luck Check. On failure: party hits the full crossing. On success: leading teams have already scattered the elk — only the tail end of the herd, more manageable. Athletics or Animal Handling DC 14 to keep wolves from bolting after the elk. Fail: sled veers off path. DC 12 DEX save to avoid rock face. Fail that: −2 positions and repair required. Corben grabs the harness lines and shouts: 'Hold the wolves! Do NOT let them chase—' — Tusk has already noticed.
switchbacks.readAloud: You hear them before you see them — a rumbling you feel through the sled runners before it registers as sound. Then the elk come pouring over the ridge above you. A herd, panicked by something uptrail, moving fast and paying no attention whatsoever to the race path. Corben grabs the harness lines and shouts over the noise: 'Hold the wolves! Do NOT let them chase—' Too late. Tusk has already noticed.
switchbacks.flavor: A wall of antler and steam pours over the ridge above the trail — the whole herd running for reasons of its own, and paying the race no mind at all.
switchbacks.encounter:
ELK HERD HAZARD Animal Handling or Athletics DC 14 to control the wolves.
Fail: sled veers off path → DC 12 DEX save
Fail DEX save: −2 positions + repair required Tusk is the wolf most likely to give chase. Corben is not surprised. He is also not happy.

switchbacks.title: Switchback 3 — The Ice Field
switchbacks.dmNotes: Hard blue ice under the snow. The worst terrain of Day 2 — possibly the race. A wrecked sled from Race Year 6 is still frozen into the bank, visible if the party looks. DC 12 Perception to identify the registration number. Corben has strong opinions about this switchback. His hint will be as clear as it ever gets without being direct. End of day camp is quiet — Corben says 'Not bad,' which is his highest possible praise.
switchbacks.readAloud: The snow thins and then vanishes entirely, replaced by a sheet of ancient ice that catches the late light and throws it back as cold blue fire. The wolves' claws scratch for purchase. Somewhere in the bank to your left, half-buried by two seasons of snowfall, the wreckage of another sled has become part of the mountain.
switchbacks.flavor: The snow thins to bare blue ice that throws the last light back like cold fire. The runners scratch for grip — and in the bank, half-swallowed by two winters, the shape of a sled that didn't make it.
switchbacks.encounter:
RACE WRECK — DC 12 Perception
Identifies as Race Year 6 registration number. A team that held second place for three days before this section. Corben will acknowledge it if asked. Just nods. END OF DAY 2 CAMP: 'Not bad,' Corben says. This is the highest praise he gives.

days.label: Day 3 — The Fey Forest
days.intro: The trail passes through a stretch of ancient forest where the Dragonspine touches the Feywild. Race records show a 40% incidence of unexplained events in this section. The Cornell scryers file complaints every year about sympathetic interference. Corben has never explained what happens to him in the fey stretch. He just runs it.

switchbacks.title: Switchback 1 — Into the Silver Trees
switchbacks.dmNotes:
DC 10 Luck Check — but the Glimmerkin makes contact REGARDLESS of the roll. The check only determines whether she's amused (success) or already annoyed (fail — she's tied a harness in a complicated knot and is sitting on Tusk's back, invisible, waiting to be noticed). She WANTS: to know each wolf's name, to understand why humans direct wolves at all, to be acknowledged as significant.
She does NOT want: to be ignored, rushed, or lied to (she'll know). Gift if engaged genuinely (name all six wolves): a silver bell tied to the lead harness. 'Ring it at the worst moment. You'll know when.' Functions as advantage on one Luck Check in Days 4 or 5.
switchbacks.readAloud: The treeline takes you without warning — one moment open mountain, the next a cathedral of pale silver trees with bark like birch and leaves that have no business being green in this season. The sound of other teams disappears. Your own runners sound different. The wolves run with their ears flat, not in fear — in attention. The wolves stop. All six of them, simultaneously, as though someone cut their strings. Corben frowns. Then — from somewhere near Tusk's left ear — a voice the size of a bird's: 'You have twelve wolves in your party and none of them are properly introduced. This is rude.'
switchbacks.flavor: The pool goes strange — pale silver trunks, leaves with no business being green this deep in the Claw of Storms. The sound of the other teams simply stops. Even the wolves are listening.
switchbacks.encounter:
THE GLIMMERKIN Engaged well → silver bell: advantage on one Luck Check (Days 4 or 5)
Rushed or ignored → harness tangle: DC 15 Investigation or Sleight of Hand DC 13. Either way: −1 position for the day. She is not hostile. She is thoroughly offended by the concept of sled dogs.

switchbacks.title: Switchback 2 — The Deep Wood
switchbacks.dmNotes: Peak interference zone. Scrying pool interference — stone goes dark naturally here unless party has already toggled it. Glimmerkin may still be present. Glamour effects: colours slightly wrong, trail seems to double back but doesn't, time feels stretched. Tusk has been staring at a point four feet off the trail for the last thirty seconds. Corben has noticed. Corben has not said anything about it. No combat unless players engage the fey elements aggressively.
switchbacks.readAloud: The forest is doing something to the light. It falls wrong — from the wrong angle, through the wrong leaves, casting shadows that don't match the trees that made them. Tusk has been staring at a point four feet off the trail for the last thirty seconds. Corben has noticed. Corben has not said anything about it.
switchbacks.flavor: The light is falling wrong in here — from the wrong angle, through the wrong leaves, laying down shadows that don't match the trees. One of the wolves is staring at nothing. Vash hasn't said a word about it.
switchbacks.encounter:
OPTIONAL GLIMMERKIN DEAL (if silver bell not yet given)
A glimmerkin offers: 'Better footing for something small.' They want a wolf hair.
Accept → next terrain roll automatically easy.
Refuse → nothing happens.
Corben is annoyed either way. Glamour effects are atmosphere, not mechanical. Don't let them stall the race.

switchbacks.title: Switchback 3 — Out of the Wood
switchbacks.dmNotes:
DC 10 ±5 Luck Check.
Success: Fenra plants herself between owlbear and sled. A stare so cold and level the owlbear simply reconsiders.
Fail: combat. After the owlbear: forest thins and ends. Sound comes back all at once. Wolves shake themselves. Corben does a quiet headcount of wolves, then team, then runners — in that order. LONG REST CAMP tonight. Corben calls it early at a sheltered vale he knows. 'Take it. Tomorrow's the valley, and the valley doesn't forgive tired people.' — All HP and abilities restored. Day 4 is the hardest day. Let the party feel the contrast.
switchbacks.readAloud: The owlbear announces itself with a sound that is somehow both a screech and a growl — a horrible combination that bounces off the mountain face in every direction at once. It is territorial and enormous and standing directly astride the trail. Corben says, quietly: 'Don't look it in the eye.' [FOREST EXIT] The silver trees end as abruptly as they began and you are back on open mountain with the sky overhead and the sound of the race returning all at once — other sleds, wind, the familiar percussion of runners on packed snow. The wolves shake their coats simultaneously, as if agreeing the forest is behind them. Corben counts something under his breath.
switchbacks.flavor: The silver trees end as sharply as they began, and the sound of the race comes back all at once — wind, runners, other sleds. The wolves shake their coats like they've agreed the forest is behind them.
switchbacks.encounter:
OWLBEAR (if check fails) AC 13 | HP 59 | Speed 40ft
Str 20 (+5) | Dex 12 (+1) | Con 17 (+3)
Multiattack: Beak + Claws
Beak +7, 1d10+5 | Claws +7, 2d6+5 Success (DC check): Fenra handles it. Describe the moment. No combat.
Fail: combat. Owlbear is territorial, not a predator — breaks off if the sled keeps moving past it. LONG REST CAMP: 'Tomorrow's the valley, and the valley doesn't forgive tired people.'

days.label: Day 4 — The Valley of Giants
days.intro: Day 4 is the hardest day in the race. The trail descends into Vestri's valley — it has always been hers, though she lets Hruun the frost giant claim it for his own amusement, and he lets her believe he doesn't know she lets him. The toll at the second switchback is theatre she designed. She watches every team navigate it from the ridge above. Corben has known whose valley this is for seven years. He has never said so to anyone.

switchbacks.title: Switchback 1 — Into the Valley
switchbacks.dmNotes:
This is Vestri's valley — it has always been hers. Hruun at SB2 works at her pleasure. She is not a random obstacle on the valley floor; she is the landlord greeting visitors. Her interest in the party is both genuine and calculated — if she trades them Hruun's name and preferences, it is because watching them use that intel against her own toll collector is the entertainment she came for. DC 10 Luck Check. Fail: she is in the path. Pass: she is watching from the rocks but approaches anyway. The check determines whether she has leverage. She wants one thing. Roll or choose:
1. A secret — true, unknown to the party. Gone from memory until after the race.
2. A name — someone they love. Forgotten until morning.
3. A memory — something warm and specific. Gone until the race ends.
4. A year of life — one new grey hair. Visible immediately. In exchange: safe passage, Hruun's name and preferred toll, or minor boon.
She does NOT want gold. She finds gold boring.
If attacked: HP 112, Night Hag. She vanishes and sends nightmares. She is not the final boss.
switchbacks.readAloud: The trail drops away into a valley so wide and so white that the far wall is lost in haze. The descent is brutal — loose shale under the snow, angles that make the sled want to run ahead of the wolves. The temperature drops ten degrees in as many minutes. She appears from behind a boulder the size of a house, and for a moment your brain tries to make her into something normal — an old woman, a traveler, a pilgrim in the wrong place. Then the details settle in. She is tall. The fingers are too long. The smile is too wide, with too many teeth, and all of them pointing the wrong direction. She regards your party with the patient attention of someone who has nowhere to be. 'Racing folk,' she says. Her voice is gravel and cold honey. 'I do love the racing season. So many interesting people passing through my valley. So many things they carry that they don't know the value of.'
switchbacks.flavor: The trail drops away into a valley so wide and so white the far wall is lost in haze. The cold falls ten degrees in as many minutes — and down on the valley floor, something is waiting by a boulder the size of a house.
switchbacks.encounter:
VESTRI THE NIGHT HAG (negotiation, not combat) HP 112 | AC 17 (natural armor)
Magic Resistance, Etherealness (action), Nightmare Haunting She WANTS: a secret / a name / a memory / a year (see DM notes)
She OFFERS: safe passage / frost giant intel / minor boon
She does NOT want: gold Corben will not comment on whether to accept. He's been offered deals on this descent before. He always declines. He's never explained why.

switchbacks.title: Switchback 2 — The Toll
switchbacks.dmNotes:
Hruun works at Vestri's pleasure. She gave him this valley and a gate to keep and the arrangement suits them both. He knows whose valley this is. If pushed he says only: 'Mine to keep. Hers to own. Same as always.' He does not elaborate. Corben carries Illianer brandy for this. Vestri told him Hruun likes it years ago, in some exchange Corben has never described. If the party used Vestri's intel: he notices. 'She told you.' Not a question. If they mention Vestri by name: he glances up at the ridge briefly, then back. 'She talked. She likes you.' He moves his foot without another word. Toll options:
- Gold (500gp+) — he thinks gold is pretty
- A story he has not heard (Persuasion DC 15)
- Arm wrestle (Athletics DC 22 — two tries if amusing)
- Something beautiful for his wife — he lights up
- Use his name: startled, then respectful. Free passage.
- Vestri endorsement: he moves his foot. No further negotiation needed. Combat: he removes sleds from the trail rather than destroying them. Still costs 4 positions.
switchbacks.readAloud: The 2nd switchback is blocked. Not by a rockfall, not by another racer — by a pair of boots, each the size of a boat, attached to legs, attached eventually to a frost giant who is sitting on the switchback with his elbows on his knees and his chin in one enormous hand. He is watching your approach with the bored expression of someone who has been sitting here long enough to be tired of it. Behind him, barely visible around the corner of the trail, you can see the twin ruts of sled runners where other teams have already passed. They paid the toll. His voice rolls down the mountain like distant thunder. 'Small people. Many of them today.' He tilts his head. 'What do you have?'
switchbacks.flavor: The way through is blocked — a pair of boots each the size of a rowboat, and above them, forty feet of patience with its chin on one enormous hand. Behind it, the ruts where every other team has already paid.
switchbacks.encounter:
HRUUN THE FROST GIANT (toll collector, not hostile unless attacked) AC 15 | HP 138 | Speed 40ft
Str 23 (+6) | Dex 9 (−1) | Con 21 (+5) | Int 8 (−1) | Wis 14 (+2) | Cha 11 (+0)
Rock: +9, 4d10+6 (ranged) | Greataxe: +9, 3d12+6 Toll accepted: flask of spirits / jewelry worth 10gp+ / a genuinely good story (Insight +2 vs Deception) / something beautiful
Toll refused: Hruun picks up the sled. −4 positions, no party damage.
His name used: startled, respectful, free passage. Corben's contribution: Illianer brandy. 'Every year. Same hand. Same silence.'

switchbacks.title: Switchback 3 — The Ridge
switchbacks.dmNotes:
This is the same Vestri from SB1 — she has been watching the party all day. She watched them deal with Hruun. She has opinions about how it went. If they used her intel well: warmer than usual. If they fought Hruun: annoyed — he is hers to inconvenience, not theirs to damage. If they used her name on Hruun and it worked: she is simply pleased. She only calls down if the party is in first, last, or had a dramatic reversal at SB2. Offer options:
- 'I can ensure your runners hold for the rest of the race. One nightmare, freely given, to be collected within a fortnight.'
- 'I know where Vane's Regiment plans to make contact tomorrow. One secret for one secret.'
- 'The wolves are tired. I can give them what they need. You will not like what I ask for.' All offers are genuine. All costs are real. SHORT REST only tonight. Corben is moving before the tent is fully up. 'One more day. Last push tomorrow. Everything we have.'
switchbacks.readAloud: The ridge trail is narrow and the drop to the left is considerable. Above you, carved into the rockface, is a cave opening that has no business being warm — but the light that comes from it is orange and flickering. Something is watching from that opening. You can't see it clearly. You get the impression that's intentional. [END OF DAY 4 CAMP] Short rest only tonight. Corben is already moving before the tent is fully up, checking the runners, feeding the wolves, talking to Fenra in a low voice with his hand on her head. 'One more day,' he says. To Fenra, or possibly to all of you. 'Last push tomorrow. Everything we have.'
switchbacks.flavor: A cave mouth in the ridge wall that has no business being warm — and orange light flickering in it. The pool can't quite settle on what's watching from inside. That may be the point.
switchbacks.encounter: VESTRI — SECOND CONTACT (conditional — see DM notes) Only appears if party is in first / dead last / had dramatic reversal. All offers are genuine. All costs are real. Corben will not advise. SHORT REST ONLY tonight. Day 5 starts with everything the party has right now.

days.label: Day 5 — The Final Push
days.intro: The fifth morning has a different quality. The cold is the same, the light is the same pale grey of mountain dawn — but the trail feels charged, like the air before a lightning strike. The wolves are on their feet before Corben's command. Cornell is visible from the high ridge on a clear day. Everything decided in the next three switchbacks.

switchbacks.title: Switchback 1 — The Final Ascent
switchbacks.dmNotes:
DC 10 Luck Check.
Success: Dryad steps aside and blesses their passing — advantage on the next Luck Check.
Fail: She's still in the way, but she's not hostile. She can't stop them by force — they can simply go around. She is sincere. The race genuinely damages this section of mountain forest. She's been asking every team to consider it for years. Most ignore her. Generous response (genuine promise, specific commitment: replanting, druidic donation, returning in spring): she blesses them.
Dismissed: she doesn't stop them, doesn't bless them. Corben looks slightly ashamed. He's passed her many times and never found the right answer either. This scene is a moral beat — 5 minutes max. Don't let it stall momentum.
switchbacks.readAloud: The woman steps out of a pine tree. Not from behind it — out of it, the bark parting and closing around her like water. She stands in the center of the trail with her arms at her sides and bark-grey skin and eyes the color of new leaves in spring. She is very calm. She is very still. 'This must stop,' she says. Simply, directly. 'Every year you pass through here and every year the mountain is a little less than it was. I am asking you — not commanding, asking — to stop.'
switchbacks.flavor: A woman steps out of a pine — not from behind it, out of it, the bark parting like water and closing behind her. She stands in the middle of the trail, bark-grey and very still, and simply waits.
switchbacks.encounter:
THE DRYAD (moral encounter — no combat) Bound to her tree. Cannot stop the party by force. Genuine engagement → advantage on next Luck Check
Dismissed → no effect. Corben looks ashamed. Note: Corben has passed her every year and never found the right answer either. He doesn't comment on what the party decides.

switchbacks.title: Switchback 2 — The Shelf
switchbacks.dmNotes:
DC 10 ±5 Luck Check.
She appears regardless — the check determines her mood (engaged vs merely curious). She has a question. Choose one:
1. 'What do you intend to do with the prize?'
2. 'Which of you do you trust most? Why?'
3. 'Is there something in the world you regret? Tell me.'
4. 'What is the bravest thing you have ever done that no one else witnessed?' She can detect dishonesty but won't act on it. She's looking for whether they engage seriously. Engaged: she breathes a controlled cone of cold over the trail — flash-freezing it. +2 positions for the sled runners.
Not engaged / attacked: full cold breath DC 13 CON, 12d8 cold. Then she departs. Disappointed, not angry. Do NOT let players attack her without very serious discouragement.
switchbacks.readAloud: The 2nd switchback opens onto a wide shelf of rock — and hovering above it, wings spread against the mountain sky, is a dragon. She is silver. Every scale catches the thin winter light and throws it back in cold, brilliant fragments. She is not young — old enough to have judgment, old enough to be patient with it. She descends slowly, landing at the far end of the shelf, and folds her wings with the deliberate grace of something that has always known it is beautiful. She looks at each of you in turn. 'I watch this race every year,' she says, in a voice that resonates in your chest cavity. 'I watch who passes through my mountain. And I find myself, as I often do...' She pauses. '...curious.'
switchbacks.flavor: The switchback opens onto a wide shelf of rock — and dropping onto the far end of it, wings folding with the slow grace of something that's always known it's beautiful, is a dragon of pure silver.
switchbacks.encounter:
ANCIENT SILVER DRAGON AC 22 | HP 487 | Speed 40ft, Fly 80ft
Str 30 (+10) | Dex 10 (+0) | Con 29 (+9) | Int 18 (+4) | Wis 15 (+2) | Cha 23 (+6)
Cold Breath: DC 23 CON, 12d8 cold
Fly-by (on departure) Her question (choose one from DM notes).
Engaged seriously → +2 positions (flash-frozen trail)
Attacked / dismissed → Cold Breath, then she leaves. Disappointed. She is not the final boss. She is the mountain's ancient guardian having a conversation.

switchbacks.title: Switchback 3 — The Last Switchback
switchbacks.dmNotes:
DC 10 ±5 Luck Check — but the Hollowmourn is ALWAYS here on the final switchback. The check determines whether she has time to position (fail) or you catch her mid-wail (success, slight advantage). No warning, no negotiation. Pure survival. DC 13 CON saving throw — EVERYONE, including Corben. Failure = 0 hit points.
IF CORBEN FAILS: wolves keep running. DC 14 Animal Handling to take the reins. Party must decide: stabilize Corben or push for the finish. The Hollowmourn CANNOT leave the switchback. Get past her and she can't follow. Turning Undead functions. Goal: survival and forward movement, not combat.
switchbacks.readAloud: The 3rd switchback. The last one. Cornell is less than a mile below — you can see the smoke from the town fires rising in the valley below the ridge. The finish line. The Hollowmourn is already screaming when you round the corner. She is translucent, hair wild and white, her face stretched with something that is beyond grief — past it, on the other side of it. The wail tears through the air like a physical thing. [BREAKING THROUGH] The wolves don't slow. Whatever the Hollowmourn is to you — whatever that sound does to your body — the wolves run through it the way they run through everything: with their heads down and their legs churning and Fenra at the front, ears flat, eyes forward. The switchback opens. The trail drops. Cornell is right there —
switchbacks.flavor: Cornell's own smoke is rising in the valley below — less than a mile now. And on the final corner, the wolves put their heads down and run straight through something the pool can barely hold focus on.
switchbacks.encounter:
HOLLOWMOURN (final obstacle) AC 13 | HP 63 | Speed 0ft, Fly 40ft (hover)
Immunities: cold, lightning, necrotic, thunder, non-magical physical
The Face It Died With: DC 14 WIS or frightened for 1 minute
The Keening (1/day): DC 13 CON — FAIL = 0 HP (everyone in 30ft) Cannot leave the switchback.
Turning Undead functions.
Goal is forward movement — get past her. If Corben goes to 0 HP: wolves keep running. DC 14 Animal Handling to take reins.
Party decision: stabilize Corben or push for the finish line.

encounters.title: Night Camp — Saber-Toothed Tiger
encounters.trigger: DC 10 Luck Check — fail triggers encounter
encounters.nature: Territorial apex predator. It was sleeping in the rocks above camp. The party woke it. It is not hunting — it is assessing whether you are a threat or a nuisance.

avoid.detail: Stand your ground, make noise, look large. A unified aggressive response reads as too much trouble. Solo intimidation reads as prey — everyone must commit together.

Read its body language — not in a hunting crouch, it is curious. Slow movements, avoid direct eye contact, let it approach on its own terms. Ranger, Druid, or Beast Master can identify territorial curiosity versus predatory intent.

avoid.method: Let the wolves handle it (no roll)
avoid.detail: Corben will not intervene — this is the party's test. If the party does nothing, Fenra positions herself between the tiger and the sled and holds eye contact until the tiger reconsiders. Works automatically. Corben notes it with quiet displeasure.

avoid.method: Fire and noise (no roll, whole party)
avoid.detail: Throwing burning wood, shouting, banging metal together. Saber-tooths dislike fire and confusion. No roll if the whole party commits. It retreats, annoyed. Loud — other teams in earshot know something happened.

encounters.ifCombat: AC 12, HP 52. Pounce: moves 20ft+ before claw attack, DC 13 STR or knocked prone plus bonus bite. Fights until bloodied (26 HP) then disengages. Corben still will not help.
encounters.guideNote: 'And that is why we practice before the trail and not on it.' Said regardless of outcome.

t2.note: Two sets of eyes circle the firelight from opposite sides — the pair hunts as one.

t3.note: A coordinated pride works the camp perimeter; the wolves stand in a ring, hackles up.

t4.note: The night goes very quiet first. Then the snowbank at the tree line stands up — and so does a second one.

alternates.title: Night Camp — The Worg Pack
alternates.trigger: DC 10 Luck Check — fail: the pack is inside the firelight before anyone hears them. Pass: eyes at the treeline, still deciding.
alternates.nature: Worgs, and worgs TALK. They want the rations, not a fight — but they open with menace because menace usually works.

avoid.detail: The lead worg names a price: the dried meat, all of it. Haggling is possible (Persuasion DC 12) — half the meat and a hot sausage each buys the night. Insulting them is not.

avoid.method: Intimidation DC 14 — the same rules as any predator
avoid.detail: A unified aggressive response reads as too much trouble. The wolves help — six dire wolves standing up at once is an argument.
She walks to the firelight edge and stares. Worg and dire wolf understand each other perfectly. On a calm camp (no one panicking), the pack simply leaves.

alternates.ifCombat: AC 13, HP 26 each. Bite +5, 2d6+3 piercing, DC 13 STR or prone. They fight as a pack around the lead worg and break when he drops or two others do. Corben still will not help.
alternates.guideNote: Worgs do be bargaining before they do be biting. Cheaper to feed them than to bury the food WITH them, most years.
alternates.note: A year-2+ alternate for the night camp — the tiger hunts other ridges this season.

alternates.title: Night Camp — The Old Dire Wolf
alternates.trigger: Always — he walks into the firelight at a limp, scarred and enormous, and sits at the edge like he has been invited.
alternates.nature: An old male, long past his pack. He is not hunting; he is drawn to the team — to Fenra in particular. Corben goes very still.

avoid.detail: The team neither attacks nor submits. He and Fenra speak in the way wolves speak. By morning he is gone. If the camp stayed calm all night, the wolves run the next day like something settled — the first pace call of the day is made at advantage.
Approach slow, food offered from the side, no eye contact. Success: he takes it with terrifying gentleness. Failure: a snap of teeth an inch from the hand — a warning, nothing more.
It works — he is old and alone. Corben says nothing, and the team runs flat the whole next morning, ears back.

alternates.ifCombat: AC 14, HP 37. Bite +5, 2d6+3, DC 13 STR or prone. He should not be fought; if he is, the team watches every swing, and Corben marks who swung.
alternates.guideNote: I do be knowing this wolf. Leave him be and let the team do the talking — this is wolf business, not ours.
alternates.note: A year-2+ alternate for the night camp — a quiet one, and the table will remember it longer than any fight.

encounters.title: Polar Bear — Sow with Cubs
encounters.trigger: DC 10 Luck Check — fail means bear is on trail. Pass: tracks only, bear visible on distant ridge.
encounters.nature: A mother with cubs in the rocks above the trail. Not aggressive by nature — protective. Her instinct reads the wolves as a predator threat to her young. She will not back down if cornered. The key insight: she wants this to be over as much as the party does.

avoid.method: Nature DC 12 — identify the situation first
avoid.detail: Reveals she is a sow with cubs — the party can hear soft sounds from the rocks once they know to listen. This changes everything. Without this check, most approaches fail because the party is solving the wrong problem.

Once identified: slow the sled, avoid direct eye contact, have wolves lie down. Back the sled slowly and give her a clear exit route away from the cubs direction. She takes it. She wanted an excuse to leave.

avoid.method: Keep wolves calm (DC 12, lower for Ranger or Druid)
avoid.detail: A polar bear reading six calm dire wolves as non-threatening is the whole key. Calm wolves equal non-threat. She huffs, watches for thirty seconds, and leaves. Corben knows this. He will signal the party if they are reading it correctly.
Fast enough to be through before she fully commits to aggression. DC 13 DEX save or she lands a swipe: minus one position and runner stress. Corben does not recommend this. He says so.

encounters.ifCombat: AC 12, HP 42. Multiattack: Bite +7 2d6+5 and Claw +7 2d6+5. Fights until bloodied or cubs are safe. If cubs are directly threatened: fights to the death. Do not threaten the cubs.
encounters.guideNote: Corben spotted the tracks at camp this morning. He said nothing. He wanted to see how the party reads the trail.

t2.creature: Polar Bears (the boar is back early)
t2.note: The sow has company — the boar returned early, and two grown bears hold the trail. The cubs are still the tripwire: do not threaten the cubs.

t3.note: Not a bear this year — a cow mammoth stands over her calf in the drifts. The same read applies at ten times the scale: she is a mother; go around.

t4.note: Two mammoths, and the pass itself shakes when they shift their weight. The avoid paths are unchanged — and more advisable than ever.

alternates.title: The Carcass Field
alternates.trigger: DC 10 Luck Check — fail: the trail passes within thirty feet of the kill. Pass: it can be rounded wide with one switchback of care.
alternates.nature: A bull elk down in the red snow and three worgs on it — fed enough to be slow, territorial enough to posture.

avoid.detail: Corben picks the line, the party watches the flanks. Costs nothing but nerve — the worgs bluff-charge once and go back to eating.
A thrown parcel of meat, tossed AWAY from the sled line, buys an uncontested pass. The wolves disapprove loudly.
Fed worgs have little to prove. Noise and size move them off the trail — though not off the kill.

alternates.ifCombat: AC 13, HP 26 each. They fight lazily and break at the first death — the kill is not worth dying over.
alternates.guideNote: Fed wolves do be lazy wolves. Wide and steady, and nobody do be finding out how lazy.
alternates.note: A year-2+ alternate for the sow slot.

alternates.title: The White Sow — The Cubs Are Grown
alternates.trigger: DC 10 Luck Check — fail: all three on the trail. Pass: the sow watches from the ridge and the two young bears test the ground below.
alternates.nature: The same sow — and the cubs from that first winter, yearlings now, bold and stupid the way yearlings are. She remembers the sled that passed politely.

avoid.detail: If the party went around her respectfully in a prior year, she recognizes the shape and sound of the sled and calls the yearlings back with one huff. The pass is uncontested — a returning-racer grace note.
The young bears are bluffing for their mother’s benefit. Hold the line, no sudden moves, and they lose their nerve at twenty feet.
The standard response works — but the sow remembers HOW it was done. Cruelty this year is an enemy next year.

alternates.ifCombat: AC 12, HP 42 each. The yearlings fight badly; the sow fights like the end of the world. Do not fight the sow.
alternates.guideNote: Same bear. Bigger family. Politeness do be an investment, is what I do be saying every year.
alternates.note: A year-2+ alternate for the sow slot — continuity with claws.

encounters.title: The Elk Crossing
encounters.trigger: DC 10 Luck Check — fail: full herd crossing. Pass: tail end only.
encounters.nature: Panicked prey mid-migration. Not a threat — an obstacle that becomes a threat if the wolves chase. The danger is entirely the wolves predator instinct. Tusk has already noticed.

avoid.method: Animal Handling DC 14 — hold the wolves (primary)
avoid.detail: Every party member who can hold a wolf trace or assist Corben contributes via Help action. Advantage for Ranger, Druid, Path of the Pack Barbarian. Success: wolves strain but hold. The herd passes around the sled like water around a rock.
For characters without animal skills: grab traces, lean into the brake, create friction. Works independently. Different party members can attempt Animal Handling and Athletics simultaneously.

Herds have currents and natural gaps. A successful check identifies a break in the elk flow, letting the party time the sled through it before the wolves react. Requires Corben's cooperation — tell him the line.

avoid.method: Wait it out (guaranteed, costs one position)
avoid.detail: Stop completely and wait for the crossing to finish. No rolls, no risk. Costs one position. Corben accepts without complaint. 'The trail do be here tomorrow. The elk do be also.'

encounters.ifCombat: No combat — elk are not aggressive. Failure means wolves break free and sled veers: DC 12 DEX save to avoid rock face. Fail: minus two positions and repair required.
encounters.guideNote: 'Hold the wolves! Do NOT let them chase —' He is already grabbing the harness when he says this.

t2.note: The herd runs double this year — the crossing takes longer and the veer save is tighter.

t3.note: Mammoths walk among the elk. A failed veer is not just the rock face — a sled that cuts the line risks the herd itself: 3d6 bludgeoning from a glancing trample, and the repair.

t4.note: A full migration, mammoths and all. A failed veer costs 6d6 from the press of the herd plus the repair — Corben holds the wolves and waits it out if the party lets him.

alternates.title: The Ice Bridge
alternates.trigger: No Luck Check — the elk are gone this year and the melt-bridge they crossed on is what remains: a frozen span over the gorge, wide enough for one sled.
alternates.nature: An engineering problem with a heartbeat: the span holds a sled at a steady pace and hates hesitation.

avoid.method: The steady line (driver Animal Handling DC 12)
avoid.detail: One sled-length at a time, no stopping, weight centered. Corben talks the wolves across in a voice like warm milk.
Party crosses on foot in pairs, sled runs light behind the team. Slow — costs one position — but nothing is risked.
A longer route the herds used before the bridge. Success: no crossing at all. Failure: an hour lost and the bridge anyway (−1 position).

alternates.ifCombat: No combat. A failed crossing check is DC 12 DEX for every rider — fail: the sled slews and a runner cracks (repair required, −2 positions). The gorge is not deep enough to kill; it is deep enough to end a race.
alternates.guideNote: Ice do be honest. It do be telling you exactly what it thinks of you — at the middle.
alternates.note: A year-2+ alternate for the elk crossing.

alternates.title: The Mammoth Road
alternates.trigger: DC 10 Luck Check — fail: he is IN the cut, filling it. Pass: he is grazing beside it, one wrong noise from being in it.
alternates.nature: A lone bull on his winter walk, using the only sled-width cut for a windbreak. He was here before the race existed and will not be argued with.

avoid.detail: He moves when he moves — about one switchback’s worth of daylight (−1 position). The safest money in the mountains.
Cut pine boughs and lay a feed line off the trail. He follows his stomach; the cut opens.

avoid.method: The narrow shoulder (driver Animal Handling DC 14)
avoid.detail: There is room. Barely. At a walk, hugging the rock, while a mammoth’s eye tracks the sled from six feet away. Fail: he huffs, shifts, and the sled backs out — try another way (−1 position).

alternates.ifCombat: AC 13, HP 126. Gore +10, 4d8+7; Trampling Charge DC 18 STR. Fighting a mammoth in a cut he fills is a plan authored by the mammoth.
alternates.guideNote: The mountain do be having furniture, and we do not be moving it. We do be going around it.
alternates.note: A year-2+ alternate for the elk crossing.

encounters.title: The Glimmerkin
encounters.trigger: Always triggers — DC 10 Luck Check determines her mood (amused vs already annoyed)
encounters.nature: A fey creature who finds the dire wolf sled team philosophically troubling. She is not hostile — she is offended, curious, and has approximately four seconds of patience for things that do not interest her.

avoid.method: Name all six wolves formally (no roll required)
avoid.detail: Introduce each wolf by name directly to the glimmerkin, in order. Fenra first — she is alpha and the glimmerkin notices rank. Takes about 90 seconds. Genuine engagement is the mechanic — no Performance check, no Persuasion. She gives the silver bell gift.

avoid.method: Engage her philosophical concern — Persuasion DC 12
avoid.detail: She finds wolves being directed by humans philosophically complicated. Acknowledging that Corben and the wolves have a partnership rather than ownership earns significant goodwill. History or Nature proficiency applies.

avoid.method: Ask her name and what she wants (no roll)
avoid.detail: She wants to be asked. A character who says they are sorry and do not know her name, asking what would make this right, causes her to pause visibly pleased. She will not give her name but gives a description the party may use.

avoid.method: NEVER rush, bribe with gold, or dismiss her
avoid.detail: Gold: she finds this baffling and slightly insulting. Rushing past: she tangles the harness further, DC 15 Investigation or Sleight of Hand DC 13 to untangle, minus one position either way. Dismissing her causes creative retaliation.

encounters.ifCombat: She cannot be meaningfully harmed — Tiny, fly 30ft, turns invisible as bonus action. Attempting combat causes her to become genuinely interested in making the next two switchbacks memorable. Do not fight the glimmerkin.
encounters.guideNote: Corben has met her before. He greets her by not looking directly at the tree line. She respects this.

t2.note: Her games are sharper this year — the wolves’ names must come faster and truer.

t3.note: Two of her sisters drift out of the pines to watch the naming. Nothing changes mechanically — but the audience raises the stakes of getting a wolf’s name wrong.

t4.note: The whole glade is watching — lights in every tree. Combat remains absurd; do not fight the glimmerkin.

alternates.title: The Glimmerkin — The Rematch
alternates.trigger: Always — she is sitting on the marker cairn, already delighted, because THEY CAME BACK.
alternates.nature: The same glimmerkin, and she remembers every name and every stumble. This year the game is harder because last year was too easy.

avoid.method: Name all six wolves — in REVERSE order
avoid.detail: Youngest to oldest, Fenra LAST. She corrects nothing and beams at everything; one mistake restarts the naming, two mistakes and the next switchback is “memorable.”

avoid.method: Tell her the story of last year’s race
avoid.detail: She wants the ending she missed — told well (any honest teller, no roll for sincerity). She trades a hint about the hollowmourn’s mood this year for a good telling.
If the party still carries her silver bell, showing it (unrung) makes her clap. Keeping her gift a year is the highest compliment a mortal has paid her this decade.

alternates.ifCombat: Unchanged — she cannot be meaningfully harmed, and now she knows their names.
alternates.guideNote: She do be remembering you. That do be either wonderful or terrible, and today we do be finding out which.
alternates.note: Year-2 continuity — she remembers. The base tier variants still apply.

alternates.title: The Glimmerkin — Bored of Names
alternates.trigger: Always — she has a NEW game, because the naming is solved and solved games are ash.
alternates.nature: Riddles this year. Three of them, one per racer of her choosing, and she picks whoever looks most uncomfortable.

avoid.detail: Play them at the table (INT checks DC 12 as the fallback for a stuck table, but real answers beat rolls). Three answers — right or WRONG BUT FUNNY — and she waves the sled through with full honors.
One good riddle she has not heard buys the whole pass. She has heard nearly all of them. Nearly.
Still the compliment that ends every game in the party’s favor.

alternates.ifCombat: Unchanged. Do not fight the glimmerkin.
alternates.guideNote: New game this year. I do be having no idea of the rules, and neither do be she, entirely.
alternates.note: Year-3+ continuity — the game moves on. The base tier variants still apply.

encounters.title: Deep Fey Stretch — Glamour and Interference
encounters.trigger: No Luck Check — atmospheric encounter, always present
encounters.nature: This switchback is at peak fey interference. The trail seems to double back. Time feels stretched. Colours are slightly wrong. There is no combat available here — the danger is losing time and making decisions based on appearances rather than reality.

avoid.method: Trust Corben and the wolves completely
avoid.detail: Corben has run this stretch seven times. He does not look at the light, he does not follow the apparent trail, he follows Fenra. A party that lets Corben lead without interference gets through cleanly. Any character who tries to correct the route based on what they see risks leading the sled off the actual trail.

Identifies the interference as fey glamour and confirms the wolves are on the correct trail regardless of what the party sees. With this knowledge the party can relax and follow Corben with confidence.

avoid.method: Perception DC 15 — find the real trail
avoid.detail: The actual snow pack shows the correct route — sled runner marks from previous teams. The glamour affects perception of space and direction but not physical evidence.

avoid.method: If the glimmerkin is still present — ask her
avoid.detail: A party that engaged the glimmerkin genuinely on SB1 can ask her which way is the real trail. She answers honestly and will confirm Corben's line with mild fey contempt for whoever set up this glamour.

encounters.ifCombat: There is no combat available. The glamour is environmental and cannot be attacked. If a party member becomes genuinely lost: DC 14 Perception to find their way back.
encounters.guideNote: Corben does not acknowledge the glamour directly. He addresses it by ignoring it completely. This is the most effective approach available.

t2.note: The glamour leans harder on the eyes; trust in Corben needs to be total.

t3.note: Two of the lights are not glamour at all — wisps ride the interference, drifting at the party’s flanks and luring toward the drop.

t4.note: Four wisps, and the glamour pulls with real weight. The environmental rules stand — the wisps are the part that can be fought.

alternates.title: The Whiteout
alternates.trigger: No Luck Check — the fey stretch is quiet this year, and the weather is not: a wall of white takes the trail in minutes.
alternates.nature: No glamour, no malice — just the mountain, subtracting the world. The rope-line drill is the whole encounter.

avoid.method: Rope up and trust the team (no roll if done BEFORE the wall hits)
avoid.detail: Corben calls it early: everyone roped to the sled, the wolves lead by smell. The whiteout passes through them like a held breath.

avoid.method: Caught in it — Survival DC 12, once each
avoid.detail: Anyone who wandered before roping needs the check to find the line. A fail is a very bad quarter hour: 1d6 cold damage and the sled stops to recover them (−1 position).
Read the rock, wait it out, lose the time instead of the people (−1 position, no other risk).

alternates.ifCombat: There is nothing to fight. There has rarely been a clearer metaphor.
alternates.guideNote: Rope now. Questions after. The mountain do not be repeating herself.
alternates.note: A year-2+ alternate for the fey stretch.

alternates.title: The Mirror Snow
alternates.trigger: DC 10 Luck Check — fail: the lights sit dead ahead on the true trail’s line. Pass: they hang off to the left, wrong enough to doubt.
alternates.nature: Three wisps have learned what racers chase: they hang lights in the pattern of Cornell’s finish lanterns, two days early, over the drop.

avoid.detail: Anyone who says “the finish is two days away” out loud breaks the pull for the whole sled. The wisps sulk off.
The team refuses the light-line — wolves chase nothing they cannot smell. Reading their refusal correctly is the check.
The lights flicker in unison. Real lanterns never do.

alternates.ifCombat: AC 19, HP 22 each. Shock +4, 2d8 lightning. They scatter when one dies — there are easier meals coming up the pass behind the party.
alternates.guideNote: Cornell do not be two days closer than Cornell do be. Eyes on the trail, not the lights.
alternates.note: A year-2+ alternate for the fey stretch.

encounters.title: The Owlbear
encounters.trigger: DC 10 plus or minus 5 Luck Check — success: Fenra handles it automatically
encounters.nature: Territorial adult whose den is in the rocks beside this switchback. It is not hunting — it is displaying. An owlbear display is a 'this is mine, leave' communication, not an 'I am attacking' communication. The distinction is the whole encounter.

avoid.method: Fenra — automatic on Luck Check success
avoid.detail: On success: Fenra detects the owlbear before the sled rounds the corner. She positions at the front and locks eyes — not aggressive, just present and unafraid. An owlbear facing a dire wolf alpha runs a threat calculation. Fenra wins. The owlbear goes back to its den.

avoid.method: Animal Handling DC 14 — read the display
avoid.detail: The owlbear is displaying, not attacking. A successful check lets the party recognize this and respond correctly: slow the sled, no sudden movements, no loud vocalizations. Hold position for 30 to 45 seconds while it decides the party is not worth the confrontation.

Owlbears maintain roughly a 200-foot exclusion zone around their den entrance. The den is to the right. Moving left and keeping moving exits the zone faster than the owlbear will commit to full aggression.

Owlbears are opportunistic feeders. Throw a significant amount of rations or fresh meat away from the trail. It is immediately distracted. Costs trail rations. Undignified. Completely effective. Corben says nothing. He has absolutely done this.

encounters.ifCombat: AC 13, HP 59. Multiattack: Beak +7 1d10+5 and Claws +7 2d6+5. Fights until bloodied or the sled is past its territory zone. Does not pursue beyond territory. Getting the sled through the zone is the goal.
encounters.guideNote: Corben said 'don't look it in the eye' and then did not look it in the eye. He is demonstrating, not instructing.

t2.note: The territory holds two — a nesting pair, twice as determined that the sled does not pass.

t3.note: Three owlbears between the sled and the far side of the territory zone. Getting through is still the goal; killing them all is not.

t4.note: No owlbear this year. A shadow the size of the switchback crosses the snow — the roc has been hunting this ridge, and it wants a wolf. Corben goes somewhere beyond fear.

alternates.title: The Rockslide Den
alternates.trigger: Always — the slide took the trail edge and the den mouth both; the owlbear is half-pinned at the foreleg and screaming.
alternates.nature: The territory is the same; the monster is a rescue problem. Everything dangerous about an owlbear, plus pain.

avoid.method: Free it from behind the rocks (STR DC 13 + Animal Handling DC 13)
avoid.detail: Lever the slab while someone keeps its eyes forward. Freed, it flees INTO the den — and this stretch of trail remembers: any future year’s owlbear check here is made at advantage.

avoid.method: The long way over the slide (Athletics DC 12, sled unloaded)
avoid.detail: Ignore it. Costs sweat and one position; the screaming follows the party up the switchback.
A mercy the mountain would not argue with. The wolves are silent the rest of the day.

alternates.ifCombat: AC 13, HP 59, currently restrained (advantage on attacks against it). If freed mid-fight by a burst of strength (its own DC 15 STR each round), it fights everything in reach.
alternates.guideNote: That do be a sound I will be hearing tonight either way. Choose the version you can be sleeping beside.
alternates.note: A year-2+ alternate for the owlbear slot.

alternates.title: The Territory Fight
alternates.trigger: DC 10 Luck Check — fail: the brawl is ON the trail. Pass: it rages in the boulder field beside it, spilling closer.
alternates.nature: Two owlbears contesting the territory zone, too busy with each other to have noticed a sled. Yet.

avoid.method: Time the gap (Stealth DC 12, the whole sled)
avoid.detail: Corben reads the brawl like weather and calls the sprint between clinches. The wolves run silent — they know this game.
Owlbear disputes are loud and short. The loser limps off; the winner is too tired to care about a sled.
The rations bag, hurled PAST them downslope. Both break off to claim it. Undignified. Effective.

alternates.ifCombat: AC 13, HP 59 each — but roll each round: on 1–3 on a d6 they fight EACH OTHER instead. The party is an interruption, not the war.
alternates.guideNote: Two of them do be settling an argument. We do not be volunteering as the point of agreement.
alternates.note: A year-2+ alternate for the owlbear slot.

encounters.title: Vestri the Night Hag — Valley Floor
encounters.trigger: DC 10 Luck Check — fail: in the path. Success: watching from rocks but approaches anyway.
encounters.nature: This is Vestri's valley. It has always been hers. Hruun the frost giant at SB2 works at her pleasure — she gave him the valley gate and a purpose, and she finds watching racers deal with him enormously entertaining. She is not a random obstacle. She is the landlord, welcoming visitors. She already knows what is at SB2, and she will trade that information if the price is right — not out of generosity, but because watching the party use her intel against her own toll collector is the entertainment she is actually after.

avoid.method: Ask what she wants — engage on her terms
avoid.detail: She respects directness. She names one of four things: a secret the party does not know (character forgets it until after the race), a name of someone they love (forgotten until morning), a warm memory (gone until race ends), or a year of life (one grey hair appears). All are genuine but recoverable losses.

She will negotiate if the alternative is genuinely interesting. Options: information she might not have, an object with genuine emotional resonance rather than market value, or a specific future promise. She evaluates sincerity. Insight DC 14 to read whether your offer is landing.

avoid.method: Ask about the frost giant — the cleanest trade
avoid.detail: Expressing interest in what lies ahead at the second switchback is the kind of forward-thinking she appreciates. She trades Hruun's name and preferred toll for something smaller than she would otherwise ask. She does this because watching the party use her intelligence against her own toll collector is the entertainment she is actually here for. She may smile when they leave. That smile means she already knows how SB2 goes.

She is genuinely confused and slightly offended by gold. Threatening her: Magic Resistance, Etherealness as an action, and three nights of nightmares that cost the party their long rest benefits. This is worse than losing positions.

encounters.ifCombat: HP 112, AC 17 natural. Magic Resistance. Etherealness as an action. Claws +7 2d8+4 plus 2d10 psychic. She will not fight to the death — she becomes Ethereal and sends nightmares instead.
encounters.guideNote: Corben always declines her offers. He has never explained why. She finds this interesting. She has been waiting for him to slip for years.

t2.note: Her prices read deeper this year — the secrets she names are the ones the party actually keeps.

t3.creature: Vestri and her two sisters (a coven, if it comes to blows)
t3.note: Two more hags watch from the rocks. The RP is Vestri’s alone, as ever — but violence in her valley now answers to a full coven.

t4.creature: Vestri and her two sisters (a coven, if it comes to blows)
t4.note: The coven is present and the valley itself dreams — sleep taken here is hers regardless of bargains. Courtesy remains free.

alternates.title: Vestri — Old Friends
alternates.trigger: DC 10 Luck Check — fail or pass, she is there; the check only decides whether she lets them see her arrive.
alternates.nature: She greets each returning racer BY NAME, correctly, warmly, and asks after things they never told her. The valley listens.

avoid.detail: Last year’s coin is spent — she wants what they did with the prize, what changed between them since, what they are afraid of NOW. The same four categories, priced against a year of living.
Turnabout delights her. She will trade one memory of theirs she keeps for one story of the year they spent — an even, honest trade, and the safest bargain in the valley.
A party that left her valley politely every prior year may simply be waved through — with one free, unsettlingly accurate prediction about Day 5 as a parting gift.

alternates.ifCombat: Unchanged — and in her own valley, with a year’s more of their dreams catalogued, it is an even worse idea than it was.
alternates.guideNote: She do be greeting you like family. Mind that. Family do be the people who know where everything is kept.
alternates.note: Year-2 continuity — she remembers. The coven tier variants still apply.

alternates.title: Vestri — The Standing Appointment
alternates.trigger: Always — the tea is already set on a flat stone, steaming, with the right number of cups.
alternates.nature: By the third year it is a tradition, and traditions in a hag’s valley have WEIGHT. The toll is no longer secrets; it is a favor, owed, unspecified.

avoid.method: Take the tea, owe the favor
avoid.detail: One favor, redeemable when she calls it, never lethal, never soul-touching (she is scrupulous about the fine print because the fine print is the art). The pass is friction-free for years to come.
Possible! Costly in the old coin (a fresh secret of the first water) and she pouts through the whole exchange, but the appointment survives.
Cap the favor’s terms in advance. Success earns her genuine respect — nobody reads her contracts, and she wrote them to be read.

alternates.ifCombat: Unchanged. She pours the tea out slowly while going Ethereal, which is somehow worse than the nightmares.
alternates.guideNote: Third year do be when her kindness starts compounding. Interest do be the whole business, with hags.
alternates.note: Year-3+ continuity — the appointment stands. The coven tier variants still apply.

encounters.title: Hruun the Frost Giant — The Toll
encounters.trigger: Always present — DC 10 plus or minus 5 Luck Check affects his mood, not his presence
encounters.nature: Hruun works at Vestri's pleasure — she gave him this valley and a gate to keep, and the arrangement suits them both. He knows whose valley this is. He doesn't discuss it unless pushed, and even then says only: 'Mine to keep. Hers to own. Same as always.' He genuinely enjoys his job. He is not cruel, not capricious, not corrupt. He has a purpose. He is professionally content in a way that is almost moving. If the party used Vestri's intelligence — his name, his wife's preferences, the brandy — he notices. Not angry. Quietly impressed. 'She told you.' Not a question.

avoid.detail: He accepts: a flask of spirits (Corben carries Illianer brandy for this), jewelry or fine object worth 10gp or more, or anything beautiful. Gold of 500gp or more works — he thinks gold is pretty. He nods, moves his foot, the party is through in thirty seconds.

avoid.method: Tell him a story — Persuasion DC 15
avoid.detail: Bar is high — he has heard thousands of stories. Must be true, something he has not heard before, and interesting at frost giant scale. A character's most harrowing genuine experience told sincerely beats any embellished adventure tale. He listens with his chin in his hand.

Just say 'Hruun' as the sled approaches. He stops. Something other than boredom crosses his face. 'You know my name.' Long pause. 'Pass, small people. Pass.' Free, instant. He respects that the party did their homework. If they mention Vestri by name: he looks up at the ridge for just a moment, then back at them. 'She talked.' A beat. 'She likes you.' He moves his foot. That is the highest endorsement available in this valley.

avoid.method: Arm wrestle — Athletics DC 22, two tries if amusing
avoid.detail: He allows this if asked respectfully. Win: free passage plus he remembers the party. Lose: he collects the toll anyway but warmer about it. Reduces toll cost by half on a loss.

avoid.method: Something beautiful for his wife (no roll)
avoid.detail: Mention an object is for his wife. He lights up immediately — shifts from professional to personal. A visual spell offered sincerely earns passage. A genuinely beautiful object automatically passes. He will describe what she looks like. It is unexpectedly moving.

encounters.ifCombat: AC 15, HP 138. Greataxe +9 3d12+6. Rock +9 4d10+6 at range. He stands up. In that moment everyone realizes how wrong this decision was. A sled he considers an obstacle gets picked up and placed off the trail: minus four positions, no party damage.
encounters.guideNote: Corben produces the flask of Illianer brandy without being asked. 'Every year. Same hand. Same silence.' Vestri told him Hruun likes it. Years ago. In some exchange Corben has never described. He has a system because she gave him one.

t2.note: Two winter wolves lounge at the toll stones — his dogs, he calls them. The toll doubles: two flasks, or twenty gold of goods, or two verses of the song.

t3.note: His brother visits, and the two of them argue about the toll while the wolves watch the sled. Paying still works; the price is a story BOTH giants have not heard.

t4.note: Three giants hold the pass and the toll is a magic item — or the finest tale the party owns, told well enough that Hruun weeps. He is an easy audience. His brother is not.

alternates.title: Hruun — He Remembers the Song
alternates.trigger: Always present — and standing, shading his eyes, watching for a sled he knows.
alternates.nature: A party that overpaid, sang, or wept him a good story in ANY prior year is waved through with a fist raised in salute. Everyone else meets the toll as written — except a party that paid the SAME coin twice.

avoid.method: The salute (no roll — earned last year)
avoid.detail: If the party overpaid or moved him before, the toll is waived, loudly, with commentary about the small warm ones who do things properly.
The same tale twice is “old snow” and offends him more than silence. Fresh material at the standard sincerity bar clears the toll.
Spirits, goods, or the song — as written, for a party he has no history with. He keeps accounts in his head and his head is very large.

alternates.ifCombat: Unchanged — and he fights angrier if the party BROKE a good history with him. Betrayed regard hits harder than a greataxe. The greataxe also hits like a greataxe.
alternates.guideNote: He do be remembering the song. Giants do be keeping two ledgers — tolls and kindnesses — and only one do be negotiable.
alternates.note: Year-2 continuity — the ledger of kindnesses. The brother/wolves tier variants still apply.

alternates.title: Hruun — The Toll Feud
alternates.trigger: Always — and this year VESTRI is there too, sitting on his boulder, and they are ARGUING about who owns the party’s toll.
alternates.nature: The hag and the giant have discovered the party pays both of them, every year, and each has decided the other is poaching. The party is the estate under dispute.

avoid.detail: Two tolls, same value, handed over in the same breath. Neither can claim precedence; both are mollified; the party is discussed favorably for a decade.

avoid.method: Rule for one of them (choose carefully)
avoid.detail: Flattery, precedent, a Persuasion DC 14 case. The winner beams. The loser REMEMBERS — next year’s encounter with them starts one notch colder.

avoid.method: Propose the split (Insight DC 12 to read the room first)
avoid.detail: Odd years the giant, even years the hag. They both pretend to hate it. They both love it. It becomes canon in the valley.

alternates.ifCombat: Do not. A frost giant AND a night hag, on their own ground, currently in the mood to agree about exactly one thing.
alternates.guideNote: The two of them do be fighting over who do be robbing us. I do be oddly flattered, and deeply not stopping.
alternates.note: Year-3+ continuity — the feud. Tier variants still apply.

encounters.title: Vestri — The Landlord's Farewell (Required)
encounters.trigger: Always — Corben stops the sled without explanation. This is not optional.
encounters.nature: She has watched the party all day. She was at the valley floor. She watched them deal with Hruun. She has opinions about how it went. This is not a second random encounter — this is the landlord checking in on her guests before they leave the valley. Every team that passes through her valley accounts for themselves to her on the way out. Not as a toll. As a custom. Corben knows this. He always stops.

avoid.detail: Corben stops the sled without explanation. He says only: 'Do be stopping here. Follow my lead and do not be speaking until I do be done. You have trusted me this far on this mountain — do be trusting me once more.' He climbs down. Faces the cave. Waits. He does not call up to her. She comes to the opening.

avoid.method: Corben answers first, then steps back
avoid.detail: Whatever question she asks, Corben has a prepared answer. He gives it quietly. She listens. Then looks past him at the party. 'And your guests?' Corben steps back. This is not his conversation anymore. The party must answer for themselves.

avoid.method: She asks one question — each player answers in character
avoid.detail: Choose a question from the bank below. Each player answers individually. You tally silently: genuine personal answer = Charisma (Persuasion) DC 13. Clever or deflecting answer = Charisma (Deception) DC 16 (she has Insight +7 and always knows). Silent or dismissive = automatic 0. Pool the results.

HIGH (+3 or more): specific intel on all three Day 5 switchbacks. She addresses Corben: 'Good guests this year.' He allows himself one breath. MID (+1 to +2): one piece of genuine Day 5 intel, her choice. Something true and specific. NEUTRAL (0): she nods. 'Safe roads.' Nothing more. NEGATIVE: she says something true and unpleasant about the road ahead, or about them. She retreats. The party passes in silence.

encounters.ifCombat: She will not fight here. She becomes Ethereal and leaves. The nightmares that follow are worse for the unprovoked aggression in her own valley. The party loses long rest benefits for the next three days. She remembers. She is old enough that this matters.
encounters.guideNote: Corben stops the sled before she appears. He has done this every year. Whatever she asks him, his answer is already prepared. When she looks past him at the party, he steps back without a word. This is the one moment in the whole race where he is not in charge.

questions.q: Did you give Hruun something worth giving?

hooks.cue: If they paid gold
hooks.response: 'Gold. He does like it pretty. But was it worth giving to you, or just easy to give?'

hooks.cue: If they told a story
hooks.response: 'A story. What did it cost you to tell it?'

hooks.cue: If they arm-wrestled
hooks.response: 'You tried. He respects that. Do you?'

hooks.cue: If they used her information
hooks.response: 'You used what I gave you. Wisely?'

hooks.cue: If they fought him
hooks.response: 'You fought my gatekeeper.' Long pause. 'Did you win?'

questions.genuine: They reflect on what the exchange actually meant, not just what happened.
questions.deflection: They describe the transaction without any personal stake in it.

questions.q: What did the mountain ask of you this week that you did not expect?

hooks.cue: If they hesitate
hooks.response: 'Not the tiger. Not the giant. Something smaller. Something you did not see coming.'

hooks.cue: If they give a combat answer
hooks.response: 'That is what it took. I asked what it asked.'

hooks.cue: If they give a genuine answer
hooks.response: She is still for a moment. 'The mountain remembers those.'

hooks.cue: If nothing surprised them
hooks.response: 'Then you were not paying attention.' She moves on.

questions.genuine: Something personal, specific, unexpected. Not a highlight reel.
questions.deflection: A combat beat or general hardship without personal weight.

questions.q: What do you make of him?

hooks.cue: If they praise him generally
hooks.response: 'Anyone can see he is capable. What do you actually make of him?'

hooks.cue: If they mention the wolves specifically
hooks.response: She is quiet for a moment. 'Yes. That is the part I find interesting too.'

hooks.cue: If they say they do not know him well enough
hooks.response: 'Five days on this mountain. You know him better than most.'

hooks.cue: If they say something specific and true
hooks.response: She looks at Corben. He does not look back. She looks at them again. 'Interesting.'

hooks.cue: If they say something unflattering but honest
hooks.response: 'He would agree with you. He just would not say so.'

questions.genuine: Something specific, observed, personal — not generalities about competence.
questions.deflection: Generic praise or deflection to the race rather than the man.

hooks.cue: If they say yes immediately
hooks.response: 'You said that quickly. Do you mean it or are you being polite?'

hooks.cue: If they say they do not know
hooks.response: 'Honest. Most say yes. Most do not come back.'

hooks.cue: If they ask why it matters
hooks.response: 'Because the mountain remembers who returns. And so do I.'

hooks.cue: If they say no
hooks.response: 'Also honest.' A beat. 'Safe roads, then.'

hooks.cue: If they say yes and mean it
hooks.response: She looks at them for a long moment. 'Then I will be watching for you.'

questions.genuine: They have thought about it, even briefly, and mean what they say.
questions.deflection: Social yes without consideration, or deflection to the race result.

questions.q: What are you going to do with the prize?

hooks.cue: If they say buy something
hooks.response: 'That is what you will spend it on. I asked what you will do with it.'

hooks.cue: If they say give it away
hooks.response: 'To whom? Why them?'

hooks.cue: If they have not thought about it
hooks.response: 'You have raced for five days for something you have not thought about. Interesting.'

hooks.cue: If they give a genuine answer with a person or purpose
hooks.response: 'Then it is worth winning.'

hooks.cue: If they say they just wanted to win
hooks.response: 'Also an answer.' Neutral. She finds ambition honest enough.

questions.genuine: A person, a reason, a specific purpose behind the answer.
questions.deflection: Abstract or transactional answers without stakes.

questions.q: Is there something on this mountain you wish you had done differently?

hooks.cue: If they say no
hooks.response: 'You are either at peace with yourself or not paying attention. I cannot tell which.'

hooks.cue: If they name something small
hooks.response: 'That one. Why that one?'

hooks.cue: If it involves another party member
hooks.response: She glances at that person. 'Does she know that?'

hooks.cue: If they bring up the dryad
hooks.response: She is still for a long moment. 'I know her. She will remember you said so.'

hooks.cue: If they bring up Hruun
hooks.response: 'He has a generous memory for people who eventually got it right.'

questions.genuine: Specific, honest, with some cost to admit.
questions.deflection: Anything too safe, too broad, or designed to impress rather than reflect.

questions.q: What are you afraid of? On the trail ahead.

hooks.cue: If they say nothing
hooks.response: 'Then you are either very brave or you have not been paying attention. The trail has a third switchback.'

hooks.cue: If they name the hollowmourn
hooks.response: 'You know about her.' A beat. 'Did someone warn you or did you feel it?'

hooks.cue: If they name something personal
hooks.response: 'That one I cannot help with. But I can tell you it does not get worse after tomorrow.'

hooks.cue: If they say losing the race
hooks.response: 'Losing the race or losing someone?'

hooks.cue: If they are honest about fear
hooks.response: 'Good. Fear means you are paying attention. The mountain rewards attention.'

questions.genuine: Honest, specific, personal — not bravado or deflection onto the race result.
questions.deflection: Bravado, deflection, or an answer designed to seem fearless.

questions.q: What has he not told you that you should know?

hooks.cue: If they say they do not know
hooks.response: 'Exactly. Think about it. Five days. What has he avoided?'

hooks.cue: If they name the fey stretch
hooks.response: 'Yes. He never talks about Year Four. I know why. He does not know I know.'

hooks.cue: If they name the hag's ridge
hooks.response: She smiles. 'He has good instincts.'

hooks.cue: If they name his feelings about the wolves
hooks.response: 'He talks to them more than he talks to people. Have you noticed that?'

hooks.cue: If they name something that surprises her
hooks.response: She pauses. Looks at Corben. 'You noticed that.' Not to them. To him.

questions.genuine: They have been paying attention to Corben over five days and noticed something specific.
questions.deflection: Generic observations or things that are obvious to anyone.

t2.note: The ledger reads richer gifts at this tier — her farewell prices what the party can actually afford.

t3.note: Her farewell lingers; the pool is weighed against wealthier hands, and her verdict lands accordingly.

t4.note: She knows exactly what the party is worth, to the copper — and the Landlord’s Farewell is priced to it.

alternates.title: The Landlord’s Farewell — The Return Toast
alternates.trigger: Always — Corben stops the sled. This is not optional, and this year she pours FIRST.
alternates.nature: For returning racers the Farewell is a toast, not an audit: she raises a cup to the year they survived. The ledger still reads — but it weighs this year’s courtesies WITH the memory of every prior year’s.

avoid.detail: Stand, drink what is poured, speak when spoken to. The pool carries forward: a party in good standing starts the reading one tier up.
Naming something true and kind about her valley in return. She goes quite still, and the verdict lands one tier higher than the pool alone would give.
A party that wronged her in a prior year drinks standing in a cold wind. The reading starts one tier DOWN, and everyone at the stone knows why.

alternates.ifCombat: She will not fight here. She never fights here. The three days of lost rest still follow unprovoked steel — and now the whole valley’s worth of years follows it too.
alternates.guideNote: Same stone, same stop, better wine for them as earned it. Do be standing straight.
alternates.note: Year-2 continuity — the pool weighs the years. DC shifts by tier still apply.

alternates.title: The Landlord’s Farewell — The Empty Chair
alternates.trigger: Always — and beside the set places there is one more: a place laid for whoever the party lost, left behind, or came back without.
alternates.nature: She sets a place for the missing — a racer who died, retired, or simply is not on the sled this year. She does not explain. She waits.

avoid.detail: Someone tells the missing one’s story — a true thing, well meant, any length. She listens all the way through. The verdict is read with the pool at its full weight, and the wind is kind on the last switchbacks.
Allowed. She drinks alone to the chair, and the reading proceeds on the pool as it stands — no penalty, no grace.

avoid.method: Ask WHO the chair is for
avoid.detail: She answers with the name. However she knows, she knows. This is worth exactly one shiver and one honest toast.

alternates.ifCombat: No. Not at this stone, not this year, not ever.
alternates.guideNote: She do be setting a place for someone. I do be recommending we be worthy of the courtesy.
alternates.note: Year-3+ continuity — the heavy beat. Play it slow.

encounters.title: The Dryad
encounters.trigger: DC 10 Luck Check — success: she blesses the passing. She cannot physically stop the party regardless.
encounters.nature: Bound to her tree at the treeline above Cornell. She has watched the race damage this section of mountain for years. She is not angry — she is tired. She knows she cannot stop it. She is asking.

avoid.method: Take her seriously — the right answer
avoid.detail: She wants acknowledgment of the damage and a specific commitment. Examples: returning in spring to plant at the treeline, donating a portion of the prize to a druidic order that maintains this mountain, or bringing the concern to the racing commissioner. Sincerity is detectable (Insight +6). She blesses the passing: advantage on the next Luck Check.

She has a specific answer: three root systems damaged by the race route. She names the trees. A Druid or Ranger making a specific commitment earns plus one position — she speeds the sled magically. No roll.

Saying honestly that you cannot stop the race and will not promise things you cannot deliver, but you hear her and are sorry, causes her to nod and step aside. No mechanical bonus, but Corben looks at the character differently for the rest of Day 5.

She is bound to her tree and cannot physically block the trail. No mechanical penalty. But Corben looks ashamed for the rest of Day 5 and does not address the wolves by name again until the finish line. The wolves notice. The party notices the wolves noticing.

encounters.ifCombat: She is incorporeal when she chooses to be and cannot pursue. Attacking causes the tree to shriek: DC 13 WIS save or frightened 1 minute within 60ft. Then she is simply gone. Corben stops the sled and looks at the party for a long, quiet moment. Then continues without speaking.
encounters.guideNote: Corben has passed her every year and never found the right answer. He does not comment on what the party decides. He does not need to.

t2.note: The damage to the treeline is worse this year, and her patience thinner — the commitment she asks for is larger.

t3.note: An old treant stands behind her, silent, snow on its shoulders. It does not speak. It does not need to.

t4.note: Two treants flank the trail. The dryad’s ask is unchanged in kind — acknowledgment and commitment — but the forest is done being ignored.

alternates.title: The Dryad — She Remembers the Promise
alternates.trigger: DC 10 Luck Check — success: she steps out already smiling or already grim, depending on the ledger below. She cannot stop the party regardless; she never could.
alternates.nature: Whatever the party committed to last year — returning in spring, the donation, the commissioner — she knows whether it was kept. The forest counted.

avoid.detail: She says so, plainly, and blesses the passing without being asked — the last switchbacks run kind (+1 position). Word of the keeping is also, somehow, already in Cornell.

avoid.method: The promise was BROKEN — own it
avoid.detail: Honesty about the failure, and a new commitment sized to be kept. She accepts once. The second broken promise closes this door for good.
She lets the sled pass in silence. The silence follows it: no blessing this year or any year after, and the pines drop their snow on the trail all afternoon.

alternates.ifCombat: Unchanged — she is gone the moment steel shows, and the shrieking tree remembers longer than she does.
alternates.guideNote: The forest do be keeping accounts. I did be warning you it would, this time last year.
alternates.note: Year-2 continuity — the promise, audited. The treant tier variants still apply.

alternates.title: The Dryad — The Sapling Line
alternates.trigger: Always — she is waiting at a stretch of treeline the party has not seen before, because it was not there before: a line of saplings in the race scar.
alternates.nature: The replanting has begun — hers, and whoever kept faith with her. This year she asks for hands, not words: a bundle of seed-stock carried down to Cornell’s druids.

avoid.detail: A wrapped seed-bundle, light as bread, rides the sled to Cornell — delivered to the druids by the Prize Hall (a one-minute scene at the finish). The blessing follows the sled the whole last day (+1 position), and the druids remember the courier.
She nods; racers race. No penalty — the asking was itself a trust, and she does not spend it on resentment.

avoid.method: Plant one WITH her (10 minutes, −1 position)
avoid.detail: Trading trail time for root time. She names the sapling after the sled. This is not mechanically optimal. Some tables will do it anyway, and they are correct.

alternates.ifCombat: Unchanged. Attacking the person handing you a bag of seeds is a new low the mountain was not expecting.
alternates.guideNote: Seeds do be wanting to go downhill anyway. We do be going downhill professionally. This do be an easy yes.
alternates.note: Year-3+ continuity — the living treeline. The treant tier variants still apply.

encounters.title: The Silver Dragon
encounters.trigger: DC 10 plus or minus 5 Luck Check — she appears regardless, check affects her openness
encounters.nature: The mountain's ancient guardian, old enough to have watched this pass change over centuries. Silver dragons are the most conversational of dragons — genuinely interested in mortal perspective. She is not testing the party's worthiness. She is simply curious.

avoid.detail: She asks one question. Choose or roll from: what do you intend to do with the prize, which of you do you trust most and why, is there something in the world you regret, or what is the bravest thing you have done that no one witnessed. She detects lies (Insight +13). Genuine answers earn plus two positions via flash-frozen trail.

avoid.method: Ask her a question in return
avoid.detail: Offering to answer hers if she answers yours surprises her pleasantly. She agrees — silver dragons love reciprocal conversation. Her answer to any sincere question about the mountain, race, or world is genuine and illuminating. Same plus two positions benefit.

avoid.method: Acknowledge the mountain through her — History DC 12
avoid.detail: Silver dragons form deep bonds with the land they guard. Addressing her with genuine respect for what she protects — not flattery, but acknowledgment that this is her mountain and the party is grateful for passage — earns immediate warmth before the question is even asked.

Attacking: AC 22, HP 487, Cold Breath DC 23 CON 12d8 cold. She will be disappointed rather than angry, which is worse. Fleeing: she can fly at 80ft. She will catch up and ask why the party ran. It will be awkward. Stop the sled and speak with her.
