encounters.ifCombat: AC 22, HP 487. Legendary Actions 3 per round. Cold Breath DC 23 CON 12d8 cold. Wing Attack. Tail. She will not fight to kill — she incapacitates and then asks what the party was thinking. She is genuinely curious about the decision.
encounters.guideNote: Corben stops the sled himself when he sees her. He has met her before. He does not say what was asked of him. Whatever his answer was, it was apparently acceptable — he has come back seven times.

t2.note: She meets the party at her true size for a stronger age of heroes — an adult, wings wide across the switchback.

t3.note: Ancient, and unhurried. The question is the same; the being asking it has watched this pass for six hundred years.

t4.note: Ancient — and she asks TWO questions this year, the second sharper than the first. Honesty in both, or the openness is gone.

alternates.title: The Silver Dragon — The Answer’s Weight
alternates.trigger: DC 10 plus or minus 5 Luck Check — she appears regardless; the check affects how much of last year she admits to remembering first.
alternates.nature: She remembers the answer they gave. This year’s question is what they DID with it — the prize, the trust, the regret, whatever they claimed. Silver dragons collect follow-through.

avoid.detail: What actually happened — kept promises or broken ones, honestly owned. Honesty about failure lands BETTER with her than success reported smugly. The flash-frozen trail follows a true accounting (+2 positions).

avoid.method: Ask her what she did with THEIR answer
avoid.detail: She tells them — where it sits in six hundred years of collected mortal moments, and what it sits beside. Reciprocity earns the same benefit and a story no bard owns.
She lets it pass, visibly disappointed, and the openness is gone — no benefit, no penalty, and a colder mountain next year.

alternates.ifCombat: Unchanged, at whatever age the tier gives her — and she opens with “LAST year you said—” which is worse than the breath.
alternates.guideNote: She do be remembering what was said. Seven trips I have made, and she do be quoting me to myself every one.
alternates.note: Year-2 continuity — follow-through. The aging tier variants still apply.

alternates.title: The Silver Dragon — The Question Returned
alternates.trigger: Always — she lands, settles, and says nothing at all. The silence is the invitation.
alternates.nature: This year the party asks HER one question — any question — and she judges them entirely by what they choose to ask.

avoid.method: Ask a question worth her answering
avoid.detail: About the mountain, the long view, what she regrets, what she guards — anything sincere and larger than the race. She answers fully (a gift beyond price) and the trail freezes flat for the finish (+2 positions).
“Will we win?” gets the answer it deserves: “Yes, someone will.” No benefit. Mild draconic amusement, which has its own weather.
Respectful silence back is a legitimate move — she inclines her head, and the pass is simply peaceful.

alternates.ifCombat: Unchanged. Attacking a dragon who offered you a free question enters the region’s folklore immediately.
alternates.guideNote: Her turn to be asked, this year. Do be making it a good one — she do be grading.
alternates.note: Year-3+ continuity — the reversal. The aging tier variants still apply.

encounters.title: The Hollowmourn — Final Switchback
encounters.trigger: DC 10 plus or minus 5 Luck Check — always present, check affects positioning
encounters.nature: An ancient spirit of grief bound to this switchback. She is not malicious — she is trapped in an emotion so large it has become a force. She wails because she cannot stop wailing. There is no negotiation. There is only survival and momentum.

avoid.method: DC 13 CON save — everyone including Corben
avoid.detail: This is the encounter. The wolves are unaffected — they are animals, they keep running. Fail: 0 HP. The sled keeps moving because the wolves keep moving. Get through the switchback. She cannot follow — she is bound here. The goal is not to defeat her. The goal is to get past her.

avoid.method: Turning Undead — creates a safe corridor
avoid.detail: Any Cleric or Paladin can use Turn Undead. The Hollowmourn must succeed on WIS save versus spell save DC or be turned for 1 minute — she cannot approach and her Keening has a 30ft range. This creates a window to push the sled through the switchback.

avoid.method: The silver bell — if the glimmerkin gave it
avoid.detail: The glimmerkin said to ring it at the worst moment. This is when. Ringing the bell cuts through the Hollowmourn's wail for 6 seconds. Every creature at 0 HP regains 1 HP. The bell then goes silent forever. It was made for exactly this moment. The glimmerkin knew.

avoid.method: Corben goes down — Animal Handling DC 14
avoid.detail: If Corben fails his CON save: DC 14 Animal Handling to take the reins. The wolves know the way to Cornell and are running toward it right now. Choice: stop to stabilize Corben (Medicine DC 10, one action) or let the wolves carry the sled and stabilize at the bottom. If in contention for first, this is the dramatic heart of the session.

encounters.ifCombat: AC 13, HP 63. Immune to cold, lightning, necrotic, thunder, and non-magical physical damage. The Face It Died With: DC 14 WIS or frightened. The Keening once per day DC 13 CON fail equals 0 HP. Cannot leave the switchback. Turning Undead works.
encounters.guideNote: Corben will be on the ground or on the runners. Either way, Fenra is at the front, ears flat, eyes forward. She has done this before.

t2.note: Two voices braid on the final switchback — the wail comes twice if the party lingers.

t3.note: Three of them walk the last stretch. The wolves keep running; everyone else holds the line one save at a time.

t4.note: The choir. Four hollowmourns, wails staggered across the rounds — the finish line is EARNED at this tier. The visage and the wail both read at the tier DC.

alternates.title: The Hollowmourn — She Knows Their Names
alternates.trigger: DC 10 plus or minus 5 Luck Check — always present; the check decides whether the first name is called before or after the sled enters the switchback.
alternates.nature: She wails the returning racers’ NAMES now, one by one, in a voice each of them knows from somewhere private. The mechanics sharpen: hearing your own name in a dead voice is harder to hold against.

avoid.method: The CON save, named (DC 13 +2 for anyone whose name she calls)
avoid.detail: The named save is the year’s price of being remembered by the switchback. Everything else — the wolves running, momentum as survival — is unchanged.

avoid.method: The bell, kept a full year
avoid.detail: If the party STILL carries the glimmerkin’s bell, its ring this year buys a FULL ROUND of silence — the glimmerkin’s gift has steeped. She knew. She always knew.
Shouting back “I am here, and alive!” — the racer makes the save at advantage. Grief hates a live answer.

alternates.ifCombat: Unchanged at the tier’s count. She cannot leave the switchback; the goal has never moved: get past her.
alternates.guideNote: She do be calling for YOU this year, by name. Run through it. Living do be the only argument she hears.
alternates.note: Year-2 continuity — the personalized wail. The choir tier variants still apply.

alternates.title: The Hollowmourn — The Grief Given Back
alternates.trigger: Always — and as the sled enters, the wail falters, just once, like a breath caught.
alternates.nature: Familiar racers give her something no stranger can: recognition. One of them may try to hand her a grief of their own — and grief shared is, for one hour, grief stilled.

avoid.method: Share one true grief (RP; Persuasion DC 13 as the fallback)
avoid.detail: A racer stops IN the switchback — everything the rules say not to do — faces her, and speaks one real loss aloud. Success: the wail stops entirely this year; the sled passes in a silence that feels like snowfall. She does not thank them. The silence is the thanks.
The CON save gauntlet as written, at the tier’s numbers. Not every table wants the quiet ending; the loud one still works.
Its six seconds stand, as ever, for the table that kept it.

alternates.ifCombat: Unchanged — but any damage dealt to her after a grief was offered UNDOES the stillness, permanently, for every future year. Some doors close from the inside.
alternates.guideNote: One of you could be stopping. I have never seen it done. I have heard it CAN be.
alternates.note: Year-3+ continuity — the quiet ending, if the table reaches for it.

sledRace.encounterTiersNote: Encounters scale by Party Tier: each entry carries a `tiers` object ({t2:{creature,count,stat,also,dcShift,note}, t3:{...}, t4:{...}}) read at render and at the ⚔ muster — Tier I is the written level-3 tuning, and an absent field falls back to it. The active tier is set on the crew strip.

npcs.title: Corben Vash
npcs.description: The party's guide and the last one in Zethel with a full team — because his team is six dire wolves. Seven years racing, brought to the finish line every year he's entered. Warm, easy, completely unbothered by cold or by Lord Vane. Genuinely pleased to take the party on — not desperate, just satisfied. Meticulous about camp, firm about his rules, and quietly devoted to the wolves, especially Fenra.

stats.label: Role
stats.val: Guide, musher, trail expert — 7 years racing

stats.label: Team
stats.val: Six dire wolves (Fenra, Greyback, Shadowfoot, Blizzard, Tusk, Runt)

stats.label: Cut
stats.val: 20% of any purse — negotiable to 15% if pressed hard, no lower

stats.label: Rules
stats.val: Keep him alive · stay put if he falls · base camps are exit points

npcs.notes: Carries a flask of Illianer brandy specifically for Hruun the frost giant — 'Every year. Same hand. Same silence.' If he goes down (Hollowmourn, Day 5), the wolves keep running: DC 14 Animal Handling to take the reins, then the party chooses stabilize-or-finish. His three rules are the spine of the whole race — surface them in Scene 5 and hold him to them. If the party has no sled name and asks him, he says, after exactly one second: 'The Wolves.'
voice: "I be Corben Vash. The best of the best of guides — if my track record does show."
"I'm the reason they had to add the quotes. My team is all dire wolves. Every single one."
"Keep me alive. If you want to win this race, I need to be alive to run it."

npcs.title: Lord Aldric Vane
npcs.description: Hereditary noble, third consecutive year racing. Has never finished better than fourth. Has never understood why. His crew is professional, well-equipped, and instructed to make contact when advantageous. He is not evil — he's a man shaped by winning at everything until this race. He will be gracious if he wins and confused if he loses. He will return next year.

stats.label: Race record
stats.val: 3 starts, best finish 4th

stats.label: Aggression
stats.val: 35% chance per switchback within 2 positions

stats.label: Motivation
stats.val: Cannot understand why he keeps losing

stats.label: Party potential
stats.val: Can be recruited as 4th member — desperate but too proud to show it

npcs.notes: Vane was at Bethalyn's tent trying to register solo with servants as party members. She turned him away. He is still near the tent when the party arrives. If recruited: he's difficult about the wolves, difficult about terms, ultimately agrees. He will be a liability and also occasionally useful. He genuinely believes the rules don't apply to him because they've never been enforced.
voice: "Charming animals. Absolutely charming. I didn't realize the 'dog' part was literal this year."
"The stewards have been informed. They will, of course, do nothing."
"This is an outrage. My companions are more than capable—"

npcs.title: Bethalyn
npcs.description: Eleven-year registrar of the race. Has opinions about everything. Considers Lord Vane a personal insult to the event she has given her professional life to. Knows every team's history, every wreck, every disputed finish. Is the person to consult on tiebreakers and rule disputes.

stats.label: Role
stats.val: Registration, rules, results arbitration

stats.label: Tenure
stats.val: 11 years — has seen everything

stats.label: On Vane
stats.val: Unconcealed contempt, professionally managed

stats.label: On Corben
stats.val: Respectful. Would never say so.

npcs.notes: Key information Bethalyn provides: the route (5 days, Zethel to Cornell), the prize (10,000gp + bonus item determined at finish by Racing Commissioner), the guide situation (one left, listen for the growling), the fourth member problem (Vane is around). She does not elaborate on the bonus item — that's the Commissioner's prerogative.
voice: "Oh! Hello — my apologies, I did not see you come in while our last racer was on his way out."
"You will know it when you get there. Listen for the growling."
"Lord Vane's objection has been noted and filed with the other ones."

npcs.title: The Wolf Pack
npcs.description: Six dire wolves in racing condition. They have run this course more times than most teams' humans. They are the reason the race had to put quotes around the word Dog. They respond to Corben's voice individually. He uses all six names in sequence only when the terrain is at its worst.

stats.label: Fenra
stats.val: Alpha. Grey, scarred. Reads terrain better than Corben. Doesn't look at crowds. Never.

stats.label: Greyback
stats.val: Second trace. Runs in perfect sync with Shadowfoot. Calm under all conditions.

stats.label: Tusk
stats.val: Young. Makes direct eye contact with the CISF. Corben cannot stop this.

stats.label: Shadowfoot
stats.val: Left outside trace. First to sense fey interference. Looked at things in Year Four that Corben won't discuss.

stats.label: Blizzard
stats.val: White coat. Named for vanishing at speed. Hackles are a warning system.

stats.label: Runt
stats.val: Smallest. Pulls hardest. Showing teeth at strangers is his default. He will warm up. Eventually.

npcs.notes: Animal Handling DC 15 (advantage for Ranger/Druid/Path of the Pack Barbarian) to be accepted by the pack. Fail by 5+: 1d4 bite. Runt is most likely to snap. Tusk is most likely to be enthusiastic. Fenra decides last and her acceptance matters most.

npcs.title: Hruun the Frost Giant
npcs.description: Valley toll collector. Has been taking payment from every race team since Year Two. Bored, patient, fair in his own way. His wife likes beautiful things. He likes stories he hasn't heard and gold because it's pretty.

stats.label: AC / HP
stats.val: AC 15 / HP 138

stats.label: Toll: gold
stats.val: 500gp or more — he thinks it's pretty

stats.label: Toll: story
stats.val: One he hasn't heard — Persuasion DC 15

stats.label: Toll: strength
stats.val: Arm wrestle — Athletics DC 22, two tries if amusing

stats.label: Toll: beautiful
stats.val: Something magical or beautiful for his wife — he lights up

stats.label: Free passage
stats.val: Use his name (learned from Vestri). He's startled, then respectful.

npcs.notes: Corben carries a flask of Illianer brandy specifically for Hruun. 'Every year. Same hand. Same silence.' — If the party attacks: −2 positions minimum, sled damage risk. He picks up refusing sleds and moves them off the trail (−4 positions, no party damage). He is fair. He is very large.

npcs.title: Vestri the Night Hag
npcs.description: The valley's true owner. Vestri has held this territory for decades — Hruun the frost giant works at her pleasure, she gave him the gate and a purpose, and she finds watching racers deal with him enormously entertaining. The toll at SB2 is theatre she designed. She watches every team navigate it from the ridge above and checks in on interesting guests before they leave. All her offers are genuine. All costs are real.

stats.label: AC / HP
stats.val: AC 17 (natural) / HP 112

stats.label: Her valley
stats.val: Always has been. Hruun works at her pleasure. The toll is theatre she designed.

stats.label: SB1 — Valley floor
stats.val: Landlord greeting guests. Will trade Hruun intel for something small.

stats.label: SB3 — Ridge farewell
stats.val: Required gate. One question per player. No toll. Pool result determines Day 5 intel.

stats.label: Wants (SB1)
stats.val: Secret / name / memory / year of life. NOT gold.

stats.label: Corben
stats.val: Has been watching him for seven years. Finds him interesting. He gives her nothing.

npcs.notes: Corben always declines her offers. He's never explained why. She finds this interesting. She's been waiting for him to slip for years. Does NOT want gold. Finds it boring. If attacked unprovoked: HP 112, Magic Resistance, Etherealness. She'll make things unpleasant and vanish. She is not the final boss.
voice: "Racing folk. I do love the racing season. So many interesting people passing through my valley."
"So many things they carry that they don't know the value of."

npcs.title: Aldric Voss & Perris Tan
npcs.description: The two announcers calling the race from the Cornell scrying booth. Aldric Voss is the senior voice — nine years of race calls, dramatic, invested in history. Perris Tan is younger, faster, more likely to lose composure. Both have a soft spot for the wolves. Neither will admit this.

stats.label: Aldric Voss
stats.val: Senior. 'In nine years of calling this race...' — uses frequently.

stats.label: Perris Tan
stats.val: Reactive. Quick. Has feelings about Tusk specifically.

stats.label: Coverage
stats.val: Party sled gets most airtime when CISF is active

stats.label: On Corben
stats.val: Deep professional respect. Will not say it directly.

npcs.notes: Heard through the LRF announcer feed. Players build a relationship with them over five days. They are the crowd's voice — they feel what the crowd feels. When the stone goes dark they speculate. When it comes back they're audibly relieved.
voice: "In nine years of calling this race I have never seen a dire wolf make eye contact with the CISF. Tusk is doing it again."
"That is TEXTBOOK racing from Vash — Cornell is standing up for this one."
"We've lost the sympathetic lock. The mountain is keeping that secret."

pregens.name: Theron Ashveil

magicItems.name: Mantle of Spell Resistance
magicItems.effect: Advantage on saving throws vs. spells.

features: Second Wind (1d10+3 HP, bonus action, 1/short rest)
Order Dice — 4 order dice (d8), order DC 13
Orders: Hold the Line, Called Shot, Sweep the Legs
Drilled, Not Inspired — teach one order to a willing ally for the day
pregens.personality: Gruff veteran who follows orders well but chafes under weak leadership. Secretly terrified of cold environments after a bad campaign.
pregens.note: Best frontline tank. Great for new players.

pregens.name: Sylindra Mosswhisper

magicItems.name: Boots of the Winterlands
magicItems.effect: Cold resistance; ignore difficult terrain in snow/ice.

features: Snowmasked — hide when only lightly obscured by snow, mist or foliage
pregens.personality: Quiet and observant. Has an uncanny connection with animals. Speaks in short sentences.
pregens.note: Perfect for the wolf-taming scene. Animal Handling is key.

pregens.name: Brimstone Duskmantle
pregens.cls: Warlock (The Fiend, Pact of the Blade)

magicItems.name: Cloak of Protection
magicItems.effect: +1 AC and +1 to all saving throws.

features: Dark One's Blessing (temp HP on kill)
pregens.personality: Smooth-talking risk-taker. Will absolutely try to negotiate any cut down. Enjoys chaos.
pregens.note: Great for the negotiation scene. Strong in combat despite being cha-based.

pregens.name: Ozra Kettlewick

proficiencies.weapons: Daggers, darts, slings, quarterstaffs, light crossbows

features: Gnome Cunning (adv on INT/WIS/CHA saves vs. magic)
Omens (2 d20 rolls per long rest to replace any roll — spend the LOWER first)
The Last Word — regain a spell slot when the second omen is spent
pregens.personality: Obsessively curious. Has been trying to predict outcomes for weeks. His two omens are the numbers he has already decided the day is going to contain.
pregens.note: The ultimate utility player. The omens are VERY useful for luck checks — and having to spend the low one first turns a bad roll into a puzzle instead of a dead die.

pregens.name: Vorund Hammerstone

attacks.name: Dwarven Thrower (Warhammer)
attacks.dmg: 1d8+6 bludgeoning (+3 magic; 2d8 vs giants when thrown)

magicItems.name: Dwarven Thrower
magicItems.effect: Returns when thrown; +3 to hit/dmg as Warhammer; doubled dice vs. Giants when thrown.

features: Hammer-Blessing (+1 weapon/armor per long rest; once, its bearer drops to 1 HP instead of 0)
Channel Divinity: The Night's Work / Turn Undead
pregens.personality: Steady and reliable. Came for the prize money to buy a new forge. Takes the race VERY seriously.
pregens.note: Best healer. Heat Metal is brutal vs. armored enemies. Huge HP pool.

pregens.name: Nym Shadowstep

proficiencies.weapons: Simple, hand crossbows, longswords, rapiers, shortswords

features: Expertise: Stealth, Sleight of Hand, Thieves' Tools, Acrobatics
The Borrowed Hand — invisible mage hand, bonus action, at Sleight of Hand
Not Where You Struck — halve one hit's damage, 1/short rest
pregens.personality: Slippery and opportunistic. In it for the payout. Will immediately case any building they enter. Has a soft spot for animals.
pregens.note: Great for stealthy/skill-heavy moments. Hat of Disguise fun for roleplay.

pregens.name: Aelindra Thornwood

proficiencies.weapons: Clubs, daggers, darts, javelins, maces, quarterstaffs, scimitars, sickles, slings, spears

magicItems.name: Periapt of Wound Closure
magicItems.effect: Stabilize automatically; doubled hit dice healing.

features: Swift Change — beast shape as a bonus action, 2/short rest
Beasts of the Second Skin: CR 1 forms
The Skin Remembers — keep your own WIS save, one word per round
Give It Back — an ally heals for your druid level when you drop the shape
pregens.personality: Deeply connected to nature — alarmed by impact on mountain wildlife. Will push to leave little trace. Can scout as a wolf/bear.
pregens.note: Wildshape as a wolf synergizes with the wolf pack. Excellent nature utility.

pregens.name: Kazimir Ashfall
features: Charter: First to Move (+5 initiative, can't be surprised while you can hear)
Pack Runner (+10 ft walking speed — already in Speed above)
Set the Direction — allies get advantage vs. creatures within 5 ft of you while you rage
Speak the Pack's Mind — speak with animals and beast sense as rituals
pregens.personality: Wild and untamed. Raised partly among wolves — deep connection to the sled team. Rage represents his ancestor spirit.
pregens.note: Highest HP, hardest melee hitter. Path of the Pack synergy with the wolves is flavorful.

sq-zethel.title: Zethel — Before the Race
sq-zethel.subtitle: Claw of Storms · Mountain waystation, Kingdom of Torrentath
sq-zethel.intro: Zethel is a logging and fur-trading town of roughly 400 permanent residents tucked into the lower Dragonspine pass. For eleven months it is quiet, cold, and entirely unbothered by the outside world. For three weeks each Claw of Storms it triples in size and becomes something between a festival and a logistics problem. The locals have complicated feelings about this. The money is good. The adventurers are exhausting. No tile color coding here — that is a Twin Cities custom. Zethel establishments are identified by carved wooden signs and, in most cases, the noise coming from inside.
sq-zethel.world_note: Zethel does not yet appear in the Arret Infrastructure sheet. The establishments below are built consistent with Knakknthazn mountain town conventions from Thig Dural Thane. When you add Zethel to your spreadsheet, these can be the seed entries.

locations.name: The Cracked Tusk
locations.desc: Named for the mammoth tusk mounted above the door — a full adult tusk, cracked clean through at the midpoint. The crack happened in Year Three of the race when a half-orc fighter from a losing team decided the tusk was somehow responsible. The owner, Aldous Greatbrow (Dwarf, he/him, 187), has been meaning to get it repaired ever since. He will pay 50gp or equivalent for a Mending or Fabricate solution. He asks every race season. Nobody has ever taken him up on it. The main room fits four long tables of eight and a bar that runs the full left wall. The fire is large and kept high. Race season means standing room only after dark.
staff: Vrenda Greatbrow, Dwarf, she/her, 154 — bartender, Aldous's wife, does not share his patience
Pommit Ashblock, Dwarf, he/him, 62 — cook, speaks only to the food
Tess Oremantle, Human, she/her, 26 — server, race season hire, genuinely enjoys the chaos
menu: Mountain Stout Pint — 2 SP (local brew, very dark, very cold)
Meal — 5 SP (venison stew or roasted root vegetables, no choice)
rules: No Credit
No Fighting
No Wolves Inside

side_quests.name: The Cracked Tusk (Literal)
side_quests.hook: Aldous mentions it every time someone walks in. 50gp for a Mending, Fabricate, or equivalent solution. He has been asking for three years. The tusk is 8 feet long and mounted 12 feet up. It is load-bearing in the sense that everything in the tavern is vaguely arranged around it.
side_quests.reward: 50gp. Aldous's goodwill, which is worth more — he knows everyone in Zethel and most of the race regulars.

side_quests.name: The Pit — Fight Betting
side_quests.hook: Downstairs, accessible through a door behind the bar that Vrenda will unlock for 2cp. A stone-floored basement room with a rope circle painted on the floor. Three fighters work the pit during race season: Gormund Stoneback (Half-Orc, he/him, 34 — big, slow, hits like a forge hammer), Peska Ironwind (Halfling, she/her, 88 — fast, dirty, never fights fair), and someone who changes every year and is just called The Newcomer. Betting is handled by Sable Dimwick (Halfling, she/her, 112) who has run the book for six years. She has never lost money on a night. She will take any bet on outcome, method of victory, or round. She will not take bets on The Newcomer's identity. She knows who it is. She will not say.
side_quests.mechanics: DC 14 Insight to read Sable's tells. DC 16 Persuasion to get a tip on the night's odds from her. DC 18 Perception to notice she signals someone near the door when large bets come in. Entering the pit: DC 13 Athletics or Acrobatics to qualify. Gormund: AC 13, HP 52, Greatclub +5 2d6+3. Peska: AC 14, HP 28, two daggers +6 1d4+4, Cunning Action. The Newcomer: DM's choice.
side_quests.reward: Winnings at standard odds. Sable's respect if you beat the house. Gormund's friendship if you last more than two rounds with him — he respects endurance over technique.

side_quests.name: Race Betting Board
side_quests.hook: Behind the bar, a chalkboard updated twice daily by Sable with current race odds. All 30 teams listed. The party's sled is on there. Their odds reflect their current race position if the race has started, or their perceived quality if pre-race. Sable sets the lines. She is rarely wrong about the favorites. She is occasionally spectacularly wrong about the dark horses, and she knows it, and she hates it.
side_quests.mechanics: Pre-race bets settled at race end. Mid-race bets available on day outcomes. DC 12 Investigation to find value in the board. DC 15 to identify which line Sable has mispriced. The party's sled starts at 8:1 against.

side_quests.name: The Stranger at the Corner Table
side_quests.hook: Every night of race season, the same corner table near the back has a person sitting in it who is clearly neither a racer nor a Zethel local. They drink slowly, watch the room, and leave before last call. They have been here every race season for four years. Nobody knows their name. They do not give it. If engaged: polite, vague, genuinely curious about the party. They know things about the race that are not public. This is a world-building thread. Who they are is your call — Moonlight Strategy operative, Cornell Commissioner's agent, someone with a personal stake in a specific team's outcome, or simply someone who finds the race interesting for reasons they will not explain.
side_quests.mechanics: DC 15 Persuasion to get any real information. DC 18 Insight to read whether what they say is true. DC 20 Investigation over multiple conversations to piece together who they represent.
side_quests.reward: Information. Potentially a contact for future sessions.

locations.name: Ironwake Lodge
locations.desc: The largest building in Zethel proper — three stories of hewn stone with a common room on the ground floor that smells permanently of pine resin and wet wool. Fully booked during race season. The proprietor, Houndra Stonefoot (Dwarf, she/her, 203), runs it with the efficiency of someone who has done this seventeen times and has stopped being surprised by anything adventurers do.
staff: Brek Stonefoot, Dwarf, he/him, 198 — kitchen, Houndra's husband, excellent cook
Wimble Caskpour, Halfling, he/him, 67 — front desk and room service
Dassra Oaklatch, Human, she/her, 31 — cleaning and morning service, race season hire
menu: Room (shared, 4 per room) — 5 SP per night

side_quests.name: Houndra's Missing Delivery
side_quests.hook: A supply wagon from the valley with two barrels of fine wine and a case of good spirits was due four days ago. It has not arrived. She cannot leave the inn during race season. She will pay 40gp for anyone who finds out what happened or retrieves the supplies. The wagon belongs to a merchant named Tolber Ashcoin (Human, he/him, 52) who has made this delivery reliably for eleven years.
side_quests.mechanics: DC 12 Investigation in town locates someone who saw the wagon on the south road three days ago. DC 14 Survival to track from there. The wagon is stuck in a snowdrift half a mile south — one wheel cracked on ice. Tolber is fine, cold, and irritable. The wine is intact. The spirits are mostly intact. One bottle did not survive the cold.
side_quests.reward: 40gp from Houndra. Tolber Ashcoin as a contact — he trades throughout the southern Dragonspine and knows things about the road between Zethel and Cornell.

locations.name: Kessa's Provisions
locations.desc: A double-wide storefront crammed floor to ceiling with exactly what you need and nothing you do not. Cold-weather gear, trail rations, climbing equipment, rope, lanterns, wax, flint, snowshoes, and the specific kind of runner grease that keeps sled runners from chattering on ice. Kessa Ironmantle (Dwarf, she/her, 241) has been supplying racers since Year One and has strong opinions about every team. She shares them freely. She is usually right. She has refused to sell to exactly one team every race season since Year Two, always a different team, always without explanation. This year's team is Vane's Regiment. She will not discuss this.
inventory: All standard adventuring gear except Arcane/Druidic Focus, Holy Symbols, Spellbooks
Cold weather gear — Furred cloak 8GP, Thermal underlayer 5GP, Mountaineering boots 12GP
Snowshoes — 2GP
Sled runner grease (Dragonspine formula) — 1GP per application, 3 applications per jar
Trail rations (mountain grade, high calorie) — 1GP per week
Ice axe (as handaxe, also climbing tool) — 5GP
Piton set x10 with hammer — 1GP
Hemp rope 50ft — 1GP
Silk rope 50ft — 10GP
Lantern, hooded — 5GP
Oil flask x4 — 1GP

side_quests.name: Why Did Kessa Refuse Vane
side_quests.hook: Kessa refused to sell to Vane's Regiment this morning. He sent a servant three times with escalating offers. She refused each time and asked them to leave. If a player asks her directly: she says only 'Some teams I supply. Some teams I do not.' DC 20 Persuasion or DC 18 Insight after extended conversation. What she knows: Vane's Regiment used a product she sold them two years ago to deliberately damage a competitor's sled runners. She cannot prove it. She will not sell to him until she can. This is a world-building thread.
side_quests.mechanics: DC 15 Investigation among other vendors confirms Vane's Regiment is blacklisted from two other suppliers. DC 18 finds a racer from Year Three who will talk about their runners failing unexpectedly on Day Two.
side_quests.reward: World information. A reason to keep an eye on Vane's Regiment beyond the race mechanics.

locations.name: The Blue Lamp
locations.desc: No sign. Just a blue lamp hung in the window of a rented stall near the market edge. Operates only during race season. Vorris Quickmelt (Gnome, he/him, 140) sets up the same stall every year, pays Kessa a nominal rate for the corner space, and sells potions and cold-resistance tinctures to anyone with coin. He has a nervous energy that suggests either excitement or guilt. Probably both. Some of his items are of uncertain provenance. He does not discuss provenance.
inventory: Potion of Healing — 50GP x4
Potion of Greater Healing — 150GP x2
Cold Resistance Tincture (advantage on CON saves vs extreme cold, 4 hours) — 25GP x6
Antitoxin — 50GP x3
Healer's Kit — 5GP x4
Potion of Climbing — 150GP x1
Elixir of Health — 120GP x1 (clears disease, poison, blindness, deafness, paralysis)
Something in a dark bottle he keeps under the counter — price negotiable, effects unclear

side_quests.name: The Dark Bottle
side_quests.hook: If a player expresses curiosity about the bottle under the counter, Vorris becomes briefly more nervous than usual. He will sell it for 200gp but strongly recommends not using it without knowing what it does. DC 15 Arcana to identify it as some kind of divination or scrying compound. DC 18 to identify it specifically as Oil of Etherealness — not harmful, but not something a gnome alchemist should have in a mountain waystation during a sled race. He acquired it from someone who passed through Zethel six months ago and preferred coin to questions.
side_quests.mechanics: The bottle is Oil of Etherealness. Vorris does not know that. He thought it was something more mundane. The person who sold it to him had a reason for passing through Zethel in the off-season. World-building thread.
side_quests.reward: Oil of Etherealness if purchased. A mystery if pursued.

locations.name: Temple of the Traveler
locations.desc: Small, stone, always open, inexplicably cold inside despite the brazier that burns continuously near the door. The priest, Brother Aldric Copperholm (Human, he/him, 52), is deeply aware that he shares a first name with Lord Aldric Vane and considers this a personal test from the Traveler. He offers healing, blessings, and a small lending library of trail maps. He charges nothing. He will accept donations for the heating fund. The heating fund has never purchased heating because every time it gets close, someone needs healing that they cannot afford.
services: Cure Wounds (1st level) — donation suggested, none required
Blessings for the trail — free, takes about 4 minutes, genuinely moving if you let it
A quiet place to sit — always free

side_quests.name: The Heating Fund
side_quests.hook: Brother Aldric mentions the heating fund to no one specifically and everyone generally. The temple has been cold for eleven years. The fund needs 35gp more to purchase and install a proper hearth insert. He will not ask for it directly. He considers asking for more than what healing requires a misuse of his position. He has enough for healing. The cold is not technically a problem.
side_quests.mechanics: No check required. Just give him 35gp or help him fundraise it among the other racers. DC 12 Persuasion with any racer to get a 1-5gp donation. Vane's representative, if asked, says Lord Vane will match whatever the party contributes. This is the most genuine thing Vane's organization does all week.
side_quests.reward: Brother Aldric's genuine blessing. Advantage on one Wisdom saving throw during the race, communicated to the player privately. The temple gets a hearth. The next time anyone visits Zethel it will be warm inside.

locations.name: The Race Commissioner's Office
locations.desc: A converted storage room behind the registration tent, accessible through a locked door that Bethalyn has the key to. The Racing Commissioner, Baern Ironquill (Dwarf, he/him, 412), occupies this room from three days before the race to one day after. He has been Commissioner since Year One. He intends to die in the position. He may outlast the race itself given dwarven longevity. The bonus prize is in this room. Nobody has seen inside except Baern and Bethalyn. The door is locked (DC 22) and Baern is almost always in it.
locations.proprietor: Baern Ironquill, Dwarf, he/him, 412 — Racing Commissioner

side_quests.name: What Is the Bonus Prize This Year
side_quests.hook: Rumors in the Cracked Tusk range from a wish spell to a Dragonspine relic to a vorpal blade to a small house in Cornell. Baern will not say. Bethalyn does not know — she processes the registration, not the prize. The Commissioner's courier arrived from Cornell eight days ago with a sealed chest. Baern signed for it personally. The courier left the same day without speaking to anyone else. DC 20 Investigation across multiple conversations in Zethel to piece together: the chest arrived from the east, not from Cornell. Cornell is west. The courier's horse had mountain mud on its shoes, not road dust.
side_quests.mechanics: The prize is whatever fits your campaign — wish spell, vorpal weapon, relic of significance to your world. The eastern origin is a mystery thread you can pull or leave alone.
side_quests.reward: The actual prize at race end. The mystery of where it came from, if pursued.

locations.name: The Betting Hall
locations.desc: A separate establishment from the Cracked Tusk's pit — a proper canvas-and-timber hall erected by a consortium from Cornell each race season. Licensed, regulated, takes bets on overall race outcome, individual day placements, specific events (first retirement, first bully incident, first runner casualty). Run by Ithara Glassman (Human, she/her, 34) who dresses for summer regardless of the temperature. She has been asked about this every race season for four years. She says only 'I run warm.'
staff: Pelwick Shortmark, Halfling, he/him, 78 — odds keeper, chalk and board
Durra and Brek Stoneshield, Dwarf twins, they/them, 89 — security
services: Day placements (party finishes top 5 on Day X) — 3:1
First retirement — 4:1 (usually Vane's Regiment by Day 3, per Pelwick)
First bully incident — 2:1 (usually Day 1, per Pelwick)
Corben Vash places top 3 — 5:2 (Pelwick has learned to respect the wolves)

side_quests.name: Ithara's Proposition
side_quests.hook: If the party places a large bet on themselves (100gp+) and then significantly over-performs on Day 1, Ithara approaches them quietly on the first night. She is not accusing them of cheating. She is interested in the information they have about their own sled that the market does not yet reflect. She offers a partnership: inside information for a cut of her winnings on the party's bets. This is not illegal under race rules. It is extremely normal in Cornell finance circles.
side_quests.mechanics: DC 14 Insight to read whether this is a good faith offer. It is. DC 12 Persuasion to negotiate better terms. Accepting means Ithara starts actively working the odds in the party's favor when they place bets — not fixing the race, just using information correctly.
side_quests.reward: Ithara as a financial contact. Better odds on subsequent bets. A window into the Cornell financial establishment that could be relevant for future sessions.

sq-cornell.title: Cornell — After the Race
sq-cornell.subtitle: Claw of Storms · Mountain market town, Kingdom of Torrentath
sq-cornell.intro: Cornell is larger than Zethel but not by much — perhaps 600 permanent residents, a proper market square, and the distinction of being the northern terminus of the kingdom's main mountain trading road. It has been hosting the finish line for eleven years and has developed a comfortable relationship with the race. The finish is an event. The celebration afterward is a local institution. The morning after the celebration is a logistical recovery.
sq-cornell.world_note: Cornell does not yet appear in the Arret Infrastructure sheet. The establishments below are built consistent with mountain town conventions. Seed entries for your spreadsheet when ready.

locations.name: The Finish Line Inn
locations.desc: The only inn in Cornell. Always full during race finish week. The proprietor, Oswin Brackwall (Human, he/him, 61), has a system: race participants get rooms regardless of booking. Everyone else is sorted by how much they annoy him. The food is excellent. The beds are narrow. The common room is the social center of Cornell during race season and stays loud until the early hours.
staff: Maren Brackwall, Human, she/her, 58 — kitchen, Oswin's wife, the reason the food is excellent
Tomas Brackwall, Human, he/him, 22 — server, their son, deeply embarrassed by both of them
Pip, Halfling, she/her, 34 — cleaning and rooms, has worked here for six years, knows where everything is
menu: Meal — 8 SP (genuinely good, Maren uses actual spices)

side_quests.name: Oswin's Debt to Corben
side_quests.hook: If Corben Vash is mentioned to Oswin, something in his expression changes. He will refill the party's drinks without being asked. He says only: 'He saved my brother on the trail. Year Two. Never asked for anything.' If pressed: his brother was a guide who went down in a snowstorm between Zethel and Cornell. Corben found him. It took two days. Corben said nothing about it until someone else told Oswin four months later. This thread is about Corben's character and his history on this mountain.
side_quests.mechanics: No check. Just conversation. Oswin gives the party one night free if they won. He gives them one night free regardless if Corben came in with them.
side_quests.reward: Character depth on Corben. Oswin as a long-term contact in Cornell.

locations.name: Cornell Prize Hall
locations.desc: A permanent stone building on the town square that exists for three functions: official weights and measures, civic announcements, and the race prize ceremony. Baern Ironquill arrives here before the race ends — nobody knows his route — and is waiting when the first sled crosses the finish line. The prize ceremony happens within two hours of the final result, regardless of time of day.
locations.proprietor: Baern Ironquill, Dwarf, he/him, 412 — Racing Commissioner
services: Prize ceremony and formal result registration
Official race complaints and disputes (Bethalyn presides if she is present)
Historical race records back to Year One — accessible by request

side_quests.name: The Race Records
side_quests.hook: The historical records go back to Year One. They include weather, incidents, retirements, and unusual events. DC 14 Investigation to find: Year Four has a gap in the records. Three days of the race are documented only as 'conditions precluded normal recording.' Corben Vash ran that race. He finished second. The Year Four records for Day 3 — the fey section — list only a single note in Baern's handwriting: 'Vash. Noted. Do not pursue.'
side_quests.mechanics: Baern will not discuss Year Four. DC 22 Persuasion. He says: 'Some things the mountain keeps.' That is all.
side_quests.reward: A mystery that connects Corben's past to the fey stretch. A reason to return to Zethel and ask him directly.

locations.name: The Scrying Pool Viewing Area
locations.desc: A purpose-built stone amphitheater around a large enchanted scrying pool in the town square. During the race it broadcasts the feed from the Cornell Scrying Booth — Aldric Voss and Perris Tan's commentary fills the square. After the race it becomes the social gathering point. The party will be recognized here if they placed well or did anything memorable on the feed.

side_quests.name: Aldric Voss Wants a Word
side_quests.hook: If the party finishes in the top five, Aldric Voss finds them in the square within an hour of the finish. He is exactly as dramatic in person as he is on the commentary. He wants to do a formal post-race interview for the recorded archive. He has questions. Some of them are about the race. Some of them are about Tusk. He has feelings about Tusk that he has been professionally managing for three days and the professionalism is showing some strain.
side_quests.mechanics: No check required. The interview is flavor. If a player says something genuinely interesting or funny, Voss will quote it in next year's pre-race commentary. Perris Tan is there too. He is calmer in person than on the commentary. He immediately asks if he can meet the wolves.
side_quests.reward: The party becomes part of the race's official record. Next year they will be mentioned in the pre-race coverage. Perris Tan and Tusk may have a moment.

side_quests.name: The Cornell Connection
side_quests.hook: Cornell is a market town at the northern end of the kingdom's main trading road. The race ends here but the road continues south through the Dragonspine pass all the way to the lowland cities. Several people at the post-race gathering are not here for the race — they are here because the race brings traffic and traffic brings opportunity. At least two of them have work they would pay for. At least one of them has information they would trade. The Stranger from the Corner Table at the Cracked Tusk is here. They nod at the party across the square. They do not approach.
side_quests.mechanics: DC 12 Investigation in the crowd to identify the two people with work to offer. DC 15 to identify the information broker. The Stranger will meet the party in private if approached — DC 10 Persuasion to arrange it.
side_quests.reward: Leads into future sessions. The Cornell trade road as a campaign hook. The Stranger's identity if you have decided what it is.

locations.name: Trollgranite Outpost
locations.desc: A permanent trading post run by an affiliate of the Trollgranite family from Thig Dural Thane — Fess Trollgranite (Dwarf, she/her, 134) manages the Cornell location year-round. Sells provisions, mountain gear, and a selection of Thig Dural Thane manufactured goods including Bittermaster ironwork and Kegborn-forged tools. Prices are slightly higher than Zethel due to transport, but the quality is reliably good.
inventory: All standard adventuring gear
Cold weather gear — same selection as Kessa's, 10% higher prices
Bittermaster ironwork — tools, hardware, custom items available on 2-week commission
Kegborn forged blades — longsword 15GP, shortsword 10GP, handaxe 5GP
Trail provisions for the journey south — mountain-grade rations 1GP per week
Maps of the southern road to the lowland cities — 2GP each

side_quests.name: The Thig Dural Thane Connection
side_quests.hook: Fess mentions, if the conversation goes long enough, that there is unusual demand from Thig Dural Thane this season for a specific type of iron alloy that only comes from the eastern Dragonspine — not the race route, the other side of the mountain. She says this without apparent concern. She has been saying it for two seasons. She does not know why the demand has increased or where it is going once it arrives at Thig Dural Thane. The Thane has not explained. World-building thread.
side_quests.mechanics: DC 12 Investigation to identify this as unusual. The eastern Dragonspine is not a trade route — it's a mining corridor. DC 16 to connect it to any other information the party may have picked up about mountain activity.
side_quests.reward: A hook into Thig Dural Thane and the eastern Dragonspine for future sessions.

locations.name: The Iron Scales
locations.desc: The Prize Hall keeps the kingdom's certified weights, and it keeps them downstairs — a low stone undercroft, cold in every season, where the scale beams hang on chains from the ceiling and the standard measures sit in a locked iron press. For nine nights of finish week the beams come off their chains, a circle is chalked on the flagstones, and Cornell's oldest institution that nobody south of the pass has heard of opens for business. Every bout is entered on the register upstairs — same ledger, same seal, same office as the race results. The house is certified honest. That is the joke, and it is also true, and it is the second part that unsettles anyone who came up from Zethel expecting a basement. Where Sable signals someone near the door when large bets come in, Ilsa Truemark posts her line on a board and does not move it once the room has seen it. She has no tells. She has a ledger.
locations.proprietor: Halda Brakestone, Dwarf, she/her, 208 — Cornell Weights & Measures, and the holder of the circle's charter
staff: Ilsa Truemark, Dwarf, she/her, 168 — the book; Ithara Glassman's Cornell consortium keeps it under charter while the betting hall itself is still packed in canvas down in Zethel
Vurl Kettleback, Dwarf, he/him, 141 — the weighmaster's hammer-hand, and the house's champion
Emmet Wray, Human, he/him, 44 — the chirurgeon at the rope; the charter will not let a bout start without one
Little Ash, Halfling, she/her, 41 — works the door between her own nights on the card
rules: Every Bout on the Register
No Blades
No Spells on the Chalk
A Chirurgeon at the Rope
The House Pays on the Register, Never on a Handshake
Wolves Welcome on the Stair

side_quests.name: A Place on the Card
side_quests.hook: Finish week fills Cornell with people who just spent five days being carried over a mountain by dogs and have a great deal left over. The circle is where it goes. If the party finished at all, Halda Brakestone sends word to the Finish Line Inn before the celebration is properly underway: there is a line open on the register with their name at the head of it. If they WON, the charter has a custom for that — the house puts the winning sled up against Vurl Kettleback, and the whole town comes down the stair to watch.
side_quests.mechanics: DC 13 Athletics or Acrobatics to qualify — the same bar Zethel sets, because it is the same charter language, borrowed. A chip earned in Sable's basement is honored here on sight: the register reads it, Ilsa prices it, and nobody asks the party to prove it twice. The purse runs to double what the southern houses pay — Run the Table › Fighting Pits › The Iron Scales carries the live line, the roll-off, and the book.
side_quests.reward: The purse, at Cornell's rate. A line in the register that will outlive the party. Vurl Kettleback's respect, which he gives once and does not take back.

side_quests.name: What the Register Remembers
side_quests.hook: Eleven years of bouts, kept by the same office that keeps the race records, in a building where the two ledgers sit one floor apart. Halda will hand the register over without being asked — it is a public document and she is visibly proud of it. Read against Baern Ironquill's race records upstairs it agrees on everything except Year Four, where the register carries three nights of bouts the race records do not have at all. One name on those nights has been struck through and re-entered in a different hand.
side_quests.mechanics: No check to read it — DC 12 Investigation to pull a single fighter's whole career out of it, DC 16 to notice the Year Four discrepancy against the records upstairs. Halda says only that the charter was suspended for three nights that year, and that the suspension is on the register too, which it is. Who was struck through is your call — it pairs with The Race Records upstairs and with whatever the fey stretch did to Year Four.
side_quests.reward: A second thread into the Year Four gap, from a direction Baern does not control. Halda as a contact who keeps records and does not lie about them.

vestriLedger.note: Vestri the Night Hag keeps a ledger of what the party has given and taken. The pool tallies across her scenes; her disposition at the Landlord’s Farewell reads from it.

tiers.label: +3 or more
tiers.detail: Specific intel on all three Day 5 switchbacks. To Corben: “Good guests this year.” He allows himself one breath.

tiers.label: +1 to +2
tiers.detail: One piece of genuine Day 5 intel — her choice. Something true and specific.

tiers.label: Negative
tiers.detail: Something true and unpleasant about the road ahead, or about them. She retreats into the cave.

rolls.notes: Advantage: Ranger / Druid / Path of the Pack Barbarian. Fail by 5+: 1d4 bite.
Starting position. Tell players where they sit in the pack.
Fail: saber-toothed tiger enters camp. Pass: it's out there but moves on.
Drive off without combat. Corben watches. He is not helping.
Fail: bear is on trail. Pass: tracks only + bear on distant ridge.
Identify sow with cubs, back away safely. Fast speed past her: DC 13 DEX save.
Fail: full crossing. Pass: tail end only.
Hold the wolves. Fail: sled off path → DC 12 DEX → Fail: −2 pos + repair.
Glimmerkin contacts regardless. Check determines her mood.

rolls.roll: DC 15 Investigation / Sleight of Hand DC 13
rolls.notes: Untangle harness. Fail either: −1 position for the day.
Success: Fenra handles it. Fail: combat.
Fail: she's in the path. Pass: she approaches anyway. Check = leverage.
Only appears if party is 1st / last / had dramatic reversal.
Check affects his mood. He always demands toll regardless.
A story he hasn't heard. He's heard a lot.
He allows two tries if you're amusing.
Success: blesses passing (advantage on next Luck Check). She can't stop them by force.
She appears regardless. Check affects mood. Engaged seriously: +2 positions.
12d8 cold. Please talk players out of this.

rolls.roll: DC 13 CON save — ALL party + Corben
rolls.notes: Fail: 0 HP. The Hollowmourn cannot leave her switchback. Turning Undead works.
Take the reins. Party decides: stabilize Corben or push for finish.

guides.guide:
CORBEN VASH — FULL NPC PROFILE Personality: Brash, confident, deeply loyal to his wolf pack. Speaks in a slightly old-fashioned dialect ("I be Corben Vash..."). Reads as arrogant but backs it up — he genuinely IS the best. Why he's last: Every other racer was afraid of the wolves. Corben's fine with this. Stats (if needed):
Corben Vash — Human Ranger (Hunter) 7
HP: 52 | AC: 15 | Initiative: +3
STR 14, DEX 16, CON 13, INT 11, WIS 15, CHA 12
Attacks: Longbow +6 (1d8+3), Shortsword +6 (1d6+3)
Skills: Animal Handling +8, Nature +4, Survival +6, Perception +5 Dire Wolf Pack (6 wolves):
NAMES: Fenra, Greyback, Tusk, Shadowfoot, Blizzard, Runt
Stats: use the Dire Wolf — HP 37, AC 14, Bite +5 (2d6+3, DC 13 STR or knocked prone)
They will NOT attack party members unless provoked or badly failed Animal Handling (-5 or more). Key Corben quotes:
• On his team: "They're family. You hurt them, we have a problem."
• On the race: "Five days. No complaining. No stopping unless I say stop."
• If party is losing: "I've come back from worse. Trust the wolves."
guides.vane:
THE RIVAL PALADIN — RECURRING NPC Name: Lord Aldric Vane, Paladin of the Radiant Court
Race: Human | Class: Paladin 5
HP: 45 | AC: 20 (full plate + shield) Personality: Pompous, entitled, genuinely believes he is doing everyone a favor by participating. His "retinue" are servants, not adventurers — Bethalyn correctly ruled them ineligible. Role in adventure:
• Scene 1: Seen exiting Registration tent, unhappy
• Guide tent: Arguing with Corben (Corben's refusing him) • Optional: He finds a team at the last minute — becomes the rival racer throughout the 5 days
• Day 5: Could pass the party if they've been struggling, raising stakes Key quote: "I assure you, my companions are MORE than capable. This is an outrage." If he finds a team: His team is all hired muscle, good but not experienced as adventurers. They'll likely crack on Day 4.

stakes.title: The stakes, by tier
stakes.note: The purse and the mysterious bonus prize scale with the league the party races in. Corben's 20% and the four-way 80% split read from the same purse; the bonus item is distributed by party vote, as ever. Ithara's odds and Vestri's gift tiers stand as written — they price reputation and courtesy, not gold.

1.bonus: The rumor mill as written — vorpal blades, wish spells, wands of untold power; the DM’s relic, revealed at the Prize Hall.
1.label: as written

2.bonus: The year’s rumor made real at VERY RARE — whichever tale the table fed, the Commissioner’s locked room holds a very rare item to match it.
2.label: the rumor runs true-adjacent

3.bonus: THE VORPAL BLADE IS REAL. It is in the locked room, and Baern has not slept properly since it arrived.
3.label: the vorpal blade is real

4.bonus: THE WISH IS REAL — one wish, held in a sealed scroll the Racing Commissioner breaks at the ceremony. Every champion team in the north entered this year. This is why.
4.label: the wish is real

stakes.completionNote: Every sled that crosses is paid the completion purse — first across to last in — because Cornell has never sent a finisher home with nothing and has no intention of starting. It splits exactly as the winning purse does: the guide's cut off the top, the remainder among the racers who actually rode. The figures below are the book's; a Commissioner who wants the year to mean more can raise them at the ceremony and nobody in Cornell will argue.

annual.note: The race is an ANNUAL winter event — the annual-return kit for a table that comes back. The Year counter and last-year history live in race state; at Year 2+ every encounter slot offers its alternates (the signature NPCs remember the party rather than being replaced), Corben greets returning racers, the team they beat by one place carries a grudge, and a defending champion is raced dirty.

guide.y2: Corben is at the same camp table, and this year he stands up when he sees them. "Same terms. Twenty percent. The wolves do be remembering you — Fenra has been watching the road three days." The negotiation scene plays as a reunion: no vetting, no argument, the contract signed over a shared meal. The wolves greet known racers by shoulder-leaning, which is how a dire wolf hugs.
guide.y3: By the third year there is no negotiation at all — the contract is on the table, already signed, held down by a stone. "You do be knowing where the harness hangs." Corben has told the town they are HIS team; Bethalyn lists them in the registry as returning contenders; the Cracked Tusk has opinions about their odds. Home is a strong word. It is also the right one.

grudgeCalls: And there's the story of the year, folks — {rival} finished ONE place behind {party} last season and they have not stopped talking about it. Watch those two on the switchbacks.
{rival} drew the start line right beside {party} this morning and the LOOK that passed between those sleds — that is last year's finish order, still burning.
A year of training, folks, and every hour of it aimed at one sled: {rival} wants {party}, and the mountain is about to find out how much.
championCalls: And wearing the champion's harness rings — {party}! Defending the title, folks, and every rough rider on this mountain knows exactly where they are.
The defending champions {party} at the line — and if you think the field forgot last year's finish, you have never met a sled racer with a losing ticket.
{party} comes back as the team to beat, and on the Dragonspine, being the team to beat means being the team they TRY to break. Buckle in.
And at the line, the reigning {title} — {party}! They rode that mountain to the bottom last winter and came back to do it again, which is either confidence or a grudge against geology.
The {title} return, folks. {party}, who this time last year were just another sled at Zethel, and who are now the reason twenty-nine crews spent the summer training.
invitationalCalls: THE CHAMPIONS' INVITATIONAL, folks — thirty title-holders on one mountain, no easy sleds in this field, and the pass does not care about any of their trophies.
Every sled in this draw has won it before. The Invitational field is the meanest, canniest, DIRTIEST start line this race has ever formed — and the crowd came for exactly that.

invitational.label: The Champions' Invitational
invitational.note: Unlocked once the party has won the race TWICE: an invitational year where the whole field is past champions. Every rival races canny and rough — the rough-rider draw runs six teams deep and everyone rides at champion aggression. The purse is the tier’s, doubled in prestige if not in coin; declining the invitation is itself a story.

defended: {party} DEFENDS IT — across the line first for the second year running, and the harness rings they came in wearing they are going home still wearing. Not one sled in this field wanted that sentence to read that way.
The title stays exactly where it was. {party} came to Cornell as champions and they leave as champions, and every team on this mountain spent five days trying to make that come out differently.

Defended. Say it out loud, folks — {party} carried the champion's target up the pass, took every rough rider this race could point at them, and crossed FIRST anyway. That is the hardest way there is to win this thing.
lost: And the title changes hands — {winner} take the Dragonspine, and {party} come home without the rings they carried up the pass. That is this race. It gives them to you and then it asks for them back.

{winner} are your new champions, folks. {party} defended for five days and came up short on the last one — and if you have never watched a champion lose a title, you have never heard a finish line go that quiet.

The reign ends at Cornell. {winner} first, {party} behind them, and tonight the rings go onto somebody else's harness. Nine years I have called this race and that walk off the ice has never once gotten easier to watch.
dynasty: {n} IN A ROW. Say it again — {n} straight years for {party}, and at this point the Dragonspine is not a race they enter, it is a road they own.
That is {n} consecutive and {wins} in the book, and folks, I want to be careful here, because I have called this race a long time and I do not use this word lightly. {party}. Dynasty.
{n} years running. Every sled in this draw came here knowing exactly who to beat and exactly how to do it, and {party} did it to them AGAIN. The mountain is starting to look like it takes requests.
crowned: AND THEY ARE CROWNED — {party} take the Dragonspine, and folks, you know what that makes them. SCALE CONQUERORS. Say it. They got up on the back of that mountain for five days and the mountain could not throw them.
{party}, first across at Cornell — and the title comes with it. The Dragonspine has a new set of {title}, and every one of them earned the word the only way it is ever earned: by staying on.

That is the finish, and that is a coronation. {party} are {title} now — souls who fought on the back of a monster and won — and the Prize Hall will have their name in the register before the wolves have stopped panting.

beats.arrival: They arrive as champions, and Zethel knows it before the wagon stops rolling. The bonfire crowd turns; somebody starts a slow clap that does not quite catch, which is somehow worse than if it had; two children run ahead to tell the registration tent. Nobody in this town is neutral about a title-holder — half of them want to buy the party a drink and the other half want to watch them lose.
beats.registration: Bethalyn does not ask their names. She has the form half-filled before they reach the table and turns it around with the pen already uncapped: "Champions of record. I still need four names and the guide's mark, I still need them within the hour, and no — the title does not move the deadline." She is pleased to see them. She would deny it under oath.
beats.tusk: Sable has had them at the top of her board since the broadsheets went out, and the line on them is short enough that everyone in the basement understands it: she is not offering value on a champion, she is offering the chance to say you were there. If the party goes to read the chalk she does not look up. "Everybody's money is on you. That's not a compliment. That's a target."

milestones.note: Anniversaries are keyed to the party's own Year counter, not to an in-world jubilee — they fire at Year 5, Year 10, and every fifth year after that (15, 20, 25...), the later ones reusing the ten-year material. Each carries booth calls that land at the horn, a beat for Corben, and a line for how the two towns have changed toward them.

y5.label: Five years on this mountain
calls: Five years, folks. FIVE. {party} have been coming up this pass since before half this field owned a sled, and the Dragonspine has not managed to keep them yet.
That is a five-year sled on the line. Perris — five years. The mountain has had two thousand chances at them and it is still waiting on the first one that sticks.
y5.guide: Five years in, Corben does the thing he has never once done: he introduces them. Not to a person — to the wolves. Formally, one at a time, by name and by lineage, the way you would introduce family at a wedding. It takes six minutes. Nobody interrupts him. At the end he says "Right. That's done," and will not explain it, then or ever.
y5.town: Zethel has quietly stopped treating them as visitors. Oswin keeps their table without being asked and gets short with them if they sit anywhere else; the Prize Hall clerk in Cornell writes their sled name from memory and spells it right the first time. Somewhere in five years of register lines they stopped being a team that runs the race and became part of what the race is.

y10.label: Ten years — and every fifth after
calls: Ten years on this mountain, folks. TEN. There are racers in this field who were children when {party} first came through that gate — they grew up watching the sled they are about to line up against.
A decade. {party} have run this pass ten times, I have called every one of them, and I am telling you: the mountain stopped trying to break them a while ago and started trying to keep them.
y10.guide: Ten years, and Corben has gone quiet about it in the way that means it matters. Somewhere in the negotiation that is no longer a negotiation he mentions — to the table, not to them — that he has guided this race longer than anyone else alive, and has taken exactly one team up it more than three times. Then he changes the subject fast enough to leave a mark.
y10.town: The register goes back eleven years and they are in ten of them. Baern Ironquill, Commissioner since Year One and fully intending to die in the position, has started reading their line at the ceremony without checking the page. In Cornell they are no longer a team that wins the race. They are something the race has.

title.name: Scale Conquerors
title.meaning: Souls who fought on the back of a monster to victory.
title.note: The winners of the Dragonspine Mountains “Dog” Sled Race are the SCALE CONQUERORS. The mountain is the monster — five days spent on its back, over its scales, with it trying the whole way to shake them off — and a team that crosses the line at Cornell first has beaten the Dragonspine, not the other twenty-nine sleds. That is why the title says nothing about racing. The booth uses it when it names the reigning champions at the line, the towns use it the way towns use a name they are proud of, and a team wears it until somebody takes it off them the following winter. It is PLURAL and it is the whole sled — you do not get on the back of a mountain alone.

specialDocs.001_T_A_Bridge_Guards:
Bridge Guards

In the middle of each bridge of the Twins Channel is a grand structure called the Twins Channel Station. The center Station houses one more room on a third floor where the rest have two stories, but are otherwise identical. Ten foot tall and wide arches in a row of three a few feet apart with three sets of stairs going up to the base of those arches. You can see clearly through the building on the other side, the exit looks identical to the entrance on this side. One of the first things you notice are the uniforms of the soldiers that are guarding those arches, eight on each side and three in between each set of stairs. The uniform being yellow and of a different cut than that of the Sovereign or the Council of Twelve guard uniforms.

#### Interaction with Guards

- Very professional

- DC20 persuasion to convince one of them to talk on duty

- Otherwise met with “we’re not allowed to have conversations on duty. Please move along.” 

- Any mention of the other guard is met with contempt

- They don't train enough

- It’d be us doing the fighting if any real trouble came to the Twins

#### Perception on sight of the building within 30 feet

- 30

- 25

- Two such signs next to the stairs say Arrivals and on the other side of the building Departures

- 20

- The guards are very disciplined in their actions

- There are several signs showing where visitors should go based on the actions they want to take

- 15

- There are stairs that go up to the second floor on each side of the building

- There is a line of guards stemming from the end of each side of the oval desk in an alternating facing forward and facing backward pattern ensuring both direction from the doors are covered and no one can pass their line without someone seeing

- They are an arms length apart

- 10 

- There are doors that can be closed that are just barely visible and well hidden to make the building look inviting

- There is a large oval of a desk, broken by a space on either side where a person could walk through, in the middle of the expansive room

- in the center of this desk are 12 clerks working at each side 

- each set of 4 clerks has a queue dedicated to it

- guards are directing the flow of those who wish to move into or out of each side of the Twins.

Upon entering the building these checks go down by five.

#### First Contact

Upon entering the building you are greeted by a guard. You can see that there are other guards performing this greeting duty  as he states:

“Welcome to the [East][Central][West] Twins Hub. I am Specialist Hobbs of the Bridge Guard. Are you seeking passage, travel or immigration?”

Hobbs is a Human, 22, He/Him

Just then the changing of the guard starts. From the stairs to either side a double file of guards trotts down and moves into position breaking to either side of the single file line of guards positioned next to the oval desk. Each file faces the direction of the closest set of archways. The middle file then faces toward the wall of the stairs from which their relief came and starts to trot toward and up the stairs. Once the last of the file has left the enclosure of the other two files, they take two steps backward and are in the same pattern the previous file was in. Both sets of guards are changed in sync.

Hobbs:

“It’s a sight to behold, but please, are you seeking passage, travel or immigration?”

Hobbs will direct them to the correct queue for whichever they choose

#### Passage 

Note - Doni Forehare, mielario interacted as given the writ and said “the empress will here of this”...

creates moonwalk with his exit.

- The passage desk is always to the left

- The toll is 1s

- Special papers can be drawn up to change this with a process that requires a sponsor from either city. A list of the approved sponsors are available.

- Office of the Sovereign

- Office of the Council of Twelve

- Captain of the Guard for Ru Ailmen

- Captain of the Guard for Yuvl Ilmern

- Representative of Clearwater Co.

- Representative of Banminster Co.

- Representative of Applesor Co.

#### Travel

- Ship Charter

- Sailing Ship Ocean Travel 8 GP

- Galley Ocean Travel 12 GP

- Locations available

- Port of Beni Ali, Corasant Coast, Tellason

- Port of Heerisim, Turum Coast, Telleson

- Isle of Rockporth

- Sierra Archipelago (Large Chain of Volcanoes)

- Locations unavailable (unsafe)

- Broth Isle

- Anywhere along the Serrated Island Chain

- Teleportation Circle

- There are two teleportation circle rooms set up in the barrics above the Twins Hub Stations

- One is for Arrival the other is for Departure

- One Mage is in charge of each Circle 

- Each circle is heavily guarded toward the center of the building

- There are two berrics, one on each side of the building with a lead lined iron wall in between

- When you reach the top of the stairs there is a long hallway with two doors immediately to your left and right. At the end of the hallway two identical doors flank the hallway and then there is a large iron door opposite the entrance with hooks for two bars which can be seen on the floor on each side of the hallway laid on each side halfway down for the departure door. For the arrival door they are barred.

- The Central Twins Hub 

- within the berrics (all four) there are stairs to a third floor which is known as the Empress’ Teleportation Circle

- This is not common knowledge as no one is allowed up there

- Only through a leak from the guards or an official who already knows would be the way to gain this information

- Travel by Appointment

- Only announced travel from one major city to another is allowed.

- Flat rate of 100 GP

- Locations Available

- Bethal

#### Immigration

specialDocs.001_T_A_Twins_Channel_Underwater:
Twins Channel Underwater

While traversing the bottom of the channel there is a place adventures can stumble upon. While dodging the large patches of seaweed that reach ten to twenty feet upward and boulders that can be ten feet wide and bigger there is a 20 x 20 foot altar on the channel floor. There seem to be four 10 foot crescent moon shaped plinths facing curve side inward all pointing at a somewhat tarnished and mossy red plinth standing at chest height with a purple chest sitting atop it.

There is a magical trigger when anyone passes the plane outside of the crescent plinths in toward the red plinth with the chest. This activates a homing signal for  giant sharks that roam this channel and summons two water elementals.

The box is magically sealed to the plinth though that spell can easily be dispelled. The chest is trapped and locked. Identify spell will reveal the Chest is a magical item as well as the complexity level of the Trap and the Lock including the 24 hour reset.

# Chest

Trap

- DC 20 investigation to spot

Cyrus Ryukyu
