twins.title: The Twins
twins.intro: Ru Ailmen and Yuvl Ilmern — the twin cities of the southwest, capital of the realm of Aria, facing each other across the Twins Channel beneath three great arched bridges. A city almost as big as the imperial city on either shore: miles of stone buildings, roof tiles in every color of the Tile Code, floating mooring docks and stairs lining the channel walls. The party arrives here in Chapter 4 — and if the campaign runs its course, this is where they make their home.
twins.tileCodeNote: Respect the gray ones. — a riverboat captain's advice
highlights: The central road shopping crawl — arcane mysteries behind impossible walls, a master smith who works mithral, and a market matron whose diamond sack never seems to empty.
The sick house — an open treatment room where a party healer can empty the ward of injuries, and a staff that remembers generosity.
The honest bureaucracy — banking thorough enough to eat a full day, and a city worth loving for it.
The underbelly — a warehouse contact, a 380-foot shaft elevator, and the dwarven-carved sewers that tie the Twins together.
Home — a deed, a thirty-day deadline, and a house in Yuvl Ilmern with more beneath it than anyone guessed.

cities.name: Ru Ailmen
cities.note: The Sovereign's city — one ruler, one palace, and the Sovereign Docks at the northern tip. The party's port of entry in Chapter 4, and the first Twin they walk.

pages.name: Ebony Camp
pages.atDoor: Blue roof tiles mark this as an inn, per the Tile Code. The three-story stone structure is adorned with beautiful worked-iron fenced balconies on the second and third stories. Through the front door is a common room with a small stage in the left corner and six tables seating four and six. Behind the bar at the back stands the proprietor, Rinys Glowseeker — a stout halfling in a blue coat, white ruffled undershirt, and brown britches wrapped in a bleach-white apron.

people.name: Rinys Glowseeker
people.note: Halfling, she/her, 180 — behind the bar most hours

people.name: Panver Applehands
people.note: Halfling, he/him, 122 — cooking here 50+ years; started as an apprentice

people.name: Xanvyre Glendance, Trynrana Stoutflower, Maelile Wildearth, Gelcey Warmsurge, Ulvias Fatwood, Kasnan Rosefinger

voice.cue: Warm host's patter, but she reads every newcomer head to toe before the first hello — an old professional habit she can't shed.
Talks recipes and inn history if drawn out; he remembers every proprietor back fifty years.

items.name: Second floor (6 rooms)
items.note: 16 gp for a tenday

items.name: Third floor (4 rooms)
items.note: 34 gp for a tenday

items.name: Private dining
items.note: Two rooms off the stage hall — seats 12 and 8

quirks: DM only — this inn is the operational hub of the Moonlight Strategy thieves' guild. Off the main dining room, a first-floor storage room hides a secret door to a closet with a hatch: a sturdy ladder drops thirty feet into a domed den carved from the island's bedrock.
DM only — Rinys Glowseeker is the den's gatekeeper and a former Master Thief of the Moonlight Strategy. Entry goes through her, always. See the Moonlight Strategy page for entry rules.
hooks: Cross-reference: Moonlight Strategy (Thieves Den, this city) for the den beneath, its roster, and how entry is vouched.

pages.name: Triple Seaside
pages.atDoor: Blue roof tiles, per the Tile Code. A comfortable stone inn of the Twins pattern: common room and bar below, rooms for rent above. The proprietor Dargwen Loneshadow keeps the house; the smell of Shara Roanton's cooking carries to the street.

pages.name: Ancient Blossom
pages.atDoor: Blue roof tiles, per the Tile Code. This three-story stone structure wears wooden balconies on its upper floors. The common room holds a small stage in the right corner and five tables — four seating four, one seating six. Behind the bar, the elderly halfling proprietor Bresira Deepwind reads a leather-bound book at most hours of the day when not tending customers.

people.name: Tipton Septon, Xivyre Riverstride, Nefira Forebrush
Brelile Rumblegrove, Unaris Applecrest, Sanys Commonflower, Faycey Mistfinger, Yesbrix Stoutspell, Yesda Leamane
people.note: Halflings, 39–67 — the Septon family and a halfling crew run this house together

voice.cue: Marks her page with one finger and peers over the book before speaking. Never hurried. If asked what she's reading, she'll trade the answer for your story.

items.name: Rooms, second & third floor
items.note: 16 gp for a tenday

pages.tableHook: A natural first-night house in Ru Ailmen — Bresira shows guests to their rooms, and the common room below invites a party to gather, compare the day's discoveries, and send off magical messages of warning.

pages.name: Sapphire Horizon
pages.atDoor: Blue roof tiles, per the Tile Code. A stone inn of the Twins pattern kept by Idaris Tallfingers: common room and bar below, rooms above.

pages.name: Saffron Paradise
pages.atDoor: Blue roof tiles, per the Tile Code. A stone inn of the Twins pattern kept by Elikis Underbottle: common room and bar below, rooms above.

pages.name: Pleasant Hill
pages.atDoor: Blue roof tiles, per the Tile Code. A stone inn of the Twins pattern kept by Jisdalar Morlar: common room and bar below, rooms above.

pages.name: The Rare Coin
pages.atDoor: Red roof tiles mark the tavern, per the Tile Code. This sprawling two-story channel-side stone building on East Channel Street throws its shutters wide beside double doors. An aisle splits two sets of six round tables. Through the mirrored back door and windows: a partly covered patio with six more tables, four snug against a hip-height wall — gulls wheel above the dampness of the Channel beyond. Two bars run the middle of the building to the back windows, serving anyone who walks up. “The Rules” are chalked on a board above each bar.

people.name: Saleigh, Ximia, Chennys & Eolyse Brightmeadow
people.note: Halflings, she/her, 48–58 — the whole house is one family

voice.cue: Will not leave from behind the bar — the sole exception being to eject a customer who breaks the Rules. Order at the bar or at the windows; nobody comes to you.
Points at the chalkboard before answering a complaint: “No Credit. No Fighting.” Family teasing flows constantly between the two bars.

quirks: DM only — members of the Moonlight Strategy have been known to congregate here of late. The tell: a crescent moon with an adjacent four-pointed star tattooed in the web of the left hand, easily hidden by pressing thumb to forefinger.
hooks: Cross-reference: Moonlight Strategy (Thieves Den, this city) — this tavern is where a streetwise character can first find the guild's edges.

pages.name: The Lively Melons
pages.atDoor: Red roof tiles, per the Tile Code. A Twins-pattern tavern kept by Ostran Thistlehollow: round tables, a busy bar, and the Rules chalked above it.

pages.name: The Kind Boulder
pages.atDoor: Red roof tiles, per the Tile Code. A Twins-pattern tavern kept by Yardal Truecreek: round tables, a busy bar, and the Rules chalked above it.

pages.name: The Itchy Butcher
pages.atDoor: Red roof tiles, per the Tile Code. A Twins-pattern tavern kept by Finkin Smoothsurge: round tables, a busy bar, and the Rules chalked above it.

pages.name: The Unknown Llama
pages.atDoor: Red roof tiles, per the Tile Code. A Twins-pattern tavern kept by Sazana Cinderlade: round tables, a busy bar, and the Rules chalked above it.

pages.name: The Hare's Haversack
pages.atDoor: Yellow roof tiles mark the general store, per the Tile Code. Adventuring and dungeoneering gear fills shelves left and right — coils of rope, pitons and grappling hooks beside lanterns, quivers, buckets of ball bearings, and so much more. Wimia Stillberry sits at a desk in the corner beside a beaded threshold.

voice.cue: Greets every patron with a hearty “Hello and welcome to the Hare's Haversack! Something for every adventurer!”

items.name: Adventuring Gear
items.note: Most of it is in stock

items.name: Not carried
items.note: Acid, Ammunition, Antitoxin, Arcane focus, Druidic focus, Healer's Kit, Holy Symbols, Holy Water, Potion of Healing, Spellbook

pages.name: The Antique Tusk
pages.atDoor: Yellow roof tiles, per the Tile Code. Adventuring and dungeoneering gear on shelves left and right — rope, pitons, grappling hooks, lanterns, quivers, ball bearings by the bucket. Duzik Giantaxe sits at a desk against the middle of the back wall of the single-room shop.

voice.cue: A nod of the head and a gruff “The Antique Tusk has everything you need for an adventure beyond our city walls. Welcome, welcome.”

items.name: Adventuring Gear
items.note: Most of it is in stock

items.name: Not carried
items.note: Acid, Ammunition, Antitoxin, Arcane focus, Druidic focus, Healer's Kit, Holy Symbols, Holy Water, Potion of Healing, Spellbook

pages.name: Clean Getaway
pages.atDoor: Purple roof tiles mark the magic shop, per the Tile Code. A shop for those with an interest in the arcane — scrolls above all, with some magical outerwear and maybe a wand or staff on occasion. Cellica Theyra stands behind a bar-height counter that runs the length of the room across from the door, and the day's offerings are chalked on a board behind her.

people.name: Cellica Theyra
people.note: Elf, she/her — behind the counter whenever anyone enters

voice.cue: Never touches the merchandise until the ritual is complete: coin on the counter first. She quotes contract scroll work with quiet confidence — “A free quote. Give me a day, perhaps two, for the research.”

items.name: High-quality incense, parchment reams, inks & pens
Contract scroll work
items.note: 24–48 hours for research

items.name: Cloak of Invisibility
items.gated: Only offered on a second or later visit

quirks: DC 18 Perception — this room has no door to a back room, yet the space accounts for only a few steps to the counter and the building looks bigger from the outside.

The payment ritual: once an item's price is placed on the counter, the item floats out from the seemingly solid wall into Cellica's hands. She hands it over — and the money on the counter is gone as if it were never there.
Repeat custom is rewarded: the finest stock only appears on later visits. Let returning parties notice new chalk on the board.
hooks: Sister establishment in spirit to Bits & PCs down the road — same impossible interior, same counter ritual. Players who notice may start asking the right questions about the Twins' arcane trade.

pages.name: Bits & PCs
pages.atDoor: Purple roof tiles, per the Tile Code. A shop for those with an interest in the arcane — this one specializing in weaponized magic and potions. Ailmar Dakian stands behind a bar-height counter running the length of the room, the stock chalked on a board behind him.

people.name: Ailmar Dakian
people.note: Elf, he/him — behind the counter whenever anyone enters

voice.cue: Recites the arrow list like a sommelier — effect first, price second. Commission work gets the same line every time: “A free quote. The research takes a day, perhaps two.”

items.name: High-quality incense, parchment reams, inks & pens
Poison Cloud arrow
items.note: On hit: poisonous gas, 10-ft sphere, lightly obscures; lasts 10 rounds unless strong wind. 1d4 poison entering or starting a turn in the cloud

items.name: Magefire arrow
items.note: Ignites when fired; +1d6 fire, lights unattended flammables

items.name: Explosive arrow
items.note: On hit: DC 15 Dex save, 10-ft radius, 2d10 fire; ignites unattended flammables

items.name: Ice arrow
items.note: +1d8 cold; DC 15 Con or −10 ft speed and disadvantage on Dex saves, 3 rounds (no stack)

items.name: Acid arrow
items.note: +1d8 acid; DC 15 Con or −2 AC and disadvantage on Con saves, 3 rounds (no stack)

items.name: Thunderclap arrow
items.note: On hit: DC 15 Con, 10-ft radius, 2d8 thunder, pushed 5 ft and prone; loose objects pushed 5 ft

items.name: Lightning arrow
items.note: Streak in its wake: DC 15 Dex for creatures within 5 ft of the line, 1d8 lightning

items.name: Contract arrow work
items.note: 24–48 hours for research

items.name: Defender Longsword
items.gated: Only offered on a third or later visit

quirks: DC 18 Perception — no door to a back room, yet the interior is a few steps deep and the building looks bigger from the outside.
The same payment ritual as Clean Getaway: coin on the counter, and the item floats out of the seemingly solid wall into the proprietor's hands while the money vanishes as if it were never there.
Repeat custom is rewarded — the Defender only chalks itself onto the board for a party on its third visit.
hooks: The two impossible shops (this and Clean Getaway) share a trick and a discretion. Whether they share an owner, a wall-space, or a guild is left to the DM.
pages.tableHook: The Ring of Warmth waits behind this counter — and the counter ritual that comes with the sale makes an impression that outlasts the ring. Play it whole.

pages.name: Crazy Chestnut Potions
pages.atDoor: Green roof tiles mark the apothecary, per the Tile Code. Alytria Torra stands behind a counter halfway down the building. Behind her, low shelves of stoppered glass bottles flank a central pathway; beyond those, counters with cauldrons and labeled shelves of all manner of potion ingredients.

voice.cue: Answers questions about a brew with the ingredient list first, the price second, and a raised eyebrow if you ask to hurry the cauldron.

items.name: Cauldron time
items.note: For guest brewing — DC 10 proficiency test required

quirks: Guests may rent cauldron time to brew their own — the DC 10 proficiency check is Alytria satisfying herself you won't blow a hole in her shop.

pages.name: Trusty Rocket
pages.atDoor: Green roof tiles, per the Tile Code. Gwenrin Fadi stands behind a counter halfway down the building — the same trusted layout as any Twins apothecary: stoppered bottles on low shelves, cauldrons and labeled ingredients behind.

voice.cue: Proud of carrying the strongest bottle in the city — she'll mention the Supreme before you ask, and watch your face when she names the price.

items.name: Cauldron time
items.note: For guest brewing — DC 10 proficiency test required

pages.name: Barbedbane's Forge and Arms and Armor Shop
pages.atDoor: A sprawling single-story forge and storefront — the ring of hammers announces it before any roof tile could. The storefront is minded by three apprentices; the master works the forge behind.

people.name: Dornaek Barbedbane
people.note: Dwarf, he/him, 239 — one of the few smiths in the realm who knows how to handle mithral

people.name: Ted Mable & Jeff Mable
people.note: Humans, he/him, 22 and 25 — front of house

people.name: Malon Umena
people.note: Elf, he/him, 49 — front of house; the one to see for pho-armor (worked wooden armor)

voice.cue: Only emerges from the forge for serious commissions. Talks metal, not pleasantries — quote a weight or an alloy and you have his attention.
Handle the rack stock cheerfully and defer anything custom: “That'd be the master's work. He'll want to meet you.”

items.name: Mithral Half Plate +1, made to order
items.note: Two months on commission

items.name: Pho-armor (wooden armor)
items.note: Malon Umena's specialty

quirks: Mithral work draws customers from across the realm — a party asking after it will be measured, literally and figuratively.
pages.tableHook: Any shopping day stops hard at this forge — a master blacksmith who knows how to handle mithral will turn browsing into commissioning if the party lets him talk.
pages.tile: No code — watch for the smoke

pages.name: North Docs Market
pages.atDoor: Orange marks the market quarter, per the Tile Code — though the North Docks Market needs no tiles: a sprawling dockside maze shaded by canvas tarps, its stalls permanent fixtures of heavy canvas and plank walls. All manner of trinkets, baubles, artifacts, food, and services. Some stall keepers sleep beside their wares; others pack their valuables home each night.

people.name: Bethal Kurneal Shaseth
people.note: Dragonborn, she/her, 74 — sells trinkets and baubles at the back of her stall from a rocking chair

voice.cue: Asked about diamonds, she croaks that her baubles are nicer than the diamonds — then sells you the diamonds anyway.

After showing anyone diamonds for the first time she always finds a reason to rise — reaching for some trinket — and looms to her full seven feet, flexing biceps that never lost their strength. The slouch and the robes are camouflage.

items.name: Large diamonds
items.note: Always at least 5 on hand — the burlap sack by the rocking chair seems replenishable

items.name: Medium diamonds
items.note: Always at least 7 on hand

items.name: Food, services, artifacts, oddments
items.note: DM's discretion — nearly anything mundane can be found with an hour's wander

quirks: DM only — Bethal is a battle-hardened fighter hiding her bulk behind robes and a deliberate slouch. Where the diamonds keep coming from is a thread the table can pull or leave.
hooks: Diamonds at reliable prices make this the city's quiet lifeline for revivify and raise-dead components — word of mouth among adventurers points here.
pages.tableHook: A party hunting diamonds gets pointed to an old lady who sells baubles — and meets the loom-and-flex. Give her the room; tables talk about her for years.

pages.name: Flower Carnival
pages.atDoor: A small traveling carnival camped in the open — wagons set as trade stalls, canvas shades on poles out front, and barkers calling the games.
quirks: A traveling fixture - an entity of its own, and it may not be in the same place (or the same city) on a return visit. The full carnival - roster, voices, wares, and the midway - lives in Side Quests > The Flower Carnival.
hooks: Run the games live from Run the Table > Carnival Games; the whole entity - who is here, what they sell, and every game's rules and prizes - lives in Side Quests > The Flower Carnival.

pages.name: Ru Ailmen Sick House
pages.atDoor: A long, simple one-story building, white-washed stone under a blue and yellow tiled roof. The entrance opens to a receiving room where a healer in white robes triages patients, the less severe waiting in chairs. Through double doors: a treatment room of twelve beds, six a side. A door at the back leads to a single-table room where life-threatening wounds take utmost priority.

people.name: Qicaryn Humbleman, Thamprys Proudwoods, Chenree Goodflower
Valeigh Highshadow, Uvifice Keencrest, Conace Heartspark, Davdak Swifthands

voice.cue: Receives everyone with the same calm question — who is hurt, and how badly — and will not be rushed out of triage order.
Accepts help and donations with grave courtesy; anything offered goes to the needs of the house, and she says so plainly.

items.name: Triage & treatment
items.note: The house treats first and settles after; donations sustain it

pages.tableHook: An open door: a healer who walks in unannounced will be shown to the treatment room — a broken leg and three lesser hurts waiting for kindness. Lahorn, Cror, two apprentices, and Wisys witness everything, and the staff here remember generosity.

pages.name: Sovereign Palace
pages.atDoor: Walking up Sovereign Road into the cul-de-sac, the Palace rises behind ten-foot walls, spires capped with brass cones, the multicolored tiled roofs of several keeps showing beyond. A huge arch with a drawn portcullis — large spikes pointed at their resting holes below — looks to be the only entrance. Sovereign Guards flank it, two on each side, spears all at the same angle at the shoulder, shortswords at their hips.

people.name: Quinpos Teabrace, Wenumo Bronzeshine, Zenbin Roseearth

voice.cue: Spears never waver from their angle. All business goes through the Sergeant on Duty in the open barrack — the guards at the arch redirect everything with the same practiced phrase and no second sentence.

quirks: DM only — past the portcullis, a 30-foot arched tunnel ends at iron-bound double doors; the wicket gate stands open on a paved courtyard. Barracks flank left and right housing a Sergeant on Duty, two Corporals, and twelve Specialists.
DM only — two murder holes in the tunnel ceiling, each accessible from one of the barracks. The on-duty barrack always keeps its door open, the Sergeant at the reception desk within.
hooks: The Sovereign's Steward has not been seen in a tenday — last seen on procession toward the Council of Twelve. Inquiries here run into a wall of protocol; the street knows more than the gate will say.

pages.name: Moonlight Strategy
pages.atDoor: “It's just a social club.” Those who like the finer things in life — and know how to get their fingers on them — join this club to rise in its ranks and find finer things. The Moonlight Strategy is transient by trade: without moving around they would be easily found, and that would be bad for business.

people.name: Xannys Truebridge
people.note: Halfling, she/her, 136 — keeps the office/bedroom at the back of the den

people.name: Valfer Keenlade
people.note: Halfling, he/him, 165 — usually at the den bar

people.name: Elielle Nimblesurge
people.note: Halfling, she/her, 123 — usually at the den bar

people.name: Ruglal Vuzrubor
people.note: Dark Elf, she/her, 200 — cowl drawn, tight leather gloves, watching the entrance from a darkened alcove over maps of manor houses

people.name: Pimric Cloudearth, Arvias Mooncloak, Halwrick Twilightcheeks, Davlan Littlemouse
Kat, Mosh, Brarvork, Zor, Tholtrad
people.note: Half-Orcs, 29–34 — one always guards the tunnel door

people.name: Prusica Heartbridge, Belphina Teaman, Wihaly Foredance, Oditrix Dustvale, Verzira Goodbraid, Iraace Warmwater, Sharfire Rivershadow, Yender Brushgather
Zefree Fernbloom, Eoora Heartbridge, Trillion Mondobeth & 13 more
people.note: The recruit tier — several Mondobeth siblings among them

people.name: Knob, Wilkin, Dialile, Susan, Elitina, Deb
Rinys Glowseeker
people.note: Proprietor of Ebony Camp; former Master Thief of the Moonlight Strategy — all entry goes through her

people.name: Grothen
people.note: Hulking Warforged — steel brow, hinged jaw, faintly glowing blue gem eyes, white button-down under a bleached apron, forever wiping mugs. Staff call him G; everyone else is normally intimidated enough not to ask

voice.who: Any member, asked about the guild
voice.cue: “It's just a social club.” Delivered flat, every time, at every rank.
Knows every city member by face. Strangers get one unhurried question at a time until the vouch is established — or the conversation is suddenly about rooms and ale again.

quirks: The den: beneath Ebony Camp Inn. A first-floor storage room hides a secret door to a closet; a hatch drops thirty feet by sturdy ladder into a large domed structure carved from the island's bedrock.

Den layout — bar to the left (the Warforged tending, four tables before it, two recently pushed together); a roped sparring pit to the right, twenty-foot painted circle with two lines ten feet apart; three beaded thresholds at the back so any breach is heard: kitchen (left), hall to storage and the Master Thief's office/bedroom (center), and a guarded stair down to the city's tunnel and sanitation system (right — a Half-Orc Blackcap at all times).

Entry — through Rinys, always. City members are known to her. Strangers need a vouch: a member of Operative rank or higher, or significantly convincing physical evidence handed over for a 24-hour inspection (a deliberate test of patience). The Empire Rank insignia is accepted, of course.

The sign — a crescent moon with an adjacent four-pointed star shining in four directions, tattooed in the web of the left thumb; hidden by pressing thumb to forefinger. Members have been congregating at The Rare Coin Tavern of late.
hooks: Cross-reference: Ebony Camp (Inn, this city) — the hub above the den.
Cross-reference: The Rare Coin (Tavern, this city) — where a streetwise character finds the guild's edges.
The stair down ties the den into the city's tunnel and sanitation system — one more thread into the Twins' underbelly.
pages.tableHook: A streetwise operative who works this room can come away with a route across the channel that no bridge toll will ever see. Let it be earned, not bought.

pages.name: Running Smiths
pages.atDoor: A second, quieter club in Ru Ailmen's underworld — smaller than the Moonlight Strategy and careful to stay out of its way.
quirks: Not yet detailed beyond its master — a blank the DM can shape. Rivals, subcontractors, or a front for someone else entirely.
hooks: Cross-reference: Moonlight Strategy — how the two clubs divide the city is undefined, and deliberately so.

pages.name: Fletcher Humblegrove
pages.atDoor: A family home that trades from its front room — the Humblegroves are fletchers, and good ones. Feathers, shafts, and glue-pots share space with family life.

people.name: Dankas & Flynzin Humblegrove
people.note: Halflings, 29 and 19 — both in the trade

voice.cue: Inspects any arrow a customer brings in before talking business — and will tell you, kindly but exactly, what's wrong with your fletching.

items.name: Arrows & bolts, made and mended
items.note: Custom fletching on commission; quality work, family pace

hooks: Pairs naturally with The Sad Rug across the channel for a party arming an archer — bows there, arrows here.
pages.tile: No code — a home that trades

pages.name: Mayor's Office
pages.atDoor: Gray roof tiles, per the Tile Code — respect the gray ones. This three-story stone building with white tiles is more functional than the other buildings you've seen in the city. Through the front door is a well-lit reception room with two doors behind the reception desk.

voice.cue: Every question is routed to the correct clerk by portfolio — community, legal, commerce, tax, infrastructure, military. Nothing skips the queue; everything gets a form.

hooks: Any official inquiry about the missing Steward or the lockdown lands here first — and gets referred, politely, elsewhere.

pages.name: Magistrates Offices
pages.atDoor: Gray roof tiles, per the Tile Code. The city's courts — hearings, judgments, and the long benches of those waiting for both.

people.name: Halver Humblelade, Lizlanna Umelana, Tharhulsia Granitefoot

hooks: Only High Crimes trigger a city lockdown — a fact a magistrate's clerk might confirm where a guard would not.

pages.name: Tax Building
pages.atDoor: Gray roof tiles, per the Tile Code. Ledgers, queues, and the city's share of everything.

people.name: Wulfrun Forester, Oston Shadowlade, Zenster Humblehill

voice.cue: Styles himself “City Investor” and corrects anyone who says tax collector — while collecting the tax.

hooks: A Wulpher runs the tax house in each Twin — Herbert here, Dilbert across the channel. Brothers, rivals, or the same joke twice: DM's choice.

pages.name: Shipwright School and Dockworker Guildhouse
pages.atDoor: Gray roof tiles, per the Tile Code. Half school, half union hall — apprentice shipwrights learn their trade above while the dockworkers' guild runs the waterfront from below.
hooks: Anything that moves across the docks is known here before it's known anywhere else.

pages.name: Trade Guild/Bank
pages.atDoor: Gray roof tiles, per the Tile Code. The city's money: trade licenses, letters of credit, deposits and withdrawals — each with its own queue, its own form, and its own stamp.

voice.cue: Nothing moves without the correct sequence: reception, then manager, then teller — and any irregularity restarts the sequence. They are not being difficult; the sequence is the institution.

pages.tableHook: The honest bureaucracy of banking can eat a full day here — and it should. Let the city be exactly this thorough; tables come to love it.

pages.name: Messengers Guildhouse
pages.atDoor: Gray roof tiles, per the Tile Code. Runners in and out at all hours — the city's letters, parcels, and paid discretion.
hooks: Messengers see every threshold in the city. A coin here buys legwork; more coin buys memory.

pages.name: Transportation/Horse Handlers Barn/Guildhouse
pages.atDoor: Gray roof tiles, per the Tile Code. Stables, wagons, and dispatch boards — the guild that moves people and freight through the city's streets.

pages.name: Sanitation Guildhouse
pages.atDoor: Gray roof tiles, per the Tile Code. The least glamorous guild in the city — and the one whose domain runs beneath every other.
quirks: DM only — the Twins' sanitation system was commissioned from the dwarves, who carved the greatest such works in the Empire beneath both cities. The guild holds the maps of what's mapped — which is not all of it.
hooks: Cross-reference: the Twins' underbelly. Every route below the channel eventually touches this guild's territory.

pages.name: City Guardhouse
pages.atDoor: Gray roof tiles, per the Tile Code. Tarry Hillbrand holds the reception desk — unhurried, seen everything, gives away nothing.

voice.cue: “This is basic procedure for the type of crime that is under investigation.” Same words, every time.
“Only High Crimes qualify for this procedure. That is something anyone could find out, of course — but it is not widely known.”

hooks: The lockdown, the manhunt, and the ways in and out of the city being watched all route through this desk — and forward into the Locked Twins chapter.
pages.tableHook: A party arriving with a body from the river voyage and pre-filled paperwork finds the desk too swamped by an ongoing city crisis to make trouble. While the forms are stamped, a sharp-eyed PC can glimpse the working documents: a manhunt is on, and no one moves in or out of the city until an order says otherwise.

pages.name: FIre Watchouse
pages.atDoor: Gray roof tiles, per the Tile Code. Watch bells, water wagons, and long ladders — a city of tile roofs still burns from the inside.

pages.name: Clack Tower Guildhouse
pages.atDoor: Gray roof tiles, per the Tile Code. The clack tower relays coded messages across the realm at speeds no rider can match — the guild guards its codes as tightly as its tower.
hooks: DM only — even under the lockdown, the clacks still deliver information across the channel. Nothing else goes over. That asymmetry is a lever.
A Forehare runs the clack guild in each Twin — Diani here, Doni across the channel.

pages.name: Clearwater Co., Ru Ailmen Holding
pages.atDoor: Brown roof tiles, per the Tile Code. One of the three great trade companies' holdings on this side of the channel — crates, tallies, and hired watchmen.

pages.name: Banminster Co., Ru Ailmen Holding
pages.atDoor: Brown roof tiles, per the Tile Code. One of the three great trade companies' holdings on this side of the channel — crates, tallies, and hired watchmen.
quirks: DM only — a “warehouse worker” contact can be positioned here to open the way into the Twins' underbelly: a shaft elevator inside descends roughly 380 feet to the sewer system below.
hooks: Cross-reference: the underbelly route in the Locked Twins chapter begins at this door for parties working through underworld contacts.
pages.tableHook: A streetwise operative can arrange a contact here — “They will know who you are and approach you” — and a warehouse worker will lead the party to the shaft elevator and the long descent into the sewers.

pages.name: Applesor Co., Ru Ailmen Holding
pages.atDoor: Brown roof tiles, per the Tile Code. One of the three great trade companies' holdings on this side of the channel — crates, tallies, and hired watchmen.

cities.name: Yuvl Ilmern
cities.note: The Council's city — twelve portfolios where its twin has one throne, and the Council of Twelve Docks mirroring the Sovereign's across the water. In time, the party's home city.

voice.cue: A nod of the head and a non-energetic “The Sad Rug — Bows n Ammo. Bows, or ammo?” — with a gesture at the back wall. That is the whole pitch.

pages.name: The Sparkling Book Toy Store
pages.atDoor: Yellow roof tiles, per the Tile Code. Books of every shape and size adorn the shelves left and right; odds and ends hang on the back wall and sit on the shelves below. Qivira Earthsun rocks in a chair to the right of the back wall.

voice.cue: A kind “Welcome to The Sparkling Book Toy Store — anything you are looking for in specific?” She calls everything in the shop a book or a toy, including the cauldron.

items.name: Some Adventuring Gear
items.note: A partial selection

quirks: The “toy” shelf casually holds items worth more than most city blocks. Qivira does not advertise; the right customers find her.

pages.name: Go Figure
pages.atDoor: Purple roof tiles, per the Tile Code. A shop for those with an interest in the arcane, specializing in wondrous items. Mirrin Fentumal sits among her wares behind a corner desk — preserved alligator heads, stuffed owls, bowls of fine crystal, ivory, incense, and the list goes on, hanging from racks and crowding low shelves.

voice.cue: If she doesn't have what a customer wants, she'll look into finding it — purely, she says, for the curiosity of finding an item for an adventurer. She means it, and she remembers every request.

quirks: Stock rotates day to day — what's on the shelves tomorrow is the DM's to invent (or Mirrin's to procure on request).

pages.name: Cheering Hammer Pharmacy
pages.atDoor: Green roof tiles, per the Tile Code. A Twins-pattern apothecary kept by Norgun Woldbraid: stoppered bottles on low shelves flanking the counter, cauldrons and labeled ingredients behind.

items.note: Stock at DM's discretion — mirror the Ru Ailmen houses

pages.name: Palace of the Councle of Twelve
pages.atDoor: The seat of Yuvl Ilmern's government — where Ru Ailmen answers to one Sovereign, this city answers to twelve. Multicolored tiled roofs rise behind its walls, and the Council Guard keep its gates and its docks.

voice.cue: Twelve portfolios, twelve doors, twelve schedules. Petitioners are asked, first and always: which Counsel does your matter concern? The wrong answer costs a day.

quirks: DM only — the Sovereign's Steward was last seen crossing the Sovereign Bridge toward this palace, a tenday before the party arrives. What the Council knows, and which of the Twelve knows it, is the thread of the Locked Twins chapter.
hooks: The Council of Twelve Docks below the palace mirror Ru Ailmen's Sovereign Docks — heavily guarded, and the first thing a river arrival sees of this city's power.

pages.name: Mayor's Office
pages.atDoor: Gray roof tiles, per the Tile Code. The city's civic front desk — functional stone, well-lit reception, a clerk for every portfolio.

voice.cue: Every question is routed to the correct clerk by portfolio. Nothing skips the queue; everything gets a form.

pages.name: Magistrates Offices
pages.atDoor: Gray roof tiles, per the Tile Code. The city's courts — hearings, judgments, and the long benches of those waiting for both.

people.name: Marlyse Fatfound, Eliola Boulderhill, Hilzira Reedbrace

pages.name: Tax Building
pages.atDoor: Gray roof tiles, per the Tile Code. Ledgers, queues, and the city's share of everything.

people.name: Teamin Forewillow, Idolan Swiftfoot, Yenvon Keenseeker

voice.cue: Styles himself “City Investor” — exactly like his counterpart across the channel, and neither will admit who used it first.

hooks: A Wulpher runs the tax house in each Twin — Dilbert here, Herbert across the channel.

pages.name: Shipwright School and Dockworker Guildhouse
pages.atDoor: Gray roof tiles, per the Tile Code. Half school, half union hall — this city's mirror of the trade across the channel.
hooks: Anything that moves across the docks is known here before it's known anywhere else.

pages.name: Trade Guild/Bank
pages.atDoor: Gray roof tiles, per the Tile Code. The city's money: trade licenses, letters of credit, deposits and withdrawals — queues, forms, and stamps.

voice.cue: The sequence is the institution here too: reception, manager, teller. Vault access requires the manager and the proprietor both.

pages.tableHook: A party returning to sign the deed to their home finds their group name recognized at the counter — and any funds left in their name waiting. Small courtesies land hard here.

pages.name: Messengers Guildhouse
pages.atDoor: Gray roof tiles, per the Tile Code. Runners in and out at all hours — the city's letters, parcels, and paid discretion.
hooks: Messengers see every threshold in the city. A coin here buys legwork; more coin buys memory.

pages.name: Transportation/Horse Handlers Barn/Guildhouse
pages.atDoor: Gray roof tiles, per the Tile Code. Stables, wagons, and dispatch boards — the guild that moves people and freight through the city's streets.

pages.name: Sanitation Guildhouse
pages.atDoor: Gray roof tiles, per the Tile Code. The least glamorous guild in the city — and the one whose domain runs beneath every other.
quirks: DM only — the dwarven-carved sanitation works run beneath both Twins. This guild holds the maps of what's mapped — which is not all of it.
hooks: Cross-reference: the Twins' underbelly.

pages.name: FIre Watchouse
pages.atDoor: Gray roof tiles, per the Tile Code. Watch bells, water wagons, and long ladders.

pages.name: Clack Tower Guildhouse
pages.atDoor: Gray roof tiles, per the Tile Code. The clack tower relays coded messages across the realm at speeds no rider can match.
hooks: DM only — even under a lockdown, the clacks still deliver across the channel when nothing else moves. That asymmetry is a lever.
A Forehare runs the clack guild in each Twin — Doni here, Diani across the channel.

pages.name: City Guardhouse
pages.atDoor: Gray roof tiles, per the Tile Code. Flynster Brushbrace holds this city's reception desk with the same practiced neutrality as his counterpart across the channel.

voice.cue: “This is basic procedure for the type of crime that is under investigation.” The line is identical on both shores — which is itself information.

hooks: The lockdown and the manhunt route through this desk too — and forward into the Locked Twins chapter.

pages.name: Dark Star
pages.atDoor: The Dark Star operates at Empire scale — a cell-based organization whose reach extends far beyond this city. Its Yuvl Ilmern presence is a den like any other club's, and nothing like any other club's.
quirks: DM only — the Dark Star recognizes an Empire-level Operative insignia; carrying one opens doors here as it does in guild dens across the realm.

DM only — the organization's guide document is a stub in the source material. Roster, den location, and local leadership are the DM's to shape. The campaign book's Dark Star cells (agents and cutthroats in Appendix A) are the mechanical anchor.
hooks: Cross-reference: the Dark Star cell aboard the Lithgow (Contingency C1) and Dark Star appearances through the campaign chapters — this den is their home port in the Twins.

pages.name: Earthshroud
pages.atDoor: Yuvl Ilmern's homegrown club — smaller and quieter than the Dark Star's operation, and careful about it.
quirks: Not yet detailed beyond its master — a blank the DM can shape. How Earthshroud coexists with an Empire-scale outfit in its own city is the interesting question.

channel.name: The Channel
channel.note: The water, the bridges, and the yellow-uniformed Bridge Guard between the Twins — neither city’s territory, and busier than both.

pages.name: Twins Channel Hub Stations
pages.atDoor: In the middle of each of the three great bridges stands a grand structure: the Twins Channel Station. Ten-foot arches in rows of three, a few feet apart, with three sets of stairs rising to them — you can see clean through the building to an identical exit on the far side. The first thing you notice is the uniforms: yellow, and of a different cut than either the Sovereign's or the Council of Twelve's guard. Eight soldiers on each side, three between each set of stairs. The center station carries a third floor the others lack.

people.name: Specialist Hobbs
people.note: Human, he/him, 22 — Bridge Guard; one of several performing greeting duty

voice.cue: “Welcome to the [East / Central / West] Twins Hub. I am Specialist Hobbs of the Bridge Guard. Are you seeking passage, travel, or immigration?” — and he will steer you to the correct queue for whichever you choose.
Very professional. Attempts at conversation are met with “We're not allowed to have conversations on duty. Please move along.” (DC 20 Persuasion to get one talking.)

voice.who: A guard, on the city guards
voice.cue: Any mention of the other guard forces is met with contempt: they don't train enough — “it'd be us doing the fighting if any real trouble came to the Twins.”

items.name: Toll-exemption papers
items.note: Requires a listed sponsor: Office of the Sovereign · Office of the Council of Twelve · either city's Captain of the Guard · a representative of Clearwater, Banminster, or Applesor Co.

items.name: Destinations
items.note: Port of Beni Ali (Corasant Coast, Tellason) · Port of Heerisim (Turum Coast, Tellason) · Isle of Rockporth · Sierra Archipelago. Unavailable (unsafe): Broth Isle · anywhere along the Serrated Island Chain

items.name: By appointment, city to city
items.note: Announced travel between major cities only. Destinations: Bethal · East Omaththyr · Kitetown · Brimwater

quirks: Perception, on approach (within 30 ft; all DCs drop by 5 once inside): DC 10 — a large oval desk in the center, twelve clerks in sets of four, a queue per set, guards directing flow, and doors that can close but sit just barely visible so the building looks inviting. DC 15 — stairs to the second floor on each side; a line of guards off each end of the desk, alternating facing, an arm's length apart, so no one passes unseen. DC 20 — the guards' discipline is exceptional; signage routes every kind of visitor. DC 25 — Arrivals and Departures signs flank the stairs on opposite faces of the building.

The changing of the guard is a spectacle: double files trot down the stairs in perfect sync on both sides, envelop the standing line, and relieve it without a word — worth narrating once. The greeter's follow-up writes itself: “It's a sight to behold — but please, are you seeking passage, travel, or immigration?”

DM only — above each hub, two barracks (lead-lined iron wall between) hold two teleportation circle rooms: one Arrival, one Departure, each with its own mage and heavy guard. The Departure door's bars rest on the floor; the Arrival door is barred.

DM only — the Central Hub's third floor is the Empress' Teleportation Circle. This is not common knowledge: no one is allowed up there, and only a leak from the guards or an official who already knows can reveal it.
hooks: Under the Locked Twins lockdown, these desks are where 'no one in or out' becomes a scene rather than a sentence.
Present an imperial writ at the passage desk and watch officialdom meet paperwork it cannot refuse — a favorite scene waiting to happen.

pages.name: Twins Channel Station Immigration
pages.atDoor: The immigration queue at any Twins Hub leads here: the office where residency in either Twin becomes real. If you plan to reside in one of the Twin Cities, you must register your deeds and permits at this desk.

voice.cue: Precision courtesy. Every deed, every permit, every signature has a correct form — and a deadline. They are genuinely helpful right up until the deadline passes.

items.name: Deed & permit registration
items.note: Required for residency in either Twin

quirks: DM only — a property granted to a group can be deeded under a group name, or a single representative may sign with a signed affidavit of leadership from the remaining members. Transfers carry a thirty-day deadline from delivery of the notice, after which the transfer is null and void.
hooks: After a party is awarded a home in Yuvl Ilmern, this office's missive — sign within thirty days or lose the deed — turns paperwork into a session-opening scene. The letter template works for any party that puts down roots here.

pages.name: Beneath the Channel
pages.atDoor: On the channel floor — past thick, deliberate seaweed and boulders ten feet wide and bigger — a wide, rune-etched circle glows on the silt. Crescent-moon stones are set around its heart, where a tiered stone altar, tarnished and mossy, rises to chest height with a purple chest resting atop it.
quirks: The trigger — anyone breaching the perimeter of the circle toward the chest activates a homing signal for the giant sharks that roam the channel and summons two water elementals.
The chest is magically sealed to the plinth (easily dispelled), trapped, and locked. Identify reveals it is a magic item, plus the complexity of trap and lock and their 24-hour reset.

Trap — DC 20 Investigation to spot. DC 18 Insight: it's a puzzle box, and the box should be removed from the plinth to work it (allows a help action or a separate proficient Insight); DC 25 Insight grants advantage on the disarm. Disarm: DC 25 Sleight of Hand, +2 per retry until the 24-hour reset. Triggers: unlocking before disarming, or rolling 14 or lower on a disarm attempt. Effect: DC 17 Dexterity for half; 20-ft blast, 6d6 lightning within 10 ft, half beyond.
Lock — DC 25 Dexterity (thieves' tools), +2 per attempt until the 24-hour reset.
hooks: This is the rumored treasure in the middle of the Twins Channel — the rumor circulates on both shores, and retired bridge guards tell it best.
Dive it with water breathing, fight off the guardians, and claim the chest itself. The full run lives in Side Quests: The Treasure of the Twins Channel.

maps.name: The Twin Cities — City Map
maps.caption: The Twin Cities — Ru Ailmen & Yuvl Ilmern
maps.blurb: The hand-drawn map of both cities across the Twins Channel, framed and lettered. Numbered roof tiles key every keyed building to the Tile Code — pair it with the legend page. Player-facing: safe to push.

maps.name: The Tile Code — Legend
maps.caption: The Tile Code — learn a building by its roof
maps.blurb: The keyed legend for the city map: every numbered tile named, grouped by roof color. Push it beside the map so the table can read the streets themselves.

maps.name: The Underbelly — Sewer Leg (Ru Ailmen)
maps.caption: The Underbelly — the sewer leg, beneath Ru Ailmen
maps.blurb: Schematic survey of the dwarves' sanitation works under Ru Ailmen and the thieves' road through it. The console copy carries small gold room keys (S1–S18); the pushed copy is bare. Fog of war is yours: click rooms below to reveal them, and the push carries the fog with it. The route, the locks, and the callouts live in Chapter 5 (5.2–5.4).

maps.caption: The Underbelly — the vault leg, under Yuvl Ilmern
maps.blurb: Schematic survey of the far side of the Channel Expanse, under Yuvl Ilmern — the survey's printed keys 1–26. The console copy carries the room keys; the pushed copy is bare. Fog of war is yours: click rooms below to reveal them, and the push carries the fog with it. The route, the sealed door, and the fixed features live in Chapter 5 (5.2–5.4).

maps.name: The Underbelly — Legend
maps.caption: The Underbelly — how to read the survey
maps.blurb: One key for both legs: floors, channels, bridges, doors, grates, stairs, and the survey glyphs. No room keys, no fog — push it beside either map.

maps.name: Race up the Spiral — Lower Turn (6.3)
maps.caption: Oospufmorn — the trunk stair, lower turn
maps.blurb: One full turn of the trunk stair at three-quarters height, gridded at 5 ft. Enter at the star (bottom), ascend clockwise, exit through the pale STAIRS UP wedge onto the upper turn. The console copy carries the party entry and scout positions with tactical notes; the pushed copy is bare terrain. Rise ~20 ft per turn; the outer edge has no rail.

maps.name: Race up the Spiral — Upper Turn (6.3)
maps.caption: Oospufmorn — the trunk stair, upper turn
maps.blurb: The final turn: scouts falling back, the STAIRS UP wedge opening onto the platform (6.4). Console copy shows the scouts' fallback positions; the pushed copy is bare terrain. Same grid, same clockwise ascent, +20 to +40 ft over the lower turn's start.

maps.name: The Platform — Heart of Oospufmorn (6.4)
maps.caption: Oospufmorn — the platform
maps.blurb: The top platform: trunk core and a 15-ft gridded ring, railing everywhere but the south stair gap where the party arrives at the star. The console copy carries the bore, the sawdust, the hidden teleport circle, and every enemy start position; the pushed copy is bare terrain — the bore and circle stay verbal until the table sees or finds them.

maps.name: The Estate — Manor Floor Plan
maps.caption: The Estate — the party's new home in the Twins
maps.blurb: The full floor plan of the manor: front and back courtyards, covered porches, dining and living room, kitchen and servants' wing, coach house, office, bar — and up to seven bedrooms. Player-facing: safe to push.

maps.name: The Estate — Basements & Second Floor
maps.caption: The Estate — the house's other levels
maps.blurb: Three structures on one sheet: the small basement below br1 (upper left), the main basement with its secret door on the north wall (center), and the second floor at the spiral stair (bottom). The secret door is drawn on the sheet - push when found, not before.

bhindarul.title: Bhindarul
bhindarul.intro: Bhindarul, capital of Knakknthazn — the enormous underground city beneath Lake Sala'amas: a perfect stone dome two hundred fifty miles in radius, hub of the wheel that spirals beneath all four realms. Candlelit windows and blue street lamps outline the dark, the rune-turned waters keep the climate unreasonably kind, and once a year the city gets its Week of Sun & Sky. The party arrives in Chapter 10 as honored guests of the Low Keep. The keyed streets are Thig Dural Thane, the Royal District — and there are no roof tiles to read down here: every door carries the kingdom's official signs, pictures and words together, so that all who walk the deep roads can read them.
bhindarul.signFrame: Every door in the Royal District carries the kingdom's official sign: an iron plate beside the door, the trade cut deep enough to read by fingertip, the words beneath in Dwarvish and Common — pictures and words, for all.
signCode: A bed beneath a hanging lantern
A tankard, foam three lines high
A wand crossing a four-pointed spark
A hammer above an anvil, the forge-clan's mark beneath
An open awning, the market-clan's mark beneath
A banded crate under the Thane's crown — the mark of a Thane Reserve
No trade plate — the clan's own crest, cut in stone above the door
A candle cupped in an open palm
The crowned mountain, cut in iron
The crowned mountain, cut in gold
bhindarul.signCodeNote: "The pictures are for strangers. The words are a courtesy. The signs are the law." — posted in four tongues at the Drrosh Doors
highlights: The forge crawl — four clan forges, contract arrow work with a free quote, and a wand store called Wicked Arsenal.
The Transportation building — no vehicles, no counter, just a small circle under an archway; the polite thing is to step on mid-sentence.
Markets A–D — four clans, four awnings, and everything the deep roads carry.
Mercy Vale and the three pharmacies — the district takes its healing seriously.
The Week of Sun & Sky — ask any local; they will stop what they're doing to tell you.

districts.name: Thig Dural Thane — the Royal District
districts.note: The eight clans in their balance: Bittermaster (Ri), Barrelshoulder (Ro), Kegborn (Li) and Woldtank (Lo) hold the forges; Trollgranite (A, Ri), Bluntjaw (B, Ro), Hilltoe (C, Lo) and Barbedbreaker (D, Li) hold the markets. Every clan keeps its Mannor and its Thane Reserve. The ledger keys every door by quadrant — Ri northeast, Ro southeast, Lo southwest, Li northwest, quartered by the four main roads — blocks 1–14 clockwise in a horseshoe: 1 at the dome gate, in to 7 at the Inner Sanctum, 8 back out to 14 at the far gate. Mannors at 5 and 10 on the inner circle; each clan's Thane Reserve at 4 and 11, straight across the market on the outer. Forges at 7, remedies at 8 — the Hospital holding Li8, the block beside the Low Keep — and blocks 3, 6, 9 and 12 keep their doors unkeyed.

pages.name: The Storm Hammer Garage
pages.atDoor: An iron plate by the door — a wand crossing a four-pointed spark, per the Sign Code — though the clutter spilling toward the street says it first. The Storm Hammer Garage is a working being: a bit cluttered and grungy, but solid wares for the hard-core adventurer. Khulgroubelynn Koboldaxe keeps the floor.

items.name: Stormcleave
items.note: magic battleaxe — full properties in Appendix C: Stormcleave

items.name: Poison Cloud arrows
items.note: On hit: poisonous gas in a 10-ft sphere, lightly obscuring; lasts 10 rounds unless removed by strong wind. 1d4 poison on entering the cloud or starting a turn in it.

items.name: Magefire arrows

maps.name: Bhindarul — City Map

The DM copy keys every door: each block wears its trade's sign with the number beneath in the trade's color, the Keep and markets A–D on the Sanctum ring, quadrant letters in the corners. It shows the five capitals as the world believes them: Trionshen, Bethal, East Omaththyr, The Twins, Kitetown. The spiral west of Arret is THE CRASSAC GYRE. Player-facing: safe to push — the island at the gyre's centre (The Still) is deliberately NOT drawn, so nothing on this image gives it away.

pits.note: Pit boss commentary bank — one voice for every house. The console picks a line to match each moment on the board (bets opening or closing, a knockout, a dominant or narrow or drawn round, a natural-1 stumble, sudden death, a decision, an upset, the favorite holding) and never repeats a line until its shelf is empty. {w} and {l} are filled with the fighters' names at the table.

commentary.text: The chalk is up and the line is honest — tonight, anyway. Coin on the board or opinions to yourself.
Bets are open. The house takes all comers and keeps all grudges.
The line's posted. Don't ask me to explain it — the chalk did the thinking.
Board's live, purses out. You've got until the rope drops.
Chalk's wet, odds are fresh. First bet of the night rides lucky — that's a lie I tell every night.
Chalk's closed! What's on the board stays on the board.
Bets are done. Anyone still holding coin, hold it tight and watch.
The rope drops, the book shuts. Nobody bets on a fight they can already see.
That's the close. Your coin's the house's problem now — or you're mine.
Book's shut. From here on it's just two people and bad intentions.
Down! {w} puts {l} to sleep and the circle counts nothing — there's no counting from that. Pay the window, mind the boots.
One clean shot and the lamps went out for {l}. That's the pit, friends — hours of maybe, one second of certainly.
{w} found the button. {l} found the floor. The house finds your slips.
Knockout! Somebody fetch water and somebody fetch the ledger — in that order, we're not animals.
That's a finish. {l} will remember none of it and the winners will retell all of it.
Good night, {l}. {w} by knockout, and the chalk never lies twice in a row.
{w} takes the round walking. {l} is still in it the way a fish is still in the boat.
That round wasn't close and everybody's coin knows it. {w}, clean.
Round to {w}, and not politely. Somebody check {l}'s corner for a plan.
{w} owned every inch of that one. The chalk said this could happen — the chalk is smug about it.
One-way traffic. {w} takes it, {l} takes the lesson.
That's a statement round from {w}. The house has seen statements answered before — but not many.
Round to {w} — by a whisker and a judge squinting. This one's alive.
{w} edges it. If you blinked, you bet on the blink.
Close round, {w}'s round. The book stays nervous and so should you.
{w} by inches. {l} will want those inches back.
That's {w}'s round on the count, barely. Nobody in this room could tell you why, including me.
Razor thin, {w} takes it. Fights like this pay for the roof.
Even round! Both still standing, both still ugly about it.
Nothing between them. The chalk holds its breath — so does the book.
Round's a wash. Give them a minute, they'll give you a reason.
Dead level. Somebody has to want it more, and soon.
{l} slips! The pit's oldest opponent is the floor and it's undefeated.
Oh, that's ugly. {l} throws it, misses it, and wears it. Round to {w}.
{l} tripped over nothing but ambition. The room will not let that go.
A gift! {l} hands {w} the round wrapped in ribbon.
That wasn't fighting, that was falling with confidence. {w}'s round.
Level after three! Sudden death — next round takes it all, and the room knows it.
Dead even and we go again. One round, no tomorrow. Hold your coin and your neighbor.
Three rounds and nothing settled. The pit settles everything eventually — right now, in fact.
It's done — {w} on the rounds. No sleep, no doubt, just arithmetic.
{w} takes the bout. {l} walks out, which around here counts as a good night.
Final: {w}. The chalk called it in dust and it calls it now in coin.
That's the fight — {w} by decision. Settle up, and no crying at the window.
Well now. {w} just beat the chip off {l}'s belt. The book bleeds and the room roars — enjoy it, it's rare.
Upset! {w} takes down {l} and the chalk eats its words. Winners, form a line. House, form a grudge.
The line said no and {w} said watch. That's why they fight the fights, friends.
{w} holds, as the chalk said and the chip promised. Order is restored and the house sleeps easy.
No miracle tonight — {w} handles {l} the way the tier says. The line was a warning, not an invitation.
{w} does exactly what the odds paid so little for. Favorites, friends: cheap to back, dear to doubt.

pitch.note: The pit boss's pitch — pushed whole to the player screen from Run the Table › Fighting Pits. One voice for every house; the display attributes it to the venue's named boss. {p1}–{p4} are filled from pits.purse at push time so the patter can never drift from the payout.

beats.head: THE BOOK
beats.text: I write the line, you lay your coin against my book. Your fighter wins, I pay your stake times the odds — 10 gp at 2:1 walks away with 20 of mine on top of it. Your fighter loses, your coin stays behind to keep me honest.

beats.head: STEP IN
beats.text: Anyone can enter the circle — and I mean anyone, friend. You start at Tier I like everyone before you. Two wins at your tier or better and I stamp you the next chip. The chip is yours forever, and it is honored at every pit on the continent. The chalk remembers you. So do I.

beats.head: YOUR OWN EDGE
beats.text: My fighters roll their tier — plus two at Tier I, plus four at II, plus six at III, plus eight at IV. They earned it. You roll your own skill on the d20: Athletics, Acrobatics, whatever your approach argues — name it before you step in. A natural 20 puts somebody to sleep. A natural 1 hands the round away.

beats.head: THE PURSE
beats.text: Win in my circle and I pay you like a fighter — the bout's tier sets the purse: {p1} gp at Tier I, {p2} at Tier II, {p3} at Tier III, {p4} at Tier IV. Beat somebody above your chip and you take their tier's purse. Lose, and you still leave with the story.

pitch.outro: That's the whole game, friend. The rest is bad intentions.

dans.note: Above the four house tiers of the fighting pits sits a ladder of TEN DANS that has nothing to do with any one pit and is not owned by any house. A dan is a grade, not a title — it is not held against comers and cannot be taken by beating you. It is bestowed once and it stays.
dans.openKnowledge: THE LADDER IS PUBLIC KNOWLEDGE AND PRIVATE RECOGNITION. What the ranks are and how they are attained is easy to learn — any hall will tell a stranger the whole thing in an afternoon, and nobody treats it as a secret. But OUTSIDE MARTIAL CIRCLES THERE IS NO RECOGNITION AT ALL. A dan is a fact about a fighter that most of the world has no reason to hold: no civic honour, no herald, no announcement at a race, no crowd that knows what it means. Knowing what a sixth dan IS and caring that someone is one are different things. Only the tenth reaches further, and only as legend.
dans.gate: THE PITS ARE THE FILTER. A fighter does not enter the dan ladder — they qualify for it. Tier IV, the top of a house's chalk, is the GATE: reach it and the ladder is open to you, and the pit tiers stop being a ceiling and start being an entrance. Everything below the gate is chips and accumulated wins. Everything above it is tested.

testing.summary: EVERY RANK IS TESTED. Nothing above the gate accumulates: there is no counting of wins, no time served, no chip. For each rank in turn, the candidate fights ONE bout — the testing — and a panel decides.
testing.opponent: The opponent must hold a rank ABOVE the candidate's target-1 — in practice, at least the rank being tested for. You are never tested against a peer.
testing.panel: THREE judges, each at least one rank higher than the candidate. They may be of any higher rank; a Si Jo qualifies to judge anybody.
testing.verdict: THE PANEL DECIDES, NOT THE SCOREBOARD. The three watch the bout and each says yes or no. The result of the fight is evidence and nothing more — it is entirely possible to win the bout and not be given the rank, and that possibility is the reason a panel exists instead of a win condition.
testing.refusal: A refused fighter may ask the same panel again, or assemble a different one, WHENEVER THEY LIKE. There is no waiting period and no limit on attempts. The cost of a refusal is not a timer — it is that you must get four of your seniors into one room again.
testing.logistics: That is the real limiter, and it tightens as you climb. Four seniors is easy at the bottom of the ladder and nearly impossible at the top.

summit.title: Si Jo
summit.note: The tenth is not a better ninth. A tenth dan founds a school: they name a style and it exists, and it outlives them. This is the only rank the world at large has heard of — Si Jo are legends outside martial circles as well as in them, which no other rung manages.
summit.style: THE FOUNDER NAMES THE STYLE, and the console records the name and then gets out of the way. It grants nothing — no feat, no bonus, no mechanic. A style with a rider becomes a feat; a style with a name becomes a legacy, and the second is the reward. The three styles known in Arret are Dragon Fang, Chuan Lu and One Punch, and each was named by the person who made it.
summit.standing: A NEW SI JO JOINS THE POOL PERMANENTLY — they always have a place at the chalk as an opponent or as one of the three, for anyone who rises to where testing is required. A party's own fighter becomes the furniture the next one climbs.

arret.note: ARRET HAS EXACTLY THREE SI JO, and the arithmetic of that is not a coincidence — it is the shape of the whole ladder. A testing bout needs FOUR seniors: three judges and an opponent. Against the roster below, the 8th-to-9th test has exactly four eligible people on the entire continent (the lone 9th dan and the three Si Jo), so there is precisely ONE possible configuration of that bout in Arret and it requires the sitting 9th dan to stand across the circle from whoever is coming up behind her. And the 9th-to-10th test needs four TENTH dans. Arret has three.
arret.wall: THE TENTH DAN CANNOT BE EARNED ON THIS CONTINENT. The fourth is fetched from across the water, or the candidate travels to where the fourth already is. The Si Jo gather in a handful of places in the world and one of them is reachable from Arret: THE STILL, the inhabited floating island in the eye of the Crassac Gyre, west of the continent — DM knowledge, not drawn on any map, and the reason the world map matters to this feature at all. The obstacle and the solution are the same place.

siJo.name: Kuori “One Punch” Vaimei-Laga
siJo.seat: no fixed address — a walking circuit of the One Punch towns: Brimwater · Mutemere · Kitetown · the Dragonspine, and Zethel in race season
siJo.problem: Hard to find, trivial to ask.
siJo.note: Finding him is the entire work; once found he says yes to almost anyone, because that is what the style is. A goliath's nickname is earned and descriptive — the mountain named the man, and the man named the style after what he was called.

siJo.name: Lu Wenshan
siJo.seat: Bethal — the Lu hall, in the Shining City
siJo.problem: Easy to find, impossible to move.
siJo.note: Everyone knows the door. She does not travel and she does not judge anywhere but her own hall, so a panel that needs her is a panel that convenes in Bethal. Chuan Lu is named for the HOUSE, not the technique — the Lu family's fist — and she is the first Lu.

siJo.name: Kairon Malveth
siJo.seat: THE STILL — the floating island in the eye of the Crassac Gyre (DM-ONLY; not drawn on any map)
siJo.note: A journey, not a conversation — and the one seat that is also a door. Dragon Fang's ranked fighters sit in Trionshen; Aurel Sannecht teaches it at the palace and Threx Ordal is its showpiece. The style became the Empire's and its founder left. Dragon Fang is courtly BECAUSE Malveth is not there.

say.note: SAY IT RIGHT AT THE TABLE. A dan is pronounced DON — it rhymes with “on”, not with “man”, so a fourth dan is a “fourth DON”. Si Jo is SEE-jo — two beats, the first stressed, the J soft as in “Joe”. The words are borrowed and the halls are particular about them: an NPC who hears a PC say “DAN” the way you would say the name will place them instantly as someone who has read about the ladder and never stood on it. That is a free and very cheap character beat, and it costs a PC nothing to ask a hall how it is said.

carnival.note: The Flower Carnival's midway - barkers, rules, and prizes for Run the Table > Carnival Games. Rules pushes read from here so the screen and the booth can never disagree; DM notes stay on this side of the table. The Wand of Smiles is once only, ever - the console keeps the flag.

games.name: Ring Toss
games.barker: Hello! I am Lareth and this is the Ring Toss! Three silver for three rings! You have to stand on the rug and ring the post! One point for each ring on the post. Three levels of prizes!
rules: Stand on the rug - the post is ten feet out, the rings are three-inch copper.
Each throw is a Dexterity check, DC 18 - meets it, beats it. One point for each ring on the post.
Prizes by points - one: a strawberry. Two: a caramel apple. Three: a small package with high potential.
games.dm: The small package: a packet of glimmerdust (fly your speed for 1 minute) - one packet per customer, ever; the console tracks the names. Reveal what it is only when all three rings land - until then it stays a package.

games.name: Wrestling Match
games.barker: Hello, I am Hans and this is Frans and we are here to… pin you. The price is two silver but the prizes differ, for I am Hans the apprentice and he is Frans the master. Which do you choose?
rules: Choose your opponent: Hans the apprentice (+2) or Frans the master (+4). The six-foot painted circle is the whole world.
Each turn is an opposed roll - declare the pin (Strength) or the ring-out (Dexterity). A tie is no fall, and the turn is spent.
Three falls inside five turns takes the prize: Hans - an adorned wooden shortsword. Frans - the pot, 22 gp 8 sp, sitting in plain view on the stool.

games.name: Shell Game
games.barker: Three shells, one pebble, one silver. Eyes open, coin down - I shuffle honest, which is the part nobody believes.
rules: One silver a play - up to five rounds in a row for one player. Call it - LEFT, MIDDLE, or RIGHT - and the shells come up.
Watch the shuffle - Wisdom (Perception) DC 20, meets it beats it: Odo's hands slow, and the board narrows to two shells. A true 50/50.
Three wins inside the five rounds takes the face paint (disguise self, 1 hour).
games.dm: On a DC 20 watch, push the 50/50 - the screen highlights two shells, the pebble's and one empty, and never says which is which. Below 20, no help - the hands were faster.

games.name: Flowers in the Bouquet
games.barker: One silver, one guess - how many flowers in the bouquet? Count sharp. There's always one more than you think.
rules: One silver a guess. An Intelligence check, DC 17, lands the right number - the bouquet is yours.
DC 22 counts even the flower tied around the stems - the bouquet, and once only, a nine-inch wooden wand twined with silver.
Under 17, the flowers keep their count - and Petalla keeps the silver.
games.dm: The silver-twined wand is a Wand of Smiles - never name it; let Identify do the introducing. 3 charges. Action, 1 charge: one humanoid within 30 feet makes a DC 10 Charisma save or smiles for 1 minute. All charges return at dawn - and when the last charge is spent, roll a d20: on a 1 the wand becomes a Wand of Scowls (same wand, but frowns).
